I need the protein but not the egg. My online search finally bore fruit the other day when I came upon Acai matcha tea. This fine tasting tea has more protein than eggs. Hurray! What a relief...

After reading some reviews I was hesitant to buy this taffy but decided to give it a try. I'm glad I did! It arrived on time and was chewy and soft. Wonderful flavors I love and some I have never tried before were a real treat! I'll defenitely order this again.
After suffering from flu like symptoms for a week, I tried this tea with honey and it was not only delicious, but after using for a day... I feel so much better.

Summary: Got this for my dad for Christmas and he loved it
Text: This basket was perfect for my 89 year old father, who is tough to shop for. He enjoyed the meat and cheese, but returned the coffee bits to me (he's not a coffee drinker). So I got to share in the festivities too! If you're looking for something to get someone who is difficult to shop for or to please, you can't go wrong with meat and cheese, sweets, or coffee generally.
Nice tasting coffee ... taste is not overbearing .. light vanilla hazelnut flavor.  And the price was right.

I'm on my second order for these Frontier White Onions. They smell and taste great. I find them so handy for meatloaves, soups @ stews,and all sorts of casseroles. In an air tight container, they last well to the end of the bag. I've used the store brands, and the dollar jars, of onions, but these are a far greater quality. They're simply great.
Our dog MUST have her Greenies!  She actually will be very patient until 4:00 and then she will start stomping her feet at you to tell you it's time for the G. We try never to run out of these.

Summary: Great for Senior Dogs/priced too high
Text:
My dog has always consumed and loved pedigree, but with age she had needed some additonal help. The Healthy Maturity formula has all the nutrition needed for healthy joints which has slowed her down lately. I think this dog food has helped her to get along better than before we started it. Since it is loaded with salmon/fish oil, it has a rather potent smell and has made the dog very 'gassy' if you know what I mean. Of course my kids think it is funnier than anything on TV.
As for the price $18.99, that is outrageous. You can get this for under $11 at Walmart and Kmart.

Summary: Great alternative to traditional popsicles/ice cream treats!
Text: I was looking for something more natural than traditional frozen treats for my kids to enjoy during the summer, and found Smooze on Amazon and had to try it.  Overall, they are pretty fantastic.  You do need to make sure you shake them REALLY well before freezing or they can get pretty icy and less creamy.  My kids (8,6 and 3) are pretty picky, so I was worried they would reject these.  They love them and we have already devoured the first 2 boxes!  Highly recommend!

Was very happy with this product. Reasonable price. I ordered cashew pieces but actually received whole cashews which are generally more pricey. I use them in cooking so it didn't matter which ones I got. They are packaged well and arrived in good time.

I prefer the Vanila but either "flavor" is great. I drink it plain or I mix my protein/fruit/calcium shake mixes in with it.

I sometimes like to mix it with Soy milk, but I also enjoy the Rice milk by itself because it is lighter in viscosity than the Soy milk, and you can chug it.

Either way, Rice Dream rice milk is a tasty and healthy alternative to my lactose intolerance problem.

Rice Dream has been around for a long time -- they make delish ice creams too.

It mixes well with certain fruit juices (but beware -- some fruit juices will curdle it), and is a good alternative to coffee cream.

For anyone over the legal drinking age, it goes well with liquers too!!

I love this tea! It's holiday spice fragrances fill your senses even before you brew a cup. It's the best holiday tea I've ever tasted and worth the price. Originally, I had received the tea as part of a gift basket from a friend. I loved the tea so much I searched until I found it on the Internet at Amazon. I've given this tea out to my friends who have also become fans. It is delicious- you can smell the cloves,nutmeg,cinnamon and orange peel-- but they are not overpowering. Instead they are well-blended to make this tea my greatest holiday find. Try it and you won't be disappointed. I have mine with honey. I'm anxious to try it as ice tea in the summer months. Davidson's Tea Christmas Tea, 100-Count Tea Bags

These cookies have a clean, crispy chocolate taste -- without the chemical-laced aftertaste of other commercially produced cookies. They are all-natural and made with canola oil, as opposed to the oils that can add to cholesterol problems. The ingredients are mostly organic and they are sweetened with dehydrated can juice, as opposed to the less-healthy commercial alternatives.

Now, for the problem: I have never found these cookies in a market near me, and we have only purchased them through Amazon. Because these wonderful cookies are not pumped-up with weird chemical preservatives, the necessity of purchasing them in such big lots means that you are going to be eating a lot of cookies in a short period of time, or going in with a friend on sharing the case! However, given the high quality of this product, you should have no problem splitting up the order.

Yummy and highly recommended!

These are healthful, smallish (about the size of vanilla wafers), tasty and flavorful snappy cookies.  They are sweet but not overly so and have a bit of that molasses taste that ginger snaps are known for.  They have a really nice ginger bite too.  They are great to have with some tea, milk or even coffee.
Love them, very "gingery".  Great with your favorite tea or coffee.  Love that they are using natural ingredients.

Summary: Not Very Chocolately, A disappointing texture and flavor
Text:
I bought these cause I'm a chocolate snap lover, and I had been craving some. The lack of trans fats and description drew me in.

Let's just say this: I took these over to a family party, and none of the kids liked it. NOT ONE. And most of the adults, the best they could say was, 'Eh.' I think two folks had more than one.

I'd have to say skip these cookies. They don't make your mouth sing with chocolatey snappy joy.

These cookies are hard & somewhat
lacking in taste. We threw out half the bag.
Mostly because my children did not like
ginger snaps & my husband and I did not care for these.
Try it and you'll agree! Can't find this local anymore. glad it's available on Amazon. Perfect combination of crunchy chewy, all-natural, with a slightly coconutty flavor. Truly the best ever!

It's one of the big things I miss most about New York, since having moved to Colorado in April of 2007 - Bakeries. And specifically a really good Coffee Cake. Unless you are living in the heart of Denver there are just no real bakeries to be found. King Soopers and Safeway do try but then I just don't think they really know just how good a good coffee cake should be.

Grandma's definitely fills that void for us. This is just a scrumptious coffee cake.

I have ordered this in the past from QVC but have found the quality of it different by ordering this from Amazon. The two times I ordered it from QVC - the cake and the sample cakes were wet and mushy and nearly inedible. From Amazon it was moist - as it should be - but not wet and well - simply delicious.

I will definitely be purchasing this again, although I wish that the shipping charges were less expensive. I get my head around it by defining it as a treat that anyone hankering for a good coffee cake should allow themselves the luxury of having at least once and a while.
This is the best coffee cake I've ever had and in fact the entire family ate all of it on Xmas morning.  I wished I had ordered two.

Very simple design and snaps together.  I purchased a carousel type stand for my wife, me being a man I did not want to replace a coffee cup every time I took one out so I opted for the basket-style. Trust me as a man this is a better buy, just dump them in and call it good.
I needed to clean up and neaten up my counterspace, wanted to get rid of the boxes of k-cups.  This basket worked perfectly, and it fits more K-cups than i expected.
The price caught my interest and gave it a try.  The basket sits in my office and looks nice next to my machine.
While I highly recommend Spry gum, especially since Xylitol is good for your teeth and gums, this flavor is weak and the gum is tougher to chew.

picture of the product looked good - when i recieved it the individual candies were all upside down & a complete mess.  the cardboard strap holding the candies together was almost completely ripped. the crate was all chipped & discolored. i would never order or recommend this to anyone. i never did recieve the other 3.90 shipping charges i was entitled to .

My parents both love chocolate, and drink fine drinks every now and then, so I figured this would be a great gift. You'll have to ask them how they taste, but on my end this was a great product

Pros:
-Quick Shipment
-Excellent Presentation in the box
-Great selection of Liquers - Grand Mariner, Stolichnaya Orange (great with chocolate I presume),Jim Beam, and Remy Martin.

Cons:
Lots of tape on actual product, took some work to remove without messing up the label or wood.

Great product overall - Would be great gift for parents, or any chocolate lover.

Summary: Top Quality, you should do better locally
Text:
We are addicted to these little pickles and keep at least one spare jar on the shelf. They are much crisper and cleaner than the other jarred brands sold on here and in stores. Many of the brands of cornichones sold in local chain supermarkets taste bad. I have had only two that compare in France. These are not sweet, nor overly sour but well spiced. They are not overpowered by vinegar. They are near perfect pickles for putting with high quality cold meats and cheeses. Great for tuna. Nice in or alongside crusty breads and grainy mustard. Fruity wine or all kinds of beer pair well. Slice the long way for hot dogs and sausages on a bun.

I like the pull up insert that takes the place of going spear fishing or sticking your fingers down, or worse, spilling out the brine.

See if you can get them for about $7 per jar locally. The shipping is too costly on top of a higher than happy unit cost.
delicious hazel nut taste in a cunchy bite- size wafer cookie. highly recommended. will buy these again.remind me of the hazel nut coffee creamer
These are super high quality wafers. I have had many kinds and this brand is the best I have ever had.
We bought some in grocery store by accident and all of us love it but price in store is bit high so we googled on line and found the direct sell.

I have to say I was looking forward to getting my favorite cookie, without paying the local $4.89 per package.  I always buy from Amazon whenever the price is right, and they have what I want.  The packages of wafers came as expected, however when I got them, one package had it's seam split and wafers throughout the box and they were less then fresh.  The other packages appeared to have gotten excessively warm as the wafers had slid off of each other, causing a "slanted' wafer.  Not the upright wafer cookie I expected.  All in all, I will take a second look before I buy eatable items from Amazon.

Summary: Spendy, but non-corn source is worth it.
Text:
For me, the source of the sugar being organic cane sugar and not corn makes it worth the price. I don't use it too often though since I believe it is one of the most if not the most expensive brand of erythritol available. We have a corn allergy in the family and this is the only one I've found that is not made from corn. If there is another cheaper brand not derived from corn, I'd love to know! Corn subsidies would explain why other brands can be so much cheaper, it's just not worth it for us to chance a reaction.

For baking, I recommend using only part erythritol and some other form of sweetener. Of course, if the dessert will be chilled it's not so much an issue since the mouth cooling effect will go largely unnoticed. If you are avoiding sugar altogether, the more forms of alternate sweetener you use, the better flavor you will get. One tip for working with erythritol is to powder it in a coffee/spice grinder or magic bullet. Otherwise it doesn't dissolve well, especially in cold liquids. Adding a touch of honey works well to round out the flavor and it only takes a tiny bit since honey has a strong flavor. A little bit of stevia is good too. I use the erythritol most often when I am trying to desugar for a while and for one particular favorite treat. I recently made some almond flour blueberry muffins with part Splenda, part Zero and part liquid stevia. They had great flavor, even the kids loved them. I don't prefer using splenda though and when I am done desugaring I will go back to part evaporated cane or muscovado sugar and part erythritol.

I have only used this in my coffee and tea.  In those applications it works great.  I can't tell that it is not sugar.  I really do not like the flavor of the fake sugars, plus they are not good for our bodies.  This will cut the calories and will still allow the sweet tooth to feel appreciated!  I have had no side affects like they list as possible in other places.  But I have not consumed more than 4 spoonfulls at a time.  It does take more of it than real sugar but that it ok!  Amazon has the best price ever!  My local market sells this for over $13 per bag!  I love the ease of ordering here.
This creamy sauce has a good amount of spice to it, which really complements the smoky, BBQ flavor. I enjoyed this unique sauce.

Summary: Good chipotle flavor for your tacos
Text:
Taco Bell's Bold & Creamy Chipotle Sauce is the third of the Taco Bell's Bold & Creamy line we have tried at home, and it is our favorite. Both my wife and I liked this one the best out of the three. The other two were the Jalapeno sauce and the spicy ranchero sauce. We liked all three, but we liked this one a bit more.

We actually make tacos at home quite often, and that is when we used this sauce. However, it could be good on other things too. It has a good flavor, and if you are like me and order chipotle items off of menus when you are out, you most likely would like this sauce at home as I do.

There are 110 calories per 2 Tbsp. 100 of those calories come from the 11g of fat. (Soybean oil is the main ingredient So this is not a diet condiment, but how many are? No different than most mayo you get. If you want less fat, you should use salsa type toppings on your tacos.

If you like chipotle flavor, this is a good sauce for your tacos and other foods. I like it and will get it again.

Summary: Much better than their spicy ranchero sauce
Text:
Taco Bell's Chipotle sauce is much better than their ranchero sauce which had a burnt taste that I didn't like at all. This sauce hits the taste buds with a sharp creamy pepper, vinegar, and smokey barbecue taste, and leaves a smooth barbecue and vegetable aftertaste with it. I know the thought of vinegar and barbecue sauce on mexican foods sounds strange but it actually compliments tacos quite well. It's a little too strong for dishes with plenty of flavor already like fajitas, and it might also be too much for a dipping sauce, but it adds a nice kick to tacos, nachos, burritos, and even cheese pizza.

If you don't like the kick of vinegar or prefer milder salsas or sour cream flavors, this is not the complimentary sauce for you, but in the ranks of chipotle in general, its definitely worth a try.

I've tried using this on chicken and hamburgers and really liked it. It's a nice change from ketchup and BBQ sauces. The Chipotle has a spicy tang but it's overwhelming. It's probably even milder than the spicy sauces in an actual Taco Bell restaurant. It actually has a slightly sweet taste. It is a bit salty and creamy for those who are health conscious, but I find that even a small bit provides a lot of flavor and can be spread quite far over your meal. The bottle seems a bit smaller than you might expect, but other than that I'd recommend this.

I must admit that I am NOT a fan of Taco Bell. That is, unless I'm hungover. But since I'm not 99% of the time, I was reluctant to try this sauce. But, honestly, it's quite spicy and goes GREAT with chicken! I used it to cool some chicken breasts and they were quite flavorful. I also used this to top a Mexican salad, which also tasted nice. The sauce is very hearty and robust and gives off some good heat. I was thinking I wouldn't like it, but I must say that I look forward to picking it up at the grocery store!

I really wasn't sure what to expect when I got this, but I was pleasantly surprised. I made some taco salads and these worked great. Tastes good and pours well. Has a nice open and close top which makes it convenient.

Probably the only downside is the limited use of the product. What can one use Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce on?

Will I buy it again? Probably, but only if my budget allows it, as it seems cheaper to just mix salsa and sour cream together to make the same thing.

Taco Bell has outdone themselves this time. This chipotle sauce is just right. The sauce itself resembles French dressing, but milder. The pureed chipotle pepper is a mild but pleasant chile, so they blend perfectly. The oil used is soybean oil. There's just a tinge of garlic flavor, as well as red bell pepper, to even things out.

It contains 110 calories per serving size (two tablespoons), 300 mg. sodium, and the daily value of vitamin A is four percent.

This sauce would be great on a salad or a sandwich. It is also recommended for tacos, but I require more of a tomato-based salsa on my tacos. To each his own.

Yes, I will make this a permanent staple in my home. Not too hot, not too intrusive. Yet not dull. Pleasantly pleasing would be the words to best describe it.

We love all things spicy and Mexican but this sauce is not worth it. It is very mild and has little chipotle flavor. It looks like Thousand Island dressing but adds no flavor. Empty and flavorless calories. My recommendation (if you want a kick to your sauce) is the Frontera brand. Now that one has flavor and spice!

Like most food products this will either fit your tastes or it won't. It has a nice smokey chipotle taste, a little bit of a kick but not all that hot. Very creamy but a slight texture of granularity can be felt, just like they ground up real chipotle peppers.  I like it.

This sauce was just average for my family. Everyone reached for the other flavor (the jalapeno one). For both flavors, the preference was to use it to spice up some chicken tacos or chicken sandwich. Between the two, if you are serving beef (ground or shredded or a hamburger) -- then this one, the Chipotle, is the better choice. The sauce is very creamy, so if you like mayonaise type sauces, you will probably like this. No one in my house found it very spicy, so you have no worries if you don't like spicy food.

Taco Bell chipotle sauce has just enough "zing" to it to be interesting, but not overly hot.  It's great on taco salads, hamburgers, as a dipping sauce for hot wings, or anyplace you like a creamy, zesty sauce.  Taco Bell makes some pretty decent products, and this one will be at the top of my "favorites" list.  I love chipotle flavored anything, and this does not disappoint!

As a vegetarian, I'm always looking for a way to add zing to food. Luckily, I added the chipotle sauce from Taco Bell to my meal, and it was delicious. You only need a small amount to get a lot of flavor.

I cooked 1/2 cup of Morningstar crumbles and 1/2 cup of Rotel tomatoes in a skillet till the liquid was cooked. Then I removed from skillet, added 2 tblsp. chipotle sauce, added daiya non-dairy cheddar cheese and put in a tortilla wrap.

Goes great with a side of refried beans, black beans, or Mexican corn. Low in calorie, healthy, and filling. I definitely recommend. The only thing that would make it better is if the product were vegan.

This sauce is okay, but nothing to write home about.  In the past, my experience with chipotle was on a sub at Subway, which I absolutely loved.  Ever since then, I've been trying to find a close match.  If I'm buying Chipotle sauce in the future, I'll try other brands to see if I can match Subway's perfection.  If there are no other brands, I'll probably pass on buying any type of chipotle sauce.

This sauce looks like an orange tinted thousands islands salad dressing and tastes similar as well. There is a hint of horseradish that smells stronger than it tastes. The sauce is more tangy than hot. It is fairly thick and after refrigerating the last quarter of the sauce doesn't flow out very easily even when the bottle is shaken. The bottle will give you maybe 6 servings.

If you like orange colored food and the taste of thousand island dressing you will like this sauce.

This is a good, classic chipotle flavor sauce. It has the thickness of a creamy salad dressing and delivers the chipotle flavor. I used it on a grilled chicken sandwich with avocado and cheddar cheese and this worked great. I could also see using on burgers, tacos, maybe even as a salad dressing. Taco Bell did a good job with this sauce.

I was really interested in trying this product one I saw it.  I usually like the taco bell products that come out at the store.  They make some decent products that are available in the grocery stores.  This one is a new chipolte sauce and Sounded great as a way to spice up your meals.  I added some of this to tacos and also to some hamburgers.  It added a good flavor and a nice change to the meals.  The sauce wasnt as spicy as i would like but overall it tasted good though.  I would recommend if you want a little something different to add to your meals though.

I received this product through the Vine program. As described, this is a creamy chipotle sauce that has a pronounced flavor without being hot. While a bit high on fat at 11 grams for a serving (two tablespoons), the flavor is strong enough that you can reduce the amount used to control the fat content.

This sauce works well for wraps where you do not need a lot of sauce to carry the flavor. It does not work as well in salads in that the tendency is to use more than a serving portion and that really can drive up the fat content of your salad(although the flavor is good)!

Over all, I would recommend this product and only suggest a little self control in the portion size.

The only thing chipotle about this sauce is in the name. Don't get me wrong, it's pretty darned tasty. It's thick and spoogy, which isn't everyone's thing, and I needed a bit of hot sauce to really add zing to my fajita, but it's good stuff.

Summary: it will make your tacos taste completely different
Text: I think the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is worth getting as it will make your tacos taste completely different.  This sauce has a nice blend of both spicy and creamy tastes.  It wouldn't hurt to try more than one flavor too, as these sauces will make you re-think what a taco should taste like.  I also like how the bottle has a less messy squeeze-top cap.  The sauce will also be great for other things too; I can't wait to try this sauce on wraps and toasted grinders.

My 18 yr old son thinks Taco Bell is ok and said this sauce is very much like what you get when you go to Taco Bell. My wife thought it too spicy, but she is not a fan of spicy foods. I thought it was ok - a bit like 1,000 island dressing with a slight kick - not quite as sweet. It also reminded me a bit of the dip you get when you go to Outback and get their bloomin onions.

It did not 'wow' any of us, we'll use it until it is gone, but no plans to buy more. Since other reviewers have gone to great lengths to list the ingredients, nutitional information, etc I will not duplicate their work.

This is glueten free, so that is a +

Tasting a dab of this on a fingertip wasn't too pleasing: it felt too rich, too fake, and too underspiced (basically thousand island dressing with a slight aftertaste of chipotle).

So I tried adding it to some food, and in most cases I couldn't even tell it was in there - with the exception that my burrito made orange drips on the plate.

I'm sure I could get more of a taste profile (and more orange drips) if I added a LOT more of the sauce to my food...but that would boost the calorie count unacceptably. All in all, Taco Bell might do well to change the name from "Bold & Creamy" to "Bland & Fatty."

Summary: Spicy Complement to  Salads, Eggs & Wraps
Text:
I tried Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce on a traditional salad, scrambled eggs, and a turkey wrap. On the salad, the sauce completely dominated because of its spicy flavor. I wasn't able to distinguish clearly the other ingredients of the salad. I like spice, but I prefer salads with a more gentle dressing. I enjoy both creamy and oil/vinegar dressings. The Taco Bell product is the creamy variety.

I tried it on scrambled eggs which gave the eggs an Eggs Ranchero kick. Not bad if you can take the spice that early in the morning. I used a little and it went a long way on flavor (and spiciness). Would I use the sauce on eggs again? Maybe.

The best results occurred when I used the sauce on a turkey wrap. The wrap contained white meat turkey, iceberg lettuce and tomatoes. Since turkey is rather a bland meat, the Taco Bell dressing put some zing in the sandwich, making it far more enjoyable than a wrap with mayonnaise or mustard.

I know many people have sensitive palates when it comes to spice. For those folks, I would suggest steering clear of this product. But for those who enjoy spice, I would heartily recommend it.

Creamy and tasty with a nice chipotle flavor.  Not very spicy hot.  In fact, very mild.  Probably best described as tangy.  I wasn't sure how I was going to use this when I got it, but I found the perfect use for it.  It really jazzes up plain baked chicken.  I am not much of a fan of baked chicken, but my family eats it a lot and this sauce turns plain chicken into chipotle chicken.  I imagine that it would go good on tacos too to give them a little extra flavor, although have not tried it yet on tacos.  I know it would be great on chicken tacos; not sure if it would be as good on beef tacos.  I tried this sauce on fish too, but that would be a thumbs down for me.  Not a good compliment for fish.  This sauce is something different if you are tired of salsa all the time on your tacos.  If you like chipotle flavor, you'll no doubt like this.  Certainly not a "bold" flavor; just a nice, mild, tasty and very creamy sauce.  I can't imagine anyone not liking this sauce, but if you are looking for something really spicy, look elsewhere.

The smokey flavor and vinegar come through strongly and really give it tang, but with no tomato it's kind of a hollow, thin flavor that hints at BBQ but doesn't really deliver or stay with you. It's not particulary hot either.

I tried it on hard and soft shell tacos, as well as on pork and chicken cutlets. It works best on simply seasoned meat - just salt and pepper - where it's not competing with other strong flavors.

The texture is like a thick salad dressing and it's marketed as a finishing sauce for tacos and Mexican salads. It doesn't spread or mix as well as a Thousand Island or Russian dressing so I wouldn't use it for salads that are mostly lettuce.

It would probably make an interesting Reuben sandwich.

On first taste, bacon seems to be the most dominant flavor..followed by smokiness.  It is somewhat bold but not hot, as I would consider it. Advertised as chipotle sauce, you would think it would be quite spicy. The flavor is strong enough to hold up when I used it for sauce on the boneless skinless chicken I was cooking. Really did make a good tasty sauce!  Also put on hamburgers after they were cooked..just not very good at all.  Maybe if you mixed it in yr ground beef before cooking, it would really enhance yr burgers w/that bacony smokiness..I will try that next, enjoy!
It's not a bad sauce over all.it has a nice flavor,its has spice but its not bad at all.highly recommended.tasted good with the taco,with salad and chicken nuggets lol..good stuff
I tried this sauce on a wrap and pitched the rest of the bottle. All I could taste was salt (300 mg of sodium in two tablespoons). Ken's Boom-Boom sauce has a better taste.

There's nothing really bad about this sauce but it's nothing I find myself craving either.  It's reasonably spicy and seems to have a variety of uses but I still don't find myself using it much.  I tried it on tacos, burgers, etc and it's fine but not great.

I liked this one and I was relieved to see there is no MSG included in the ingredients list, unless they're hiding it under an unfamiliar name. It's spicy but not hot spicy, creamy and tastes good. I used it as a dip for chicken strips and think it would make a good dressing for taco salad and in burritos.

Like the other Taco Bell sauces, this one is also tasty and full of the patented Taco Bell flavor. Good with fajitas and taco salads. I mixed with some hot sauce to give it a bit more kick (not that much as is).

Summary: Awful tasting protein partially masked by rich chocolate - 4x as expensive as rice protein alternatives
Text:
As an omnivore with a 100-200 gram daily protein intake, I am always looking to diversify my protein sources. For protein supplements, I find the best value at Costco when purchasing Cytosport whey protein that costs approximately 2.2 cents per gram of protein. Yet, it gets boring eating from the same six pound bag for months. So, I recently evaluated two vegetable-based protein supplements: Nutribiotic Rice Protein and Manitoba Harvest Hemp Protein, both with chocolate flavoring. While the Rice protein has great economics, tastes fantastic and contains few carbs, this hemp protein fails in all three categories.

When I initially tasted Manitoba Harvest Hemp Protein, the first thought that came into my mind was "is this product really suitable for human consumption!?" Olfactory memories from large-scale grass cutting arose. Even with the rich dark chocolate, I can't consume this protein straight or even mixed with milk. The pungent taste needs to be blunted with large amounts of cinnamon and Splenda and/or mixing with high protein cereals such as Kashi or Special K.

Another undesirable aspect of this protein includes the large amount of carbohydrates: 2.1 grams for every gram of protein. The economics are underwhelming as well. It costs about 10.8 cents per gram of protein versus 2.7 cents per gram for the Nutribiotic Rice protein or 2.2 cents per gram of protein for the Cytosport offering at Costco.

Cons
Terrible taste
High carb content
Poor economics

Pros
Rich dark chocolate flavoring

I ordered this product hoping it would really change my mind about using whey or soy. I didnt. I have to mix it with my other protein just so i can drink it. It taste like dirt and grass. Not s very good product.

Quick easy meal, add some veg, some shredded meat and you're good to go!  I like a little more liquid than the package recommends to get more of a sauce.  Definitley add more water if you're adding veg and meat.

Bought these off Ramenbox.com and I was pleasantly surprised by the noddles. I did not know what to except because I could not figure out what flavor they were. Still unsure even after tasting them how to describe the flavor but it is definitely hint sweetness that is for sure.

They aren't quite as low carb as some of the other Bold flavors - but they are soooooo delicious...sometimes I forget to care! All of the Bold Flavors I've tried are fantastic. I already have a terrible addiction to crunchy nuts, pecans, macadamias, almonds, brazil...come to mama! (not a huge fan of cashews) But the Bold line of of these Blue Diamond almonds are just outrageously delicious. Drink lots of water, because you'll be eating a lot of these!

Great product, very tasty!  I was disappointed with store-bought pop-corn in my Nostalgia kettle popper.  The only problem I have is there is too much butter flavored salt, I typically pour half of it out.

Never used this product before and was interested in the fact that it was made with avocados (which I love). I certainly wasn't disappointed. It has a wonderful clean,milded (with no after) taste. Thats the problem I have with most oils, its the after taste I can't stand. I definely endorse this product.
I came upon these shells by accident....we were having a friend ship them to us from Memphis of all places! Thin, lite, crispy, full of flavor! AND they actually stay together while you eating them!

When I get cold, I always get severe sore throat (normally lose my voice and bad coughing afterward). Same pattern everytime. Summary: Cured my cat's "inflammatory bowel disease" overnight!!
Text:
My last cat (which I had from 1987-1999) was diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease about age 5 or 6 after losing weight and throwing up a lot. When the bowels are inflamed, cats cannot absorb nutrition well, and lose weight. The intestines also gradually build up scar tissue making things even worse. He had to have a biopsy to diagnose, and was on increasing daily doses of the steroid prednisolone for the rest of his life, as more was needed to be effective. I had to put him to sleep after he eventually lost so much weight he was pretty much skin and bones, and very weak. It was extremely traumatic to go through this, and when my current cat was diagnosed with IBD as well at the same age, I was in shock. Both cats (old-fashioned Siamese) had always eaten supposedly high-quality premium dry cat food, such as Iam's and Science Diet. Was I doomed to go through this again with my new sweetie? And was he doomed to years of pill-taking, discomfort and weakness?

Thankfully, the difference this time around was the Internet. For the last three years, I've been researching IBD and reading the many sites dedicated to cat nutrition (such as the great catinfo-dot-org), which tend to advocate a grain-free canned food diet (or even raw food, although that's a little too much for me...) as the closest thing to a cat's natural diet. The moisture in canned food makes it both easier to digest (reducing throw-ups), and provides water that most cats get too little of (a drinking fountain helps encourage water consumption, but be sure to keep it CLEAN). The theory is that the grains in modern pet foods, along with the lack of moisture, are what is causing the epidemic of digestive problems in cats. (In contrast, dogs are omnivorous by nature, so grains are fine for them.)

I tried many different foods recommended on these sites (notably grain-free Wellness varieties), as well as various prescription foods from the vet, but my cat still had constant, stinky loose stools and vomiting, and the prednisolone seemed not to help much either, unlike with my previous cat.

I finally came across Chicken Soup, and VOILA, overnight NO MORE DIARRHEA!! It took 2-3 weeks to completely stabilize, but he now has formed, normal-smelling stool every time, and even better, he needs NO MORE STEROIDS! It is simply a miracle. Chicken Soup lacks corn and soy as well as wheat/gluten, and sticks to mainly chicken for the protein source (no lamb, rabbit, venison, beef, and just a small amount of salmon, turkey, and duck). It does contain some grains: barley, rice, oatmeal and millet, but these are the least likely to trigger allergic reactions. Whatever he was allergic to, I'm ecstatic that my precious baby is now getting the nutrition he needs and no longer suffering from diarrhea.

He is getting both canned and dry Chicken Soup, because he still won't eat the canned as his only food source, although I've been trying to wean him off the dry. Some canned is better than none...but he is addicted to dry after all these years. My next cat will only get canned from the the beginning!

The one odd thing I have noticed since switching to Chicken Soup exclusively is that his fur is not as smooth and silky as it used to be. Not sure why. I intend to add some cat vitamins to his food to see if that helps. I'm not taking off a star for this since I will never feed him another cat food, but just wanted to mention it and see if anyone else had this experience and what they did about it.

Excuse me for the semi-graphic nature of this review, but I think many cat are diagnosed with IBD and put on steroids when a diet change may be all that is needed. I sure wish I had known all this in time to save my other kitty. Keep trying and don't give up until you find what is right for your cat. Some cats may not tolerate chicken, but for mine, at least, Chicken Soup is the cat's pajamas!

On the other hand, I'm still searching for the perfect kitty litter...not sure there's an answer for that one!

Summary: Try this, it might become a staple!
Text:
As other reviewers have noted, this is expensive. But it's also a premium product and you won't feel guilty about having it as there are no added sugars or anything remotely artificial or overprocessed here, just a rich chocolate flavor with all the associated health benefits. In response to negative comments about its palatability: You definitely need a blender for this (a blender bottle would also work fine). There is no way to stir this into something and not taste residual powder. Raw cacao powder is also an acquired taste-- It is far more complex and richer than your ordinary pre-packaged cocoa powder, but it has such a different taste that some people might have a hard time liking it on their first try. Seriously, though, once you've had this in a properly made recipe, you'll never go back to whatever you were using before. A last major advantage is the versatility. You can easily adapt this to any recipe requiring cocoa, by adding your own sweetener. In one bag, you have the main ingredient for smoothies, desserts, and hot chocolate; and all these can be made to taste.

So far, I've made these two things, numerous times, because they're that good:
- raspberry, banana, cacao powder smoothies: 1 rounded teaspoon cacao powder, 3/4 cup raspberries, 1/2 banana, 1/2 c. almond milk, 1/2 c. water
- hot chocolate: 1 1/2 rounded teaspoons cacao powder, 1/4 c. water, 3/4 c. hemp milk, raw honey to taste
I recommend omitting the water if you use a thinner milk such as almond milk. My hemp milk is pretty sweet, hence the 1/2 c. of water.

I have an iSi Twist and Sparkle Beverage Carbonating System and wanted to make a diet cola. Most diet cola syrups on the market for home users use splenda and/or acesulfame K which I don't like the taste of. I'm used to and prefer the aftertaste of aspartame or saccharine. This was the only extract I could find that was unsweetened so I could try my own sweeteners. I ordered the cola flavor from Jack's Country Store here on Amazon.

I tried making the soda with both erythritol and saccharine (sugar twin). I couldn't get the sweetness right with erythritol, but the Sugar Twin worked fine. The extract flavor is between a cola and a rootbeer flavor. I used the following mix: 3.5 cups water + 1 tsp cola extract + 1/4 cup Sugar Twin (if using erythritol use closer to 1/2 cup) and optionally, juice of a lime to boost the acidity and push the flavor closer to a cola and away from rootbeer. You could also use a bit less extract and sugar twin, I like it a bit strong.

However, Amazon's warehouses are too stupid to recognize the difference.  When I politely pointed out to them that they had shipped me the wrong item, they very politely apologized, and promised to send me the right item...whereupon they sent me exactly the same wrong item again. Summary: A Good Tasting Pick Me Up
Text:
Admittedly I'm not a fan of that ubiquitous Red Bull stuff. In fact, I never take any energy supplement at all. It would be nice to have a "go-to" type safe and tasty energy drink for the times when a cup of coffee just won't cut it. Enter No Fear. I immediately liked the taste of this stuff. It slightly reminded me a an non-alcoholic non-energy drink I used to drink when if was around 12 to 15 years old which was called "Apple Beer". Basically it had a nice grape/apple base with good fizz and so does No Fear. No Fear gave me a noticeable lift after I drank half of the can. I did not need to actually consume the entire can to get the benefit and, as mentioned, I liked the taste. If it wasn't fairly high in calories I would not hesitate to consume the entire can at one time (this could be a help if after strenuous activity you were feeling shaky and needed some fuel/calories).

All told, a tasty energy drink that delivers what the category promises: a real noticeable lift without making you gag. I would buy this stuff.

I actually liked the taste of this drink. I would drink it without the energy factor. The taste alone is the reason I give this product four stars. There are two servings in one can. I only drank one serving at a time. I could not detect any extra energy or alertness. I am a coffee drinker though. It does have caffeine in it, but not an excessive amount. Probably just the right amount so it doesn't give one the jitters. I liked it.

I drank it before going to the gym and it woke me up, it didn't give me the shakes or jitters like some energy drinks have done to me before. The taste is decent as well, it's bittersweet and similiar to a regular red bull, it's almost like drinking a sparkling cidar without the fizz.

In comparison to other products (and pure generic 'yellow' caffeine pills), the No Fear Energy drink offers no better buzz.

Every energy formula on the market produces a different energizing feeling, some are clean and high grade, while others like this one seem full of hype without a super energetic effect.

Finally, in addition to producing a lower energy range, the taste of this formula is not too pleasing.
I love the sobe no fear drinks...no carbonation...great flavor with a little after taste...disappointed that it was discontinued but glad i was able to stock up on amazon...

Summary: Not bad, but won't make me change brands
Text:
I frequently drink energy drinks and have tried most of the major and some of the lesser known brands. This "No Fear" one is decent, really nothing with it, but also nothing great. The drink contains 87mg of caffeine per serving (take note, a can contains 2 servings!), which is about average, as well as the usual mix of vitamins and other energy-boosting supplements. The taste is comparable to what you'd expect from an energy drink - you probably wouldn't pick these things up because they taste great, after all.

All in all, there's nothing much that sets this drink apart from the pack, and because of that I'd rather go for the brands I am already familiar with. Text:

I buy a lot when it's on sale and when it's not I get the 2 for 3.00 deals that are frequently made at filling stations. The drink tasted to me a little like grapefruit, and I liked the flavor, but not enough to this is a special taste I want to have again! Frankly in something as highly competitive as the soft drink market, I don't see this hanging around for long unless there is a very big player behind it and they discount it to knock out the competition. I'm still not sure of the value of energy sodas, they appear to me to run down your health under the guise of keeping you going. At least it's not the joke like that 5 hour thing, that doesn't even have energy just some cheap stimulants and an overblown price.

The price on this one is frankly too much for me to consider, pretty much what the out of the vending machine price would be for a typical energy drink. Had they sent me more than a can I'd have evaluated the drink over a few weeks, and maybe given a feel good or feel bad report, but with just the one can, I can't make any such claims. Bottom line is cost, and cost is not very good. That said it's not awful either, so if this makes it to the grocery, and is on sale I may buy again, just for a change of pace.

Summary: Tastes Better Than Most Energy Drinks
Text:
Most energy drinks don't live up to the buzz. They taste awful and the energy boost never
equals the hype. So it was with some trepidation that I tried No Fear Super energy Supplement. One large can contains two servings so I split it with a friend. He thought it tasted like a strong strawberry soda but didn't notice any energy boost. I would describe the flavor as a grapefruit.It was pretty good, excellent for an energy drink with only a slight and short lasting metallic afertaste. I too noticed no discernable difference in my energy. I am a heavy coffee drinker however my friend does not imbibe so I can't attribute the lack of effect to caffeine resistance.. So if you are looking for a change of pace flavorwise, this might satisfy. However, if you are seeking a shot of energy, stick with coffee or coke.

I should state up front that I *like* energy drinks. I consume far too many of them. However, this "No Fear" was the absolute bitterest-tasting drink I've ever had in my life, and I actually had to spit out my first sip and dump the rest of the contents of the can down the drain. It tasted HORRIBLE. On the up-side, I really thought the design of the can was awesome, with the skull-and-bones universal sign for "poison" as a logo.

Summary: Really, how many sugar, carb packed energy drinks does this world need
Text:
66g of sugar in the form of High Fructose Corn Syrup. 260 calories (in the form of sugar carbs). 174mg caffeine. A smattering of vitamins. Yes it will keep you awake. And yes you will inevitably crash from it. (I did.) It does taste better than red bull and about the same as Rock Star. But seriously, 2 of these day as some people reported seems to be putting you on track for health problems. And why in the world does an energy drink need a skull on the front? I downed my can before doing an MMA session. The guys in my class were not extra intimidated when they saw the skull. (Bummer.) I did not have any greater than usual work out ability. Summary: Nice energy boost, followed by a hard sugar crash
Text:
The text on this can of No Fear Super Energy Supplement is very blurred, like the red ink doesn't line up with the rest of the print on the can, so I didn't try too hard to read it before I started drinking it. I was a little more than halfway through the can when I realized that there are two servings per can--does anyone save half a can for later? If you can figure out a way to do that it's probably a good idea, since each serving will give you 33 grams of sugar in the form of high fructose corn syrup. I could have eaten a candy bar and come out ahead.

All that sugar, plus 87 mg of caffeine (per serving) did give my skull wings, right before the sugar crash that followed.

The flavor is far too sweet for my tastes, with kind of a weird fruit flavor. It felt like the inside of my mouth was coated with syrup, like I'd been drinking cough syrup. Come to think of it, this would probably make a great flavor for kids' cough syrup.

It wouldn't work as a kids' drink, though. The label warns: "Not recommended for children, pregnant women or people sensitive to caffeine." Those who are allergic should know that it also contains soy.

If you're looking for a sugar boost but couldn't possibly eat another bag of Skittles, this is for you. If all you want is the "proprietary blend" containing taurine, inositol, caffeine, ginseng root extract, grape seed extract, l-carnitine, and l-arginine, you might want to check out the sugar free version.

I ordered this granola last week and was really looking forward to trying it. I can't have dairy, so before I placed my order, I checked its product page both on Amazon and on Back to Nature's own website for any milk, butter, etc. listed in the ingredients. Everything cleared (yay!), so I went ahead and ordered it.

While waiting for the granola to arrive, I perused the reviews on this page just to see what others thought about it. For the most part, it sounded delicious and that everyone had enjoyed it. But at least one person had listed "skim milk" among the ingredients, and upon reading this, my alarm bells went off. Surely Back to Nature's own website would list the correct ingredients of their product, right? Upon receiving my granola yesterday, I immediately flipped to the back of the package -- and wouldn't you know it, clearly listed (as part of the chocolate chunks) is nonfat milk.

I don't know if Vine Voices were given a beta product, or perhaps Back to Nature changed their recipe and wanted to get rid of their backstock. Which information source are we supposed to believe, the product packaging or the company website? This mislabeling won't be an issue for most people, but it is a risk for those who are lactose intolerant or who otherwise don't consume dairy.

Mislabeled or not, I wasn't willing to chance it, so I skipped eating the chocolate pieces but still ate the plain oat clusters. It was very sweet and oaty, like a decadent "dessert-type" granola -- similar to Quaker Chewy bars, except not as moist. I ate a few handfuls out of the bag but found it too dry; it was much more palatable eaten in a bowl with soymilk over it. I do think it would be nice in an oatmeal cookie mix or over yogurt. Although this granola has a pleasant flavor, mouthfeel, and crunch, I have tasted better and would rate this fairly average.

Looking down into my bag when I was done with the oat clusters, I noticed that the chocolate pieces are all very tiny, flat, brick-shaped flakes -- instead of asymmetrical, craggly, varyingly-sized chunks. I don't know why I was expecting the latter, but obviously it wasn't a big deal since I didn't eat them. :)

Overall, this is a nice-tasting average granola. You wouldn't be doing yourself a disservice by purchasing this -- it's tasty -- but there is better granola out there. If you can't have dairy, you may want to opt for another variety/flavor just to be safe.

I have tried Back to Nature products before and always been a little bit underwhelmed, but this product is pretty good. The granola is not too sweet, which is perfect, and the dark chocolate chunks are great.

Summary: Is it a snack or breakfast cereal?
Text:
When I ordered this from Amazon the description said "heavenly snack" so I had it sent to the office instead of home (the kids might make short work of it at home and I'd never see it). But rather than being like "clusters" of granola it looks more like the Sweet Home brand of granola CEREAL we buy from the grocery store - except for those chocolate chunks. But I tried it and it's pretty good, except there's so many little pieces and try as I might, it ended up getting all over my desk and lap. The taste is fine but it's a bit messy, so I figured it must not be a snack.

I took it home and tried it for breakfast. It's not bad but I'm not used to eating cereal with chunks of chocolate (and I'm a big chocolate fan, dark chocolate, too - I even love chocolate chip bagels). My 6 year old daughter, who loves granola cereal and almost always has it for breakfast, took one look at the chocolate chunks and declined.

So I'm not quite sure what this product is: snack or cereal. It's too messy for a snack but the chocolate is a bit much for cereal (to my taste anyway). Calories are higher than the Sweet Home brand of cereal we usually buy (220 vs 200 for a half cup serving - the Sweet Home brand uses honey and almonds) but calories from fat were lower (50 compared to 60). It's okay but I'll stick with the grocery store brand.

Overall, I like the way this granola tastes. It has a good ratio of granola-to-chocolate, and the chocolate tastes good. It doesn't taste cheap, and it's not too sweet.

Unfortunately it melts pretty quickly to the touch, so this can be a messy to eat with your hands. (It's worth pointing out that the bag was in a hot car before I tried some, but I still had this problem even after it cooled to room temperature.)

The granola itself is a bit dry, unlike more honey coated brands, and the pieces don't stick together that well. So, after the big chunks are gone, you're left with lots of tiny bits that are messy to pick up. I suppose this wouldn't be a problem if you like your granola in cereal or yogurt, instead of trail mix.

Even though it's healthy, I wouldn't recommend this product (or any granola) for mindless snacking. Just 1/2 a cup contains 220 calories, which in my opinion is a lot for a snack. On the plus side, it's great for a hiking food or a quick pick-me-up.

This will be a short review, because there's not much to say. All there is to say, is this: Back To Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is pretty tasty and made a good munching treat.

The chocolate bits in it aren't high quality confection, but they're better than, say, the waxy chocolate bits you might normally get in a grocery-aisle chocolate chip granola bar. The wheat and such comes in small, flaky bits (I might have preferred slightly larger nuggets), and it's very dusty, so keep a dry towel on hand. I also appreciated that it came in a resealable bag, so I could just keep in in a drawer at my work desk without needing a separate container.

I won't buy it again because eating this stuff is no way to stay a size 6 (can't I brag?).  1/2 cup has 220 calories, 6 grams total fat, 4 grams of dietary fiber, 5 mg of salt and 13 grams of sugar. Summary: Yum! Very tasty snack!  And lives up to its promise of "natural"!
Text:

Now, my next question would be, how healthy is this? I was for some reason expecting this to be another "faux healthy" snack like so many of the granola bars you find these days, which are loaded with hydrogenated oils and artificial flavorings. The ingredients list of this granola is 100% comprised of things YOU could buy at the grocery store! Sugar, skim milk, molasses, etc.. even the preservative is plain old vitamin E.

Next I was curious about the calorie/sugar/fat content as compared to my usual granola, Kashi Apple Orchard. This product (same serving size) has 1 gram less of total fat (though saturated fat is 1 g more than the Kashi), 1 gram less of carbohydrates, and one less grab of protein. Total calories are the same per serving. Contrasting with the Kashi, I would never eat this for breakfast since my days of chocolate (Count Chocula) early in the morning are long since past. But I do think this granola is a good snack and worth checking out. I bet it would be easy to make GREAT cookies out of this, as well.

Hope this helps you decide whether or not you want to try it.

Summary: Good carbonated juice product, but light on the "Black Cherry"
Text:
As a carbonated version of the juice boxes that my children enjoy, this product is good, and reasonably priced. However, as a "Black Cherry" soda, this product is a bit lacking.

Seeing as it is advertised as a "Black Cherry" product, I would have expected cherry juice to be a bit higher on the list of ingredients than it is: 100% juice (filtered sparkling water sufficient to reconstitute juice concentrates, apple, grape, cherry juice concentrates), natural flavor and color, citric acid, ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Unfortunately the taste reflects the ingredients used; though there is a bit of cherry taste in this soda it is not nearly enough to make it distinctive for me.

However, at a reasonable price point, and without the sugars or corn syrup of traditional sodas, I think that this is a fine bevarage choice for the kids if they want something "fizzy."

The Switch Black Cherry is a refreshing fruit drink with no sugar added and no preservatives. It has a nice flavor without a bitter aftertaste. The company has done a nice job of balancing the juice and carbonation to give you fruity flavor without excessive sweetness. It is all natural and has no Gluten. The Switch would be my choice for fruit drinks. I don't like sweetened drinks with sugar additives and this is an excellent alternative. I highly recommend it!

This drink is super tasty.  I am currently pregnant and I am a dr pepper addict.  I needed something without the crap and cafeine and this did the trick.  It tastes just like black cherry coke.  Tons of carbonation and a very sweet taste.  The size is perfect for me - anymore and it would be overkill.  It honestly is 100% juice and natural.  I love that.  Definitely a great drinks for pregnant women who shouldn't be drinking soda.

This slim can contains a new beverage that is tasty and refreshing. The black cherry flavor is delicious, not too sweet, and the light carbonation adds to its thirst quenching effectiveness. Will definitely be ordering more.

This is my second try of a Switch beverage, and while I wasn't overwhelmed by the other (Watermelon/Strawberry), it wasn't bad (tasted a lot like carbonated apple juice to me). This time, while I can say that the Switch Black Cherry doesn't taste like mere apple juice (there is a tart, berry/cherry flavor), it is far, far too sweet. I took my first swallow out of the can and was just completely turned-off by just how sweet the beverage actually is. Served over ice and allowed to sit for a minute made it a good bit more tolerable, but when I grab something to drink, I want to drink it right then, not 5 minutes or so later. It doesn't taste bad, mind you, it's just way too sweet, almost overpoweringly so. A quick glance at the can says it all...33 grams of sugar...6 more than the same serving size of Coca-Cola. Needless to say, if you're looking for a healthy alternative to soda, this isn't the place to look (especially since there's really very little nutritional value to be found here).

I just don't see what the market for this is. Are people crying out for carbonated juice beverages? Is this being aimed at the energy drink crowd (same 8.3 ounce size as Red Bull after all)? Does anyone actually think this is much better for you than a Coke? It's not bad, but I wouldn't pay for it, and I sure don't see much of a market for it. Maybe if they add some caffeine to the mix...

Summary: It may be a healthier soda, but not a tastier one.

Summary: Fresh tasting soft drink - all juice, no sugar added

I'd compare this to Izze, and I think they are both good. My kids said they prefer Switch to Izze. I think I prefer Izze because it has a somewhat lighter flavor, but I can see why someone would like the slightly more robust flavor of Switch.

The slogan of Switch is "100% of what you want" - pure juice - & "0% of what you don't" - preservatives, additives, etc. It is worth noting that like all fruit juices this is fairly high in sugar - fructose instead of glucose, but still it is 33g of sugar per can. Still, if you are in the mood for pure, fresh, carbonated juice, it's not at all bad.

As a nursing mom, I can't drink caffeine (it makes my baby fussy), and I'm getting REALLY sick of Sprite and Sierra Mist. So I was thrilled to try the Switch carbonated juices -- sometimes you just want something fizzy!

The Black Cherry flavor is indeed delicious (though, as some reviewers have noted, there is a strong apple flavor -- apple juice is the first ingredient), but I was shocked to see 33g of sugar on the label. That's a LOT of sugar for an 8.3-ounce can! Ounce for ounce, it's more sugar than Sierra Mist, which really surprised me.

So I'll definitely drink this again, but unfortunately, the amount of sugar and the relative lack of nutrients in apple juice don't make it a wildly better choice than pop.

Summary: Bariani Olive Oil - Is it worth it?
Text:
Generally I buy olive oil in large 2 liter containers because we use in for cooking, baking and just about anything that asks for lard or butter. We feel using olive oil is a far healthier and tastier souce of oil to use than the latter. However, when I started researching more and hearing stories of outdated olive oil and needing to have it in a dark container I became worried about where I get my olive Oil... Generally at Sams Club or Costco.... So I opted to spend a few extra bucks more to get it in a dark bottle and hopefully current year stock. I purchased this lovely Bariani EVOO and it looked and smelled great, but honestly it didn't taste any different than the EVOO that I get elsewhere and the date on the bottle was confusing.... harvested in 2010 and bottled in 2011? Since I just purchased it September 2011 I was trying to figure out why. So, I contacted the company that produces this oil hoping to get some clarification on the details (since olive oil does not improve with age) and never heard back from them. So now I won't bother spending the extra money on that product. I did buy their Bariani Balsamic Vinegar 16.9 oz. and that is superb, but again sine I never heard from the company, why should I buy from them again? Disappointed!

UPDATE----- Since the Bariani company did not respond I contacted a reputable California company "Calolea" Calolea California Mission Blend Extra Virgin Olive Oil 500 Mland they offered this informative response:

Olives are harvested here in California between late October thru the middle of January. It takes some time to do all of the blending and bottling so the oil doesn't usually hit the stores until after the new year. So it is normal that oils made in 2010 come out in 2011.
As to what makes oils extra virgin, it is a reference to how much free fatty acid is present in the oil. The international standard is .08% of free fatty acid. The California standard is .05%. Our olive oil is usually between .01 to .02% so well below the definition of extra virgin. We accomplish this by picking and pressing within 24 hours. Olive oil does not get better with age! You should try to get oils that are fresh and use it quickly. Some companies come out with Olio Nuevo, new oil, during and right after harvest, this is when the oil is at its best but beware because sometimes it is very strong.
Great price, considering the size, it is light, but complex, and has been brilliant with everything I've used it on - chicken, brussel sprouts, asparagus, you name it.  Well worth it.

Earthy? Buttery? Fruity? Peppery? Grassy?

If you're looking for something other than bitter, you might want to keep looking. I found this olive oil to be overwhelmingly acrid and bitter: a real disappointment.

I understand that the taste profile of good, unadulterated olive oil might include slight bitterness, but with this oil (at least the fall 2008 bottling) bitterness was the only note.

As a nurse practitioner, I've learned a lot about infant and child nutrition. First, you must understand that children under age 2 NEED fats for their brains to develop. Brain matter is mostly fat. If babies and toddlers don't get enough fat, their neurological development will be impaired. Human breast milk is mostly fat (about 50% of calories); while the other half is milk sugars (lactose). Protein is actually a very small part of human milk. Nature naturally has saturated fats & cholesterol in mother's milk for infant mammals, as well as the yolk of egg for baby chicks. In other words, fats, particularly saturated fat and cholesterol are very necessary and healthy for a rapidly growing infant body and brain. That is why FULL FAT dairy is recommended by all doctors for every child under the age of 2.
Anyways, in reviewing the nutritional data on this drink, it is very low in calories, especially fat calories. I'd be concerned if parents tried to replace dairy with this drink. A child's brain and development could negatively be affected by not having enough fat. Plus a child would not get enough calories with this drink.
Most other countries in the world use milk for their children- not necessarily cow's milk though. I've breastfed my daughter for 1 year, and have now switched her over to goat's milk, which is recommended for children who have milk intolerances or sensitivities. The fats and proteins in goats milk are more broken down, making it easier to digest than cow's milk. If you are looking for a healthy alternative to cow's milk, I'd recommend goat's milk much more over this "rice drink".

Dark Muscovado sugar is fabulous !

It's important to note that it is absolutely necessary to store it in a sealed plastic or glass container so it doesn't turn into a sugar boulder.

Bought this sugar on a whim thinking it MIGHT be good and it certainly looked like something a different than you'd ever find in a supermarket.
What a thrill it is. Granted, the packaging is plain, nothing at all fancy about it but what's inside is very fancy with a flavor so divine that it invites you to try it in everything.

Here are a few of the things I've used it for since it arrived in my kitchen.

Adds an elegant, gourmet flavor when used as a topping on french toast.
On hot cereals such as oatmeal, cream of wheat, cream of rice it tastes rich and the steam rising smells so good.

And here's a news flash: Mix a rounded teaspoon or two in hot or cold milk for a real treat. Or if you're like me and into making from scratch hot cocoa, instead of mixing granulated sugar into the cocoa powder mix about 1/2 as much Muscovado sugar for an out of this world cup of hot cocoa. The flavor is deep and heady with an aroma that will knock your socks off.

Want to add some pizazz to your beef stew? Add a half teaspoon of Muscovado to it about 1/2 hour before it's finished cooking.
It also will add great flavor to chili when you add teaspoon full to it near the end of it's cooking time.

Cut up a few apples, an orange and add a 1/2 cup or so of dried cranberries and a handful of crushed walnuts or pecans, sprinkle a rounded teaspoon of Muscovado sugar on top and give it a light toss. Let the mix sit in the fridge for an hour or so and you have a grand fresh dessert OR - and let me tell you this is so good you'll want to do it again....instead of serving that mixture cold (it's winter here), pour it all in a sauce pan and simmer it until the apples are soft. Serve it warm. OMG! it's good.
I've also tried the warm mix with a splash of Peach Schnapps and a dollop of whipped cream added right before serving and the flavor blew me away. All of our dinner guests have given it rave reviews.

The next thing I'm going to try it in is whipped cream - I'll come back and let you know how that goes.

I read a lot about Muscovado sugar for years and decided to order some for my Christmas baking.  I give away a lot of baked goodies as thank you gifts to friends, family and those who have helped and supported me and my family over the year, like my Vet and the hospital staff.  There is no comparison.  Everyone was asking what I did to the recipes to improve on already excellent products.  As I was making the doughs and batters, one taste told me that I was onto something great.  I'm not going back to regular sugars.  Muscovado is worth EVERY penny of the extra costs.  Try it once and you'll be hooked.  I am.  Just wish I had purchased it sooner.

Ingredients contain (per 1/4 teaspoon) no calories, no fat, no salt, no protein, no carbs, no nothing. I had just gotten home from my weekly bowling league to find my fiancee in bed with our neighbor.  You know how they say that a mother has so much adrenaline pumping through her system when her child is in danger that she can just about lift a car off of it?  When I saw those two desecrating my queen-sized air mattress in the corner, I got so worked up that I could have taken that mother and her child, locked them up in the trunk of that car, and tossed it onto the roof of of the self-storage facility around the corner, the one with the orange hangar-style doors.  That's three stories high.  Anyway, the two fled out the back door and I went into a rage.  I broke everything in the house that reminded me of her.  The toaster-oven she used to make me pepperoni bagel-bites for breakfast each morning, the ironing board that we trimmed the legs down on so that it could double as a coffee table during that Pawn Stars marathon last July.  After about 45 minutes, I was totally drained from breaking stuff.  I took the truck down the road to the Citgo station to refuel and got a sleeve of those mini-powdered donuts and a Redbull Zero because my doctor says that too much sugar will make my Diabetes flare up.  It's a lot less syrupy than the regular Redbulls, but it definitely perked me back up.  On the way home, that Mr. Mister song about Broken Wings came on and I knew it was a sign because my heart was broken and Redbull gives you wings.  At that point, I knew I had to forgive her.  We've been happily married for 8-months now with a little one on the way, and I can honestly say that without Redbull Zero, I may have never gotten up the courage to patch things up.  I highly recommend this product to anyone going through a rough patch in their relationship.

I love, love, love this waffle mix. Seriously, all other waffle mixes just taste like sand to me, but Mrs. Butterworth's is so sweet and tasty. I've eaten Mrs. Butterworth's since I was a kid, so that may be part of it, but since I've introduced my fiancé to this mix, he can't seem to get enough of it, so it must not just be me. And it's SO easy to make - a touch of vegetable or canola oil, some water, and a waffle iron is all you need. No eggs, no milk, nothing perishable that you might not have on hand at the moment.

What I can't understand is why none of my local stores seem to carry this mix anymore. Pinnacle Foods is apparently still making this mix, but no one seems to carry it in my area. I wonder if that's because of the "contaminated" scare that went around when people first started noticing the brown sugar crystals scattered through the mix and assumed that the evenly distributed, dissolves-in-water, brown crystals were a contaminate of some kind. Honestly, it seems that everything has to be bleached white as a ghost these days, ruining all the flavor and nutrients, and introducing goodness knows what chemicals into your system before people will eat it. And now even Amazon doesn't seem to carry it, which breaks my heart. Fortunately, we were able to find it on Shop Food Ex dot com, and everything arrived with another year-and-several-months to go on the expiration dates, so we're all stocked up for the winter.

I originally became a fan of pouch-based cat food with the Nutro line of pouches. However, Nutro was especially hit by the nasty recall episode from a few years back where a number of pet food manufacturers had contamination issues, and they eventually pulled their pouches. I tried a bunch of canned foods afterwards, but my cats never warmed to any of them like they did the pouches.

Wellness came out with their "healthy indulgence" line of pouch foods not too long ago, and interestingly the packaging is pretty much identical to the Nutro products, down to the notches to facilitate tearing. I can only imagine that they are using the same manufacturing facilities as Nutro did, but hopefully with a superior product. Everything I've read about Wellness suggests that they make high-quality pet foods. My cats seem to love these as much as they did their old pouch foods. They have now been eating pouch foods almost daily for at least 6-7 years, so I don't have any major concerns about long-term health issues.

Overall, these pouches are great. Each single pouch is one serving for one cat, so the costs do add up fast if you have multiple cats and serve this twice a day. I give dry food in the morning and the pouches at night to help conserve costs, but they always finish the Wellness pouches within a half hour, whereas the dry food often sits around unfinished all day. Another plus is that no spoons or forks need to be involved, since you just tear each pouch and shake the contents into the bowl. No mess or debates with spouses about putting cat food forks into the dishwasher with the rest of the dishes!
I've been looking for this cat food locally; it seems that everybody is either out or doesn't carry these flavors.  This was great!  Fast Service at a great price.  I will definitely buy here again!

For an Italian salad dressing, this is my top pick.

Summary: I think this is an unsafe product
Text: Do you know those Tootsie Pop commercials where they'd see how many times the Tootsie Pop could be licked before they'd chew right into it?  That's how this Likety Stik worked with my dog.  He licked it three or four times, then immediately wanted to chew on the roller.  I repeatedly pulled it out each time he'd try, but it kept repeating.  Lick, lick, lick, chew.  Lick, lick, lick chew.  Within one minute, no exaggerating, he had chewed off the end and I was scared to death that he'd swallow the roll ball. Fortunately he spit it out, but if he had swallowed it, he easily could have choked to death on it with it blocking his windpipe.  I would never buy this product again, and highly recommend others not to.  Seriously, it was completely chewed through in one minute of opening the package.

I'm always willing to try something new for my dogs, and this sounded like a great idea, a portable no-mess treat delivery system.
The flavor I'm reviewing is "Smoky Bacon"
I experienced some of the same issues noted by other reviewers. The ball in mine did not roll freely, so once my dog licked it clean, I had to manually advance it with my finger. So much for the "no mess" aspect.
Squeezing the bottle as suggested by a few only results in a glop of foul-smelling liquid oozing out and dripping on the floor.
Yes, I said foul-smelling. I know dogs have a somewhat different take from their people on what smells good and what doesn't, but 3 of our 4 dogs recoiled at the smell of the product. Our only "outside" dog would take a lick, then take a sniff of her own rear end...presumably she found the scent similar. If you've ever seen a dog do that, then you know what I mean.

I'm also concerned about how sanitary this delivery system is. Between uses you have a ball laden with dog-mouth bacteria multiplying. I doubt rinsing the ball before storage would help much, undoubtably some slobber is going to contaminate the bottle contents during usage. Refrigeration is not suggested on the label but it might help retard bacteria growth between uses.

I think this product is another one of those things that sound like a good idea but the execution is flawed. I cannot recommend this product in good faith, and the $7.99 suggested retail price is a little steep for 1.7 fluid ounces of product.

I would have preferred to directly inform the company that makes this product vs. writing a review on Amazon but I couldn't find a way to do that.

First I would like to thank the makers of Lickety Stik for donating these things to a Canine Cancer walk I participated in this weekend.

I have 2 dogs, as it seemed, one dog liked it and the other did not.

The plastic roller ball was no where to be found, when my dog seemed ill I became concerned that she ate it but I found it later, thankfully.

I would not buy this product as my dogs are not usually mischievous or eat things that are not edible but this instance was too close for comfort. I feel the construction of the container is weak.

Length:: 1:42 Mins

I am a veterinarian with 7 years experience, and I have 3 Great Danes. I am always looking for safe, effective, fun, and innovative new pet products. I saw the video for this product, and definitely agree that carrying a pocketful of crumbling treats isn't much fun for training/rewards, so decided to give it a try. All 3 of my girls tried to bite the bottle at first (and I think most dogs will), but within a few seconds, all of them figured it out, and were licking away very happily, each taking their turn sitting down for me. I also recently used it to help keep them standing still while my 8 year old daughter gave them baths outside with the hose on a nice warm day....much less mess than doing it in the tub inside! It was also handy when we went for a short hike at a local park a while back, as I am training the 2 younger Danes to wear backpacks (that's a whole other story!). Even if the dogs jump in the river wearing their backpacks and get them soaked, their treats won't get soggy. The only thing I would like to see is using a liquid treat that's maybe a bit healthier for them...the ingredient list on the Lickety Stik looks like a lot of processed stuff. It does have a bit of an odor, too, but I didn't find it that strong or offensive like some of the other people here did. And I think it's the odor that really draws the dogs to come check it out...otherwise, why would they want to just lick a plastic roller ball?
Also, I think it would be nice to have a bottle that is just a little bit larger for the large/giant breeds like mine...but this does work well regardless. Finally, I think it would be great to have a refillable bottle, so there would be less waste...500 licks goes fast when you're training 3 big dogs!
Oh, and yes, I will re-order this, and do recommend it.

Summary: The perfect Hoisin sauce! Great in stir fry for sure!
Text:
I just used my new wok to make a stir fry, and took a gamble on this Hoisin. I usually use one from an Asian foods store. WOW, What have I been missing all this time!!?! Dynasty brand is so much better, deeper, and well...less weird than the type I was using. I didn't even know what I was using was that bad, I enjoyed it until I tried Dynasty. Now I'll never go back.

It has that earthy, rich flavor that you can never quite identify when you go to a Chinese restaurant. I used to think I just needed to add more soy sauce to make my stir fry or beef and broccoli taste like it does when I get takeout. No. It's the hoisin!! You don't need much, but this will bring out that depth and richness you want in a sauce, thick or thin, to really taste wonderful.

Personally, I used a bag of frozen stir-fry veggies (I know, life is short, frozen is okay sometimes!) and a handful of shrimp and a block of tofu cut up. I added about 1/3 c soy sauce (kikkoman, of course!!) and a dash, probably a 1/4 teaspoon or so of Dynasty Hoisin, mixed well and DANG! That was so good!!! If you like a lot of sauce you could totally double or triple it, adding hoisin to taste. I also added about 1/8th teaspoon oyster sauce, another one of those "Why is this beef and broccoli so good??" items, but you could leave that out. Also, you could add cashews and sub chicken for shrimp and make cashew chicken! Yum! Enjoy!
