The loaf kept much longer than without it.
I highly recommend this product for folks who do not have a soy alergy.

I purchased this for quick snacks and love it .this is my 3rd time buying these by case of 72 , Ive found I can eat these for a couple days and Im satisfied, the fruit and nuts go well together ,easy to carry along in purse ,or snack durning the night . I dont do reveiws ,but this is a product I can endorse for ease ,taste , and nutrition, love  it !  Planters Trail Mix ,Fruit & Nut ,2- Qunce Bags [ Pack of 72 }

Seabear products are top notch and very good.
This particular product is the wonderful Copper River Sockeye.
Rich in taste and perfectly smoked, this like other similar Seabear products, does not require refrigeration until opening.

I am pleases with these Madagascar Vanilla Beans.  Price was such a great deal for the quanity you receive!  Can't find it anywhere else.  I am on my way to making my homemade Vanilla again!  Very excited.  Thank you.

This product itself is DELISH!! My two kids (and hubby) all love fruit leather. It's healthy as well, which I appreciate as a mom. No added sugars or any junk and 1/2 serving of fruit. The hands-down CHEAPEST place to buy these is Costco or Sam's Club, but if you don't have one of those than Amazon is the place to go. A good deal on these is $0.40 or less per one. Amazon is close to that.

These were great.

But I prefer softer, more moist, and sweeter.

However, it was a nice treat and snack and enjoyable

We originally found these in the variety pack at costco and have loved them ever sense. They are 100% all natural fruit and have no artificial fillers or additives. Great flavor and I love that they are soft. Great snack for kids too!

Tastes great.  Good price.  I eat them after lunch when I'm craving something sweet.  Donuts and pastries mess up your diet, but these are great to get the sugar you crave in a low calorie treat.  I get them through subscribe and save, best way to go.
these things are so great. my gf and i always eat them within 3 days of buying them. this is the best flavor of all of them.

Who knew I'd ever buy a Tupperware Jell-O mold...but I did and this is THE BEST EVER.
Traditional shaped mold with easy-to-open dual sides. I love this set.
Perfect for the family and for entertaining and is durable and easy to use and wash.

Summary: Pay Attention To What You Order!
Text:
Only after the second bite did I decide this isn't human food! Tastes exactly like dry dog food smells. The plain re-packaging without nutrition info should have been the tip-off. Nonetheless, I bite into the thing, twice, before I decided that this isn't for me. They look great and were a hit with the dog owners at my workplace.

Amazon, I'd consider quit mixing dog and people food in your "Grocery" classification.

For me, nobody can beat Dunkin Donuts coffee. But the addition of vanilla can make just about any coffee palatable, and since this had the Starbucks name on it, I figured it was worth a try.

But I couldn't really taste the vanilla. Overall, this coffee just didn't impress me as either bad or good. It just sort of sat there. Maybe it has to do with my coffee-making skills, but I don't know why the vanilla flavor wouldn't come through.

OK...I've never reviewed a coffee product. I stick with book reviews...but I drink a lot of coffee when I'm reading and reviewing books.  So...this one was special.  I made my first pot and upon smelling the coffee, I was hooked. How good is it? I haven't tossed the ground coffee package yet!  It's empty, but it still smells good and reminds me of those morning smiles and good books.  Way to go, Starbucks!

This coffee is just not for me; the vanilla gave the coffee an off-note I just didn't like.

I tried. I really did. I brewed it a cup at a time, a pot at a time, by drip, Chemex, and French press. Each and every time, it was a no go for me.

For the record, I like my coffee strong and black. I'm sure that if you add a lot of sugar and cream, this would be just fine.

But for coffee purists, pass this one by.

Summary: Did Starbucks forget a Key Ingredient?
Text:
I was never a coffee drinker in the past. The bitter and often foul flavor of ordinary coffee was not to my liking and, other than the often-needed boost from the caffeine, I could see no reason to indulge in something with such a nasty flavor.

My opinion changed with the invention of flavored and higher quality coffees and as a result of this change, coffee is part of my regular drinking routine. Starbucks is one of the pioneers in leading these changes and when I heard about this, Starbucks Natural Fushions ground coffee with vanilla flavor, I was anxious to sample. Starbucks makes this product using natural vanilla which, combined with quality coffee, sounded like a successful culinary marriage.

So, how does this coffee measure up? Well, it certainly has a very pleasant aroma that whets the appetite and I doubt anyone would dislike this aspect of the product. The problem is, unfortunately, the taste itself. I was expecting something much more vanilla- like in flavor but the flavor is instead a little harsh, roasty, and contains only a touch of vanilla. How Starbucks managed to produce such an aromatic product that tastes so different, I am not sure.

However, this isn't to say the product is bad. I find it decent as a general coffee for everyday consumption. I also like that Starbucks encourages recycling by offering a free cup of coffee if consumers bring the empty bag to a nearby Starbucks location. The coffee is responsibly grown and ethically traded, too, as indicated by the Starbucks Shared Planet symbol. However, the bottom- line is taste and based on the lack of real vanilla flavor, like I was expecting, I can give this product only an average rating overall.

Summary: Warm, real vanilla flavor with a touch of chocolatey undertones
Text:
My husband makes the coffee, and he does his own little blends, so I'm never really sure what I'll be sipping on any given day.

One morning I was especially pleased with what my "Coffee Artiste" had come up with and called him at work to tell him I really loved the chocolate vanilla blend. He laughed and said he'd done a straight pot of the Starbucks Natural Fusions.

I was surprised since I'm usually not a fan of vanilla, especially if it's strong. This blend does the flavor with such a light hand that unless you're really focused on what you're sipping, you can miss its subtleties.

Even if you're a distracted drinker, you'll never miss the richness and overall smooth flavor of this coffee. A giant leap forward from some of the bitter and burnt-tasting brews I've had from Starbucks!

Summary: Delicious, strong without tasting like candy
Text: The thing I hate most about flavored coffee is that most of it ends up tasting like candy. The vanilla in this doesn't overpower the taste of the coffee. Vanilla meet Starbucks, Starbucks win! Good stuff, no after-taste - cream makes it smoother along with a little touch of sugar. Cafe International this is not.

This is a pleasant coffee, just be aware that it only very mildly infused in my opinion.

Coffee is a very personal thing, some like strong bold flavors, deep roasts and powerful flavor notes. Others prefer a more delicate palate. This coffee very definitely fits that second description.

The vanilla aroma, was noticeable when we opened the bag at home and the freshly brewed pot defintely gave off a pleasant vanilla scent. That said, both experiences were mild, much milder than I have experienced with other vanilla coffees and light years away from what a vanilla flavored creamer would do to your cup of coffee. In fact I found that the vanilla notes were mild enough that they could be overpowered by sugar and cream. If you like your coffee this way, this is something to note.

The coffee was also of a medium roast and milder than what Starbucks would call "bold" in their stores, and additionally milder than what I would call medium in their stores. Not harsh or acidic as others have said, though bolder than what I normally drink in the morning.

In summary, this is a pleasant coffee with medium roast character very very mild vanilla notes. Recommended for those prefer a delicately flavored coffee with these characteristics. For those searching for bolder notes, I would recommend looking elsewhere.

Excellent true vanilla coffee. Pretty much has D&D beat as well as other brands. Nice smooth consistant flavor. Had to add a tad more to the coffee pot to achieve the flavor but overall a great product.

Summary: Great taste, a tad sweet, amazing smell
Text: This Starbucks coffee is delicious. For pre-ground coffee, the beans are very fresh compared to other brands. This coffee has a very aromatic vanilla flavor with a hint of sweetness. It has that familiar Starbucks kick to get you going in the morning. Goes perfect with a croissant or delicate morning pastry.  Now if Starbucks offered this is certified organic coffee, I'd be in coffee-lovers Heaven.

Summary: Good vanilla flavor  in a a relatively mild coffee
Text: I usually like strong , dark roast coffee and find most flavored coffees to be strong on the (often phony) flavor and weak on the coffee taste.  This coffee was better than I thought it would be, in that it had a distinct but not overpowering vanilla taste that nicely complemented coffee that was milder than most Starbuck's coffee.  I am not likely to switch to this coffee on a regular basis but do think it is good for someone who likes flavored coffees and might think that most Starbuck's blends are too strong. The vanilla flavor is pleasant and not overpowering (e.g., doesn't taste like a milkshake).

Summary: Natural Flavoring doesn't equal better flavoring
Text: First, a confession. I typically don't drink flavored coffee, especially after learning that most flavored coffee is artificially flavored and usually is made with inferior beans. Still, I like most Starbucks coffee and welcomed their new take on flavored coffee. Opening up the bag, it smells wonderful and you can see small pieces of vanilla bean in with the coffee. I make my coffee fairly strong in a Braun drip pot. I found this coffee has some vanilla taste, but such an unpleasant aftertaste that I will finish the bag I have, but will not likely buy any more. I don't think they make this at their stores, so unfortunately you have to try a while bag to decide if you like it or not.

Summary: Just ok...not vanilla enough for me!
Text:
I was REALLY excited to try this coffee, since I absolutely LOVE vanilla flavored coffee.

However, while this brew was decent, I don't think it has much of a vanilla taste at all. Disappointing.

This is actually very tasty, but having the Starbucks name on it lead me to believe it was gooing to be great.  It's not.  No complaints but it's not the best either.  I've reviewed some other brands that were actually better.  I am very particular about vanilla.  Artificial vanilla is an abomination.  Genuine vanilla, just like coffee has a pretty wide range of flavors and quality levels.  This one may be natural but its not quality.  I found the vanilla in this to be aromatic but a bit underwhelming as far as flavoring.  The coffee was good but just a little bitter when consumed black.  Sugar and cream smooth it out but that pretty much defeats the point of getting a preflavored coffee as far as I'm concerned.

I am married to a coffee purist who will only drink black coffee and frequently turns up her nose at even flavored coffees such as Natural Fusions Vanilla from Starbucks. I on the other hand love to adulterate my coffee with cream, and especially flavored cream. It's not that don't enjoy black coffee--I do quite a bit--but that I also enjoy the robustness of coffee mingled with more subtle flavors. The best combinations are those which allow you to taste both the coffee and the added flavor, without one overpowering the other.

This is my first exposure to Starbucks Natural Fusions, and I wasn't sure what to expect. I decided to serve the coffee to a group of friends and see what we all thought of it (including my coffee-snob spouse!). The results were positive; everyone liked it, but certainly not rave reviews. My wife said "I like it--for a flavored coffee it's not bad." I thought it was tasty, just a hint of sweetness, and not overpowered with vanilla flavor. It did not have an oily feel like some bad flavored coffees I've run into in the past. Overall it was pleasant, tasty, and enjoyable, but perhaps not so good I'll be running out to the store to buy more. I'd give it a solid 3.5. I'll probably just go back to my usual Sumatra beans or Kona Blend, but this is a nice break from time to time.

If you're a vanilla lover, or flavored coffee lover, I'd say it's certainly worth a try. If you're a coffee purist, you can safely skip it.

I was very happy to receive a bag of this coffee to review, but need to admit up front that I am not typically a flavored coffee drinker.  I tend to drink my coffee black and bold, so this lightly flavored, more mild coffee was a departure for me.  The scent is lovely and the flavor is refreshing, although not intensely vanilla tasting.  It has a semi sweet hint and the taste lingers a bit after drinking, but not in any objectionable way.  For those who enjoy lighter and flavored coffees, you will likely really enjoy this refreshing blend.

Summary: Good cup of coffee for vanilla fans
Text:
Although vanilla coffee is not my favorite, I thought I'd try this as it was the Starbuck's brand.

A nice full-bodied cup of coffee with vanilla added. The aroma and flavor of the vanilla is not strong or overpowering like some brands. It's quite enjoyable.

I made a pot at work and it was well received.

If you're a fan of flavored coffees, I recommend you try this.

Thank you
MEF

I'm a major coffee-fiend, meaning something of a purist, so I rarely partake of flavored coffees, preferring the natural nuances of regional varietals.

But a flavored coffee can be a nice touch after a meal, in lieu of, or with, dessert. I'm loath to buy specialty beans for these limited purposes, and flavored beans also leave hard-to-remove residue in grinders, even more of an issue if you use a burr grinder, like I do, which has parts that shouldn't be wet-cleaned.

So, step back to pre-ground coffee. Starbucks takes a lot of flack for various reasons, but they reaaly do know their coffee, and always have big, robust flavors-- exactly what a coffee fiend desires. This flavored blend is no exception, it's dark and rich, with modest-but-noticable vanilla notes. I brewed it in my Krups Moka Brew, for which about 1.25Tbsp per cup of water worked well for drinking it black.

The grind is fine; much too fine for a French Press, but suitable for a drip coffee-maker with paper filters.

This isn't a flavor I would drink every day, and I especially don't see it as a morning cup, but for after-dinner coffee, it's Recommended.

I love the whole Starbucks experience: the toasty warm cafe, the smell of coffee brewing, sitting and relaxing with my drink at one of their tables and reading the paper. I did not think I would enjoy starbucks at home.

But I was able to bring my favorite coffee shop home with me, and I really enjoyed it. I just brewed a pot and my house smells like a cafe. Starbucks Natural Fusions Ground Coffee is so yumm! You can actually see the vanilla in the ground coffee! It is sooooo good! On my way to go get another cup now!

Although the vanilla & sarsaparilla flavor is best described as "subtle", this Starbucks coffee
must surely have the highest caffeine content of any coffee I've tried short of Espresso. Several
hours after I finished a normal-sized cup, I still felt wired! That, combined with the bold flavor
of the beans themselves, makes the Natural Fusions a brew not for the faint-hearted. It's also not
too highly priced compared to certain others, which makes it a very good buy of its type. You may
wish to start with a lesser amount than usual when trying this coffee for the first time, then
make adjustments according to your taste. If you are used to traditional supermarket coffee, this
Starbucks blend will blow you away. You can bring the empty bag to a Starbucks location to receive
a free 12-ouncer, which sweetens the deal. I recommend this blend, but new users are advised to
proceed with caution!

I'm not a huge fan of Starbucks regular coffees, although I admit to buying their specialty drinks (like the pumpkin spice latte). I tend to think their coffee is too strong and a little bitter. I thought the vanilla would be smoother, and if brewing it myself, I could keep it from being too strong. When I opened the pouch, the vanilla smell was definitely there, and I thought this would be smooth, delicious coffee. After brewing a pot, I really couldn't taste the vanilla at all, and the coffee tastes just like the usual Starbucks fare -- strong and a little bitter. I sweetened it, I put some milk in it -- still not very pleasant. If you like Starbucks coffee, you'll probably like this, but don't expect to get the vanilla flavor.

This coffee smells delicious, with a very vanilla aroma, but the characteristic Starbucks bitterness overwhelms the vanilla flavor. I know Starbucks isn't called "Charbucks" for nothing, but I'd hoped they would smooth it out a bit for this flavored coffee. I much prefer the Melitta Cafe Collection Parisian Vanilla Ground Coffee, 11-Ounce Bags (Pack of 3)since I normally drink coffee black. With milk, this coffee is passable.

I am not a real big fan of starbucks coffee but I do occasionally drink it and I can taste that undeniable unique flavor that starbucks has. The think about buying the coffee like this is that I can tailor it to my taste. The instructions say two tablespoons per 6 ounces of water. Me? I use 1 rounded teaspoon per six ounces and its perfect. Good starbucks flavor with a hint of vanilla and that unique starbucks flavor (and aroma). Good coffee. This is why I say buying it this way is much better than getting it in the store. Much cheaper too.

This coffee starts tempting as soon as the package is opened. The aroma of the coffee beans and vanilla are sweet smelling and made me want that pot to brew fast! While brewing I got a scent of what was to come - a smooth cup of coffee with just the right hint of vanilla and that bite that Starbucks coffee is known (and loved) for.

I don't use sugar in my coffee - just a little more than the usual amount of milk, cream or half-and-half - whatever is available. With that I had a nice smooth cup of Joe, and a nice pick-me-up to get through the afternoon!

If you like Starbucks, like vanilla, and most of all, love coffee, this is good stuff!

I don't usually buy Starbucks for home so will comment on the packaging. It's a typical foil pouch with resealable top (both tape and wires that fold in). This should keep the coffee fresh from first to last cup!

Summary: Light roast with very subtle vanilla tone
Text:
A smooth full bodied cup of coffee with a very faint hint of vanilla. Opening the bag is a wonderful experience as the bold aroma fills the air around you. Yum. The vanilla component is very strong with the fresh grounds.

I made the first cup and drank it black to get the unadulterated flavor. The recommended amount of coffee, 2 tablespoons per 6 oz, is a very, very strong cup of joe. I like strong coffee but 2 T per 6 oz of water is too strong even for me so I brewed it at about 2T for 10oz of water which is still a really strong cup of coffee.

My second cup I brewed the same as the first but added Coffee Mate Peppermint Mocha powdered creamer - super tasty. I like that creamer flavor and I wanted to see how the vanilla would stand out. Really it got lost in the stronger flavor of the creamer. There wasn't much vanilla to cover in the first place. I've used the creamer with non-flavored coffee and I cannot tell the difference in taste as far as the vanilla is concerned.

So, good coffee with a very mild vanilla taste.

This vanilla coffee is just what one would expect from Starbucks. Excellent. Though I have to admit, I'd still rather have a cup brewed by Starbucks themselves delivered to my door all hot and ready to sip.

PS: Love that Starbucks keeps to their message of "responsibly grown, ethically traded." It's worth a little extra money to me to have that satisfaction in addition to good taste.

Summary: The right balance of vanilla and coffee
Text:
Starbucks Natural Fusions ground coffee contains the right balance of (added) vanilla flavor and bold coffee. Normally, flavored (let alone pre-ground) coffees aren't very high quality; however, this Starbucks blend is very good. It's not stale or poorly roasted, nor does it have any kind of artificial smell or taste. There's no strange after-taste, either. It brews well, and I'll likely purchase it again. The vanilla "flavor infusion" doesn't overpower; the aroma is absolutely amazing - not flat, with the right amount of depth and complexity.

I prepared this coffee drip-style (not in a machine), and found it required a bit more than usual to make the strength I prefer. Additionally, though I prefer black coffee, this coffee responds well to a bit of sugar (it heightens the vanilla flavor) and cream.

I am really enjoying this coffee. It took me a little while to get the right combination for my tastes, but I think I finally have it.

First of all, it does not work well in a French press. No matter what combination of water to bean I tried, it just came out off flavored and bitter.

When I tried it in my automatic Mr. Coffee, I finally got the flavor I was looking for. Two rounded 1/8th measures per 6 cups of water. And don't cut this in half; one scoop for 3 cups is too watery. I know, it does not make sense.

The vanilla flavor is good. Subtle in the way that hints of vanilla without the over whelming vanilla syrup taste that some other brands have.

Oh, and do not use artificial sweetener, that does something funky to the vanilla flavor.

Also, as an added bonus, when you are finished with the bag, take it to your participating Starbucks for a free 12 cup of coffee. That is a nice bonus.

Overall, this is a very good cup of coffee without having to get in the car and travel across town for a midday pick me up. I suggest that you try it next time you are in the market.

Summary: a bit on the bitter side
Text: Does have a small hint of vanilla, but not as strong as you would get in a typical vanilla Latte. Leave a bitter, "chemically" after taste. We will stick to our regular coffee.

Summary: So-so coffee sold by union-busting Starbucks
Text:
I'm not actually a food reviewer. I'll do my best here, but don't expect anything special.

This coffee is entirely decent, but tastes to me a little too much like I'm trying to drink candy. The flavor is less about a 'hint' of vanilla and more about sort of rolling your nose around in a vanilla extract smell. The coffee taste itself, underneath all that vanilla, somehow manages to come off musty, if that makes any sense. It's almost a little too much in the morning, though I suppose it'd make a good dessert coffee.

Then there's the Starbucks factor, of course. If you're socially conscious enough to care that this is labeled as a fair trade item, you probably also care about the fact that Starbucks is a union-busting company. All in all, you ought to take your fair trade business elsewhere, as it doesn't make much sense to try to support fair trade on the one hand, while contributing to the abuse of American workers on the other.
I gave this as a gift to my mother, who is a fan of vanilla flavored coffee.  She said she enjoyed it, that it had a nice vanilla smell and a smooth taste.  She said she would buy it again.

My boyfriend and I both realized within the last year or so that we enjoyed Starbucks brand coffee best in our house, so it's one of our splurges. Since I work from home, I don't hit the coffee shops, I need to get my fix from the kitchen. He's also started bringing a travel mug to work instead of stopping off at a shop, so we find it's necessary to buy coffee we REALLY like. I was thrilled to try this and it didn't disappointed.

I expected something like the usual vanilla flavored coffee. But this was more subtle and natural tasting. It was a startling surprise from what I'm used to when buying flavored coffees. There was nothing fake or overly sweet about it. Boyfriend also said he liked it a lot, which I didn't expect since he's not really a flavored coffee kinda person. Delicious coffee, and I look forward to trying the other fusion flavors.

Summary: Good strong coffee with hint of vanilla
Text: We loved this coffee.  The coffee was a nice strong roast with just a touch of vanilla.  The smell of vanilla and coffee in the morning was a nice change of pace.  I wish the taste of vanilla had been a bit stronger, but I added some vanilla to mine on occasion and it tasted good too.

As of this writing there have been 255 reviews posted. Sorta difficult to add anything new. I received one bag of this coffee from the Vine program. The day preceding its arrival I had brewed some French Vanilla by a brand that I regularly use and which is rated higher than Starbucks by the best known testing and rating org. This offered me an opportunity to make a somewhat taste comparison although, admittedly, the Starbucks was not French Vanilla.

In the taste test Starbucks came in second. It was neither as smooth nor as tasty as the competitor. I drink my coffee with fat-free milk and no sugar so I get a fairly good opportunity to evaluate the taste. Starbucks afficionados undoubtedly will praise this and they have every right to do so and I have no quarrel with that. However, if you are not among that group I think you will find that you would be pleased with a different brand and save a few bucks as well.

Really nice flavor. I have it at night for a treat before bedtime. Really nice being able to make it at home instead of having to go to Starbucks and you can make it as strong as you like. True vanilla flavor, tastes like what vanilla extract smells like. Also great for company, after all, who doesn't like vanilla flavor.... Absolutely NO bitter after taste.

Summary: No Artificial Flavors and it's so delish!
Text: This coffee is great and you feel so good knowing you're not putting junk into your body!  Love it!!

Summary: Don't throw away that empty Starbucks coffee bag!
Text:
I must confess right up front that I'm not a coffee drinker, but everyone else in my family is, so this review is a composite of remarks and observations from all of them. The vanilla aroma and taste is definitely there and yet is well balanced so it isn't overpowering. This type grind worked very well in our cone shaped filter with a paper liner. There were no grounds in the brewed coffee. Even I could tell that this coffee had a very nice aroma while it was brewing, once again not overpoweringly vanilla. Everyone agreed that this is what they would consider a mild roast (milder than the Pike's Peak as a point of reference), some experienced some bitterness while others did not.

The overall opinion was that this was an enjoyable coffee which would be ideal for a specially brewed pot, but not for a standard get-you-going-in-the-morning pot. It seems that my coffee drinkers want basic medium to strong coffee for that first cup of the day. One really interesting thing I found on the package is that Starbucks will give you a free 12 oz cup of coffee if you take this empty bag to a Starbucks store before the expiration date for the coffee which is printed on the bag. That might be standard procedure with all their bags of home brewed coffee but it was new for all of us. It sounded like a great plus to my coffee drinkers.

I drink 6-10 ounces of coffee every morning from my excellent Jura-Capresso Machine. Usually I buy beans and they are ground in the machine. I've tried using already-ground coffee before and it didn't come out very strong, but with this coffee that was no problem!

The flavor is nice. I drink it with French Vanilla creamer, and the overall effect is a rich vanilla coffee that tastes delicious. I've long been a fan of Starbucks iced and specialty coffees, never so much of just coffee, but it seems the trick is to have it at home-sweet-home.

I brewed a pot once (using a different machine), and it came out not bad, but not great. The trick is to make it stronger to get the good flavor across (if you make it too strong, add some other coffee and that produces an excellent effect as well).

Admittedly, the first couple times I tried this coffee I thought it was just OK, I can understand why some people don't like it. I still prefer my coffee beans (from CoffeeAM or Costco). After several tries I came to like the flavor, but next time I want to break up the routine with some flavored coffee I'll try a different flavor.

As for the price, you can definitely find less expensive ground coffee, but in my opinion the price is good. For a cup of coffee with my Capresso machine, I used (roughly) 1.5 tablespoons of the coffee for a cup. With 22oz total package here (44 tbs) that means it should last roughly a month. $13 for a month of nice coffee - I can do that for quality flavored Starbucks grounds.

It will depend on your taste, and I recommend you give this a go.

I love this coffee! It has a nice rich taste; very premium. Has just the right balance of Vanilla too which tastes great and yet is not overpowering. For coffee that's brewed at home, this is the best you can get. I definitely recommend this, especially to fans of Starbucks coffee. You won't be disappointed! :)

My order arrived promptly but unfortunately NECCO decided to change the recipe of a long time favorite and their new "original" wafer is not at all like the true "original".  The true original had great flavor and color, the new original is tasteless and faded pastel colors.  Necco should re-label their new recipe product to avoid confusion.

I have been a Necco wafer lover for most of my life-and still am-even at the age of 65!
But, I WILL NOT EAT THIS DISGUSTING STUFF!
They have ruined Necco wafers-I can't even tell what the flavors are! I quit buying them and will continue to do so until they bring back the right ones-the GOOD ones.

Beware.  These are NOT the original Neccos!  Neccos went "all natural" in 2009.  Lime could not make the transition, so now there are 7 flavors instead of 8.  And the remaining 7 do not look like or taste like the original Neccos. They're faded in color, and I can barely discern white from purple from yellow from orange.  The flavors are just "off".  Not sure why they felt they needed to go "all natural".  I mean it is candy after all.  And the main ingredient is still sugar.  If you remember and loved Neccos, I urge you to contact them at necco.com and let them know how you feel.  Beet powder and purple cabbage in candy.  Who ever heard of such a thing?

Summary: Necco is great, but these are missing 3 flavors
Text:
Delicious as always, these packs are missing the orange, green, and purple wafers described above. I was really disappointed - it's in the photo, now that I look at it, but I didn't notice it when I ordered. I suppose that's why the price is so good compared to what you can get off the Necco website directly.

Anyway, they're still delicious, arrived in pristine form, but just so you know what you're ordering! :)

I was amazed that I found out these have been around for over 150 years, kinda makes you realize these will probably be around forever then. I use to eat these as a kid and still do on occasion. The assorted flavors are interesting and honestly, I don't think even after 10 years in storage the taste would be any different. If you havn't tried them yet you should and if you had them but not in a while, try them again.

Neccos were probably one of my favorite candies as a kid. I found some in a drugstore recently and was surprised to see them still around. I then found out what a long history they had and decided to buy some in quantity. They taste just as good as I remember.

I was so happy to find this product.  The broth is not a heavy, tomato based broth like most vegetable broths, so it does not overpower the other flavors in your recipe.  This broth has become a staple in my pantry for all of my recipes.

Fresh gooseberries and commercially prepared gooseberry pie are impossible to find, so if you like gooseberry pie, as my husband does, canned gooseberries are your only source.  The Oregon Gooseberries are the best and the label includes a recipe for the pie.  The Amazon.com price was much lower than the cost in the local supermarket for the same product.  The "use by" date on the can is sufficiently distant that we will have gooseberry pie twice a year for two years and use up the eight cans before they expire (each pie takes two cans of gooseberries).
Tried for a few years to obtain gooseberries but Amazon was the go-to place!!  Now I can bake pies just like my mothers and remember her every time I take a bite.  Thank you!!!!
glad to be able to access these berries - can't find them in the store any longer! we received our order in a prompt fashion, in time to make holiday pies.

These lack flavor, I mean there isn't really even a hint of flavor in them.

Further, the texture is unappealing; it's not quite mushy, and not quite mealy, but something between those two.

I first started drinking tea about a month ago. I tried Bigelow's GT w/ Lemon and that's all I'm drinking now on. I did not try their other flavors however their blueberry offering sounds tasty.

I eat this tuna at least three times a week. I usually put some kind of chili or hot sauce on it or pepper relish but that is it. It is sooooo delicious. Just moist enough. Just flavorful enough. Delicious!

We ordered, and it was delivered promptly and with 25% more product than we ordered "to share." That was cool.

The flavors are a little less intense, but much more "natural" tasting then the fakey Jello. Will definitely order again!

This product has very good flavor and seems to work best over rice. I have compared it to other brands with the same sized cans and found that the Libbys brand has more protein. This seems to indicate that Libbys has more beef than gravy. Great item for your pantry as an alternative meat source to chicken and tuna.
I think that both the Libby brand beef and the Hormel brand beef are very similar in flavor but I found the Hormel to be much tenderer.

I agree with all the reviewers who found this coffee smoother and less acidic than domestic U.S. brands. It is good coffee, but it is not exceptional coffee. While I consider Tchibo Gold of better quality, I found the flavor similar to regular Folgers coffee. If you think U.S coffee brands generally taste fine and you'd like something similar that is easier on the palate and the stomach, Tchibo is probably a good choice. For a flavor that is different and very outstanding, I'd recommend trying Dallmayr (also available on Amazon).

Tchibo is one of my favorite coffee brands. The wonderful aroma you smell when you open the vaccum sealed package speaks volumes. Tchibo's Gold Selection has a distinct rich but smooth flavor - A perfect choice for that first cup of coffee in the morning. Another plus: The subscription price here at Amazon definitely beats Walmart's price :)

I love pizza and love to cook and this sauce is the best out there. I used to make my own but this tastes better. Muir Glen makes amazing tomato products. The fire roasted canned tomato products are amazing as well.

I don't often buy convenience type items.  We like to make our own sauces and other items homemade.  However, after trying this pizza sauce, we've allowed it into our house.  Why?  This sauce has a tremendously good flavor!  Whether it's the tomatoes used or just the right spices, I don't know.  Either way, this has earned a prize position in our very picky pantry!

I just recently got into making homemade pizzas and until I found this sauce on Amazon my pizzas were just ok, fairly bland and nothing special.  I purchased this on faith of reviews and everyone saying how good it was.  I am glad I made the purchase as it is truley delicious!

Summary: As good as the movie, maybe better
Text:
[preparing to open the can] In the immortal words of Jean Paul Sartre, 'Au revoir,tea'.

Sorry about the poor Caddy Shack reference, but this tea is great. Tastes good, low on calories, plus one huge 23 ounce can that can satisfy about any thirst.

I won't call myself a tea expert. Organic green tea is pretty much all I drink. I'm known as the "tea expert" in my social circle because I know of the existence of white tea (although I haven't tried it yet). Onen day, I was in a Natural Foods store, and the attractive package and appealing description of this Numi tea caught my eye. Since I was on vacation, I splurged and bought the box. Tried it as soon as I got home.

And I've never looked back. I admit, the first cup wasn't eye-popping. It had a pleasant taste, but I decided it wasn't worth the $10 I had to spend on the single box (Amazon sure has a nice deal going on). Except, the next day, I found myself looking forward to having another cup. It WAS good - such a unique, warm taste. Over the next few days, I discovered that - in my opinion - it tastes best after brewing for 5+ minutes in WARM water, not boiling. I just let the faucet run on hot, and fill up the cup with it. That's probably not the "right" way to brew tea, but

I've since had a steady supply of this tea - it's just delicious. Highly recommended!
This tea was very tasty. It has bittersweet chocolate notes that are layered upon an excellent base tea. This is great to go along with dessert for people who do not drink coffee.

Summary: Agree with other reviews - inconsistent quality
Text: It's hard to review this tea because each bag I've steeped has been like a whole different experience... one was smooth and flavorful, another weak, and still another bitter.  Nothing's changing in my process except the tea bags!  Perhaps I just got a bad batch, but I cannot in good conscience recommend this product.

Summary: Too good to get a 3 rating, but not good enough to earn a 4 rating...
Text: I had really high hopes for this tea. When it arrived in the mail I immediately opened up a pack and made some tea. It's not really what I expected. I thought it would have a slightly lighter and more chocolaty flavor. Don't get me wrong, its still a good drink. I think there's a little too much nutmeg that kind of throws it off. I would definitely urge people to give it a try because it is pretty good and has a distinct flavor
I had tasted the chocolate flavor at a tea I went to, and loved it. The tea I ordered from Amazon had a funny taste, and did not meet my expectations.

My wife and I both love this Tea! She is the more picky about her tea, between the 2 of us. If she likes it than it must really be good since she has tried a great many different kinds and can be considered a connoisseur.

Personally, I prefer to drink my teas plain with no sugar or other additions. This tea tastes great plain. The very subtle chocolatey aftertaste is very pleasant. I tried adding just a bit of sugar, as an experiment, and it's still quite good that way too.

Based on my experience, I find the Numi Organic Tea to be of high quality and can definately recommend it to tea drinkers everywhere.

Every year I order some smoked salmon for my dad, and this has been, by far, the best yet. Not at all dry like some we have gotten. The trio gives you three types so you can see which you like better if you aren't sure. I will be ordering SeaBear again!

Summary: WARNING! Keebler announced "precationary hold" for Salmonella!
Text: I recieved an email from the FDA stating that Keebler has placed a "precautionary hold" on these crackers because of the salmonella outbreak associated with peanut butter. You can look up the info on Keebler's website.

I think this horchata is just as tasty as ones I've had in mexican restaurants. The nice thing about this product is that it lacks hydrogenated oils, artificial sweeteners, and dairy products which I have found in some powder mixes and concentrates. It's a little sweeter than I thought it would be, but normally my horchata from restaurants has ice so maybe I'm used to a more dilute flavor. Adding a bit of water helped cut the sweetness and allows me to extend my yummy horchata a little further.

The ingredients in this product are: Filtered Water, Brown Rice (Partially Milled), Dehydrated Cane Juice, Expeller Pressed High Oleic Safflower Oil, and/or Canola Oil, Rice Flour, Natural Flavors, Spice, Carageenan.

An 8 oz serving contains 160 calories, 25 calories from fat. 4 Servings per Container. I love this product for these reasons:

*It's great in candy-making. I've substituted it for Corn syrup (Caro syrup) with great success. Use it next time you make peanut brittle!
*It's organic.
*Brown rice syrup enters the system more slowly than many sweeteners, so it doesn't give as much of a 'sugar high' because the body takes it in over time. The technical expression for this is that it is lower on the "glycemic index" than many sweeteners--I've read that it's better in this way than molasses, maple syrup, sugar, and even raw honey!
*It is one of my favorite sweeteners in terms of taste. It has a subdued caramel-like flavor.

I like it on waffles too.

Summary: My dog can still taste the pills, and spits them out
Text: My dog had been taking pills without issue for several months.  Due to a recent surgery, her daily pill count has gone up dramatically, and it has become increasingly difficult to get her to take them. I have heard many people saying how wonderfully these pill pockets work, so I finally decided to give them a try.  First, I think they are ridiculously expensive (although reasonable at Amazon, these cost almost 30% more at my local pet store, where I unfortunately bought them).  Second, if the pills taste bad (particularly if they are tablets that are cut in half to lower the dosage), it is likely that your dogs will still spit them out if they are anything like mine.  I was hoping for the magic solution to pill taking, but this is not it.

Summary: Pill pockets, what a great idea!
Text: This is the best thing ever for giving meds in pill form to a pet.  Each little "pocket" is the consistency of a soft brownie.  So they are easy to mold around even a large pill.  I have 2 dogs and both take meds with these, no picking them apart, they just swallow them whole!  Both of my dogs are small (20#) so I usually don't even use a whole pocket for their meds, I break one in half and it's plenty to cover the pill.  Great solution and really makes things so much easier when pets are sick and not even wanting to eat.  I will always keep these on hand now.

The dog absolutely loves these! She gets anti-anxiety meds every morning and she will come running with tail wagging when she hears me open the pill bottle. Can you believe that? I don't even need to use the whole treat. I rip off about a third and they are soft so I mold it around the capsule. I then make her work for it by giving a few commands "sit, stay, come, etc" and she does them excitedly. After she gets her treat, she is so excited that she does a lap around the apartment. Overall, these pill pockets are a winner and I will use them as long as she keeps getting pills!

These are AMAZING!  I have a very slippery and sneaky cat who needed medication before a trip.  I stuck the little tablet inside the snack, put two down on the floor, and she ate them both.  No stress, no drama, no cleaning up medicine from the floor.  I will be keeping these on hand, and recommending them to everyone I know.  If your kitty is hard to medicate, you should definitely try these.

Summary: Great Product to Hide Pills for Doggies
Text: Just like kids, my dogs hate taking pills when they are sick.  Thanks to Greenies for creating this product, I can easily hide their pills and they are willing to take it with no fuss or force.  It smells like their treats.

As the owner of a dog who takes daily medication, these are a godsend. Soft and squishier than other "hide it in food" options, this works like a charm and is easily molded to any size pill and my dog LOVES them. It turns medicine into a no headache, treat time that he actually looks forward to. No really.

Like another reviewer I use the less expensive "pill pockets for cats" for small pills and they're just as good ... For dogs. My three cats, on the other hand, are WAY too smart to fall for it, easily eating around the pill pocket and leaving the pill. (They do like the taste too.) So, you know, there's that. Thank goodness dogs eat first and then forget to ask questions (and/or chew) later.

These pill pockets made by Greenies are the best invention ever in getting your dog to take their medications!  They make them for cats as well.  My dog has to take a prilosec every day and I used to fight with her to take it and then I would find the pill spit out somewhere in my house...needless to say, she was getting sick because she wasnt taking her medicine.  Now, she runs to me to take her medicine!  She thinks it is a treat!  She would eat the whole bag at one sitting if she could get into it!  I highly recommend trying these pill pockets for any dog or cat that takes daily meds or for any dog or cat that hates taking medication.  These work like a charm!

After trying to wrap my dog's pills in cheese, peanut butter and every other creative route, I realized there had to be a better solution. Greenies are a life saver. It makes the whole pill administration so much easier. My dog actually knows when it's time and walks over and is ready for her "treat". I wouldn't recommend anything else. Such a time/hassle saver. Greenies, you really came up with a great solution.

Summary: Awesome! Cat pockets save $ based on other review too!
Text: Based on another reviewer I tried the cat pockets for my Rat Terrier. The price was half based on the packet having many more and being lower.  My dog likes the salmon and the chicken just fine. The 6 pack is the best price. Giving him his pill every day is so much easier now.  I had tried for ages to cover it in the doggie cheese whiz and that was just nasty and he often licked off the whiz and left the pill.  Tricky little dog. ;-) Wish I had found these sooner.
My dog loves Pill Pockets! They make giving medication so easy. Just wrap it around the pill and your dog will take it and beg for more. They must taste great!

I couldn't get my dog to take her incontinence pill (which is supposed to be a chewable). Put it in a hotdog, she would eat around the hotdog & spit the pill out. Same with any other type of food, food gone, pill left on the floor. Wrapped the pill in one of these pill pockets & she doesn't even chew, she wolfs it down so quickly. Now my only problem is getting the pill in the pocket fast enough so that I don't have to clean up a puddle of drool.

This product is ingenious!! My Rottie mix will run from anywhere in the house if she even thinks I'm opening the package. She has 3 different illnesses which force her to have to be on meds for at least a year, maybe more and this makes it so much easier on her and on me! HIGHLY recommend!!

These are fantastic ways to get the dog to take her pills. They work well and make life a lot easier. The small pills are a lot smaller than in a previous purchase buying the larger ones. Since our dog takes a lot of pills, I would pay slightly more for the larger ones because it would be more cost effective in the future.

Again, these are fantastic and really makes life a lot easier.

I think that Pill Pockets are just WONDERFUL!!  I have a small dog and it was very hard to give her pills and the veterinarian sold me a package of these, now my dog just loves when it is time to take her pill, she does not even know anything is in there.

WONDERFUL, WONDERFUL, WONDERFUL PRODUCT. I was so impressed with this product, I just wrote a letter to the company (S & M NuTec)that developed and make them, telling them how thrilled I am. I've got 3 elderly dogs all on daily medications ( two are on oral chemotherapy, one on Thyroid, one takes Arthritis Medications and one is on Antibiotics)....and they actually LOOK FORWARD to getting their pills!!! I started out giving them an empty pouch or two then the one with a pill in it....and after the 3rd day, I didnt need the empty pouchs.

No more wasted, half dissolved pills or capsules found in corners, no more dragging them out from under the kitchen table, no more cleaning the pill syringe after every use, no more prying open jaws. NO MORE PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS INFLICTED ON MY ELDERLY POOCHES ON A DAILY BASIS.

I buy the LARGE size and cut them in half, then mold the pill around it, so I get 60 pieces out of the Large 30 chew bag.

I see they now have Chicken available and will be ordering some of them too. THIS IS A MUST HAVE PRODUCT for Dog and Cat owners.

I found wrapping  my tiny tot's pills in a little ball of wet dog food was simple and seemed more palatable than the greasy, foul smelling greasies oops I mean greenies.  He used to toss them around but hesitated to eat them for ages until I became concerned.  Wrapping the pills in a wholesome freshly opened canned dog food is better in my opinion.

Summary: Beware of First Swallow And Then Enjoy a Tasty Cold Green Tea Drink
Text:
Some people will be turned off by ChanTea Green Tea & Aloe Vera with passion fruit flavor because of the particles that will enter their mouth when taking their first swig.

In fact, without any warning, the first-time user might spit out the first drink not knowing what was entering their mouth. The particles, which have the texture of small, damp pieces of rice, actually are Aloe Vera pulp. I was not troubled by these rice-like particles entering my mouth but some will be.

This Chantea Passion Fruit product is a ready-to-drink chilled green team beverage with Aloe Vera and all-natural ingredients. The passion fruit, native to South America, has a tart flavor that sweetens as the fruit ripens. The passion fruit combined with Taiwanese provides a tasty duo which is pleasant when chilled.

My knowledge of Aloe Vera is that it might offer protection from the sun and/or help sunburn heal - either or both. Some believe Aloe Vera is a beauty enhancer. What I learned though is that Aloe Vera is a natural ingredient that contains helpful vitamins and minerals. Aloe Vera is said to detoxify the body and cleanse the colon, and specifically might help with digestive problems. Aloe Vera juice acts as an antibacterial, antiviral and antifungal agent. And so the combination of Aloe Vera and passion fruit aims to provide a healthy yet tasty refreshing drink.

I hesitate to affirm any of the health benefits but will recommend it as a tasty beverage for those, like myself, who enjoy green tea and cold beverages.

Summary: Great Flavor & it's healthy to boot!

Chantea won the Best New Product Award at the 2011 World Tea Expo and Buyer's Choice Best Ready to Drink Tea at the North American Tea Championship in Las Vegas. And it's no surprise as to why. Summary: A little lumpy but overall pretty tasty...
Text: I love tea.  I especially love green tea.  I also love passion fruit (they flavor everything with that these days, don't they) and I really love the soothing pallet cleansing quality of aloe vera.  So, I was particularly pleased to get to try this Chan Tea product; this green tea infusion.  I'll start by warning that this looks really unappealing upon receipt and that judging from the large amount of floating debris (pulp) and the murky green color one may be almost repulsed by the presence of this product.  That said; I had to try it, so I did and I must admit that I was pleasantly surprised.  First off, this really doesn't taste anything like green tea or passion fruit, but there is a familiarity to the flavoring so maybe the subtle hints are sparking memories on my tongue.  What I will say is that the flavor is solid, with no aftertaste at all and the sweet levels are balanced to the point where this tastes fresh and authentic and organic and, well, sort of delicious.  The texture of the drink can be a little off putting, considering that there is so much pulp your constantly rolling balls off the roof of your mouth.  Still, there is substantial flavor here so give it a whirl and see what you think.

Likes: a really pleasant taste, that is not too sweet, just nicely so, it would be very refreshing over ice. I wasn't quite sure about the idea of little chunks of aloe and they are good. Now, I do like pulpy orange juice and bubble teas though, so a little chewy stuff in my beverage is not a problem for me. If you don't like that whole "texture" in your beverage thing, you might want to pass, but I really liked it. No preservatives, real green tea infusion....all pluses in my book.

Dislikes: It has 120 calories per bottle....that's really all I can come up with. I wish they had a diet version, maybe flavored with stevia for us calorie watchers. Because it is 120 calories I won't indulge daily, but that is really the only drawback for me.

Overall, the passionfruit flavor was delicious and I would definitely purchase this and also be open to trying new flavors.

Summary: Updated: Why These F-Cups Will Never Work Correctly
Text:
I'm no lawyer (Or am I?) but I'm pretty sure BBR can't call these "K-Cups." This is a suggestion to Ruth at BBR - you need to change what you call these in your responses - you can't say, "After all, we're filling these K-Cups with BBR Coffee."

I'm not an engineer (Really, I'm not) but I can tell you that making something look like a K-Cup and not engineering it to work like a K-Cup is a recipe for disaster. My initial thoughts were the adhesive wasn't viscous enough, but it's wayyy more than that. The plastic is not thick or rigid enough to be punctured and rooted at the bottom of the K-Cup basket. Instead, the plastic just bends and re-forms in the basket - one of the reasons the coffee grounds are exploding UPWARD. You'll need a thicker, less bendable material.

The foil cap isn't durable enough either, though if you replace the plastic with one that's stiffer, the foil may work. The adhesive should be upgraded to a material that can be heated, cooled, heated, cooled and never lose its qualities. You may of tested these in your office, but imagine materials that have to withstand sitting in the back of a UPS truck in Phoenix for 5 days. And after that must work in the pressure of a K-Cup basket just like a K-Cup. And you need to make sure that before sealing, you have a clean surface. Otherwise, no adhesive will work, and the adhesive is the weakest link among these materials. You do realize that steamy coffee grounds exploding can burn your customers, right? You can probably get an engineering student to intern for free to advise you, or hire an engineer. Thus ends my free advice.

Our dogs just go crazy for this.  They can eat them pretty quickly though.  If there was a 4.5 star rating I would have to give it that just because they dont last as long as they should.  However, out dogs just love this!  Oh, FYI, they are medium sized.

Make sure you cook the pasta for the recommended time.This is as close to the "real" thing I have found in glutten free pasta. It is not gritty or too heavy. I just love this mac n cheese.  I have been gluten free for over two years now per the advice of my neurologist. The problem is that one box does not make very much :( I need to make two boxes to make to make enough for my family. It is pricey as well and spending almost $3 on a little bit of comfort food is only worth it now and then.

It's great for a treat but not a staple in my pantry.
If you can't eat regular mac & cheese due to gluten-free diet, this is the next best thing.

Annie's rice pasta has a firm, toothsome texture that semolina pasta can't match, and the cheese is mildly sweet and tangy (the instructions say the cheese will stand up without butter, but use it anyway to cut minor Cheetos-like overtones). Though pricy, it is nutritionally rich and has a good flavor, unlike regular macaroni, which is mostly filler and serves to deliver the cheese.

This product has the advantage of being gluten-free, but even if you're not on a restricted diet, I recommend it. Both healthy and tasty, it's a step up from the garbage that got most of us through college. You need to eat less of it to feel full, thus offsetting the greater price, and it's so tasty that you need to eat WAY less of it to have your taste buds satisfied. Savings, nutrition, and good flavor... what more could you ask for?

I'm new to the gluten-free way of eating and have been experimenting. I just happened across this in the supermarket and thought I'd give it a try. I generally don't eat much in the way of pasta, but since I often feel unwell, the convenience was appealing. Other reviewers commented on the need to cook the noodles a bit longer than the directions call for and I think there may be something to that. I ended up using the 14K BTU burner on my gas stove for a full 10 minutes and they came out great. I think if I had used the regular 9K BTU burner and stuck to the required cooking time, the noodles may not have turned out so well. You also need to stir the noodles within the first few minutes that they come to a boil or they will start sticking to each other and the bottom of the pot.

I was a little apprehensive about how this dish would taste and I have to state that I really couldn't tell the difference between this product and the "regular" version. I was never a huge fan of the Kraft product because I prefer homemade to stuff out of the box. But allergy season is looming and I knew that I needed a variety of convenience foods on hand for the high-pollen count days that always make me too sick to prepare meals from scratch. But as grateful as I am to find another gluten-free food that I actually enjoy and want to stock in my pantry, this is one that will have to be an occasional indulgence. Because even though it is gluten-free and its target market is more health conscious than average, this product is quite high in sodium. I'm very surprised that health-conscious parents would feed this to their children often enough to need a subscription! Especially when frozen vegetables are so quick and easy to prepare.

Boiling the noodles a minute or too longer makes the noodles softer if that's your preference (it is mine). Make sure that you have a lot of water in the pot to boil the noodles and remove the starches. Then before you add the noodles back into the pot, melt two pats of butter and two slices of Kraft sharp cheddar cheese in the pot until it is the consistency of a rich cheese sauce.  Don't overcook this sauce - it will dry out!  When mixing the powdered cheese, use whole milk instead of the reduced fat milk and wisk the mixture until it is smooth.  Add the sauce you wisked into the pot with the noodles and the first cheese sauce base.  Heat the entire mixture again for just a minute or two until the sauce thickens up.  The final dish is incredibly rich and delicious.  Easily comparable to the best box product out there...seriously! And it's gluten free.

Summary: A great alternative to dessert - simply delicious!
Text:
Well, I don't quite know what the other reviewers are talking about... I've tried this tea and found it absolutely delicious. When I first opened it, I did get a strong rooibos smell, as this is the tea base. However, once brewed, the smell changes to a sweet, tangy smell with chocolate undertones. simply wonderful.

However, I add a splash of vanilla coffeemate and it tastes very close to me. I get the chocolate undertone and the flavor is sweet and amazing, with a bit of a tange, not unlike true red velvet. Overall, I plan on buying this over and over again in the future!

Betty Crocker Gluten Free Yellow Cake Mix, 15-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6) Thank you Betty Crocker! We have waited a long time for this! Excellent flavor, moist and just like the real thing! Nobody knew it was wheat free, gluten free!

So excited that there is an easily accessible product that is good and GF! Now it will be easy for those that want to bake for GF friends/family. Here are the ingredients for those that are interested:

Rice Flour, Sugar, Potato Starch, Leavening (baking soda, sodium acid pyrophosphate, monocalcium phosphate), Xanthan Gum, Salt. May contain soy ingredients.
It calls for water, 1 stick of butter, 2 t of vanilla and 3 eggs.

Hope that helps!

I have several motivations for writing this review:
First: To counter the folks who dissed it in this forum without trying it. Amazon has now provided the full ingredient list.

Second: To extol praise and thanksgiving that a mainstream, nationally recognized company has heard and answered the plight of the wheat-free and gluten-free community by providing us with easily accessible gluten free products, having made the substantial investment in a gluten-free factility. I believe such a commitment on our behalf deserves our appreciation.

Third, and most important: To tell whoever wants to know that Betty Crocker GF Yellow Cake Mix is really easy, and REALLY GOOD!

I found and purchased the Betty Crocker GF Yellow Cake mix in my local Kroger store, right in the "normal" baking mixes aisle. I was so excited that I nearly took a picture of it sitting on the shelf along side the products the rest of the baking world purchases!

The mix requires 1 stick (1/2 cup) of butter (or equivalent), 3 eggs, and 2 tsp of vanilla. I used 2 whole eggs, and the equivalent of a third egg using liquid egg substitute. The cake baked up beautiful, golden, and delicious. I suggest testing the cake for doneness 5 minutes before the minimum baking time, as the edges were a little bit browner than the rest of the cake, but that certainly did not detract from the taste in the least. The texture (except for those edges) was perfect. Really just like a yellow cake should be.

Please know that the mix makes a one-layer cake, just like the picture illustrates. Bake it in an 8 or 9-inch square or round cake pan, or make cupcakes. But don't plan on a two-layer cake or a 13x9 from just one box.

I took the cake (with dark chocolate frosting) to a covered dish dinner, where it was the most popular cake on the dessert table, even though I was the only person eating gluten-free. AND it is just as good the second day!

Honestly, Betty Crocker has succeeded in making a "real" yellow cake with GF ingredients, in a dedicated GF facility. And Amazon's price is better than my local store.

What's not to love? Thank you, Betty Crocker.

First of all, I do want to thank Betty Crocker for creating cake mixes for those of us who are gluten-intolerant.  That said, I was a little disappointed with the yellow cake mix.  The cake was dry and had a slightly spongy texture.  I also did not find that the flavor was as rich as it might have been.  I was also put off by the use of a stick of butter and I checked the Betty Crocker website to see if they had options for a lower fat version.  Nope!  In fact, they warned that the mix should not be altered.  Another disappointment is that the mix only makes one 9X9 layer, so, making a layer cake becomes very expensive.  I did make a half-way decent bundt cake (though not very high) by adding an extra egg, milk instead of water, 1/2 cup brown sugar, and a package of lemon pudding.  It was fairly moist and very tasty, especially with the addition of a vanilla glaze.  I will continue to experiment with the mix just for the sake of convenience, but, I will not make the basic cake again.

Let me first start by saying we are not gluten free because we have to be. We are gluten free by choice. I made this cake to try at accommodating some family members that are gluten free.

As a cake baker, this cake is mediocre. The texture of the batter is gritty (what do you expect when it uses only rice flour?!), but may be because I didn't throw it all in as the instructions said. I was worried that throwing in a stick of butter and eggs with the water and mix would yield a weird texture itself. However, it baked well. I found that it cracked on top though and it is so dense and heavy. This is not a light cake by any means, and if you're trying to make a layered cake, you have to be careful as it will crack easily and really feels like it will just crumble in your hands if you're handling it. The taste is just ok. It has an ok texture and decent moistness, but the moistness borderlines an undercooked taste, in my opinion. When you cut it, it falls apart and pulls if you aren't just cutting straight down. Mine definitely doesn't look like the picture on the box!

I would say that if you have to be gluten free and have no other option, this might be a good quick cake for you. I think there are other choices that may taste and act more like a 'real' cake if you find the recipe. There are multiple gluten free blogs that have yummy looking and sounding cake recipes (which I intend to test). Why not a coconut flour cake? Or a combination flour cake? Rice flour alone is not my first choice.

I found this to be a very tasty gluten free cake. I baked it as per directions in  a round pan. The second time I tried one of these, I added a cup of apple sauce to the mix. Summary: Do not apply in Summer, know your grass!
Text: I love this stuff. Killed all bermuda in my yard with two applications (one Spring, one Fall). It has never returned one year later. This will only work when applied during the bermuda growing season, which is Spring & Fall. Bermuda is dormant in the summer, so don't bother applying then. And be sure you know exactly what your invasive grass is or it won't have any effect at all. Are you sure it is bermuda? Not crab grass or another invasive grass? It will kill any hybridized bermuda lawn grasses like BOB sod. So you really need to know what is in your lawn before you try this. Use your state and/or county extension website to identify your local invasive grasses. If you aren't up to the research, hire a professional landscaper to deal with it. The active ingredient, Fluazifop, is illegal for retail sale in many states, so you won't find it in the big box stores like Lowe's, Home Depot, or Wal-Mart. And an online seller may cancel your order if you are in one of those states. But even in states where retail sale is illegal, a licensed professional landscaper can apply the more highly concentated form of Fluazifop.  This is not the same as Weed-B-Gone!

Summary: I softened it in water for 6 min. & it still felt like straw.
Text: The good things about brown rice vermicelli is that it's gluten free, cholesterol free, nearly fat free, very low in sodium, low in sugar, & had a nice amount of protein.  However, there are almost no detailed preparation directions.  Instructions on the bag say to soften the brown rice vermicelli in water at room temperature for 1 minute prior to cooking.  I did it for over 6 minutes & it still felt like straw.  I did heat olive oil & garlic over medium fire in a frying pan & added steamed veggies in with the vermicelli.  I stirred well & added mozzarella & marinara sauce.  No instructions are given as to how long you need to keep heating this mixture, so I played it by ear.  I stirred it often & when the vermicelli no longer felt like straw, the dish was finished.  It was quite tasty because of all the additions I made to this dish, but I'm not sure if I'll bother to look for this product again.  Portion size is my big bugaboo on all labels.  The portions always seemed to be sized for skinny fashion models.  In this bag of just 7 oz., there are supposedly 3.5 portions.  Laughable.  The entire bag contains 731.5 calories & that's before anything is added, to give it flavor.  The cover states that this is "naturally fat free."  Well, the bag contains 2.8 g of total fat, including over 1g of saturated fat; so while the fat content is very low - it is still not fat free.  It does include 11.2g of protein.  To me a logical portion would be half the bag, so you can cut these numbers in half.  I guess it makes for a healthy meal.  I'd give it 3.5 stars, but one can only give whole numbers here.

I absolutely love Nutiva's coconut oil and so I thought I would love their Coconut Manna as well. Unfortunately that is not the case.

I followed the directions on the container to soften the product so that I could mix the oil back into the coconut. I ended up using an immersion blender to thoroughly mix it which worked very well.

I find it almost inedible. The texture is gritty and very thick. It sticks to the inside of my mouth and leaves an unpleasant dry sensation. It doesn't "melt" in my mouth as described on the container. I don't enjoy the taste either. The pure taste of coconut oil is there, but with another taste mixed in that ruins it and leaves an aftertaste.

I'm really disappointed. I'm planning on trying another brand of coconut butter and see if it's a problem with the Nutiva brand or just my own taste/texture preferences. It's not anywhere near the expiration date, it doesn't taste rancid and the container was properly sealed, so I assume that the product is fresh.

It's also packaged in a glass jar which I prefer. The taste is also somewhat better. I now know that I don't really like coconut butter, it's just not for me. I would recommend that if you buy coconut butter buy the Artisana brand.

Summary: Sinfully rich but oh so delicious!
Text:
Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna is certainly one of the most sinful of foods but, oh my gosh, is it delicious! It is a very rich but very flavorful coconut cream made from certified organic dried coconut meat from the Philippines. (I live in southwest Florida and room temperature here is just perfect for ensuring a very spreadable coconut cream).

When I first opened the jar the fresh fragrance of coconut made my mouth water! Just like a kid, I could not resist sticking my finger into the jar and taking a big, generous taste. My taste buds simply exploded when the unique flavor of this decadent coconut cream melted on my tongue like sweet butter! And just like a kid, I know I will be tempted to take those sinful dips into the luscious coconut manna jar.

I have noticed other reviewers' comments about the "grittiness" of this product and I just want to point out that coconut meat is a high fiber food and coconut manna is 100% whole coconut, so the texture is much like one should expect in a high fiber spread. Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna contains 12% fiber and 9% protein, whereas coconut oil contains none.

Coconut in general is such a versatile food with an extraordinary taste and all manner of health benefits. In Sanskrit, the coconut palm is called "kalpa vriska" meaning "the tree that supplies all that is needed to live." But I must be frank...I do not think Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna or any coconut product should be used as a food therapy for any health purpose. Coconut meat is nearly all fat, 80% of which is saturated. With that said, as difficult as it will probably be, I will be using Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna only sparingly (but with utter enjoyment!)

Being a raw vegan foodie and with the holidays quickly approaching, I do look forward to getting creative with Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna and devising culinary applications with it, such as in my raw, vegan spreads, soups, smoothies, sauces, cheeses, and especially in desserts. Of course I will have to consider it a celebration food because of the high saturated fat content. This luscious treat is not the best choice for health or waistline but it is so good to the palate! I will definitely be using Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna for special occasions, for entertaining and for those times of private indulgence when I need to treat myself... and I will do so with wild abandon!

Summary: Yummy, but not sure what to do with it
Text:
Honestly, I haven't searched the Nutiva site for recipes, so I'm not sure what all the possible uses are for Coconut Manna. I will say that all by itself it tastes pretty yummy. I keep finding my 9-yr-ld daughter sneaking spoonfuls of it! So far we've spread it on toast and tried making smoothies with it. The smoothies didn't work too well because it solidified into little chunks that wouldn't blend and then got stuck in the straws. I can imagine it would be good to bake with, though.

It's essentially pureed coconut. The consistency is dependent on the room temp, as coconut oil has a rather low melting point. When I first bought this, the weather--and hence our house--was pretty warm, and the consistency was that of oobleck. :D But as the temp dropped, it became more solid.

All in all, it's been good, but not sure I'd buy more only because I don't cook a lot. I thought this would be more something that could replace cream cheese and such for me as I'm allergic to milk, but it's not quite right for that. Still, it does taste good and I'm sure it's loaded with nutrients!

Summary: Bask in the power of the coconut
Text:
Yeah, that sounds way out there to me too. This is amazing stuff. Its basically coconut thats been dried and ground, also known as coconut butter. Its rich in fiber and protein, plus plenty of saturated coconut fat. A number of studies suggest that coconut oils, rich in beneficial fatty acids, may actually be a heart healthy fat in low to moderate amounts. People who eat coconut frequently around the world seem to have lower incidence of heart disease and certain cancers, and the main fats in coconut all have been demonstrated to have healthful effects, improving HDL and creating LDL thats smaller, harder, and less likely to plaque your arteries. About 2 or 3 tablespoons of this per day and you've picked up a bit of those oils and some protein and fiber as well. Plus it tastes really good and goes great in baked goods and candies.

When you get it, put the jar in some warm water for a few minutes and the manna will liquify. Stir thoroughly and it will become a solid again at room temperatures below 76 degrees. When its a solid, you can scoop some out with a sharp spoon or a butter knife. As a liquid, it pours.

My wife found a recipe for a 'truffle' that incorporates this, cocoa powder, dates, chia seeds and hemp seeds, cinnamon and a few other ingredients. Its like the best tasting energy bar you've ever had, and all of those ingredients are high in good plant fats, protein and fiber.

If you haven't tried this stuff, do some research online and read everyones viewpoint. I'm not sure about the science behind it but I'm sure that it tastes good and a little wont hurt you. Coconut manna is the best tasting coconut butter I've tried, and the company has a good reputation for quality. Try the coconut oil as well. It works out really well in many dishes, having a sweet, slightly coconut aroma and taste.

This delicious Coconut Manna spread can be used in smoothies, sauces, dressings, desserts, brownies, icing and baked goods. It contains 12% fiber and 9% protein and is a great nutritious replacement for butter and creams. One tablespoon has 100 calories. A teaspoon full gave my oats a tasty coconut flavor. I also liked combining the Coconut Manna with honey for a snack.
This whole food Coconut Manna (a product from the Phillippines) is made of pure, dried coconut flesh. The 15oz jar is certified organic by Ecocert & QUI and is distributed by Nutiva in Oxnard, CA.
My only reservation about the product is that it needs to be softened before using. The instructions recommend the jar be placed in hot tap water for 5-10 minutes. For me it took over 20 minutes for the Coconut Manna to soften around the jar's edges. (It never did liquefy.) Some Coconut Manna chunks also took awhile to melt in boiling hot oats.

I routinely use some coconut oil in cooking since it is a very healthy fat with zero trans fat. Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna is different than coconut oil in that it is more of a solid, but I absolutely love it! It's almost like spread butter, in fact it would be good to use as a replacement for butter. The flavor is great and would be super to use it in cooking as well. I put a spoonful in green beans and I think it adds a wonderful flavor to them.
Nutiva's website has some great recipes for smoothies, brownies, etc. I also got Nutiva's Chia Seeds and it has a recipe for cereal using both products. The product label states that it contains 12% fiber which is great and 9% protein...that is awesome!
It's also really convenient to have the pack of 2. I absolutely HATE running out of something I use often and I like having the second one on hand. When I open it...it's time to get more! You don't have to refrigerate it either so that is a plus. Great product!

Added review: Nov. 1, 2011
My husband took one of the containers to work and said it is great when you use it off the top, but if you heat it up like it recommends the taste and texture changes. He hates both! He tried it as butter on wafers and he said it was not great either. However, he did use it as butter on popcorn and it was delicious. Based on his review, I changed it to a four star.

This tea has a very comforting smell and tastes good. I'm really enjoying the cup I am having tonight before I go to bed. There is lemon grass in it but it's very subtle as is the verbena. The lemon grass which adds a nice light tang which gets a bit stronger while the tea steeps. Still, the tang never seems to get overpowering in my opinion. Seems to be a very pleasing tea all around that I feel most tea drinkers would enjoy.

I never was much of a fan of tea until about five or so years ago, when I started seeing the value it offers beyond being something to soothe your stomach when you're sick, or something hot to drink that's put on your table at a nice Chinese restaurant. And, honestly, that's exactly how I thought of green tea, especially, up until recently: it was just a substitute for water in a nice Chinese restaurant.

This Higgins & Burke tea is something I could get addicted to as a late-night mug of warm relaxation before I head to bed. It's refreshing, and fresh-tasting; warming, with just a subtle flavor - enough flavor to wake up your taste buds just a little, but not so much that they're overpowered. I brew my cups at about the halfway point with these bags - one minute, thirty seconds - and I never re-use them. I don't want the bitterness that can come from overbrewing tea to ruin the pleasant experience that I have drinking this (or, really, any other teas).

After trying this flavor in the Higgins & Burke line of offerings, I'd be happy to add this to my regular rotation of grocery purchases from Amazon. Great taste at a good price! You can't beat that!

I am on a never-ending quest to replace unhealthy beverages with healthier ones, and unsweetened green tea is one of the great saviors according to the experts.
