For $20 I bought this, took it home and had hope for about 7 minutes.  She got the treat out, and I messed up by pushing it in too hard, and getting it stuck in between the 2 sides.  (In theory, this was the most amount of time the toy went without having the treat popped out.)  After she licked at that for a while, I was able to push the treat out and get it back to the place that it belonged.  Pop. Pop. Pop.  She is now a pro treat grabber, who can get these everlasting discs out within 3 seconds flat. 2 if you don't count the time she sniffed at it.  Now I have a $20 ball to play fetch with.

I don't know how StarMark makes any money.  Other dog toy manufacturers make weak, flimsy things that my 75 lbs. pit bull chews to shreds in seconds - so I have to constantly buy new ones.  However, my friend (another pitty owner) gave us the large Everlasting Treat Ball and even after three years, its the only toy my dog hasn't destroyed - it's his favorite.  The inner cavity is pretty roomy, and the material is strong enough to withstand some pretty determined gnawing.  If you have a really smart breed, they'll managed to figure out how to free treats after some pretty intense studying, but even after that this toy is useful for many more play activities.

I have 2 dogs a 6 month old Goldendoodle and a  6 month old Chocolate Labrador Retriever and they both love this toy. I can't buy the cheap plastic toys because they will devour them within minutes, this one has lasted 4 months and I'm buying another one so that they can each have their own.

My pup solved this within minutes.  Now it's useless - hardly "interactive."  He just pops the treats out, and it's over.  The search (quest?) for the perfect interactive toy (for a super smart pup who bores easily) continues....

Summary: The treats made my dog vomit.
Text: My dog loved the ball and the everlasting treat but about 12 hours after going crazy licking it, she'd throw it all up. I tried again two weeks later, convinced that maybe it was something else that had made her sick, and like clockwork, 12 hours went by and she vomited again. She loves the ball so I will probably put her biscuits in the very inside and let her play with it that way. I regret spending so much on this toy.

Summary: My dog will not touch this toy.
Text:
I gave the ball with the treat stuck inside to my dog yesterday. He would not go anywhere near it. He sniffed the toy and treat and then walked away and it hasn't been touched since. I think what's turning him off is the smell of the plastic ball itself. It has a VERY strong fake-vanilla scent to it which is unpleasant to humans but must be overwhelmingly gross to a dog. By the way, my dog is not at all picky. He will play with anything and eat anything so this is a real first!

Also, I looked at the ingredients for the treat and it's all absolute junk. The first ingredients are wheat and gluten.

Summary: 24 hours of chewing and licking but wont buy again
Text: Our lab received this for Christmas. She loved the toy carrying it around all day licking or chewing on the treat cap. A couple of hours into the treat we noticed she would hack / cough as if a piece of the treat was caught in her throat and she needed water. Nothing alarming as her cough quickly cleared what was bugging her and she continued to feast on her treat. We noticed this happened a couple more times throughout the day. I picked up the treat to inspect it and the flavor cap was coming apart in pinch sized pieces. The blue portion was intact and was not showing signs of strain. The smell of the flavor cap was horrible, made me almost vomit but my dog loves it. Then we noticed our dog wasn't feeling so well. She had excessive gas that was room clearing. I looked up what could be causing this and most say its due to a diet change or low quality food being feed to the dog. I saw all kinds of remedy suggestions from rice and veggies to pepto. Her stool is soft but still firm so I am not alarmed. We are just going to ride out the effects and she will just play with the blue portion of her toy.  We feed our dog Blue Buff food so this large flavor cap could be a much lower quality resulting in her digestion issues.

Summary: Great product, but not for smart dogs!
Text: We bought the large ball for our power-chewing 30lb cattle dog mix, and this product was AWESOME for the first two weeks. She just chewed and chewed and was happy as can be, it kept her occupied for at least an hour each treat... but then she figured out how to pop the treats out (no joke, she wedges her tooth under the edge and just eases them out), now the treats barely last 15 minutes because she just chews a bit and swallows them. They're just too expensive to give her anymore. Luckily you can still shove small bits of dog food into the center, and she still plays with the ball but that game doesn't last very long either. Great product and really durable, as long as your dog doesn't outsmart it!

Summary: This is good but not everlasting...
Text:
Just an FYI to all those who have a smart dog like me -- this may not last as long as you hope. I've tried them all and am on a mission to find soemthing that will keep my pup entertained for a little while and won't break. Kongs don't last for Kobe and as much as he loves squeaky stuffed toys, they don't last more than 10 minutes. Gosh, did I mention he's barely 7 months old - can't fathom how much smarter he will get. SIGH. OK, so you've got an idea what my dog is like onto my review.
So I've seen these things both online and at pet stores, and always felt a little unsure about these things. For one thing, these things aren't cheap and two like I've described I've got a really smart Lab. So I broke down and bought this at the pet store after a worker I spoke with highly recommended it. Yes, this was even after I told him about my pup. He said he's got a big dog too who's a "chewer." Kobe usually knows when I've bought him something. Soon as I got home, I had to test it out. After 10 mins, not a dent so I was pretty amazed so far. 20 mins later, I see he managed to get that treat out!?!? Sigh...so I pried it out of his mouth and put that slobbery thing back in the ball. Next thing, he had it out again and this time he chewed a good chunk of it so it no longer fit. So I put it in the inner part of the ball and minutes later he got it out of there too. S-I-G-H.
I take off 1 star because in my case it was everlasting. I do give it credit for being pretty durable and the treat took a little while longer for him to eat. Also, it's got a cave you can bury treats in which isn't as easy for them to get things out of. I say it's OK.

Summary: Good taste, good gum, nice size for a home gum machine
Text:
I have an old Carousel "King" gum machine that's been sitting around my home office for years gathering dust. While I was finally cleaning up the office (it's taken years!), I decided to reinvigorate the gum machines (perhaps my daughters would stop by and say hi more often).

I looked around for some gumballs and most I found were the larger size that's typically in the $.25 commercial machines (which clearly wouldn't fit my machine).

I found these and gave them a shot. The gumballs are 1/2 inch and fit nicely in my machine, the amount filled my machine about 2/3rds of the capacity (it's hard to tell exactly since some is below the glass and the glass shrinks towards the top -- but clearly I could not fit another package into the same machine.

The gumballs were fresh (I hate stale gum) and the taste is good and varied amongst the balls. They taste lasts about as long as you get from most gum. I'm certainly happy with the product and my girls are -- the first thing they do when they get in from school is stop by the office for a gum refill.

The only reason I'm not giving them a 5 star is that I think they are a bit on the pricy side for the amount of gumballs provided. I think a more reasonable price would be on the order of $10 to $15 -- though I do have to admit that I've been unable to find similarly sized balls for that price (unless they also included a large shipping cost on top of the lower price and netted out to be even more expensive).

I use artificial sweeteners all the time, and I'll admit I was skeptical about trying this one. However, it surpassed my expectations. It's sweet like table sugar right out of the package and the grains look similar to sugar. I like the texture better than Nutrasweet, Splenda, and Truvia. It dissolved quickly in my iced coffee, which is the main place I use sweeteners. I don't drink hot beverages, so I didn't try it there.

I like the taste better than the Splenda and Truvia that I've been using and I thought this had less of an after taste. I made some iced coffees for friends with it and they said they couldn't tell it had an alternative sweetener. I say alternative, because it isn't exactly artificial like some are. Anyone who uses alternative sweeteners knows that there is some sort of after taste to all of them, so it really depends on your taste preferences. This one really scored high for me and I'd definitely buy it again.

Summary: Finally a no calorie sweetner I can use!!!
Text: I don't know what it is but I have never been able to handle no calorie sweeteners. I've tried them all. In some it's the aftertaste but in ALL of them I would get a horribly upset stomach within minutes of ingesting it. I saw a commercial for Nectresse and decided to give it a try. I had my first packet of it yesterday in a cup of black coffee. I added nothing else except the Nectresse. No after taste at all. Tastes just like I used regular sugar. Then I waited for the stomach upset. It never came!!! I believe the folks at Splenda have hit the nail on the head. This stuff is good. Real good! I'll be using Nectresse from now on.

As someone who tried many sweeteners, I was tempted to try Necrtesse.  In a nutshell, it seems to vary sweetness from one beverage to another.  I had to put several packets in a regular cup of tea to make it sweet, but not too sweet.  I then tried using it with peppermint tea.  Usually I do not need much sugar with my peppermint tea, but for some reason it made peppermint tea turn a tad bitter.  I guess this was a case of aftertaste.  In other words, this sweetener was all over the place on a sweetness scale.  That being said, I would still prefer this sweetener over aspartame.

I have a total sweet tooth, and routinely get shocked looks when people see how much sugar I add to my tea. To the extent possible, with cold drinks, I try and use Splenda, since it dissolves quickly and evenly. However, I've never liked it for hot drinks -- that wisp of bitterness and artificial taste comes across stronger. This new sweetener solves that problem, I've used it in a variety of hot teas and found it to be uniformly superior in taste to Splenda. I'll admit that I have no idea what monk fruit is, and obviously I haven't researched the effects of using this stuff for twenty years, but I'll certainly look at making the switch for my hot drinks!

Full disclosure: my doctor is one of the people responsible for bringing this product to market in the US. He had been telling me about monk-fruit based sweeteners for a few years prior to Nectresse being produced, so I was really excited to test out this sample.

I've added this to berries and smoothies, so far, and all I can say is two thumbs up. No aftertaste, micro-granules dissolve quickly, and it's great to not be worrying about this being an artificial sweetener. Recently I thought I'd try cooking and baking with xylitol, let's just say there were mixed reactions to that. Xylitol, even in small amounts, can give you wicked bad gas. Nothing like that with Nectresse. I'm hopeful that they'll offer bulk quantities soon. Due to its concentrated sweetness, I imagine baking with it might present some logistical challenges, but if you've ever used stevia or any other non-bulking sweetener, then you already understand about that.

Though this product is pitched as being made from monk fruit nectar, its primary ingredient is Erythriol, a semi-sweet sugar alcohol that has been around for a long time and is nothing new. This is just another marketing gimmick to spin off a new zero-calorie sweetener under a different label. It is a ruse not based on predominance of monk fruit sweetness which is comprised mainly of fructose and mogrosides. You could get something very similar tasting if you mixed Stevia with Erythriol, but I guess they can't do that because that's already been patented as another product sold as Truvia. My guess is all they have left is a product that combines Thaumatin with Erythriol and call it something else.

Summary: It is long over due for the Splenda Company to make a natural sweetner.
Text: This is a natural sweetner made by the company that makes Splenda.  I have waited for a long time for these companies that make artificial sweetners that can potentally be dangerous to us to come up with something healthier that does not cause tumors and things in humans. I wanted something safer.  This new one  is made with monk fruit and lists real sugar in the ingredients as well,  which I was surprised by.  Also, it taste okay but not as good as some of the Stevia products.  I will wait until they come out with something better before switching from pure via and other natural sweetners made with stevia. Addition - Seller was great. They recieved my email about the bus & offered me a full refund. They explained it was not intentional & that flooding in their area may have caused it.

I bought one of these for my dad for his birthday and he loved it.

Summary: Tasty but peanut covering is messy in the heat.
Text:
The beauty of store bought prepackaged granola bars is that they are convenient and are usually non-sticky/messy compared to homemade ones.

Nature Valley has always made some excellent bars that did not melt into a soggy mess when stashed in the car or brought on extended roadtrips/hikes/camping in the warmer months. However, this new line of bars from Nature Valley features a sweet peanut coating similar to the yoghurt coating pretzles are dipped in. This coating is quite sweet and melts in the heat.

I would not reccomend particular Nature Valley line for outdoor activities in the warmer months, but would not hesistate to for the winter months.

It is also a great treat to get kids off candy bars and into healthier granola bars as the sweet coating is quite peanuty and sweet enough. The bar itself does contain crisped rice that their original crunchy line does not, but it is still a vast improvement healthwise over other more common snack bars available.

It is now my everyday bread, because it is tastes good, has good fiber content and ingredients you could buy at any grocery store. Its really home-made bread, but you don't have to buy all those flours and try to figure out how to store them before they go rancid. Everything you need except oil and water is in this box.

As healthy as it is, I wouldn't be baking up a loaf a week if it weren't delicious. And easy! I use it in a bread machine that has a setting for whole grain breads and gives extra time for development of the dough. It comes out soft, but with an interesting texture. Because you add the oil (or butter if you prefer), it has no trans-fats.

I highly recommend!

Text: Add water and butter (or oil) - that's it.  I prepped in bread machine and baked in oven.  Makes a medium size loaf.  The product is 1 lb per package. Summary: Rare concentrate from organically grown blueberries.
Text:
Awesome product! Many are skeptical how naturally sweet this concentrate is, but if you take a bite of real blueberry and real cranberry, you'll notice right away how tangy cranberries are and how sweeter and much less tangy the blueberries taste, so comparing this concentrate to cranberry concentrate for the natural sweetness is not feasible. I'm quite this concentrate's sweetness is natural sweetness, as I'm very sensitive to the high fructose corn syrup in the drink. This blueberry concentrate is from organically grown blueberries, so a big higher price compared to others is understandable. I usually add 1/10th of glass and filled with water to drink. No need to add any more sweetness as it is naturally sweet as is. In our rural area, it's hard to come by organically grown blueberries, so this is product is great to compensate my problem!

UPDATE on June 29, 2012

Newtons Fruit Thins do not disappoint! The dried cranberries are tasty, chewy and plentiful. Then there's the citrus tang over a bed of oatmeal. Hmmm mmm! Perfect to grab and munch on the go, as I do - or to dip in a hot beverage like tea and savor slowly - my wife's preference.
Looking over the ingredients, there is no corn syrup, a plus (although there is sugar in the recipe), and no mouthful of unpronounceable chemicals.
For those who aren't fig fans, you'll want to try these. The cranberries are a flavorful alternative.
I'd say these are as close to health food as anything that tastes this good can get.

These little cookies are healthy, each one having under 50 calories and very little sugar. Eating two for an afternoon snack provides nourishment without overloading a moderate diet.

Summary: Name is misleading-Hard to identify what is really is by package
Text: ok, when i saw this, i first thought "cranberry fig newtons", hooray. This is a cross between a fruit roll up snack and a flatbread biscuit.  The fruit was very tasty and chewy and the best part.  I had to dunk the cookie into milk to soften it up a bit and smooth the texture since it was very dry.  While it is good, i would choose something else as a snack if I had a choice.  This is not a "fruit thin", it's biscuit with fruit.  I wasn't even sure what to expect by the packaging.  Either make the cookie more like a cookie or make it a flavored biscuit in a different shape (like for high tea).  But I did eat them all and enjoyed every bite.

I found these fruit thins to be pretty good.  They taste a bit like shortbread to me.  There is not a lot of fruit in them -- significantly less than in a regular fig newton, for example.  So, any cranberry fans may well find them to be disappointing.  All-in-all, assuming that I can find them at a good price, I may well buy some.

Summary: great cookie but not a filled cookie like everything else called Newton
Text:
Because These are called Newton Fruit Thins I was expecting a thin filled cookie, however, these are not filled. They are thin crispy shortbread like cookies with a nice texture and a dash of citrus flavor. There are a few bits of dried cranberry scattered throughout, the fruit adds some texture but does not dominate the flavor. I probably would not have known the bits were cranberry if it had not said so on the package. The cookies are not very sweet and are a good tea or coffee biscuit. These are very good served with cheese as well as being a traditional cookie. The oats and lower sweetness made them appeal to my healthy eating daughter though they are not actually health food.
We all liked these a lot and will probably get them again. They were eaten very quickly. family members who were not aware that these were called Newtons (fruit thins) loved them unconditionally. The family members who knew that the word Newtons was part of the name were initially disappointed because they are not filled cookies.

On the cookie-cracker spectrum, these definitely tend more toward cookie but are also no where near the typical chocolate chip cookie.  They are fairly thin and crisp, yet still soft.  I'm a fan of cranberry, so I could've done with more cranberry bits throughout the Fruit Thins but they are flavorful enough.  These make for a satisfying snack.

Summary: A snack the whole family can enjoy!
Text:
Seriously. When you have someone who has a whole mouthful of sweet teeth instead of just one (me), someone who doesn't really enjoy sweet stuff (my brother) and someone in between the two (my father), and we all thought these Newton Fruit Thins were delicious, I think it's safe to say that these crispy cookies will appeal to everyone. With a lovely citrus flavor, chewy cranberry pieces and hearty rolled oats, these are cookies you can feel good about letting your kids snack on. Not only are they made with real fruit and whole grain, they don't have high fructose corn syrup, the biggest selling point for me. No matter what propaganda the Corn Board puts out, HFCS is not an ingredient I want to put into my body and is, in fact, something I cut out of my diet several years ago (and by doing so, I lost about ten pounds without doing anything else to my diet or lifestyle).

With a serving size of three cookies--and each cookie is 2 1/2" in diameter, so these aren't small treats--at 140 calories per serving, you can indulge your cravings without totally derailing your diet. The cookies are quite filling as well. I'm not saying these are a health food item; after all, they are cookies. However, at 7 grams of sugar per serving, they're a better alternative to many of the sweet treats being offered today. And these will satisfy your sweet tooth just as effectively.

The only quibble I have is that the cranberry flavor isn't as strong as I thought it would be. That's not necessarily a bad thing, as the overall flavor is light and refreshing. It's just more on the citrus side than the cranberry side. However, that's perfectly okay with me and it's certainly not going to stop me from purchasing this flavor again. These are yummy!

Summary: Good oat & fruit taste, all-natural cookie snack
Text: While these cookies taste nothing like the original Newtons, they're really good in their own way. They are fairly thin with a oatty, slightly buttery taste with the addition of dried cranberry bits and natural citrus flavor. The all-natural ingredients gives them their all-natural taste. (Real fruit, whole grain, no high fructose corn syrup, 3 cookies are 140 calories and only 7 grams of sugar) They're crunchy but not hard and taste great with beverages like tea or milk. If you are looking for a lighter, healthier cookie with a touch of natural fruit flavor, these make a delicious snack.

While there may be some fruit in these cookies, there isn't enough to even notice when you are eating them. The taste is bland and mediocre. These cookies were supposed to be Cranberry Citrus Oat. I can't taste any Cranberry or Citrus or Oats, not sure what I am tasting. Given that these are called Newtons, I also expected them to be soft cookies (like fig newtons) but they are hard not soft. They also don't have much of anything beneficial in them either, no vitamins, essentially no fiber and very little protein but they do have some fat in them and lots of calories. They also contain fructose but not specified as to what type.

To me, these are nowhere near as tasty as graham crackers. Honey Maid Low Fat graham crackers are healthier, lower in fat, higher in fiber, with some calcium and with no fructose.

However, I would agree that these Newtons Fruit Thins are somewhat healthier than most other regular cookies.

If you liked those, you'll like these!  I happen to have been a BIG fan ... HUGE ...  So, the only thing that perturbed me about the old lemon coolers (which share exactly nada with these in the appearances department) was the the powdered sugar was messy.  These Newtons have none of that, and still remarkably similar taste.  I can't imagine they have any more calories than the oldies, and DO have a little fiber (1g) and protein (2g).  I wouldn't call 'em health food, but then again, it's hard to find true, dyed-in-the-wool health food with this kind of taste.  I love 'em, and will buy them.  They're large, thin cookies, about the consistency of animal crackers with dried fruit bits in there to yield chewy, crunchy and citrus twang all at once.  I'm really happy with them (and I'm usually a Keebler guy, thru & thru).  My take on it: try 'em.

Nabisco's new Chips Ahoy! Chewy, Gooey, MegaFudge cookies are incredibly rich. With a soft cookie that tastes more like a brownie, chocolate and white chocolate chips on the outside, and a soft and creamy chocolate filling, they definitely fulfill any chocolate craving you might have. Of course, with so much chocolate jammed in, each little cookie (much smaller than you'd expect) has 75 calories in it. So it is probably best to share a pack of these with friends, rather than give in to temptation and eat a big handful.

While the taste is amazing, the cookies are ridiculously messy. They literally fell apart in my hands when I picked them up out of the container. The fudge filling is so soft and liquidy that it has the consistency of chocolate syrup rather than fudge sauce. Using something so fluid as the center of the cookie seems like a way to guarantee they won't hold their shape. Add to that the fact that the solid cookie part is extremely crumbly and the chocolate chips have a tendency to fall off, and you've got a recipe for disaster. These cookies are without a doubt the messiest I've ever eaten. I lost more to the floor and my shirt than I managed to get into my mouth. I want a cookie that I can pack in my lunch or grab and snack on easily. These certainly don't meet those needs. Despite their amazing taste, they aren't worth the clean-up effort.

Summary: Just OK if your expectations are low
Text:

As far as chewy and gooey, I would call them more like soggy. The "fudge" was a not-too-sweet and not-too-flavorful layer of filling in the middle which simply tears apart. See my customer image. They seem to be rather crumbly and mostly held together by their oiliness. Compared to the Chocofudge variety, this Megafudge looks better but really doesn't taste any better. In fact, I'd give a slight edge to the Chocofudge.

Finally, a serving size is a laughable 2 cookies. These are so tiny, I easily ate four of them which is two servings at 150 calories an 7 grams of fat each serving. For a rather unsatisfying 300 calories and 22% of the USRDA of fat intake, I could definitely do better.

I hope you found my review and customer images useful.

I had a group friends evaluate these cookies.  The chocoholics among them liked these cookies quite a bit and thought they were delicious.  Several thought that they were better than regular Chips Ahoy.  I thought they had  lots of fudge and were chewy.  All in all about half of my friends liked them and half did not!

They are definitely yummy and not too chocolatey, but I will say I expected more "gooey" from them and really inside the fudge is thicker and not really gooey at all.  Overall though they definitely satisfied my chocolate craving and I love that they were so soft.

As a chocolate lover and sometime baker and pastry chef, I set out to find out exactly what these cookies are. The answers are not what you'd expect.

First of all, they're very sweet, as in Hostess Cupcake sweet, and there is absolutely nothing subtle about them. Second, they're made with both dark chocolate and white chocolate chips, but not enough white chocolate to take the edge off the enormous amount of chocolate and sugar they contain.

Now, as regards the name "fudge," this they ain't. If you're thinking of fudge as a candy, you won't find it here. Nabisco would have been better off calling them "chocolate cream cookies." While they have a regular cookie texture on the outside, what's inside is more like a ganache, which is what you get if you bring a pot of cream almost to the boiling point and then pour in a bunch of chilled, shaved chocolate, so that the chocolate melts slowly into the cream. The result is not as thick as frosting, nor as firm as, say, the filling in an Oreo. It is, literally, a chocolate cream. Using a ganache is a nice touch, but it's not fudge.

I suspect the "chewy, gooey" texture is a new venture for the Chips Ahoy brand. Getting a cookie to be truly soft involves using more liquid in the batter, which is the contribution of the chocolate cream or ganache, and removing the batch from the oven when it's still slightly undercooked.

All in all, I certainly wouldn't turn them down, but would probably prefer something with more flavor and texture, such as those delicious tubular European cookies filled with a chocolate-hazelnut cream. Too bad the hazelnuts give me migraines. On the other hand, I've been known to pour chocolate syrup on marble fudge (also not fudge) ice cream, so you may want to try these out for yourself.

Bottom line, interesting, but certainly not a regular purchase.

These cookies had an unusual texture- they were somehow dry on the outside and slightly tough in the middle (like undercooked pasta almost).  The chocolate chips were soft and melty, but the flavor wasn't exactly right- This is hard to explain, but it didn't taste like chocolate is supposed to- artificial maybe.  My husband didn't like them much either.  They weren't terrible, but you certainly couldn't pass them off as home-made- nor would you want to. Summary: Sodium Benzoate is Dangerous- It's in EZ-sweetz
Text:
I was disappointed to find out EZ-sweet uses Sodium Benzoate as one of it's preservatives. This ingredient, when combined with ascorbic acid (vitamin C) creates Benzene which is carcinogenic (cancer causing).

I used to use Splenda or generic sucralose packets, but they made a mess on the counter, took up too much room in our pantry when purchased in bulk, and took up alot of space near the coffee maker when compared with concentrated sweeteners. EZ sweet would be the easy alternative if it weren't toxic. I had to find a better option. I find that the only super easy way around using EZ sweet but also save on space/mess is to use the splenda mini tablets. They are much more expensive than the packets and take time to dissolve, so I've recently found another option. I can purchase 1 oz of pure sucralose powder form from the Splendex site and mix it with 3 oz of water (plus a natural preservative) to make the equivalent of 2,500 packets of Splenda. The cost of the 1oz powder is only $24.95. I found that other companies sell sucralose powder but haven't found a supplier who sells just 1oz and will supply me with a 4 oz bottle suitable for dispensing the solution. Finding the powder wasn't easy. It is not an option on their home/default web page. I had to go to order products and on the right side was an option for the powder.

I'm going to experiment with different natural preservatives (colloidal silver, GSE, natural salts, natural acids) to keep the solution from becoming contaminated with bacteria or fungus. If you're going to go this route, do some research on natural preservatives and if you find one that works well, please leave a comment to this review.

Summary: Good Taste and Usually Good Portion Control
Text:
Good Taste and Good Portion Control

EZ-Sweetz

This is concentrated liquid sucralose plus preservatives. Unlike the granulated forms, it truly has zero calories. The flavor is good, but there is a slight difference between this form and the granulated form, which is no surprise because the granulated form uses a sugar (malto dextrin) as a filler. The product stays in the bottle, even if it falls over with the cap off. You have to squeeze the bottle to get the product to come out, which is does one drop at a time, so it is very easy to get precisely the number of drops that you want. Some people may feel that you have to squeeze too hard to get the drops out and may need to use both hands.

Update: usually the portion control is good, but sometimes you get one with a hole so big that the product comes out as a stream instead of drops. Other times the hole is so small that a man using two hands and squeezing as hard as he can, can barely get anything out of the bottle.

I usually use Sweetzfree, but decided to try this as it was cheaper and I was surprised that another liquid Splenda was available.

The taste was only OK and a little bitter, but bearable. The major problem I had with it was that it actually made my tongue numb. I usually put it in my tea by putting it in the glass before I pour the tea; even so, the drops seemed to sit on top of the tea and would not stir in completely. I even cut way back on the amount I put in and it still numbed my tongue.

I gave it 3 stars because once the numbness subsided (after about 5 minutes) the taste was close to sweet and would probably be acceptable to some users of artificial sweetners. The numbness kind of worries me, though, so I will be switching back to Sweetzfree

Summary: Love the product, but don't buy online until they learn how to package
Text:
I love, love, love Lee Kum Kee Chili Garlic Sauce. I use it in several dishes, but I especially love to make vegetarian dishes with it. When I lived in the DC area, I could find it at almost any grocery store, but I've moved to an area where local grocers don't carry it, so, I thought I'd buy it online and ordered 4 jars. The GLASS jars were shipped in a bubble envelope with a large fragile label adhered to it. Lee Kum Kee is on the west coast; I'm on the east. Every jar arrived broken. It was an incredible mess.

I complained and requested a refund, which I got without a problem, but honestly, I wanted the chili garlic sauce.

If you order anything from Lee Kum Kee, make sure they know that you know that packaging must be appropriate to the product shipped. People who ship glass containers of anything should know how to package so that breakage is rare. Lee Kum Kee may save a bit on shipping costs by using bubble envelopes, and maybe some packages make it to their destination intact, but it's a bad business decision. People like me are going to share so that others don't have the same bad experience.

If anyone has a recent, better experience please let us know. I do love their products.

Also, check out the (short!) ingredient list. My dog is allergic to just about everything but this chew contains none of usual offenders. It's basically made of milk.

Two downers for me would be the price and the sound effects. Text: Since my husband has celiac disease we are always looking for great gluten-free products.  This fits the bill.  It tastes just like original brownies and they are so easy to make. I've converted the box recipe to make chewy chocolate cookies, which is even better than the brownies! My family prefers these cookies to any other regular cookies they can have. WOW.

Make up the recipe as directed on the box, but let the batter sit for 15-30 minutes to dissolve the sugar granules. Preheat oven to 350. Line cookie sheets with parchment paper.

Use a cookie scoop to drop dough onto lined cookie sheets, leaving plenty of room to spread out--about 2" between cookies. (A small scoop will make about 20 cookies, a medium scoop will make about 12 cookies)

Bake 1 sheet at a time in 350 oven for about 12-13 minutes for small size, 15 minutes for medium size The cookies will be flat and shiny, but set.

Remove from oven and cool for several minutes on cookie sheet so the cookie can harden and set up, and not fall apart when removed with a spatula. They will retain their shape if left to cool on a flat surface.

These make rich chocolate cookies that are crisp around the edges, but incredibly chewy and soft in the centers. I've tried chilling the dough to see if it will bake up more "fluffy", but they still flatten out quite a bit.

*The cookie can be used as the cookie in ice cream sandwiches as well, but I think they are better assembled and eaten immediately, unfrozen, rather than made up in advance and frozen to firm up the ice cream.

Taste good, easy to make.  However for the price, I expected a full 9x13 pan, not an 8x8 pan. So I'll stick to making them from scratch. I am thrilled though, that a well known company is taking on gluten free items.  Who knows? Maybe it wont be long until we can buy little debbie snacks too. :)

Oh well. I tried this stuff for 3 months to no avail.

Summary: Great Product at a Great Price!!!
Text: This is the only product I've used that has really helped! I work full time and it is much easier to pump when I drink it in the morning.

This doesnt taste half as bad as some of these reviews are letting up.  The licorce taste is there but its very subtle!  Its well worth it in the long run and adding honey helps.  Go for it mommy's!!!! Your baby is sooo worth it!
This tea has a great hearbal taste to it and my wife has good results from using it. She finds it especially helpful for days when her milk supply is low due to stress.

I have purchased CASES of this tea, and without it I don't know if I would have enough milk for my very hungry boy. I only drink two cups a day but they really help, and when I don't drink them my breasts do not get nice and full, which frustrates my son (I have a slow flow so when they are not bursting he has to work so hard to get satiated)

This tea really does work, especially (for me) at first.  I have trouble with my milk supply - and IF I pump TWICE at work, I'll get a whopping total of about 5 1/2 ounces.  I can't imagine pumping 8 ounces, let alone 15.  While this tea didn't make me produce gallons of milk, it allowed me to sustain my milk supply.  After a couple of months, though, it didn't work as well.... or maybe it's just that my little one needed even more milk.  Motherlove's goat's rue tincture works really well though. For me, it's better than the tea, but I take both daily anyway.

I returned to work when my little guy was 3 months old and by 5 months I had used ALL my freezer stash. My baby had only had breastmilk but I couldn't keep up with what they fed him at daycare.

He eats 16oz while I am at work. I was pumping 3-4 times at work for 20 minutes at a time and only getting 2 1/2 oz per session. I was so frustrated and exhausted! I tried everything: more water, more frequent pumping sessions, more frequent nursing while with the baby, I even took a nursing weekend where all I did was nurse and pump and rest but I still couldn't get more than 3 oz per pumping session.

I started with 5 cups of tea per day. I don't like the smell or flavor of black licorice so I was worried that I would have to gag this tea down...it isn't pleasant but it is tolerable. I can even drink it without adding sugar, honey, or milk but it will never be a drink I like or want.

Day one I really didn't see any change at all.

Day two I pumped 3 times and got 11 oz which was the most I had gotten at work in weeks.

Day three I pumped 3 times at work and each time I got 5 oz or more. I ended the day with 17 oz and was thrilled! That evening I nursed my son when we got home but could tell I wasn't empty so I pumped right after nursing and got another 2oz. That night I leaked through the night and had to change my shirt...now I don't drink any tea after 6 pm.

I've been using the tea for only ten days now and have started a new freezer stash that is currently at 20 oz. The peace of mind is great, knowing I have extra. I am consistently pumping 5oz per session and getting the extra 2-3oz after my nursing session with my son at 5:30 and sometimes I pump at 8 p.m. after nursing and get another 2-3 oz. As an added bonus, my little guy was still waking every two hours until I started drinking this tea. The past three nights he has slept 4 hours at a time.

I have a lot of milk to begin with so I am not sure if this product worked! my breastfeeding lasted for almost a year... I just had to stop. I love drinking tea anyway, so might as well drink this one and help me lactate. I also gave this product to 4 of my cousins that are pregnant right now...
You can buy this tea for under $5 at Wegmans grocery store. It is great and it works!The tea does taste pretty good unlike the fenugreek tea which does the same thing.

i drank this tea for 4 days, only did 2 cups a day.  the four days that i was drinking it, my baby was fussy and kept pulling away from the breast.  he stared waking up in the middle of the night after 3 hours when he had been sleeping 7 hours.  i stopped drinking it and he went back to normal sleep and eating patterns.  the taste was okay.  i started taking Nursing Blend Supplemnet and baby likes it.  it is basically the same ingredients but with added daily vitamin.  maybe it was the method of delivery, pill vs tea, that my body does better with the pill.

Summary: It doesn't work as it supposed.
Text: We bought 6 boxes. and drink the tea every day, did see any improvement unfortunatedly.

I understand that the product does not guarantee increase in milk production, that is why I can't complain that it did not or helped in any way. It has a very strong herbal fragrance, which my coworkers weren't crazy about. So, if you have a sensitive nose, you will probably have a hard time consuming it.

Just to let you all know, this product is readily available at GNC for $5.49, same amount of bags...Don't pay for it online, it will cost you too much!  Especially if you are using it 3-5 times daily as the package says.

I've been drinking this tea for two months now.  At first, I didn't know if it was working until I skipped a day.  On that day, I didn't seem to fill up as much.  The next day, I drank four cups and they runneth over.  They were so full that I had to wear pads all day.  This tea works.

After my son was born prematurely it was too stressful for him and for me to nurse. I have opted to pump my breastmilk and he takes it by bottle.  This tea has been a life saver.  It has been 2 months and I am still able to keep my supply up!  There are times when my supply has been lacking (mostly early evening); as long as I make sure to drink plenty of Mother's Milk tea throughout the day (4 mugs with honey is what I drink) and the evening hours are not as much of a problem.

After getting the stomach flu my first week back to work, my milk production seriously took a plunge to almost nothing. I panicked and contacted my local La Leche League and they told me about this tea. I have to admit I was not wild to hear that it tasted somewhat like licorice since I do NOT like it but optimistic since I didn't want to stop nursing and thankfully with this tea and a tremendous increase in my water intake I am back to normal and now producing more than my precious baby needs. I highly recommend this tea to anyone who needs a boost in production!  Happy Nursing!!!

Summary: This tea has helped SO much!
Text: I started drinking this tea a few weeks ago when my daughter was about 4 weeks old.  I was worried about my supply.  She was fussy (especially in the evening, which I know is normal, but she seemed very hungry).  I went to a lactation consultant when she was 2 weeks old and found out she had a tongue-tie.  We went to an ENT and got her tongue clipped, but she didn't seem to really learn to nurse correctly and I think she still wasn't drinking enough.  At four weeks I was getting more worried.  A friend heard about this tea from a lactation consultant and recommend this as well as pumping several times a day after feedings to stimulate more production.  I think both the tea and pumping were very helpful.  Now my daughter is 6 weeks and starting to look a bit chubby (so cute!).  She is much less fussy too.  I am pumping only after her 4 AM feed (so just once a day now) because I get extra milk then for my freezer stash.  I borrowed a hospital grade scale from a friend and did test weights before and after feedings for the past 24 hours.  My daughter drank 24 ounces in 22 hours and I pumped 2 extra ounces for the freezer.  I think this is fairly normal for a six week old, but I am so, so happy because this is much more milk than I was making just 2 weeks ago!  I think this tea may also be helping my milk ejection.  My daughter eats so much more quickly now.  In about 15 minutes she takes 3 or 4 ounces.  Weeks ago I did a test weight and she had drunk only .5 ounces in 40 mins.  It is so nice that she is nursing faster!  In short, I highly recommend this tea.  I love the licorise taste and feel it was a major component in increasing my milk supply!

This tea is a "must" for nursing mothers.  It really does help to increase milk production, and would always help my baby spit up less.  Tastes awful, but you get used to it.  Recommend for all nursing moms who are concerned about their "supply."

Summary: This is a great product at a great price
Text: I'm currently breast feeding my 3rd baby, and I've never been one to have an abundant milk supply.  I first tried this tea with my first and I felt that it worked, but I bought it at the grocery store (1 or 2 boxes at a time) and didn't drink it more than twice a day in order to make it last.  When I saw that I could get a pack of 6 in Amazon for such a great price, I jumped at the chance (I got a cheaper price by choosing the subscribe and save option) and religiously drink at least 3 cups a day. Not only does it work; it's delicious! I have more milk now than I ever did with my 2 previous kids. And did I mention how yummy it is?  This tea is available in most grocery stores and health stores; buy a box, give it a try, and if it works come back and buy it in bulk.

Text: I have used this tea with all three of my children to help my milk supply.  I highly recommend it!

I have tried so many things to increase my milk supply so I could continue to breastfeed my 6-month-old boy/girl twins.  This works better than the Earth Mama and the Yogi Nursing Support teas by far.  I drink about 5 cups a day.  Someone said not to drink it before bed, but I did even after my twins were sleeping through the night and woke up and pumped 16 oz.!  All Traditional Medicinals teas I've tried work great.

Summary: An easy option to increase your milk supply
Text: I've been using Mother's Milk Tea for a little over a month now & it seems to be working quite well.  Before I started drinking the tea, I would only be able to pump a couple ounces at a time, creating a problem of not having a decent supply of breastmilk built up in my freezer.  After drinking the tea, I can now pump about 4 ounces at a time.  I noticed a difference after just a couple cups of this tea.  They say that when you return to work that your milk supply is bound to go down but, I think this tea has counter-acted that theory because I haven't noticed much of a difference in my milk supply since I've been back to work.  There may have been a slight decrease but, not much in my case.  This seems to be an easy option to increase your milk supply.  I'm glad I tried this tea because I did not want to have to supplement my son with formula.  The taste isn't too bad either.  It has a anise or licorice taste.  I add a little honey to it & it tastes just fine.  I don't always drink 5 cups a day of this tea but even when I don't, I still notice a difference in my supply.  I sometimes brew a couple tea bags in a mug & let it sit and get really strong before drinking it.  Seems to do the trick for me. Amazon also seems to have the best price that I could fine for the tea.

I am into non-medicinal care as much as possible. I don't do well with all sorts of prescribed medicines; last go around caused my immune system to crash and I was a long time in rebuilding it. When you find something that works so well with simple herbs you are delighted. Gypsy Cold Care isn't bad tasting. Sort of a twiggy with a strong mint-type flavour. Only who cares what it takes like! This stuff works for me. At the first hint of a cold or sore throat, I brew a pot and drink it. Generally all the cold symptoms just fade away in just a few hours. I have recommended it to dozens of friends and it works well for them, too.

So if you are looking for all natural alternatives, you might consider this the next time you feel a cold coming on. I keep it on hand all winter.

I don't go in for herbal remedies. When I'm sick, I grab some Robitussin or Sudafed, and that's that. If this has any legitimate medicinal value, it's just a nice bonus. From my standpoint, this is just a Damned Good Tea!

We have been using this formula for years (currently using for our third child).  As far as the product goes we have no complaints.  We even loved Amazon's pricing, although find it "ironic" that they rose the price significantly after our first purchace.  The new price is very competitive, but the original was of course outstanding.  Hard to complain when you are not being overcharged, but I can't help being a little dissapointed with sudden increase.

This is my favorite oatmeal! It has little pieces of real apple in it and lots of cinnamon. Delicious.
If you want to make it by boiling your water first (negating the need for a microwave) you can just pour 1/2 C of boiling water over it in a bowl. it cooks up in just a couple of minutes.
Try this! You'll love it!
This product is wonderful for diabetics or anyone else who loves honey but wants to cut down on sugar.
This is a great substitute for honey.  Works in recipes and on waffles, biscuits and in tea.  Anyone who must forgo sugar but still would like the interesting flavor of honey will enjoy this product.
This is a very good product and reasonable amounts do not upset my control parameters.

Summary: Big Mess All Inside the Box
Text: I can't rate the imitation honey because it was spilled all over the inside of the box and the bottles when I received it. Summary: Healthy portions of flavor despite healthiness
Text: This is a tasty cereal with all kinds of vitamins and minerals. The grains and seeds make for a healthy breakfast (even by modern The Evolution Diet: All-Natural and Allergy Freestandards). I expected more in the vanilla blueberry clusters, which were noticeably sparse. Fortunately, the flavor is still there, and so makes up for the lack of clusteration.

Summary: Delicious, but not really THAT healthy
Text: Granola is awesome, KIND is a great company and this was delicious, but this is perhaps not the healthiest choice. There's a surprising amount of sugar in here, and not to be super-picky, but the flax seeds pretty much just get stuck in your teeth, where they have minimal health benefits. This was also rather on the tough side as far as chewing, which can be a concern for some.

This is a lovely little granola. Just enough sweet, but not TOO much. The vanilla/blueberry clusters add taste interest without being overpowering. I can take or leave the flax seeds since they aren't well digested in whole form for most folks. Ground whole flaxseed sprinkled on your food, or flax seed oil are both more beneficial since they are more easily digested and utilized by the body. The whole flax seeds do give some good textural interest along with the grains. Very nice with Greek yogurt and fruit and NOT "cardboard-y" at all. Definitely a two thumbs up rating from me.

Summary: It took some time to find the right combo...
Text: I wasn't fond of this with yogurt, but it's SUPER with milk and a splash of fruit/nut mix. I let it soften a little and snarfed it all up! Very highly recommended.

Not only are these really tasty, the ingredients list is pretty awesome as well. I decided to order some more after this Vines-provided bag was gone. For the record? The peanut butter flavor tastes like someone mixed granola with Nutter Butters. Amazing. The cinnamon is a hit with my wife, who hates all forms of healthy granola/seed foodstuffs.

Great product.

We've been gluten free for several years now, and one of the things that has been missing is a good, crunchy, gluten-free granola.

The Vanilla Blueberry granola boasts a punch of delicious vanilla flavor and crunchy oat clusters. It's packed with a variety of healthy grains in addition to the gluten free oats. It's a healthier granola. The only downfall is the lack of blueberries in the granola. When a granola is labeled vanilla blueberry clusters, I tend to look for blueberries or at least a noticeable blueberry flavor. (The lack of blueberry is the reason for the 4 star instead of 5 star review.)

The Cinnamon granola had a very nice cinnamon flavor. The granola tasted great with milk as well as eating plain as a snack.

It would be nice if the granola came in larger packages as we went through the granola very quickly. If you use it on top of yogurt or ice cream, it will last much longer.

This is my first experience with any sort of healthy grain snack. I have to say, I've become a fan. I find it difficult to enjoy healthier options because I do have such a sweet tooth but with the vanilla and the blueberry mixed in with these grains I don't miss the sugar. Plus, it helps to know that this snack is very healthy, not to mention quite tasty. When I think of healthy I don't usually think it will taste good as well.

I've actually been looking for ways to add some sort of Omega-3 into my diet but it's been difficult because I don't like fish. This snack is full of flax seed which is full of the heart healthy Omega-3.

When I first received the bag I thought, this reminds me of cereal. While reading the back label it actually say's you can add milk and have it just that way. I've yet to do that because I brought this product into work to have as a breakfast filler. It works perfectly for that as helps control your appetite. It fills me up and I feel good knowing it's a healthier option than what I'd usually go for.

For me I'm so happy I found this product. Its low in sugar, full of Omega-3, and is made with 100% whole grains. They suggest trying this on top of yogurt or with milk. Both seem like delicious ideas that I can't wait to try.

I am pleasantly surprised I like this. I'll definitely be getting it again.

I recently reviewed another flavor of Kind Healthy Grains. The one here was a little less dry and tastier than the other. Also, it had more of what I would call clusters which made it easier to eat right out of the bag.

As with the other, I think eating with milk or with yogurt would work out well. I only tried it out of the bag so far.

I liked both flavors, but this one was a little better in my opinion.

A bit pricey perhaps, but it seems to be very healthy.

I've been looking for healthy snacks for myself and my two year old, and these fit the bill nicely. These are delicious-probably one of the best foods I have reviewed on Amazon and certainly the best as far as gluten-free goes. I enjoyed these straight out of the bag, and as a cereal. They are sweet but not too sweet, and have a surprisingly low glycemic index which is important for those who need or like to monitor their blood sugar. One caveat thought: The clusters come apart quite easily. This didn't bother me, but this may be a concern for those looking for an on-the-go snack.

I ordered this because I love oat clusters and stuff like this for breakfast with some almond milk.  When I got it the first thing I did was read the ingredients and to my dismay, one of the things in this bag is Chickory Root extract.  :(  This is an ingredient that companies put into their products to bump the fiber content.  But in doing so it causes excess gas and bloating.  This is one of the key ingredients that I avoid when looking for healthy foods to buy.  I did taste the product and it is actually very good and if I didn't know it would upset my stomach I would really enjoy it.  I hope I can find something like this without Chickory root in it.  I would recommend it for the flavor if you don't care about that one ingredient.  (the same one used in all Fiber One products to make them so high in fiber)

The Cinnamon Oat Clusters are so addictive and a perfect snack to grab when you're in a rush. It tasted a little like a good cinnamon flavored oatmeal. All the flavors complimented each other perfectly - none overwhelming the other. My only complaint would be that I wish the clusters held together better. I had very few clusters left when my bag arrived.
It was great with yogurt and I would love to try it with a little milk as the bag suggest.

As a huge fan of KIND bars, and as a granola-crazed eater, I eagerly took the opportunity to try KIND Healthy Grains Cinnamon Oat Clusters. I was not disappointed. The diverse grains are sweet and crispy, the nutrients are plentiful, and the price is right. I generally eat the granola dry, straight from the package, but I have eaten it with both almond milk and yogurt, making for a delicious, nutritious breakfast or snack.

For those who are curious, here is a breakdown of the nutritional content, as well as ingredients:

Serving Size: 1/3 cup (29g)
Servings Per Package: About 11

Calories: 130
Calories from Fat: 30
Total Fat: 3g (5%)
Saturated: 0g
Trans Fat: 0g
Cholesterol: 0mg
Sodium: 20mg (1%)
Total Carb.: 22g (7%)
Dietary Fiber: 5g (20%)
Sugars: 6g
Protein: 3g

INGREDIENTS:

Whole grains (gluten free oats, brown rice, gluten free oat flour, buckwheat, amaranth, millet, quinoa), evaporated cane juice, flax seeds, chicory root fiber, canola oil, vanilla extract, molasses, cinnamon, sea salt, Vitamin E (D-Alpha Tocopheryl Acetate).

The cinnamon flavor really shines in this, which is a big improvement over other brands of granola, where the flavor tends to get lost in the mix. The variety of grains is incredibly robust, especially the inclusion of quinoa. So there is a little something to please everyone.

So, for those seeking a delicious, healthy granola blend, I highly recommend KIND Healthy Grains Cinnamon Oat Clusters!

I was previously only familiar with the Kind brand through their yummy (though very sweet) granola bars available at Borders and various locations. This is the first time I have tried their granola. I like that it can be topped on yogurt or eaten as cereal. It is important that my food products be able to multitask that way. It is just the right amount of sweet, and fairly addictive. I think that it is basically healthy but keep in mind it is high calorie if you eat more than a handful. A good treat, though use sparingly if trying to lose weight. Cinnamony granola goodness. Yum.

If you are used to healthy eating, you'll like it. It's fragrant, not too sweet for me, (also with a hint of honey), crunchy and very filling after about a cup of it.

By healthy eating, I mean...you are used to food that doesn't have a lot of artificial flavorings, oil, or sugar. Flax seeds have a nutty flavor in them. They are where Omega-3 fatty acids come from. I tasted them alone before. They also taste a bit like "olive oil," but very subtle in these Cinnamon Oat clusters.

I really enjoy eating them out of the bag. It's perfect for snacking and on the go. It doesn't make me tired or sluggish after like a piece of cake would do.

Indeed, I had no clusters in my shipment, just a few clumps in a sea of grains. Not deterred, I really liked the flavor of the product. It echoes the quality and general flavor of other Kind offerings. Its texture is a little more brittle-like than I prefer in granola, which seems to contribute to it being very sweet and candy-like. This is the one factor that would keep me from enjoying it regularly. The flavor of the grains is very nice, though the blueberry could come through a bit more.

The inclusion of whole flax seeds is a bit distressing, however. Whole flax seeds are hard to chew, which when factored into being indigestible would seem that their health benefit is somewhat lost. Generally speaking, this granola is a tasty treat, though not something I could keep as a staple in the pantry.

My wife is trying to eat ultra-healthy, so I ordered these as a treat for her.  I'd already gotten her the blueberry one, which she liked, so I tried these.  She loves them.  The package size is convenient for her to take to work.  She works 12 hour days at the hospital, so having some quick energy food helps get her through the long day.They make her happy, and that makes me happy.

I love granola, and probably go through a box or two every few weeks. One of my favorite brands has been Kashi since it's pretty healthy overall, and doesn't have a lot of added sugar. This KIND granola, however, takes the cake: it's one of the best-tasting commercial granolas I've tried!

Granola can often be high in fat, so I was pleasantly surprised to see that one serving of this (1/3 cup) has only 3 grams of fat (5% of your daily value). While it still has the typical higher calorie counts that granolas usually have, coming in at 120 calories, it's really high in fiber (5g, or 20%). The ingredients are all-natural, and, overall, it's a really healthy option if you like granola.

A granola isn't worth its weight in grain, however, if it doesn't taste good, and this one is delicious! Even my husband, who's not a huge granola lover, really liked this one when we were sampling it, and he came back for more.

I also like how this has nice, big clusters, so that you can actually grab some out of the bag and snack on it. Granolas that have smaller clusters have to be mixed into cereal or eaten with milk, but not this one.

Overall, I found this to be delicious and am happy to have been able to try this out. I will definitely re-purchase it!

It has a great collection of grains, it tastes good, and even has chicory root fiber, a great prebiotic (selectively nurtures beneficial bacteria in the gut). And the package opens easily and seals back up easily, which is very unusual for a cereal for some reason.

The downsides: It smells a little like rancid oil. And although it's nice and crunchy, there is an extra little crunch at the end of the bite that is too much, like a little seed that is a little too hard and cracks more than crunches at the end. And the little seeds got stuck in my teeth.

The bag for these clusters recommends enjoying them in milk, on yogurt, or as snacks right out of the bag, so I decided to try them in every manner that did not involve buying yogurt that I would then be disinclined to finish. First, I snacked on them dry out of the bag. They definitely tasted delicious, with all the cinnamon and sweetness promised on the label. They had a really satisfying crunch without being too hard, and I would definitely keep buying them for snacking purposes at my office. My main problem with the dry snack method is that the clusters aren't very cohesive, so sampling them mostly involves scooping them up in your hand, pouring them into your mouth, and trying not to lick your fingers before going back for another scoop - I don't recommend this method for people with germ issues. There were some clusters that were easy to pick up and enjoy, but most of the bag was loose or powdered.

I next tried them in a bowl of milk, and again, the taste was delicious. Sweet with cinnamon, exactly what I want in the morning. Again, though, texture became an issue. They stayed crunchy in the milk for the first minute or two, then got very soggy - still tasty, but not nearly as satisfying.

Texture issues aside, though, I really enjoyed this product by both methods. I love that it has so much fiber and flax, and so many simple ingredients on the list. I also love that it is gluten-free (I eat my share of gluten, but I have close friends who can't eat it, and I am always on the lookout for more tasty products that I can share). This is definitely something that I would eat again.

Summary: Very tasty, fairly healthy, so-so value
Text:
I'll get the ugly out of the way first. The 11 oz bag is rather small -- not much bigger than your hand. It contains 11 1oz servings of 1/3 cup. I could easily eat 1/2 a bag without really trying. They are not really clusters as pictured, but crumbs like in a typical oat cereal.

I don't have any special dietary requirements, but I do mind pretty carefully what I eat, so here's my review:

Very tasty. Much better than expected. A little on the sweet side. The cinnamon was not overpowering. Very versatile as well. You can eat it loose as a snack (although a bit messy the further down you get in the bag since there are few "clusters" -- more crumbs and dust). You can also put it over yogurt or other dessert, or eat it with milk as a cereal.

Nutritionally, I really like that it has whole grains which give it a nice texture, but not too hard to chew. Refreshing compared to all those heavily processed foods out there. Here are the Nutrition Facts per 1/3 cup 1oz serving:

Calories: 130
Calories from Fat: 30
Total Fat: 3.5g
Saturated/Trans: 0g
Cholesterol: 0mg
Sodium: 20mg
Total Carb: 22g
Dietary Fiber: 5g
Sugars: 6g
Protein: 3g
Basically trace/minimal amounts of vitamins/everything else

My "reference" cereal is GoLean Original which is 140 calories for 1 cup serving. Compared to this, the GoLean has 13g of protein and 10g of fiber while being 3x the volume. The Kind clusters do have more whole grains 16g (versus 8g) and 720mg of omega-3, so it is still fairly healthy, especially if considered a snack in its small portion size.

The list price of over $100 is a joke. Amazon's price in the mid-teens is fair, but it would be a lot more palatable if it was cheaper or with a subscribe-and-save. The packaging seems to be trying to promote the KIND movement by the KIND CEO which I found as a weak sell and possibly only contributing to its higher price.

Clusters? I didn't get any clusters. A couple of residual clumps, but thanks to insufficient packaging, all I got was essentially a bag of powder.

I'd attribute part of that to Amazon choosing to send me the single bag in nothing more substantial than a bubble mailer, but the factory packaging should be air-tight, and have enough air (well, nitrogen to keep it fresh) to survive a trip from Seattle to northwest Oregon. I could mail a bag of potato chips (of most major brands) and the chips ought to survive the trip intact.

The powder tastes okay. But crushed that much, I can't really consider this a snack anymore. I am very disappointed.

Maybe I'll try some from the grocery store where I can make sure it's not already crushed, and then transport it myself in a suitable fashion, but even if it turns out to be good, I can't recommend buying it from Amazon unless they find a better way to ship it than a bubble mailer. I can't believe anyone could have thought that was a good idea!

Summary: Whole Wheat ? Not the way you think!
Text:
My SCAM alert went off like a claxon when I saw this.
'Whole Wheat' can mean one of two entirely different things.

1) It can mean it is made from the entire wheat berry.
or
2) It is plain old white flour stripped of its nutrient germ and bran but the product is 100% wheat and does not include OTHER grains

Read the ingredients on this and you will see "Duram Whole Wheat Semolina"
Looking up Semolina, I see that it is the endosperm WITHOUT the Bran or Germ.
In other words, this appears to be plain old common white pasta.
I imagine they added color to it to darken it.

The only thing that appears to be authentic about the term whole wheat in this case is that there is no other grain in the ingredients.
It does not appear to be made from the whole wheat berry though!
I hate this kind of misdirection, but when you see "Whole Wheat",
I would not assume that the entire wheat berry is being used,
it often is nothing more than 100% plain old white flour - of course, made from wheat and no other grain.
