Summary: Cant say anything that hasnt already been said!
Text:
Well it is coconut oil... So yeah, good stuff. lol I use it on my two month old's face and even in her hair for cradle cap. It works really well for a skin moisturizer especially for babies and toddlers because it is so mild and smells like food! I caught my three old daughter licking her hands after I put it on her one day.
I have yet to cook with it since I just started using it like a week ago, but I am actually planning on using it in the kitchen.

UPDATE:
I use this on a daily basis for cooking. I love sauteing mushrooms and onions in it, and my day doesn't go so well without my eggs fried in coconut oil. It is so good for you! Before anyone knocks the amount of saturated fat in it, do some research on the benefits CERTAIN KINDS of saturated fat. They are not all equal. I have also been using this as a diaper rash remedy for my two year old. It works way better than any other cream I have used. And I have used them all...

I purchased this and the shipment was fast which is a big plus. Ignoring the fact that it's in a plastic container, this stuff is awesome. It smells and taste just like when my mother makes coconut oil so I know that it's organic and all natural. All the other oils I've purchased usually have a strong overpowering smell and usually remain liquid even in cold temperatures letting me know they aren't good. I've made my own but it only makes a bit so I thought I'd try Nutiva and I'm glad I did. This stuff has the light nutty smell and solidifies quickly true to coconut oil. I'd definitely recommend this stuff.

I've purchased Nutiva in the past and have no complaints but now there is evidence that storing food in plastic can cause cancer because of the dioxin so I'm opting for the glass container.  Also a couple of months ago I purchased two of them for $13.00 now it's 26.00 so glad to see there are other brands in a glass container with the option to purchase only one at a reasonable price.

The coconut oil's aroma when I put it on toast or rice is just heavenly. The taste is amazingly good too! Since it came in two tubs, I have one in the kitchen for consumption and the other one in my bathroom for my hair since I researched and found that coconut oil is supposed to be good for natural hair. My mane is definitely softer to touch although it is typically not course or difficult to manage. I just got it last week so will see how it goes. The hot oil treatment with coconut oil is next on my to-do list. Careful when you use it on hair though, when I don't wrap my hair, I wake up with zits (prolly from the oil on my pillow). Some say it works to relieve acne, some say it causes acne. I blame it for the acne I have since I had been acne free for weeks until I applied the coconut oil on my hair.

Overrall, I will be a regular buyer of this product.

Summary: Don't keep plastic spoon in jar!!!
Text:
I've been using this brand for a couple of years now. It has a light coconut hint at times. I use it for popping corn and I can't taste any coconut, other items like meats or veggies sometimes have a hint of coconut...it's not necessarily a bad thing.

I thought I would save washing a spoon each time I used this and put in a clear, plastic spoon (Kirkland brand) into the jar so I could reuse it. DON'T KEEP PLASTIC IN YOUR COCONUT OIL!!! About 1 week later I went to make popcorn and I pulled out the handle of the spoon with no bottom of the spoon to be found!!! The acid in the coconut oil will eat away at certain plastics! Had to throw the 1/2 full jar away! Lesson learned! Just reordered and went on subscribe and save.

Nice.

I bought this to add into my hair routine. And so far so good! I combine it with pure organic cold pressed olive oil- my hair loves it.

The quality and texture are great.
I like the containers- they're plastic jars which makes storing them a breeze.

I also use this on my skin sometimes, and it works GREAT. It really saturates into the skin- makes it very smooth and extremely soft. I actually use the olive oil/coconut oil combo on my skin, so I guess its both products at work... but either way it goes it'll leave you with softer skin.

It's a little messy for me because I have to transfer it into a smaller bottle, but I just started using the top of a straw/sippy cup as a funnel and that helps. The smell is strong, if you like coconut you'll love this. I'm not that huge on it, so at times its a bit much for me.

This is the best deal on on this product you'll find- 2 for $16 (and free shipping if you spend $25)... but I still wish it was more like 2 for $10.

Using it for cooking, hair repair and skin moisturizer. Love the smell, really great! Good product and price.  Will purchase again.

Summary: Great quality, versatile product, LOVE IT!!!!
Text: I use it not only for cooking, but also I made my own lotion (olive oil, bee-wax and coconut oil, vitamin E)...perfect. The food tastes good and my skin looks great. All natural, no chemicals. Great product, very versatile at a great price.

This is the first time I have ever used coconut oil and I love it!

I first tried cooking with it--I used one tablespoon in the pan, added onion, garlic, mushrooms and peppers. I usually use EVOO so I was a bit worried about the taste difference. It defininely smells like coconut, but surprisingly, it is not overly strong. The taste was pleasant with my veggies. First try: delicious and easy.

Next, I put some on my face as a moisturizer. Again, the smell was pleasant and mild. In the past I have also used EVOO on my skin because it is a milder moisturizer than a store bought facial moisturizer. EVOO takes hours and hours to soak in, so I only use it at night before bed. I thought the coconut oil would be similar. I put in on in the evening and sat down to watch a movie. It was completely absorbed before I even hit the sheets! And by the time it was absorbed, the smell was gone (not that the smell of coconut on the skin would be a bad thing!) So it is lovely as a facial moisturizer.

Then I read on the label that it could be used in place of butter, so I spread some on a cracker and tried it that way. It was delicious! I love the oily texture--similar to butter, with the coconut taste. So it is a wonderful substitute for butter.

I am sure I will find more uses for this incredible product and I can't wait to try it again.

I have to admit I'm floored by this product.  I'm originally from the West Indies so needless to say I love coconut.  I've tried other extra virgin coconut oils and wasn't impressed, they tasted and smelled more like vegetable oil than anything, and forget about trying them straight.  I was very skeptical about Nutiva but reading some good reviews and being hounded by my vegetarian friend who swears by it, I said what the hell.  It arrived from Amazon and it was in liquid form, which was to be expected as it's 96' in the shade here in Florida.  I removed the lid off the jar and before I even took the seal off, I was entranced by this wondeful coconut fragrance.  I stuck my finger in and even in liquid form, I was tasting nothing but melted coconut.  Later, when it turned into solid form I tried it again, a dap on a teaspoon, once again, nothing but coconut.  Definitely will buy this coconut oil again.  Nutiva did a great job of impressing an Islander ;)
Great coconut oil to use in cooking, baking, and even as a snack (grab a spoon and go!). Will definitely order it again!

Besides being just plain tasty, a small addition of Nutiva coconut oil to my daily diet lowered my triglycerides and "bad" cholesterol. It also ended nightly coughing from what my doctor diagnosed as gastric reflux. Better coconut oil than prescription proton inhibitors that leach calcium from your bones!
I use this stuff for my hair and skin.  It makes my hair shiny and soft.  Makes my skin smooth and soft, but a little sticky.  Smells good, but I haven't tried eating it yet.

I just loved this product. It is healthy and a delicious (best) substitute for any type of bread spread. French toast cooked with this oil are just heavenly. Has zero cholesterol and delicious flavor, what else can you ask for? Kids will love it too.

It moisturizes my hair very well, i use it as a daily moisturizer, i have created an oil mix with Jamaican Black Castor oil and Peppermint oil, and i also use it as a pre-poo. I love this product, I have been using it topically for my dry skin and it works wonders, I am sure it tastes amazing in food also!
I was surprised how much I like this product and coconut oil in general. I use it in place of butter and oil for everything.

Lovely coconut oil. I bought the pack of two 15 ounce jars, one for cooking and one for the cat's food, my own body, and my hair, and it's just heavenly. It smells brilliant on, but the smell fades after awhile so it doesn't totally overpower you and everything around you, my cat likes it so much that he licks it off my legs--he needs a bit of extra fat since the raw meat you get at the grocery is generally lean--and my incredibly picky boyfriend tried some teriyaki pork I sautéed in coconut butter and he loved it--huge surprise, since I was ready to go overboard apologizing to him for the coconut flavor. I've made raw truffles with this, carob powder, almond extract, agave, and crushed almonds, and they turned out so yummy that SAD eaters loved them. But--warning!--if you live in the South, and especially in the summer, be really, really careful peeling the protective bit of plastic on the top off! Mine is permanently liquid, but especially so when it sat outside in a box waiting for me to come home.

Another bit of advice: buy the 54 ounces; it's a better buy, and you'll use it!

To whoever hated the plastic jars: yeah, you're right, but I'd still buy this coconut oil again. No, plastic isn't ideal, but I just transfer the oil to my old glass olive oil bottles and add one of the metal dispensers on the top--easy to use and it's glass.

I have been having problems with my skin. The moisturizer I was using felt kind of scummy on my face after I added my foundation and I was having troubles with facial redness and dry patches. I was also having heat rash problems in my underarm area. I started using just a little of the coconut oil on my face in place of my moisturizer, then applying my foundation and wow! What a difference! My skin has cleared up and I love the soft smooth way my face feels. My foundation spreads and blends much better. Also, the coconut oil really helps with the heat rash, immediately soothing the discomfort. I like using this as a hand cream too. I look forward to seeing how well it works this winter when the air is much drier.

Other folks have mentioned that the oil leaked during shipment. I was concerned about this since I ordered it during the summer. I ordered 4 tubs (2 pks of 2 tubs). The plastic containers arrived packed in plastic bags, 2 tubs/bag, within the box. Even though the lids felt pretty tight on the tubs, both of the plastic bags had some coconut oil that had leaked, but not enough to feel cheated. A little oil leaked out of the plastic bags into the box, but they were the only things packed in the box so nothing was ruined. I can see that if the lids had been any looser though, there would have been a mess. Oil is hard to keep in a container with a wide mouth like this.

Summary: Was hoping for a little more heat, but love the flavor
Text:
I've been hooked on pepper spreads for a long time and especially since I was in Italy and brought home a few. I love the distinct Italian pepper flavors which are different than Mexican and Asian peppers. This spread is actually pretty mild but it does have a great, unique pepper spread flavor. it's also a lot of diced stuff, and reminds me of the texture of an olive tapenade. It is not super oily. there is oil that collects around the top when you first open it, but overall it's a pretty 'dry' spread as opposed to something that is soaked in olive oil and drips everywhere. That makes this very suitable for putting on crackers. It also works great for bread of course, though I'd want it more oily for breads. No problem though, just have some olive oil handy.

Because of the cost, I would not bother using this a part of a sauce. It's best as a spread or maybe used as topping for stuffed peppers or pizza. All in all it is very high quality and an excellent appertiva/tapas addition.

Summary: They dont mention the Gobs of Artificial Sweetner.
Text:
Like being misled much? If they are willing to mislead you from the start, what else are they doing that they arent telling you about?

The front of the bottle says "reduced sugar"

The promotional literature says "This Ketchup recipe has 75 percent less sugar than our classic Ketchup, but 100 percent of that rich tomato flavor. Just like all Heinz® Ketchup varieties, it contains no artificial colors, flavors or preservatives."

Notice something?? They dont mention that they replace sugar with sucralose; a chlorinated sweetener (chlorine has a byproduct dioxin which the EPA found to be 300,000 times as carcinogenic as the pesticide DDT.-mercola)

When i wrote Heinz to suggest they print "artificially sweetened" below their massive 'reduced sugar banner' their response to me was search for the fine print on the back of the bottle. Does that sound forthright to you? Does that sound like they are trying to keep the customer fully informed? Kind of a shady practice and a shady response from the company.

We bought this as a low carb substitute for the 17-Day Diet program. My wife and I could not believe how genuinely terrible this stuff tastes when compared to regular Heinz Ketchup. We either had to forego ketchup altogether or just cheat on the diet with regular Heinz. We chose the latter and lost weight on the program anyway. We had absolutely no hesitation in dumping this product right in the garbage.

Sure, we're all too busy to make our own ketchup (with Stevia, a healthy sweetener with no carb or glycemic load), but it would be much better to try to do so especially if you're feeding kids too. For those needing low carb, low or no sugar, watch out for the ingredients "sucralose" or "splenda" (and of course most already know about the harmful effects of aspartame, saccharine and "Equal"). Don't believe me? Do your own web search to find out more. A great site is the EWG, Environmental Working Group, a non-profit group which tests many products for toxicity levels. Also check out [...].
If you think it's all hogwash or not so important, oh well, I tried to warn ya!

This is a terrific product, and I highly recommend it. Whenever I have people in my house, they're always fascinated by it and ask me lots of questions. I've only planted the gourmet herb seed kit that came with it so far, and all of the herbs were delicious. It's so convenient to have the garden right there in my kitchen, and I love that it's low-maintenance.

I do have a few minor complaints, which is why I only gave it 4 stars instead of 5:

* The cilantro didn't grow at all. I got absolutely nothing. I received my AeroGarden as a birthday gift in July. We were in the middle of remodeling our house at the time, so I stored the package, unopened, in the garage. The 90-100 degree garage. For a month. I am going to assume that the heat destroyed my cilantro seeds. Oddly, everything else grew just fine. Maybe I just got bad cilantro seeds. My husband despises cilantro, so our joke is that he poisoned the seeds when I wasn't looking. :-)

* The mint seemed to die a couple months after planting. The two basils, the parsley, and the dill are still doing well. The chives are looking a little iffy right now, but I haven't been very consistent with pinching back the other herbs. I think the chives are being overpowered by their neighbors. This wasn't the issue with the mint, though.

* The herbs included in the kit that comes with the garden would not be my first choice. I love the basil. It's convenient to have parsley on hand since a lot of recipes call for only a few tablespoons of it. I used to hate buying a huge bunch of parsley, only to use such a small amount. I'd like to say the same thing about the cilantro, but of course, mine didn't grow. I rarely need mint, dill, or chives, though. That's just my personal preference, of course. Maybe this mix of herbs is perfect for some people. I am going to choose a different herb kit for my next planting.

I still really love my AeroGarden, despite its few drawbacks. In fact, I want to plant some salad greens, but I don't want to give up having fresh herbs available. I am actually considering buying a second garden. I've noticed other reviewers have had the same dilemma. :-)

This is a very easy, tasty meal for two. It has a significant amount of "heat," so if you don't like "spicy," you probably want to skip this. For me, it was just about perfect.

My favorite combination is shrimp, carrots, red bell pepper, and either snow peas or just some frozen green peas (OK, I KNOW that's not "authentically" Asian, but it tastes good ... ). You soak the noodles for 3 minutes in hot water, stir fry the protein (shrimp, chicken, whatever) in the sauce for a minute or two, add the veggies and stir for another minute or two, then mix in the softened noodles. Divide onto two plates, and you're ready to eat.

This isn't too salty -- some Asian sauces taste like soy sauce with a hint of other flavorings, but not this one. It's full of citrus flavor (mostly orange), slightly sweet, with that punch of heat.

Will buy again!

Yesterday I spent my day in the strawberry patch. I picked eight quarts, and while most of the berries were destined for jam, I made sure to set aside a bowl full of berries to make the first strawberry shortcake  of the season.  Shortcake in our family consists of a generous portion of sugar-sprinkled fruit, a large helping of fresh-whipped cream (sugar and vanilla, too, of course), and all served on top of a still-warm biscuit fresh from the oven that must be made from scratch (Bisquick? Blech.....).  We've only been gluten free for just under two years, and for that time I've neatly avoided, and sorely missed, those homemade biscuits.  Last night I grabbed the  Mama's Almond Blend that had been waiting patiently in my cupboard, screwed up my courage, and made my mother's old fashioned biscuit recipe with it.  Using a fresh-layed egg from one of my hens, baking powder, sweet butter, whole milk, and a small amount of xantham gum, the dough mixed up precisely as it would have had I used wheat-based flour.  The biscuits plopped onto the parchment-lined baking sheet like they always used to, and they baked up golden brown and crispy on the outside, soft and tender on the inside.  Oh, they were heavenly!  The best part of our dinner aside from the food I was inhaling (and yes, our dinner consisted solely of strawberry shortcake - another family tradition on strawberry picking day) was when my non-gluten-free partner in crime took his first bite, and then looked at me and asked, "How come you're eating these biscuits?  Aren't you going to get sick?"  He literally could not tell that these yummy treats were gluten free!  I've tried many other gluten free flours in my role as a gluten free product tester, and this one is literally the best I've had.  While other gluten free blends are decent, and can produce the end result many are after, Mama's Almond blend is stellar: texture, taste and results all parallel gluteny flours, and in my recipes Mama's outperforms the rest of the pack of gluten free flours.  My little two pound bag is nearly gone - a batch of chocolate chip cookies this morning proved that it is dollar-to-serving worth its weight (and will significantly increase MINE if I continue to bake and eat like this!); the dough didn't even need to be refrigerated like other gluten free doughs before baking.  I'm one happy camper - and this will be my personal go-to choice for flour from this day forward.  It's a marriage made in gluten-free heaven!  Next up for Mama's Almond Blend - cheddar biscuits to go with homemade chili...and with blueberry season around the corner, and peaches ripening shortly after them, I think I'd better stock up - gluten free summer baking never felt so good!

The Strawberry flavor I tried is tangy and not overly sugared like most processed strawberry flavors. The twist is brownish red, like natural strawberry preserves, not bright red. Each chewy piece contains one serving of fruit and there are no artifical colors.
The pectin leaves a bit of a waxy coating on your lips that feels not unlike lip balm--it would probably be a bonus in the cold, winter months.

Each Clif Kid Organic Twisted Fruit serving has only 70 calories, but is all organic with no added sugar. I think it's a great snack for adults as well as kids. The only slight criticisms I have is that it's a touch more tart than expected and the primary ingredients are "apple puree" and "apple juice concentrate" with no specific mention of strawberries. Also, while the price is a reasonable value, it's not a terrific one. I'd strongly recommend that you consider the "Subscribe and Save" option, which knocks an extra 15% off of the price. You can always cancel S&S later if you change your mind, so there's no downside to signing up and it will save you money.

I have been working my way back to classic cocktail recipes ever since reading David Wondrich's book Imbibe! on the great Professor Jerry Thomas and his cocktail recipes and techniques. A wealth of information there and a beginning of a long journey to try to recreate the cocktail prior to the great disaster called Prohibition. As a martini drinker, I naturally wanted to explore the tastes of the original drink so I began with orange bitters. In my market there were no retailers who carried orange bitters, so I had to rely on the ever more expensive places that will ship the stuff to your door. I started with Fee Brothers orange bitters and then tried the Peychaud version of Gary Regan's orange bitters (no. 6). Finally about 3 months ago a local liquor and wine store chain started stocking the new Angostura orange bitters. Thinking it would be easier and less expensive to support a local merchant and also wanting to try the bitters, I picked up a bottle. I was a little taken aback when I saw the retail price, $11 versus $7 for Fee Brothers and $6 for Regan's. I decided to try it anyway.

Upon opening the bottle I realized that the bottle itself was orange colored and the internal contents were virtually colorless. Having made many fruit and peel extractions for liqueurs, I was very suspicious. Forging on I sniffed the aroma from the open bottle. The first smell is definitely orange, with an underlying clove aroma and something cloying behind those aromas that does not seem to work well. In the drink the orange flavor is good and the bitterness that is necessary in a quality bitter is apparent. But it seems to me that it is quickly overwhelmed by something like a passion fruit flavor that definitely does not belong in a martini. I would consider using this product in drinks that have some fruit juice and will experiment some with it. I think wit would compliment a splash of pineapple juice in a drink like the Cobalt, but I would not use it in a martini.

Amazon.com has a fine selection of specialty products and accessories for the home bartender. I've become a big Amazon.com fan after hosting just a few cocktail parties.

The Angostura Orange Bitters are excellent in mixed cocktails ... if your recipe calls for a dash, use a half, if for two use only one. Angostura produces a robust product. I read several taste test articles before deciding on the Angostura brand. Hands down difficult to beat a true original. Do visit the Angostura web site too! I printed a file packed with mixology know how, tips on what to mix with what to achieve various flavors, and, certainly many uses for Angostura products.

Summary: UHT milk should be long life! this is not.
Text:
I bought UHT milk on-line because - amazingly - it does not seem to be ubiquitous in stores in the US as it is in the rest of the world. I need it for my disaster preparedness kit, the food supplies we store against disasters such as earthquakes which would leave us without access to electricity (including refrigerator), water, gasoline or shopping for several days. We need milk for cereal, drinks and children. I was extremely disappointed to find that, instead of a 'Use Before' date of 2 or 3 years, as I have always found on UHT milk bought in other countries, the expiry date on this product, bought in August 2011, is February 2012. This means I will have to repurchase the milk every 6 months, making it much too expensive.

It is maddening that buying the item on-line one cannot check (or ask about) the 'Use Before' date. I would of course check this if I could buy the milk in a store. This reminds one once again of the disadvantages of shopping on-line, with no recourse to asking questions of a person and getting essential information which affects the choice to purchase.

I do feel that sellers on UHT milk should give their customers the LONG LIFE product they expect.

Summary: BPA lined cans means not really organic anymore once processed
Text:
I chose Westbrae's canned beans because they are organic. However, since then I've discovered that Westbrae uses cans with BPA in the lining.

With BPA lining the cans and research showing solid levels of the chemical leeching from cans and plastics into containers' contents, showing up in Americans' blood streams (from infants to the elderly), I don't think the product can still be called organic!

BPA leeching into our food is no better or safer than products sprayed with pesticides.

At least pesticides can be washed off many foods (not all, but some). Most people, though, just empty cans of foods, like beans and tomatoes, directly into their recipes without thinking of washing them first. (How does one rinse or wash soup?) In fact, many people like the salt and other seasonings in canned foods. They believe it is safe to use the foods as they are in the can, which is a reasonable assumption since that is how such products are marketed.

I know I quit adding salt to my own recipes containing canned foods many years ago, because the canned goods already had salt in them. The canning process is supposed to kill bacteria and preserve nutrition, just as home canning does. It wasn't until the information came out about BPA in our bloodstreams, and from where most of us are exposed to it, that I realized there was a problem using such foods as is. There are still many Americans who do not yet realize that there is a problem and they are unwittingly feeding that problem to their families.

There is something especially unethical and tragic about people paying a company higher prices for organic foods, thinking they are better protecting their health, only to be swallowing BPA with each mouthful.

Until Westbrae stops using BPA lined cans or stops claiming the organic label and charging organic prices, I can't give high marks for either context.

Summary: Very pleasant but takes some experimentation to find your preferred strength.
Text:
When I first prepared a mug of Maxwell House International Coffee Peppermint Mocha Latte, I guessed at what would be the right amount of product to mix with the water. I got a strong peppermint taste with overtones of chocolate and almost no coffee flavor, and the hot water at the heart of it was very obvious. I had clearly used an inadequate amount of the product.

I didn't want to swing too far the other way with the next mug, so I boosted it by a teaspoon, and ended up with much better results. I'll probably try one teaspoon more, but I'm worried the peppermint will overwhelm the flavor at that point. We'll see.

I'm not a big fan of the package or the serving technique: it comes in a plastic container with a plastic/foil seal on top that is virtually impossible to tear without removing it, so you don't have the option to partially open the container--making it easier not to spill and to control your portions--unless you use a knife or scissors to cut the foil. I would probably mind that less if not for the 3"x2" opening at the top of the cotnainer that makes it very easy to spill. In fact, in peeling off the foil, the container "breathed" a cloud of product into the air and onto the tabletop.

In the long run, this is a pretty decent product, but it doesn't hold a candle to the better instant hot cocoas and doesn't really have enough coffee flavor to compete with a true Mocha Latte from a local shop. Of course, it also doesn't come with the coffee shop's price tag...

First of all, I believe taste in coffee is very individual, just like taste in chocolate.  Some prefer milk, some prefer dark.  When it comes to coffee, I prefer a good French roast.  I didn't have high hopes for a flavored instant coffee drink, and the best I can say about Maxwell House International Latte in Peppermint Mocha flavor is that it's drinkable.  In my opinion, it is too light on coffee flavor and much too heavy on the peppermint.  It's actually more like a hot chocolate drink than a latte.  There's a decent amount of foam after mixing in the hot water.  I added a bit of milk but did not need sugar as this was plenty sweet for me.  I'll keep it around to offer guests who might like this sort of thing, but it doesn't at all compare to a real latte.

COST: At the time of this writing this runs about $0.44 per 8oz cup. Not bad for a flavored, hot drink especially when paying nearly $2 for a plain, no flavored black house coffee at Starbucks

INGREDIENTS: Sugar; Nondairy Creamer (one of the worst things to put in your body), Maltodextrin, Cocoa, Instant Coffee, Artificial Flavor, Sodium Citrate, Modified Cornstarch, Silicon Dioxide

ALLERGY WARNING: Contains Milk

PREPARATION: Add 4 teaspoons to 6oz-8oz boiling water or hot milk

TASTE: Uh, no. It doesn't taste like a latte to me. Rather tastes like a peppermint flavored hot chocolate.

The peppermint is nice and strong. Strangely there is ZERO peppermint listed in the ingredients!!

Even when I tried it with half serving (2 tsp), the peppermint stood out but the mocha/cocoa was very light.

I mixed a full serving with a cup of black coffee and I felt like peppermint, cocoa and coffee all stood out better. When using a full serving with water, there is zero coffee taste to me.

OVERALL:
If you want a peppermint hot chocolate with a small amount of caffeine, then this is your product.
If you want more of a mocha latte, then this will fall short.

This is another example in this line of pleasant warm-drink mixes from Maxwell House. It is smooth and rich and good-tasting. You have to put rather a lot of it in the cup, and it is quite high in calories, but that is sometimes a price worth paying for something which tastes good. In any case, it is not something one would want to have every day; more for when one deserves a bit of a treat.

I was excited to try this product because I thought it was going to be the perfect drink on my cold night. When I tried it, however, I was disappointed. The drink was just extremely too minty for me. It was a menthol overload. There was too much peppermint and not enough mocha.

If you like York Peppermint Patties, you might like this drink. It is like the liquid version of a peppermint patty. I didn't enjoy it, but maybe other people will.

Maxwell House International Coffee Peppermint Mocha Latte is great coffee. I was a little hesitant to try it being I don,t eat sugar, I thought it might be too sweet. This is really good; not too sweet at all. It has a nice mild peppermint taste but the choclate latte still comes thru strong. It is really good especially as we are heading into the holiday season . Its a treat for big kids!! I made it with just the hot water to see how it performed. It was frothy & did'nt rquire milk or anything else. It was good all on its own. Try it I think you will like it !

Summary: Very minty. Very sweet. Nice chocolate flavor.
Text: I'm assuming if you're reading this review that you realize that it's instant coffee, and you know what that means (easy to prepare; often weak; lacks the bold flavor of real coffee). Some of us, like me, prefer the ease and variability of instant coffee - I can make it as strong or as weak as I like! The mint chocolate does a good job of masking the fact that this is instant coffee. My one potentially negative comment would be that the mint is very, hm, fresh (almost bordering on toothpaste) and is the strongest of the flavors.

Everyone is offering a peppermint mocha today.  Just take a drive down the road at all the major chain coffee shops and even the local ones.  You can't miss it this time of year.  Well now Maxwell House wants to bring that popular holiday flavor to your home.  First off, the recommended serving size is too small of a serving.  Your going to have to double it.  Mixing is easy, add powder to water.  The end result is a very weak latte or a strong hot cocoa.  The peppermint flavor over powers any chocolate or coffee taste.  It's nice to have the ability to make something like this at home, but I think it's a concoction best left for the experts.

Very Watery - and no latte flavor in sight here.

I received one 7oz tin and the instructions said to add 4 teaspoons into a mug with hot water (6-8 oz). Fairly easy, and it dissolved with no problems but very heavy on the peppermint and not much else there. The ingredient list isn't terribly encouraging either with sugar right at the top, followed by the *cream* with a list of things you'd rather not know, with the "instant coffee" well towards the bottom of the list. From looking at the Nutrition facts its seems rather high on the carb content.

I really didn't find much in this product that I could recommend it at all, and not one I'd try again.

I doubt it's much different than it was prior, if any. They said it's only a changed label. For what it's worth, I liked the old label better, but that's of no real substance here.
I didn't think the coffee flavor was strong enough, even with double the dose. The peppermint was a nice addition to the coffee, but neither was strong enough. I wouldn't get it again for only that reason: strength.

The idea is good, and the flavor is good...just not enough of it. I guess there's no reason to up the peppermint, since it's only supposed to be a hint of flavor, but the coffee needs some work. If the old Cafe au Lait appeals to you, i.e. weaker coffee flavor, but still not tasting like 'instant', then this might be just your thing. It certainly has that holiday aroma, and I'm just sorry it didn't offer enough "coffee" for me.

The mint is not overpowering or overly fake.  I don't like it mixed with water so much as I do mixed in with my own coffee or mixed in with milk.  It gives it a festive zip.  I certainly wouldn't mind finding some of this in my stocking come St. Nick's day.

Summary: Festive flavor for the holidays, but I think I'll stick with "real" coffee
Text: To save calories and all the artificial ingredients, I really wish I could drink plain black coffee, but I just don't like it.  I usually have brewed coffee with flavored non-dairy creamer.  When I saw this product (and the Pumpkin Spice variety) available through the Vine program, I thought I would give it a try.  It's okay, but nothing great.  It's sweet and has a slight peppermint flavor (fun for the holidays), but really no coffee flavor to speak of.  It's certainly not the quality of a latte drink you would get at a coffee shop.  On the plus side, it is super easy to make plus costs much less than a latte drink from a coffee shop.  The product does not contain much actual coffee, so it certainly won't give the morning pick-me-up that I have come to expect from my morning coffee.  So I think I will stick with my usual brewed coffee with flavored non-dairy creamer in the mornings and the occasional latte or similar drink at the local coffee shop.

It's crazy stormy outside on this November day in Oregon and my cup of peppermint Mocha Latte hits the spot wonderfully. It's the perfect blend of mocha and peppermint to make a steaming cup of pleasure on such a yucky day.

Another reviewer said she added a few t-spoons of this to her brownie batter and it turned out fantastic. So next time I'm going to have a cup and a brownie. Hello sugar high!

I'm ordering more right now.

Summary: Need to add more tablespoons to get the flavor.
Text: I have to echo the sentiments of others on here, the recommended amount is not nearly enough.  You have to add 3-4 tablespoons to really get any flavor.  The first ingredient is sugar, this is a lot of calories for little taste of peppermint and none of mocha.  Also, there's very little coffee umpf if that's what you're looking for.  It would make a nice office party gift tie with some cellophane and ribbon, the price is right.  However, if you really want a good cup of joe, you're going to have to stick with Starbucks Peppermint or get the International Delights creamer.

The two cats in this household attest that they are crazy for this stuff.  Their only complaint is that they want more of it.  As for us humans, totally convenient.  I serve it in the container it comes in, one for each cat, which keeps them busily engaged getting out every last morsel.

My cat finally has something she'll eat.  Usually she will just lick up the gravy and leave the bits so I wasn't hopeful when I ordered this.  I put out a dish of the chicken flavor and was amazed to see her actually eating the chunks before the gravy.  I hope the turkey and beef flavors work too.

I like to have a few treats on hand for my 2 cats. These were a good price, and I have twice bought the multipack of Beachside Crunch, since they tend to prefer fishy flavors. I would try the other flavors if they came in a mixed multipack, in case they didn't like the other flavors. They love these (they like most 'treats' actually) and come running, as they hear the packet opening, or if I shake the bag. They are also a good way to sneakily apply their flea medicine to the back of their necks without them realizing it. They have a sixth sense about this and make themselves scarce whenever I even think about doing this. However, they also have outsmarted me when I tried to fool them into scarfing up some of their regular dry (Friskies) cat food that I spilled on the floor when filling their bowls and thought I would try and get them to eat it straight off the floor. They ignored it, so I thought I would sprinkle a few treats among it to make them think they were getting a big treat. They came running, but managed to pick out and scarf up only the treats from among the other pieces. No problem eating treats off the floor, but regular food no way!

All of our cats love Friskies Party Mix in all flavors.  The 6oz. pouch in a pack of 7 is a great buy.  What I don't understand is why all the other flavors are significantly more expensive than the Beachside flavor.  Anyway, the Beachside flavor is a good bulk buy since the cats love it and each gets a treat time twice a day.

I have been giving my old golden retriever Happy Hips items for a few years now to help with his arthritis.  He loves these treats along with other Happy Hips items.  These are a great snack for him that I carry in my pocket when we go for walks.  I do think the glucosamine in these has made a big difference in his aching old legs and has helped him stay with me as long as he has.  Thanks for a good product.

I love this cheese popcorn by Jolly Time.
I hope I will be able to continue to find it here.

I came accross ghee while searching amazon for a good sesame oil.  After reading lots of reviews and doing a little google search on ghee & it's benefits and uses, I decided I would go ahead and try it.  I dont use butter ever in my cooking, so the ghee was a new experience for me.  I really enjoy it, especially on toasted bread with a splash of acv & some parmesan cheese.  I know, sounds weird & I get strange looks from hubby but it taste really good.  I like that this ghee can be taken oraly as a part of an ayurvedic cleanse.  It's consistency is very creamy & smooth.  And on my counter it hasnt melted in our 90 degree temps so far.

I've tried many brands of prepared ghee over the years, and have often made my own, but I keep coming back to Purity Farms.

It is the highest quality, and does not vary from batch to batch.

I like the appealing cow logo, too!

This butter is highly addictive so use it at your own disgression. It is so delicious. I heard a lot about using Ghee and it being a better product. I bought mine from whole foods and just saw it and bought it and have been hooked ever since. It is so pure and clean tasting you will want to use it for everything. Its a creamy flavor but of course not a creamy texture. Its clarified butter and it taste just like that.
I did not know butter could taste so good.  I look forward to using this to put on veggies for my kids, I'm sure it will encourage them to eat more vegtables, it's that good, and fresh tasting!

Summary: Is Ghee really that Great for you?
Text:
I purchased this having read in the Body Ecology book that it was an excellent alternative to butter, because the milk had been removed and that ghee is does promote phlegm/thick mucus in the way that other dairy products (cream/cheese, etc) does. I didn't think the taste was very strong, and was surprised to see over time, mold in my ghee. I don't know if I contaminated the container with something wet or what? I did just scrap the small spot of mold away and continued to use it.

I haven't bought it again, but thought it was a decent product when I used it. I generally don't buy butter either though.

Summary: Great Product.  Love me some Slim Jims
Text: Gotta have my slim jims everyday.  These are just right for a small snack.  The small box allows for each storage.

I received mine and all 100 of them had a tear on the end ... so the are hard as a rock... the first time I got them everything was fine..... this TIME not so lucky... won't be ordering anymore online ...(any kind of food)

I found these basically tasteless.  The macadamia content is negligible and the chocolate taste wasn't all that good either.  Obviously the company is trying to save money as macadamias are pricey.  I wouldn't order these again.

Plenty of variety, almost all of which are delicious. Chocolate-filled cookies, chocolate-covered cookies, white chocolate...basically you name it, they've got it. I originally got one of these as a holiday treat, but they were so unbelievably good that I just needed to buy more to satisfy my cravings throughout the year. This is one product I will continue to buy as long as it's available (our local Sam's Club ran out).

I would like to know how long these were on the shelf before sending if they were that hard to eat? I will never send this product again or recommend it to anyone to buy online. Not a happy camper.
I was skeptical about this product at first, but was truly happy with it the varied flavors and ease of preparation are a definite plus.  Just the right thing on a cool fall day.  Enjoy!!

After scouring the internet for various andouille, I always come back to Aidells.  It's a little hard for me to find locally, so I am thrilled Amazon has it at a fair price.  When it's on sale I pay $5.99.  Makes the best jambalaya - everyone raves and I get all the credit.  Super just grilled too.  And gumbo, oh the gumbo! yum.

Though it's now out of vogue, I'm still a fan of a healthy version of the low carb Atkins style diet. This is the perfect meal bar for that diet (probably great for South Beach, too). It is delicious, the peanut butter is creamy, and the chocolate on the outside is superb. I've used the Atkins bars for years, and they taste of chemicals and artificial sweetners. These Think Think bars, though, are practically candy bars. They have low net carbs (2 for this version, I think). Even when I'm not dieting, I still love this bar. It isn't a large, filling bar, and I can't really eat one to replace a meal, but if you're looking for a snack to cut between meals, or just a desert to eat with a nice cup of coffee at night, this is the bar for you.

This price on Amazon can't be beat, either. I pay about $1.7 per bar at Trader Joes, 2.20 a bar at the local megamart (when they have them in stock), and only about a buck fifty here on Amazon. Great deal. I was kind of sketchy ordering food online (though I order everything eles online), but Amazon grocery proved me wrong. Give 'em a try.
This bar was recommended by my strength and conditioning coach.  It tastes great and ingredients are very good.

Summary: Can't belive these are gluetin free
Text: I have tried so many Gluetin Free products and a lot of them do not taste all that great.  These bars are awesome!  In fact, I can't keep my kids out of them and I am constantly reordering.

Summary: Love these bars, but NOT from this seller
Text: I love love love these bars, but was VERY DISAPPOINTED when they arrived. The bars were NOT expired but had the appearance that they were. I ordered 2 boxes of the Creamy Peanut Butter because it is my favorite, but I will NOT order again from this seller. was definitely looking forward to getting this and ended up being disappointed! i ordered this because i was trying to find the exact saf-t pops i had when i was a kid but it tasted weird.

Summary: These kick Oreos in the Behind
Text: I'm not sure what "Hipcat 21" is referring to, but the Tim Tams I just ate from Australia would be pretty darn hard to suck milk through. They are a layered wafer cookie, and you'd have to have the suction of a Hoover vacuum to pull milk through those babies. But, they are amazing little pieces of heaven, even if completely worthless as a straw. They are crispy, and chocolaty, and so darned good that I would gladly give up my Double Stuff Oreos if these were widely sold in the US. Those lucky Australians!!

Summary: Tastes Like Something, But Not Sweet and Sour Sauce
Text: I bought Kraft Sweet and Sour Sauce, and was completely disappointed with how it tasted.  I have never had a mouth full of toilet cleaner, but this is what I would imagine it tasting like.  Very strong chemical taste with a very gelatinous plastic-like texture, highlighted in a dull orange-brown.  I looked at the ingredients and the main ingredient is High Fructose Corn Syrup, a healthy dose of cornstarch, and some oleoresin paprika mixed in.  I found the taste to be so horrible, I threw the rest of the container away.  Yuck!

THIS PRODUCT IS VERY GOOD.  IT MAKES A PERFECT LIGHT LUNCH AT HOME OR AT WORK WHEREVER THERE IS A MICROWAVE.  THIS IS NOT SALTY HAS JUST ENOUGH MEAT AND POTATOES WITH GRAVY TO MAKE YOU SATISFIED BUT NOT OVERLY FULL.  I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS TO ANYONE.

Summary: Not What It Used To Be
Text: I don't understand the positive reviews of this particular dinner.  It used to be my favorite, lean roast beef, creamy potatoes and good gravy.  But it's not what it used to be--the meat is still ok, but the potatoes are now a  solid pasty blob.  You have to break them down with a fork, and there's not enough gravy to do it.  In my opinion these are now inedible.  Try the chicken with mashed potatoes and gravy instead--the potatoes aren't as awful and there's plenty of gravy.

Summary: Salty and offputting aftertaste to the gravy
Text:
The box art always makes packaged food look so delicious, but this is basically a thin slice of processed beef on top of a bed of mashed potatoes. The potatoes are very dense and not at all fluffy like the photo, but did have a substantial and hearty texture to it. It was sort of a solid block of potatoes at the bottom of the bowl and I had to break it apart with the fork. I've uploaded a photo to show you what the actual product looks out.

Preparation is easy. Just poke some holes in the top and put it in the microwave for 1-1.5 mins. The texture of the beef and potato is about what I'd expect from processed food, but the gravy was very off-putting and didn't taste right. My dish was well before the expiration date of 12/06/12, but had a funny and unpleasant sour aftertaste to it. Sodium content is moderate at 830 mg (35% daily value) and tastes overly salty.

I will not be buying this particular variety again. It just doesn't taste good.

Text: These are hot or miss with my little one. Sometimes she likes them, sometimes she doesn't. I wish that they were in a resealable bag though, as soon as open them you have to transfer them to another type of storage to keep them fresh.

Be careful not to use too much, I only use about 5 drops in a bowl of yogurt.

Summary: Excellent food, big hit with the dog...
Text:
I bought these on sale and was hoping my dog would like them as much as he does the stella and chewy's freeze-dried. He absolutely does. And I love freeze-dried raw too, b/c the ingredients are all natural, less processed, teriffic ingredients and always a huge hit with the pup.

I feed them re-hydrated, which imo is the only way to feed when as part of or a whole meal (as opposed to tiny bits at a time for treats). I can't remember if it says it on the Nutrisca packaging, but on Stella and Chewy's packaging they make a point to write: "Your pet should consume 1/4 cup of water per patty daily". So it's easier for me to rehydrate so that my dog can start to get the amount of extra water he will need (does that make sense? lol). I just put a few patties (my dog is 8lbs) in a bowl, fill with water, wait 1 or 2 mins then take them out and break them up and put them in his dish. My dog dives in then seconds later looks to me for more. They must be yum yum yum indeed.

Anyway, of course i would not feed my dog these freeze dried dinner bites for his complete diet, they're just too expensive for that, but i do make a point to make his diet about 20+% raw, whether that is freeze-dried, air-dried (like Ziwipeak) or frozen raw. This way he gets some less processed food in his diet complete with the meat, bone and organs that is part of a dog's ancestrial diet.

The difference btwn these freeze-dried patties and S&C's is fairly minimal. The biggest difference for me is that the Stella/Chewy Freeze Dried re-hydrate much faster, which i prefer. Biggest difference ingredient wise that i can see are the probiotics in the S&C, and a slight difference in the protein to fat ratio. So even though i slightly prefer the S&C b/c of the fast re-hydrating, i would be happy buying whichever is less expensive at the time.

I have searched high and low (no pun intended) for a convenient snack bar that tastes great and does not spike blood sugar. I cannot tolerate Aspartame, Splenda or any of the other artificial sweeteners out there and trying to find products that have stevia or agave nectar are not that easy (and those I've found have honestly not been that great).

These chocolate bars have a wonderful, chewy texture and they taste (to me)like a regular candy bar. Although the other members of my family are not bound by the same dietary restrictions, they LOVED these bars. I can tell they are going to be the treats of choice in my house. I can't wait to try the other flavors.

Excellent bar with great taste and I love the fact of low glycemic. The chocolate tastes like chocolate and not chalky like other items I have tried.

Summary: Bold, Espresso Coffee with clean finish
Text: This is a bold cup of coffee--very Italian: dark, sensuous, and free of the smoky aftertaste that usually plagues espresso coffees. A nice 6 oz. coffee cup to enjoy with some frothy half and half and a first-rate homemade biscotti.
The item arrived very quickly as described and it was fresh, with aa expiration date that was a year out.

They are purposely cooked a little too long, giving them a wonderful burnt flavor.  If you like burnt pretzels or burnt French bread, you will love these!  And the texture is crisp, without being hard.  Only problem is that you have to order a whole case.

After loving Nutiva's coconut oil (great coconutty flavor and SO healthy for you!) I wanted to try the coconut manna. So I bought it and I LOVE it! It's got kind of a peanut butter consistency. It is so delicious! I take the whole jar and just grab a spoon and snack on it while watching tv or any other excuse I can find to eat it. It's a great healthy and tasty snack. I highly recommend it! YUM!

I should add that I am low carbing, so this tastes sweet to me, but may not to someone who eats sugary foods regularly...

I mixed this coffee with some regular coffee and it made a super treat for an early morning coffee. This flavor is so good. I will order some more. To me a lot of regular coffee seems a bit bitter and adding a flavoring makes it a treat.
This product was no better than the less expensive panettone I purchased at Sam's Club.

This rum flavoring is not as tasty as the Butterfly brand Rum essence that I bought in Indonesia. Dr. Oetker's Rum Essence is strong, but not as truly flavorful. The shipping cost on it was equal to the price of the little bottle. Not worth it, in my opinion.
I usually buy rice from indian grocery stores and this was my first time buying it from amazon. I really loved the India Gate Brand it is a bit pricy than other brands but it surely tastes good.

Summary: Slow to cook but great quality
Text: Can be a little annoying to cook on a pot because it takes more than the usual 30 minutes of simmering but the quality of the rice is great and 10lb for $15 is a great deal.

I have been trying many Basmati Rice in order to find the best taste and texture and I am terribly disappointed by this India Gate rice which tastes AWFUL ! like the bag that contains it. I have a dog who is to say the least, a monster chewer. I'm not sure why, because he's half cocker spaniel, and half shih tzu, Not exactly what you would think a chewer would be made of, but he is honestly a MONSTER. My suggestion would be to buy from Amazon, because at pet stores (like petsmart and petco), this thing is more expensive. I would recommend you give it a shot if you have a powerful chewer on your hands!

My strong chewer usually destroys all her toys, but this ring has lasted! She chewed through one part of it within a day or two making it more of a C-shape, but she's had it for almost a year now and she carries it around with her everywhere. She loves this toy and it is really durable!

Summary: If you love your pet, feed them Before Grain
Text:
After watching the documentary "Food Inc" I myself decided to eat only grass fed meat. Animals such as cows and pigs have a very difficult time processing grains especially corn. I didn't think about it before, but why would I feed my Daisy the food I am trying so hard to avoid? The other brands such as Iams is filled with corn. If the the bag says chicken, it should really say: grains with a dash of chicken.

Daisy is a Siamese and she just recently finished her 6lb bag and what a difference! Her coat is super silky, she has a leaner "sexier" figure. And she loves the dry food! Before BG she would only eat her dry food as a last resort if we didn't give her wet food. Now she chooses BG over the wet food. The best part is that her poop doesn't smell as bad as it used to. She literally begs for BG every morning and then again at night. She loves it. It may cost more than regular cat food, but think about what you are paying for. Regular cat food is just grains and you should only pay a dollar per bag. The first ingredient in BG is chicken then followed by veggies and fruits.

If you love your pet and want to give them the nutrition they deserve, definitely without a doubt feed them Before Grain.

Summary: Not Too Bad, Not Too Great, Either
Text: Haribo Happy Cola Gummi Candies are decent for fans of gummies like myself.  I've tried everything from gummi bears to gummi sharks to gummi toes, but gummi cola has a rather strange flavor. Summary: Tasty and better for you than a candy bar, but...
Text:
These are an excellent substitute for a candy bar or a cookie--- they have protein and fiber, and the good stuff like anti-oxidants that come along with the whole plant foods they're made of. They taste pretty good, have nice crunchy nuts, won't crumb all over your car or shirtfront, and aren't so chewy your jaw aches and you worry about your dental work--in fact, they are not overly chewy at all--more soft and slightly gooey--just enough to stick the stuff together-- than chewy like caramel. They also have about two thirds of the calories of a regular candy bar, but with the fiber and protein, may well keep you satisfied at least as long!

They do have quite a bit of sugar compared with the healthier snacks dietitians love, like peanut butter on whole wheat crackers (although for 140 calories, you wouldn't get much of those), or an apple and a piece of string cheese (again, more calories, but probably better for you). For shelf-stable, portable, grab-and-go, these are pretty healthy, all things considered.

Summary: I'm a fan.  Get your citrus here.
Text:
It took me a while to warm up to the idea of buying freeze dried fruit in individual serving bags. Brothers helped me overcome that. The fruit needs to be in the individual packaging to keep the humidity out so they stay crisp. I found the mandarin orange crisps delightful. The texture of freeze dried fruit in general takes a little time to get used to. These are sort of like a cheese puff in mouth feel, but entirely different in taste. They explode with a sweet/ tart flavor.

If you buy fresh fruit and it spoils before you eat it, or if you run out and need an alternative to canned or frozen fruit, this is a great alternative. Price an orange some time. While these cost more than a piece of fresh fruit, they are not too far off. Don't let the price per ounce fool you. You are not paying for the water content that makes up most of the weight of fresh. Compare by serving size. Grab a glass of tap water and a bag of these and you're on. I also like the pineapple, cinnamon apple and banana flavors. The berry flavors have a seed problem in my opinion so I skip them.

Summary: One of the longer lasting chew toys
Text:
I picked up the medium size bone for my miniature schnauzer (not realizing that there was also a small and large size as well) and overall I'm pretty impressed, but not amazed.

The nylon bone threads through the tough rubber ball and is secured by simply screwing one end into place over the other. You can fit one treat on each end as shown (for a total of two) in the picture or opt to have just one treat.

Overall the profuct is very durable. My schnauzer has an unusually strong jaw for his size, and most chew toys don't last long enough to justify their costs. However, the Busy Buddy does stand up very well and my dog really enjoys the gnawhide treats that come with it. It's relatively easy to clean and I don't really woryy about any choking hazards here.

However, the size of the bone in relative size to the ball doesn't really make for any decent 'bouncing' as the name suggests. It more or less 'rolls', not bounce. And I was a bit disapointed it only came with 6 treats to start with. Though you can buy refill packs with 24 discs, I think the initial outing should come with at least 10 or 12.

The discs themselves do indeed last a bit. Probably because of their placement within the toy itself, it may help add time that it takes yoru dog to enjoy these, giving an impression it lasts longer than other chew toys. But my schnauzer really does enjoy the treats. They have a rich smokey/meaty smell and will keep his attention for some time.

Overall I recommend this product.

My Vizsla puppy was given this toy and had absolutely no interest in it. But that is not even why this Toy is junk.
One afternoon in an attempt to get him to play with it, I tossed it towards him and the bone literally smashed into pieces. The only part salvaged from this toy was the rubber ball center. Which I now occasionally fill with peanut butter and he really love that. What a complete waste of money, it lasted one week. And he never even played with it.

My dogs absolutely love this toy!  Even after they have devoured the treats that go on the ends, they gnaw on them for hours.  I have used one for almost a year now and it is still holding up well... even under a large dogs teeth!  I would recommend this for anyone with a dog who loves to chew.

Summary: designed for a very tiny dog
Text: Just received this item & I was shocked at how tiny it was. The size should be described as mini. In fact, they should state the dimensions in the product description. The small size is 3 1/2" long & the "gnawhides" are 1/8" thick, 1" wide. Have a 14 week old Cairn (weighs 6 lbs.) that is a very active chewer & he'd probably try to swallow this thing whole. It would take him longer to chew his dog food than it would one of the rawhide rings. I know dog toys aren't cheap (if you're buying them all the time) but the price for this size bone ($7.73) is ridiculous to me. Especially when you add to that the cost of the refills. This toy would have been great for my Pom when she was a baby: she weighed 2 lbs. at 3 months. But for a "small" dog? Guess my idea of small is way different. Rated this item 2 stars only because it arrived quickly.

Summary: Both my dogs love this toy!
Text:
I have two dogs - a one year old WestiePoo and a 12 year old Bichon - they fight over this toy. It is very sturdy and they love the fact that there is rawhide to eat also.
It definately keeps them busy and occupied.
My wife and I really like this coffee. Not too strong but still reasonable with good flavor.  It's become our default chocolate coffee.

COOL LITTLE SPINNY THING, ITS NICE TO HAVE ON THE COUNTER & doesn't take up much space. very glad i bought it to go with my k cups
These taste like soft peanut butter chocolate ship cookies and is amazing. Great for those looking to decrease grain intake.

I've been brewing coffee manually for many years, using a plastic cone filter holder. I recently switched to this porcelain filter holder, and it really brings out a huge improvement in the taste. The porcelain conducts the heat better and eliminates any kind of plastic taste. With the cap on, the coffee stays warm for about an hour.

Two complaints: the #4 paper filters are a bit too small; you can actually use a #6 filter. Also, there is only one hole in the filter holder, so brewing can be a bit slow sometimes, and when I do try to rush things, there is sometimes clogging which requires my adjusting the filter a bit.

But this porcelain filter holder does produce the best coffee I've ever had at home, a coffeehouse, or a restaurant. With coffee, lo-tech and slow-brewed is always the best way to go.

The design of this product is fatally flawed. Notice on all manual drip coffee makers the ridges on the sides and around the hole. This keeps the filter just far enough away from the filter to let coffee flow. This one has ridges, but they are pathetic. If fact, it would be impossible to create deep enough ridges out of porcelain to do the job. The result is a drip filter that takes FOREVER to flow, to the point of being unusable. You can stick something in the base to break the seal of the filter with the sides, and that helps, but what a pain. I can't believe Melita keeps this thing on the market. They must not test their products. It's very frustrating.

Summary: bit o honey goes a long long way.....etc
Text: bit oh honey is a gluten free candy, not that that matters unless you have celiac disease which i do now but when i was a youngun i loved bit of honey and now still do

My husband actually ordered this for me. I had wanted one for awhile but panicked when I found out he ordered it. I live in MN and we have snow on the ground. Its very cold here. I thought for SURE this tree would arrive dead.

I was very wrong. This tree is beautiful! it was packed perfectly and it got here safe and sound. Not a single leaf has fallen off this tree! I was worried that it would be bone dry and dying for water when it got here and I was wrong again. They had the roots wrapped in plastic and the soil was nice and moist. I LOVED the ceramic pot it came in. Beautiful. I couldn't be more pleased. The shape of the tree is also amazing. It is very twisted, unique, and beautiful. Everyone compliments my new tree!

I have set it up with a plant light bulb in a desk lamp and set it in a humidity tray. Its just a tray with rocks for decoration and water poured over them so that as the water evaporates it gives my tree some humidity in this dry house. I look forward to many years with my new tree.

EDIT:
I bought another one for my mom for mother's day and it was fantastic! She was so happy with it! I noticed a fungus gnat flying around it, which hopefully won't turn into a problem.

EDIT: it is over a year later and these trees are still alive.

I don't normally give a review on the condition of an item as it arrives from shipping much less one I gave as a gift, but I simply must pass this on.

I bought the ficus from Brussel's Bonsai. It being a tree, I wondered if the tree would make it to my mom in one piece. Well, my mom called me today. She just got the tree and she is thrilled beyond belief. She said it arrived in absolutely perfect condition, as if someone had hand delivered it. She still can't get over how it was possible. She said it arrived in a huge box, but it was just a little tree and it looked perfect. They had packed it so well. I told her to send it back if there's anything wrong with it, but she said no, it is PERFECT. Knowing my mom, she would have told me if it wasn't.

UPDATE: I've had three trees sent as gifts to family and they have been an absolute hit! Usually, I get a nice, polite thank you; but this time it is call after call from people who are at a loss for words, just like my mom. Rarely does a present garner so much positive feedback. Thank you, Amazon!

I sent this as a gift, and it arrived with lightening speed, in perfect condition.  The only negative was that my recipient mentioned there was no tray under the plant,and usually plants come on a decent little tray.  A detail, but you need to know when ordering. Otherwise we both very happy with the plant.  I would definitely order more plants from Amazon again.

Brussel's Golden Gate Ficus Indoor Bonsai Tree

I am really satisfied with the tree. I always thought these would be a bit more expensive. Like nearly all plants needs light, inderect outside shady best, inside near window probably good.

Summary: Doesn't look like the same type of ficus in the picture...
Text: A good price on this tree.  But I was disappointed when it arrived.  The trunk was awful--it was very bulbous/tuberous, and huge compared to the leaf portion.  Just ugly.  I called Brussel's directly and explained that I wasn't sure I had even received the same type of ficus I ordered.  They promised to call me back, but didn't. Didn't get a response, but the replacement plant was much the same.  The roots/trunk were less bulbous and more compatible with the overall size of the tree. The tree arived perfectly packed in a box filled with styrofoam peanuts.
The base was wrapped in a plastic bag and nestled in a styrofoam cutout that kept it secure and upright.

After much anticipation I ordered the three main Jamon Ham products: Iberico de Bellota, Iberico de Bellota Paleta, & Jamon Serrano.

Being used to Proscuitto (Parma) and loving it by itself and in many dishes, I had high expectations. If you haven't had good proscuitto, then there isn't really anything to compare the Jamon product to. The chopped stuff at your everyday grocery store is good for a little salty proscuitto like flavor in dishes but not for slices just to enjoy.

I understand why people think Jamon is awesome, but the melting in your mouth with extreme grease/fat over your lips and fingers really sets home the fat content more than that Kobe Beef flavor burst and easier swallow.

In the high end Jamon, you can really taste the acorns in the meat. The nuttiness really comes through and it is very good. The Iberico Paleta -> you don't get the nuttiness and it's a little tougher. The Serrano really has much more meat and I preferred the flavor profile on it more than the other two.

While I would rate the Iberico Bellato around 4 out of 5 stars (minus 1 for the heavy greasy feeling and fat), the price is ridiculous. I would say it would be appropriately priced around $15-25/pound. Given that is 4-6x lower than it's actual price, I had to take at least 2 stars from the product.

You're better off with the SM Proscuitto. It's delicious and you get 4x the amount without the heavy grease.

I ordered these green tea chewy candies a few months ago, and I'm definitely going to order a bunch more! They are soft & chewy, (not too chewy though!) & creamy, and taste like green tea ice cream! Delicious!

Yes it is different and way better.  This the Nutella that I know and it is FANTASTIC, it's a product of Poland so im not sure what the ingredients are or what exactly makes it different but I love it and will order again.

I love Betty Crocker GF mixes, so I had high hopes for this one. Unfortunately, I found it to have kind of an odd aftertaste, and the cookies just didn't hold together for me at all. I tried it using crisco grease, then again tried it using butter, then even tried it using cooking oil, but the cookies just spread out too thin no matter what I did. I tried removing them from the parchment paper warm and removing them completely cooled -- no difference. They just fall apart.  Makes a good ice cream topping, or great for using as a creative decoration on top of a birthday cake, though.

I am definitely going to buy these again. The taste was on par for non-gluten boxed cookie mixes, if a bit crumbly in texture. My very picky gluten eating kids loved the cookies and said they would eat them again.

A couple of notes on making them. First, I added about a 1/2 teaspoon extra of vanilla, about a 1/2 tsp of additional water. The extra fluid made the cookie dough more pliable and allowed me to use my cookie scoop. The vanilla flavor was excellent in the baked cookies. I ended up with about 2 dozen cookies using my larger cookie scoop. I made the 1st dozen using my silpat - and the cookies did NOT turn out at all. They were not cooked properly and they didn't brown up at the edges. I made the 2nd dozen using parchment paper and they turned out great! They spread nicely and browned up beautifully at the edges. So, next time, no silpat - parchment paper only!

Summary: So good! and dairy free, too!
Text: I LOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOVED these cookies!  I made them with non-dairy margarine and they turned out fine. They are delicate, but so many gluten-free things are. I would definitely get again (and am going to)

Summary: Not as Good as Cola or Root Beer Flavors
Text:
This is the first Zevia flavor I got to try. I didn't really want it but it was all Amazon had in stock and ready to ship for Prime members (more on that later). I was so eager to try it I popped a can open right when I got it in the house. My initial thought was that it was gross but I thought I could get used to it by the time I get through the entire case. My wife tried it at room temperature and she hated it. She didn't touch anymore orange or the black cherry I got later because of that first taste. She's since had some nice cold root beer and cola Zevia which she was impressed with. My nearly three year old son also had a taste test of the orange flavor. He's not a soda drinker so maybe that had something to do with his reaction. He drank about an 1/8 of a can which surprisingly all came back up on my kitchen floor about two minutes after he drank it. He said he didn't like it. Ha. Out of the four flavors of Zevia, orange is my least favorite. I will not be ordering it again due in part to its taste, which I would say is okay, but also the price for it. I am willing to pay the price for now for a couple of the other flavors, but not orange.

There are two major problems with ordering Zevia products. First, they're expensive. At just over a dollar a can they are pricey, no other way to describe it. The second, is availability. Amazon is really having some issues with keeping Zevia flavors in stock with Prime shipping. The third party sellers all have exuberant shipping prices bringing your case of soda to over fifty dollars. I've emailed Zevia about this and did get a response from them. I hope Amazon can keep it stocked and Zevia can keep them supplied. It's a good product but it's been frustrating trying to order due to Amazon's stock. Due to the high price tag I put it on a monthly schedule to save 15%. It helps but I wonder if Amazon will have it ready to go each month.

The Zevia Orange is an okay tasting soda. I will not be purchasing any more of it even if it's all Amazon Prime has in stock.

I have tried a few of the Zevias and this orange one is really pretty good and refreshing if you don't want to give up your sodas because of all the unhealthy things in them, especially aspartame and high fructose corn syrup.  This one is sweetened with stevia.  Highly recommended!

You can bet we'll be buying our Shitakes here from now on!

- Gail Cooke

Summary: My Favorite CBTL Espresso - Highly Recommended
Text:
This CBTL Italian Espresso is my favorite beverage out of our CBTL Kaldi S04 Single Cup Brewer, White/Silver. This is a "bold" espresso that has a very strong flavor that is preferred by both my son and me but my wife does not like as much as the smoother CBTL Continental Espresso Capsules By The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf, 10-Count Box (Pack of 3) (which is also good).

Highly Recommended!

CFH

This is my absolute favorite of all the espresso flavors sold by The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf Company! I must confess, however, that I don't make or serve it as espresso. I put the capsule in my Kaldi S04 Single Cup Brewer, Red and push the button for brewed coffee and that gives me the perfect strength when diluted like that. While the brewer is working, I use the CBTL LM-145P Milk Frother, Black to prepare my milk. When that is done I add a packet of the CBTL vanilla flavored powder and whisk it. HEAVENLY! This has a very smooth flavor, their darkest roast - and is a great way to start my day without having to go to a coffee house and pay those high prices. If I don't have extra time or am in a hurry, I don't use the frother; I just add my favorite creamer to the hot espresso -- I prefer the International Delight Coffee Creamer, Caramel Macchiato, 24 Ct (Pack of 4).

The capsules are about 60¢ each when you order through the amazon subscription service or you can buy directly from the online website of the Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf company using their premium club and thus save on shipping. I do hope that these capsules will be available in my local grocery stores to make it more convenient for purchase.

The CBTL single cup brewer, the CBTL milk frother, and this Italian Espresso used in combination make great coffee. You can experiment with all the different flavors and find the one you like best. You can make coffee drinks just as good as any barista!

Summary: Addicting but don't eat too many
Text: These are delicious.  They don't taste sugar-free at all.  You can't eat too many or you'll be plagued with flatulence for the rest of the day, but still worth it.  My only complaint is that they are on the pricey side.

A few years ago Friskies produced a similar "meat & gravy" product which I quickly bought.  My five cats refused to eat it, just licked the gravy.  When I spotted this new product, I decided to try it once more.  It was A HUGE SUCCESS!!!!  My five cats loved it from the first bite and actually licked their dishes clean, all varieties.  I highly recommend it to anyone who might have had a similar experience with the original product.  I will continue to buy it as long as it is available.  Thank you, Friskies!
I've tried less expensive canned food similar to this and even the stray cats snub them. Friskies is the best quality product for a good value.

The cats love this stuff. Full of gravy, which they all love. Good variety of flavours, or so I can guess by the cats telling me they want wet food. Haven't tried it myself :) Great price. Will definitely be buying this again.

I have tried different brands of grits and find this one to be the very best. Even though they are quick cooking grits, you can cook them as long as you need to. Their flavor is also better. I would buy again. My favorite recipe is: Creamy Grits-2tbs salted butter or 2tbs unsalted butter +1/4 tsp salt. 2 cups water,1/2 c stone ground grits. 1-2 c milk, half n half or stock.Drop the butter into water,bring to boil.Stir in grits, return to boil & reduce heat. cook 10 min. or until thick,stirring to prevent sticking.Add about 1/2 cup milk or cream, simmer 10 min. As the liquid evaporates add more milk until its the consistency you want. Can cook up to an hour. Wonderful. recipe from hoppin' John's low country cooking.

Previous reviewes told of the mess involved with these, they obviously have not had freeze dried fruit before. Wether it is blueberries, strawberries, lychees or any other fruit, you will have a bit of a mess from the product. Get over it! Wash your hands, brush your teeth. Now for the item at hand, Blueberries. Typical freeze dried berries with good taste and that wonderful powder! Can not be improved.
Apples and strawberries were crunchy and satisfying.  Pears were chewy and suspect as we were expecting crunchy.. Support from company was ok as they replaced however replacement pears still soft.

That brings me to my recommendation for you to order two boxes, because I just put in an order for a box for my wife. She will be pleased.

Also, try the other flavors, I love the pineapple. I was able to buy this set with a coupon that made them a real bargain.
These are so good, and worth the money.  Everyone in your family will love this.  Good alternative to chips, or other snacky junk food.

Text:
