Most health-conscious adults know the importance of the combination of B-Complex Vitamins with C; yet, we also realize that our B6, B12, and C are water soluble vitamins-- meaning that whatever is not metabolized in our systems is lost in our unused fluids, whether it be by urination or perspiration. Some compensate for this loss through time-release vitamins, but there is a concern from some that certain time-release vitamins are not as natural as other forms, not as effective, or not as easily assimilated.

Ambrosoli-Honees honey-filled Energy Plus drop provides a tasty and effective alternative to time-release, as well as a natural alternative to the acrid potency of recent caffeine energy drinks.

The hard candy exterior is delicious and not so hard that you cannot easily chew one or two up and get to the even more delicious honey center. I weigh well over 225 lbs. so I didn't seem to have the kind of energy surge from only one drop; but two or three drops at my weight allowed me to notice a bit of alertness and energy when my energy levels would have otherwise dropped off. That put me up to about 60 calories at 20 calories per drop; yet, with the energy boost received from the three drops, I know that my activity more than compensated for the caloric intake.

One down side to the honey drops is that they may not store too well for long periods of time because the honey might seep through the end of the hard candy leaving you with a sticky wrapper. For me it wasn't really a bother at all because you're going to get something a little sticky any time you use real honey.

Summary: It has 202 cals and 53 carbs per cup. Great sweetener, but their marketing is misleading!
Text:
I like this sweetener a lot. But it is not a NO sweetener like the label claims, it is a LOW calorie sweetener when you do the math.

The company says on their website that are 202 calories and 53 grams of carbs for a cup of Ideal. So it is 12.5 cals/3.3 carbs a tablespoon, and 4 cals/1.1 carbs a teaspoon. So not an actual NO calorie sweetener like the bag says. They list 0 calories because they can since it is under 5 calories for the serving size they have listed, but on a large pouch meant for baking you would use way more than a teaspoon -- especially if you wanted to make any of the sweet items they have pictured on the front of the bag! The label should be changed to reflect its intended purpose. It's like saying a can of regular soda is calorie free if you list it as being 42 servings.

That said, I will still be using it since it has less than a third of the calories of sugar, about a quarter of the carbs and tastes very good. Their shady lack of disclosure on the bag leaves a bad taste in my mouth. But while it's not a no calorie sweetener, but it is pretty close to ideal.

Summary: A lot more convenient than a communal dipping dish

I frequently entertain guests who enjoy my cooking, Many of my guests have some to enjoy an dipping sauce for their bread, so I set the table with these.

While some restaurants that bring out a bread and a dipping sauce use a communal dish, I prefer to allow my guests to have more control over their sauce. Each guest gets one of these saucers, and I place the following on the table for their own mixing: a high quality olive oil, Alessi Dipping Spice Grinder, 0.76-Ounce (Pack of 6), Alessi Whole Mix Peppercorns, 1.12-Ounce Grinder (Pack of 6) and Alessi Grinder Sea Salt, 5.64-Ounce (Pack of 6). For those who love to mix in basalmic vinegar I have a special treat awaiting them on the table: Gia Russa Balsamic Glaze.

Another way I use these is when I am measuring out spices for some dishes. I will measure out each spice into one or more of these saucers and mix them before adding them to whichever dish I am preparing. This prevents accidentally over spicing the meal because you can always pour too much spice back into its container a lot easier than removing it from a boiling pot!

The saucers are heavy duty (I love their heft), easy to care for and convenient. I have always cleaned mine in a dishwasher with no adverse effects, so I am reasonably certain that they are dishwasher-safe.

I usually do not entertain more than three people for dinners, so this pack is more than adequate for me. If you are used to larger parties, by additional packs.

I tried this product in a desperate hope of finding a cleaner, no smell alternative to pee pads and the potty patch.

I have a 6 month old pomeranian puppy and love her dearly. When she first came at 2 months, I tried using the "Potty Patch" - the faux grass thing you can buy at Petco. My brother, who also has a pomeranian, loves the Potty Patch - one key difference - he lives in a house and I live in an apartment.

The Potty Patch gets pretty nasty after a few days, no matter how good you are at picking up poop without smearing it. It also smells after a month, no matter how much you clean it. Also, living in an apartment, I had no place to clean it outside, so my only options were my shower/bathtub or a sink. For germ-phobes like myself, these are not options at all (I'm not even that bad of a germ phobe). There is also the problem of finding a place to "hang" the faux grass so that it dries effectively but doesn't drip all over the floor. The whole process was not fun at all - carrying the bin to dump the pee, etc. etc.

I then tried pee pads, which are much cleaner because like diapers, after use, you throw it out. However, some cons are that unless your dog pees right in the middle of the pad, some pee seeps onto the floor - leaving you to have to clean constantly. My dog also refuses to use the pee pad "economically" - that is, if there is a clean spot on the pad which already has been used, she won't go - I have to put a new one down. This gets costly as my dog pees at least five times a day. There is also the smell issue - even though I bought the pricier pads.

So I tried Purina dog litter. I couldn't find any dog litter pans (checked internet as well) so I bought a carrier case and used the bottom part as the pan - the carrier case is good because the bottom part has sides and a low entry way for the dog - something cat litter boxes do not have. At first I only put a little of the litter in the box but my dog would slide all around in it. I put a lot more (about an inch) and she no longer slid all over (she is 4.2 pounds fyi). Once she peed a few times, it helped keep the pieces in place better, too - in part because the litter bits get a little bigger with liquid and they get less "shiny" - I think the shine comes from something in the litter bits that helps keep its shape or helps control odor.

There is no smell either - so I can leave it for a week and then change the pellets out. Because its in the pan, no pee on the ground. A couple of pellets do fall out occasionally when my dog exists the pan, but it's not a big deal. My dog is still not trained to go poop in it, so I don't have any first hand knowledge of how that works, but I imagine it shouldn't be a problem and I will get a scooper to scoop those sections out.

I think one of the cons is that the bag is kind of big (for an apartment) and dogs may take some time getting used to it (they may not be used to stepping onto a non-smooth surface). However, I am a fan and will continue to use it.

Summary: Great Substitute for Pilot Crackers, great with Chowder!
Text:
Since they stopped making Crown Pilot crackers I was unable to find a decent substitute till now. These crackers are great for thickening Clam Chowder, at least that is what we use them for ..Rhode Island "Rocky Point" Clam chowder. Heres the recipe...

Rocky Point-Style Clam Chowder

1/4 pound salt pork, minced fine
3 medium onions
1 garlic clove
Old Bay Seasoning, (optional)
1 quart quahog or clam juice
Water about 1 cup or more-taste the broth first to see if it needs any at all.
2 pints shucked quahogs cut up small or 1 pint clams and 1 pint quahogs
About 5 medium potatoes cut into small cubes, old potatoes are best
Pilot crackers or crushed up oyster crackers about 1/2- 3/4 cup or as needed to thicken
1 can tomato soup or tomato sauce
Black pepper

1. In a medium pot, fry the salt pork till browned well.

2. Throw in the onions and garlic and cook until translucent. You can, if you like, add a teaspoon of Old Bay Seasoning.

3. Add the clam juice and water. Bring to a simmer and add the quahogs or clams or or a mix of both, cook for 15 minutes.

4. Add the potatoes, cracker crumbs(put a a cup of broth into cracker crumbs, mix up and then add to pot so they don't clump up", tomato soup and simmer another 15 to 20 minutes till done. Stir it so the crackers disintegrate and thicken the chowder. Also break up a few of the potatoes, as that also thickens it nicely. Add pepper to taste.

5. Serve with clam cakes and more oyster crackers.

Text:

Well, the replacement came last week, and it was still the flatbread. I'm not going to bother to call Amazon again because I know it will just result in them sending me the flatbread once again.

Summary: A big winner - tasty and ultra crunchy
Text:
Just tried these for the first time - and they're a very nice snacking cracker. There's nothing I can compare them to because they're just unique. Their texture is very different from a ritz type, or saltine type cracker. These nut-thins have a MAJOR crunch - a snappy crunch - hard crunch - but still not a problem to bite down and chew since they're very thin. If you break one in half, you'll hear a clear snap. The flavor comes through as pleasantly nutty. Not necessarily an over-abundance of almond flavor, because the almond seems subtle to me, but I think the toasty rice must be the nutty flavor I get. There's a hint of a buttery flavor - and just a pleasant bit of saltiness not too much.

The ingredients list is fairly simple: Rice Flour, Almonds, Potato Starch, Salt, Expeller Pressed Safflower, Natural Almond Flavor, Butter Flavor (Contains Milk).

Health aspects: As a lactose intolerant person, I can tell you the "contains milk" has been no issue for me personally in these nut-thins - I am not getting a lactose reaction. I suspect the "milk" is mostly butter, and butter is something I never have issues with anyway. I would guess this product has no more lactose than lactose free milk - as the grams of sugar are listed as zero on the package for a serving. (The gov lets them list zero if it is below .5 grams I believe). If you're more severely affected than I am by lactose - you may still want to proceed with caution. As an ibs and acid reflux sufferer - I found this food totally neutral - no reactions - again this is my personal reaction. I'm not a doctor - so take that with a grain of salt. Also - the box notes this is a gluten free food - and the ingredients show no wheat.

So far I've been munching them plain - and they're really nice. But I can see where any topping: cheese, cream cheese, ham, etc. would be super on them. I'll buy them again for sure.

Enjoy!

In an Italian language class, I was told by a teaching assistant who lives in Italy that it is not at all difficult to find good gluten free pasta there, so I went in search of one I could purchase. I found a review of this Italian pasta online that was very favorable, so I thought... ok one more time I will try to find a decent pasta. My husband needs to be gluten free, not me, and I have SO missed good pasta. Well, wait no more.. this is it. Cooked precisely per the directions in a salty (like sea water) pot of water, topped with my homemade sauce and it is wonderful. Thank heavens!  I had almost given up on finding a decent gluten free pasta.

My wife has Celiacs and as a result I have been on a quest to find a pasta that she can eat and I enjoy. While gluten free will never be like semolina pasta, this comes really close.

It cooks well and does not suffer from what other gluten free pastas do, which is a very small window of just right. You can slightly under/overcook and you will still have an enjoyable meal.

Like regular pasta, save a small amount of the cooking water to toss the pasta with before your sauce or pesto.

This is solid with flavor.  I bought cans of grocery tuna and squeezed out the water and had half a can of ground up tuna in the can.  Grocery store tuna is now half water, but this comes in a chunk in the can with just juice from the tuna in the bottom. If you figure in the water, or lack thereof, this is about the same price per weight of the tuna itself as the grocery store tuna and you are not getting flaked garbage swimming in water!

I think a lot of this product. Very good flavor, not too strong, but distinct and with some depth. Good looking piece of fish, too. You know how some cheaper light tunas are kind of unappetizing. I don't eat a huge amount of canned tuna, but when I do, it's in a carefully constructed salad, and this tuna justifies the effort.

The real strong point is taste. I recently tried RainCoast solid albacore. Raincoast is specifically caught AND processed in the North Pacific and Canada. I suspect Wild Planet is caught and/or processed in Southeast Asia. Both are packed in plain tuna juices. After using used to Wild Planet skipjack, I found the albacore relatively tasteless. And the Wild Planet skipjack is mostly nearly "solid," close to the kind of cut you expect in "solid" tuna, rather than chunk. RainCoast doesn't offer any but albacore, so I'll stay with Wild Planet, currently the most environmentally attractive and well-packed product.

Summary: Tasty tuna, with sustainability thrown in for good measure!
Text:
Wild Planet Sustainably Caught Wild Skipjack Light Tuna:

- solid tuna steak, not flakes and small chunks

- no added water

- pole-caught or troll-caught, not long-line or purse seine

- greatly reduced bycatch

- lower mercury (smaller fish, less polluted part of ocean)... but how do you check?

- sometimes you can get it at about $2-$3 per 5 ounce can.

- tasty!

With Wild Planet Sustainably Caught Wild Skipjack Light Tuna, yes, it costs more, but still less than your grande latte. What IS it worth to eat low-mercury, bycatch-free tuna? You'd never think about paying $2-3 for 5 ounces of fine beef.

Summary: Best Salami I Have Ever Had
Text: I heard about the Pick Salami from a friend who is from Eastern Europe. He told me PICK is the king of all salami and he is right. It is not overly salty like most salami. It is like fine wine or aged cheese of salami.

My first mistake was ordering this during the summer. It did arrive in a timely fashion but it ends there. I could smell the salami before I even opened it and it didn't smell much like salami. The inside of the package was very greasy and the outside of the salami was really gross. You could see where the grease was oozing out of the ends. It smelt off, not like it was suppose to, and I know since I have had this salami before. I called the company that sold it and they kept telling me that it was fine, the heat made the grease come out and the smell was nothing. They hang salami up for months without refrigeration. After pressing him on this for about 20 min, he finally said that I could send it back at my cost, and they will check it to see if anything is wrong with it. If there is, than they will replace it but he doesn't think there is. To me, that sounds like throwing good money after bad money. So I'll be out more money and still not have a salami.
My hubby is the coffee person in our home and he thought the taste was excellent!  I would certainly purchase this item again for him.

Very salty for me, I will never get them again, I wish I knew it.
I gave them away to somebody.

This cheese proved to be exactly what I was looking for to make my special cheesecake. It's the closest thing to the old fashioned "smear case" that a person can find. Great texture and very little to no liquid. The taste is perfect for baking and no type of dry cottage cheese can compare.
Farmer Cheese 16oz (1lb)
This mango butter is very delicious.  It's smooth, creamy and goes great with ice cream.  I like it best right out the jar with a spoon.

I ordered these to have at a cross-cultural awareness session I did for graduate students. They are actually quite tasty and were a nice addition. Michael Adamovich

Summary: Convenient tasty butter flavor in packs for people on the go!
Text:
These smaller packets are so great to take with you, especially if you're intent on keeping your fat or carb intake at low levels. The product is tasty and rich in butter flavor when sprinkled on moist foods.
The other nice thing about these boxed packets is that they come with a handy little recipe sheet that in many cases also includes a coupon toward the purchase of a Butter Buds product. Highly recommended!

I don't know exactly when it was that I started buying grocery items on Amazon. It probably coincided with me getting hooked on WoW. I do recall, however, searching for Red Bull, and not finding it. Last month when I discovered I could order a case with S&S, not pay shipping, tax, or even deposit, I truly thought to my (lazy) self that prayers do get answered.

Those of you who are already hooked on Red Bull don't need convincing that this energy drink is as effective as it is delicious. Compared to the $5/16-ounce can price I pay at convenience stores, this is a bargain. And with Subscribe and Save, the case arrives (securely packed) to my home 2 days after I've ordered it.

For those people who've never tried Red Bull and wonder what it's like. It does not contain alcohol. It's perfectly carbonated, not too sweet, and has the cleanest flavor of any energy drink I've ever tried. It sort of tastes like carbonated fruit (grape-cranberry?) juice without the cloying sweetness. And it really does wake you up and help you feel energized.

Some people can't function in the morning until they've had their coffee. For me, it's Red Bull. And that goes double for a late-night-gaming session. All of the undead, trolls, witches, demons and dragons I have slain, all of the puzzles I've solved with GLaDOS nagging me, all of the raids I healed, all of the captives I have freed - well, I couldn't have logged into a game server or picked up a controller without this precious elixir.

I love you, Red Bull! And I love you, Amazon for bringing it to my doorstep just in time for Diablo III!!!

Summary: Terrific flavor and texture, a versatile pantry staple!
Text:
This has a kind of nutty flavor and a satisfying texture. It can easily work with a bit of salt and olive oil as a side dish or with a sauce as a base instead of rice or pasta. If you've never tried Couscous, it is SO easy to make! In fact, I just heat some water in a Pyrex measuring cup in the microwave. It gets to a boil between 2-3 minutes. Pour the dry couscous in a bowl (I've even used a coated paper bowl at work, so I can toss it afterward!) and just pour the hot water over it. Then just cover the bowl with a plate (paper or regular) and just let it sit for a few minutes. The water absorbs, just fluff with a fork, easy, done!

Summary: Glenny's Soy Crisps Creamy Ranch 1.3 oz.
Text: Very tasty soy crisps.  My nutritionist recommended that I eat these snacks rather than other unhealthy choices as part of a diabetic diet.  Ordering them monthly on the "Subscribe & Save" package is more economical.

Summary: Himalaya Shuddha Guggulu Cholesterol Regulator 60 Capsules
Text: This natural capsule is very easy to take and no after affects as in coming back up and having a foul taste in your mouth. Does not cause any type of heartburn and have lost a little weight wich is a good plus. Feeling great and more energy.

I drink this nearly every day, and have been for at least 5 years!  I'm not a fan of many chai teas, and have found no other brand to compare to this!  This blend has a perfect, deliciously sweet and spicy aroma (from coconut, which is subtle, and cinnammon, ginger, caradamom cloves, nutmeg, and black pepper), and full-bodied flavor incredibly without bitterness.  I don't find the taste to be too spicy or too sweet, though I think it's a rare breed in that it doesn't require sweetening.  I've shared this tea with many people, and there was only 1 who said she didn't care for it, which was simply due to her literal tastebuds.  As a sidenote, the most 2 recent tins I've bought at my supermarket in September 2011 (that have best by dates of Feb. 2014) taste and smell markedly different than older tins, reminding me of vinegar or something sour.  I e-mailed Zhena's Gypsy Tea asking whether they had changed the makeup or concoction of this blend, and they thankfully said no, so they must have been bad batches, which I've never before experienced!

I had never tried this brand of tea & there are not very many reviews on it. But recently they ran a $10 off promo so i snagged this flavor along with some of the regular white tea. It arrived yesterday & so far i have brewed 2 teapots with the same leaves. Not sure how a third steeping will go but the 2nd one was as strong as the first.

There are whole dried rosebuds mixed in with the tea, which consists of tightly rolled whole white and green tea leaves. (yes, there is green tea in this. it's not 100% white tea)

There appears to be very little if any (i don't see any) broken pieces or tea dust like i see in many of the loose leaf teas i have purchased in the past. This was a VERY nice surprise as usually a lot of little pieces of tea escape the strainer & end up in my tea cup. Well, not with this tea. :)

The packaging is cute, it comes in the pink tin pictured here. It has a metal lid that screws on/off. Inside there is another lid (made of flexible plastic) to help keep the tea fresh. This inner lid has a tab so that it can be easily removed.

The tea has a nice delicate flavor with a hint of jasmine in it. I'm not sure if i detect rosebuds in the flavor (hard to say....what do rosebuds taste like???) But they are definitely in there. While the jasmine is there it isn't real real strong. So if you prefer your jasmine tea to pack a punch this may not be for you. I really like a nice cup of strong jasmine green tea. Of course i realize that this is a white & green tea mix. Since white tea is much lighter & more delicate than green tea too much jasmine would probably overpower it. Strong jasmine flavor or not, this tea is yummy. All i know is that i enjoyed everything about brewing & drinking this tea. It is well packaged, has a pleasing aroma & flavor, and the leaves seem to be rolled with meticulous care. It's a great quality tea & a nice addition to my collection. I'm glad i bought it.

If you like good hot cereal & not the microwave 'quick oats' mush, you'll like this.  It has a nutty flavor that's especially good when mixed with old fashioned oatmeal (5Tbsp Oats to 3Tbsp Bob's, add hot H20 & microwave for 2 minutes...I add ~1Tbsp chopped walnuts & ~1Tbsp raisins).  It keeps me going till lunch.  I have not tried it by itself as I like to mix cereals whether hot or cold.

Summary: I really wanted to like it
Text:
I love cherries and cherry flavored things. I love Paramount Coffee Blueberry Muffin, Ground, 12-Ounce (Pack of 2) and drink it nearly daily. Given those two things, I ordered the Traverse City Cherry coffee, thinking I'd be just as pleased, if not more. Boy, was I disappointed.

I eagerly awaited the delivery and opened the package as soon as I got it into the kitchen. I opened one of the bags and was hit with a waft of artificial cherry scent. It reminded me of cherry licorice, mixed with coffee. Very unpleasant.

I let it sit for a day or two, thinking it might mellow with exposure to a little air. Also, I was honestly apprehensive about trying it after the first whiff. I just made a cup, using my Keurig brewer and an Ekobrew reusable K-cup, so I know the brewer wasn't the problem. My 5 year old daughter came into the kitchen, asking for licorice, because she could smell it. I had to tell her it was my coffee. I gingerly tasted it and it was actually worse than it smelled. It was a mix of cherry licorice and cough syrup. I added sugar, as I usually take my coffee with both sugar and cream. The sugar didn't help. I stopped short of adding the cream, convinced that it would make no difference in the hideously bitter, odd tasting coffee that I'd had such high hopes for.

I'm thoroughly disappointed, particularly because Amazon does not offer refunds on grocery items. I'm now stuck with three full bags of coffee that I won't drink, two of which are unopened. I'll stick to the Blueberry Muffin flavor from now on, which I recommend without reservation.

I am so elated about this bread!  I think it's actually better (taste & texture) than some breads that aren't gluten free.  The texture and flavor are both awesome.  I love it toasted.  I love that it is light and there are air pockets and it actually gets crispy in the toaster.  I don't know how they did this - I've been playing with gluten free recipes for about 6 years & haven't come close, but for me, this is the perfect bread.  At my grocery store, it's $5 for a loaf in the freezer section.  I'm the only one in my family that eats gluten free so it's fine.

In general, I'm usually poor, so I never bought Lindt's Lindor Truffles (White chocolate with a smooth filling) before.

I ended up getting small 5.1oz bag the other day and it was a big mistake!
I'll never again be able to really enjoy the gritty cheap white chocolate I usually end up getting.

White chocolate has always been my favorite... and now I found out just how good white chocolate actually is.

I'm looking at this cheap-o white chocolate easter bunny sitting on my counter knowing that it will be nowhere near the yummy smooth goodness that is the Lindor.

I'm restricting myself to one a day trying to stretch out what I have :)

Tony!

I'm amending my review to SOMETIMES: it has a very rich,sweet flavor. Great in smoothies and for making candies. It costs a little more than others, but the flavor makes it worth the additional cost and it is a staple in my kitchen. For something great, mix with tahini, a little honey and a little olive oil, adjust ingredients for taste and texture - delicious!

The LAST time I ordered, it was a totally different product, grey and tasteless and a great disappointment. Called the company and they said that the batches vary....

This is the best carob product I have found. One of my favorite recipes that I use carob powder for is a shake consisting of soymilk, frozen banana and carob powder. This carob has a milder flavor and I find this makes the best shakes. I have used it as a chocolate substitute in other recipes and prefer the taste and texture of this product to the roasted carob products.

I looked for this type of rice as recommended in the book, "the Italian Country Table" for risotto and it did not disappoint.  I think it was a good value for 6 lbs of organic risotto rice, better than I could find at our health food store for arborio.

I have tried many Chai teas and this is among the best.  Since I have a Tassimo machine it just makes sense to buy this.  It comes with the cream and I put FL honey in it.  Oh................so good.  I had strep throat this week and this was all that would go down my throat.  Now, even though I'm better, I have a cup every night.  Excellent!
I love the chai tea latte for Tassimo.  I save money and calories compared with Starbucks.  I think the taste is great!

I love the Twinings Chai Tea Latte for my Tassimo machine.  It is sweet but not too sweet.  I think the taste is great and the smell is wonderful.  As for the cost...well it's not the cheapest thing to drink but it's definitely worth the cost. :)

Expected a deeper, smokier tone to this paprika than I got.  Deserves praise for not being bitter (burnt) in processing, which some pimenton exhibit.  Taste is delightful, but if you specifically want rich smoky nose to your paprika, try another.
Smoked paprika is one of my favorite spices. I use it when I make Cordoban gazpacho. It's rich smokiness adds an unexpected flavor to anything you cook from scrambled eggs to chicken dishes.
I am deployed and need fast snacks sometimes when I am able to get to a microwave. These are perfect sized, quick and delicious. Lastly, they are cheap :) A good buy.

As I dog trainer, getting a dog to come when called can be challenging, but these are my 'secret weapon' in the war of 'coming when called'!! Dogs come running!  These are definitely staying in my dog training 'toolkit'.

My girls love this stuff however, I can't say the same thing for myself. The first time I opened a package I ended up flinging it outside while the dogs fended for themselves. The smell really stung and I lost all sense of purpose for my life. I'm saying this because there needs to be careful preparation on your end before you open a package. You will need some gloves or paper towels and a gas mask or hold your breath. The smell compares to nothing I've ever witnessed. It smacks you in the face (twice) so you should under no circumstances open the package in the house. It will linger! Once you open the package do not reach in with bare hands! That is what the gloves or paper towels are for, but remember you need to be holding your breath. I give this 4 stars because of the various lengths and widths. Being that I have two dogs it's hard to pick two that match and the smell prevents you from looking that long. Other than that, it's an awesome treat!

I give these to my dogs as a special treat. They smell stinky but the dogs love them!!!
My friends are buying them for their dogs now!!

Text: I'm so glad I decided to search for Jordan Almonds.  They are my husband's favorite and they are not readily available where I am located. This is my all-time two favorite flavors of K-cups.  I can't be without my German Chocolate Cake Coffee.  Yum!  Transaction went smoothly.  Will order again.  Love and coffee makes the world go round!  <3

Perfect. My two favorite flavors yoked together in one package. A good price, too.

My order came within twenty-four hours with free shipping, but I think that's because I'm a prime member. Oh, well, whatever. Timothy makes a great cup of java and this was not a disappointment.

These taste great!  But not so decadent and sweet that I want to eat a whole box so they are perfect for dieters and portion control.  Sad that I can't get them locally, but buying 8 boxes at a time of something I love--not so bad!

This company needs to review their shipping practices and their quality control. One the packages arrived with syrup all over the outside as several of the cups had opened and leaked all over. I opened the box to see how bad it was only to discover you can't return them once the package has been opened so I was stuck with a big mess. There were over 10 cups that had opened and gotten all over the inside so I spent an hour cleaning off the ones that could be saved. The product itself tasted very good but it was not worth all the work cleaning up the mess.

I have been in Utah over 25 years, at an altitude of about 4200 feet. My internist says that's not too high, but from all I can learn from family history, history, protohistory, and prehistory, my ancestors for at least 10,000 years have lived at or near sea level. My oxygen levels tend to get very low when the atmospheric pressure drops or I am extra tired. Since I know that coca combats altitude sickness, I decided to try it. Instead of spending the day in bed with an oxygen hose stuck up my nose to combat an O2 level of about 69, I am able to work all day with an oxygen level about 98. I dislike paying $[...] for coca tea, but I am paying $300 a month for my oxygen machine. I'll take the tea, thank you. My internist throws a tantrum about it, but my pulmonologist says that in his experience, a person with my background is unable to adjust to the altitude and it might take four generations before her descendants can do so. Since I was past child-bearing age when I moved here . . . . well, my coca tea is steeping, so I'd better go and drink it. I have a lot of work to do today.
I always have trouble getting this.  The Arbuelita type is available, but Ibarra is far and away better.  When I get a chance, I get a case or two of the Ibarra.
Trackless litter learls is the way to go. Litter stays near his litter box. Product absorbs urine with limited odor. Cat loves it.
Our 6 month old loved it and it helped him poop!  The value is good on Amazon and it seemed to have a flavor that our picky baby liked.

I wish they had these when I had my son. These pouches are such a great idea! You don't ever have to double dip or dirty up another bowl. Just squeeze some directly onto the spoon and feed it to your child. It's so sanitary! Also love that it's just the fruit and organic.

I've been eating ramen since I was a little girl living in Japan.  If you can't get it fresh from a ramen stand, these packaged instant noodles are the best alternative.  The noodles are light and slurpy and the soup base is tasty, but a wee bit on the salty side.  Sapporo Ichiban costs a bit more than other ramen noddles, but it's worth it!  My brother and I both buy this brand when buying ramen in the store.

I'm Asian-American, particularly Thai-American, and I've eaten Sapporo Ichiban ramen noodles for as long as I can remember, ever since I was a little girl. Yes, my family has been loyal to this brand for that long. I've tried many brands of ramen noodles in my lifetime, but the taste of the other ramen noodle brands is bland compared to Sapporo Ichiban. I'm very glad that Amazon sells Sapporo Ichiban products. It beats my family having to drive to an international food store, like we have always done, to get this product. Yes, this product is made in the U.S., but they're Japanese-styled. (By the way, my thoughts and prayers are with the Japanese people who are currently dealing with the earthquake and tsunami disaster mess in their nation.) I've read all the reviews on this page, and some people have complained about the taste. Each person is different, and personally for me, I think that Sapporo Ichiban tastes better than the other instant ramen brands out there. Plus, what can you really demand when it's instant ramen noodles, the keyword being "instant"? If you truly want an excellent noodle experience, go to Japan and Thailand and order noodle soup dishes at their noodle shops. I've traveled to quite a few Asian countries in my lifetime, and nothing beats eating noodles in Thailand and Japan and listening to customers slurp away and enjoying their noodle experience. But since we can't fly away to Thailand and Japan each time we want to, we really can't demand or expect that much from "instant" ramen noodles. My family eats the chicken and beef-flavored Sapporo Ichiban. We have also tried the shrimp-flavored and original style as well. My favorite is the chicken-flavored. But if you don't like the chicken-flavored, there are the other flavors mentioned. Plus, I like the fact that these Sapporo Ichiban ramen noodles only consist of noodles and a soup flavored base. There are no additional toppings. So, my family and I can add our own ingredients such as vegetables, meat, eggs, cheese, etc. Another good thing about the Sapporo Ichiban brand is that you get a lot of noodles for the amount you pay. One individual package fills up a big bowl. You get more noodles from Sapporo Ichiban compared to a lot of other brands. I think that Amazon is offering a reasonable price for this 24 pack of Sapporo Ichiban ramen noodles.

Summary: Tastes great for what it is
Text: I have relied on these cake mixes for a few years and find them to be handy and to taste fine.  As with most sugar free products they taste great if you have not been eating sugar, but taste a little off if you switch straight from eating full sugar/fat desserts.  The cake mixes only require water to make. A teaspoon of real vanilla or almond extract improves the flavor.  I like to make the chocolate cake with iced coffee.  Then rather than use sugar free frosting (ugggh!) I sprinkle the top with either unsweetened cocoa or with chopped coffee beans.  The bitterness of the cocoa and the coffee beans enhances the sweetness of the cake. These mixes make a very thin eight-inch layer.  My local grocery store sells the mixes for $2.79 and rarely has flavors other than chocolate or yellow so the price and variety offered here is wonderful news.
Love this cereal and was delighted finally to find it at Amazon. Doubly good to have it delivered at specific times throughout the year. Great breakfast is now continually ensured.

They are all dented, warped or damage from overzealous wrapping together.  When the 6 box was on subscription, it was just in the box loose, and one box did get damaged, but not all of them....

I love my pizzas with anchovies.  These Crown Prince anchovies sure are salty but definitely tasty.  The cans don't need opener as they have the latch/pop release.  The quality of the fish is consistent and tender--excellent in my book.

Crown Prince products are generally acceptable, but these anchovies are way too salty.

I would not buy again.

I have always loved pistachios, but living two or three thousand miles from the nearest pistachio tree, I had never really tasted fresh pistachios. But I didn't realize that until I received my order of Keenan Farms pistachios from Amazon. I was immediately struck by how green and fresh looking the nuts were. When I got the first of three two-pound bags open and tasted them, I was hooked! Each kernel was so plump, so large, so crunchy and fresh and beautifully green I had to remind myself that I was holding a two pound bag and I couldn't eat the whole thing. I will reorder this item often, and recommend that you order them too.

Text: I love this trail mix. I keep it by my bed :). It's got nuts and raisens AND M&Ms for sweetness. These are exactly what I used to buy in the grocery store.

Do you like peanuts in your trail mix? If so this is for you.
I personally don't like a lot of peanuts, but the chocolate pieces, cashews, and raisins make up for the large amount of peanuts. Also, if you have a person who loves peanuts in your household, it works out well!

Summary: Make my own organic wheat bread
Text: I have been buying this product one every month now.  We completely stopped buying store bread but make our own organic bread using a bread machine.  Loves this product.

Summary: Miserable in a bread machine, unless you blend it.
Text:
If you have a bread machine, and use this by itself as the flour, you'll end up with a bread that rises poorly, and would be turned down by a goat.

I tried adding more molasses, adding more water, adding more yeast, adding sugar, using less wheat flour and all combinations of these. It's still a brick. Just awful, but my chickens don't seem to mind it. In fact they like it. They like bugs too though ...

Outside of feeding this to my chickens, the only way I could make it palatable was to cut it with other flour. If you use it at 50/50, it comes out really good. Even 2-1 favoring the wheat flour lightens it up enough so that if you like a heavy bread, it's excellent.

I'm going to try vital wheat gluten next to see if that helps this bread. If I remember, I'll update the review at that time with whether it works well or not.

This ww bread flour makes a loaf that is much moister that I got with my other regular whole wheat flours. Now, I just need a way to make it rise up a bit more so it isn't so dense. That is not a complaint about the flour, though, since that is the nature of ww bread.  I am VERY happy with it, and look forward to continuing to use it in my kitchen.  I ordered this item, the whole wheat pastry flour, and the organic cornmeal, all from Great River.  The two flours are replacing my King Arthur White Whole wheat that I used to buy so much of at my local grocery.  The flavor of these flours is definitely superior to the KA (which I also liked).  But now, I know I am feeding my family organic.
I love Panang curry and each handy little packet gives me four to six full family meals right at home.  I haven't seen this in the stores.  As I said, great find!!!
These beans were wonderful.  My customers raved over them.  The chocolate is amazing!

These are okay, but the ratio of chocolate to bean is too much for me, and even the dark chocolate taste too sweet.  It could just be the batch I got, but the espresso bean didn't stand out as much as some other brands I've tried (even eating the bean alone), and it is overwhelmed by the chocolate taste.
the best chocolate covered coffee bean i have ever had. if you enjoy coffee and chocolate i insist that you try this product
These are a healthy treat disguised as a yummy treat!  Better than a candy bar.

Summary: The best quick oatmeal available in the U.S.A.
Text: Do not confuse this product with the Irish steel cut oatmeal that must be cooked for 30 minutes. That is the best. This oatmeal is not as good, but for a quick cooking product, it is pretty amazing. You can have oatmeal ready in 5 minutes. This oatmeal is best with a little milk, some brown sugar, and some berries or dried fruit. I like dried dates and dried black figs combined in mine, but it is fun to experiment. It's hard to believe that something this good is also good for you.

I love this oatmeal, it is easy to use, you can microwave it or cook it on the stove
It is the only oatmeal I use now.

Its a shame this is not more widely available in Grocery stores. Nothing matches its consistency. So I've resorted to getting my consistent supply online. I cook it on the stove with milk and frozen blueberries. In a few minutes I have a perfect start to the morning. No need for sugar - it doesn't get any healthier than this. Sometimes I microwave it in milk.

Now, if you are starting to eat oatmeal (good for you) without that sugar, it may taste like paste at first. It did to me. So I used less sugar everyday and eventually weaned myself off of it. Eventually everything tastes sweeter. This McCanns oatmeal tastes sweet to me now.

SO this is one of those staple foods I cant live without. My only complaint is the packaging sucks - the inner bag must be cut with a scissors to open it. Trying to open it by hand is next to impossible. It still gets a 5 star because that is a small inconvenience for the taste as a whole, and thats really what we are reviewing.

Now if they would just carry it regular grocery stores!
This oatmeal is delicious. It is quick and easy to prepare and it keeps me satisfied until lunch. I use the microwave preparation and love the convenience without having to sacrifice taste.

My partner introduced me to this a few years ago. This oatmeal tastes way better than Quaker Oats, and cooks quickly. It has a great texture, not at all like wallpaper paste, and tastes good even without additives.

When we're going to have a really long morning, we substitute soy milk for the water and add a little brown sugar. It keeps us going for hours.

Summary: When you're dieting real hard, this will strengthen you!
Text: I've got a real savvy trainer and he recommended that I try this soup when I feel like I just CANNOT stick with the program (because I am feeling weak and listless.) IT WORKS! Try this soup when you hit a plateau or have a serious craving, too, it really turns your attitude around! Trainer says often when we are on a hard program (controlled diet & workouts) the body just needs a dose of sodium to come back. The spices really help, too! I like to eat this soup "American style" (with a spoon) or just drink it if I'm in a hurry, so I crush the noodles before I brew the soup. Just put em in a bag and get a hammer. (No way can you cut up these noodles!) Try it next time you are under the weather or just need a pick me up! Per container: 280 calories, 8 gr fat, 45 carbs, 6 gr protein, 1610 mg sodium, just 26% of calories from fat. Crystal Noodle Spicy Sesame Paste, 2.47 Ounce Cardboard Cup (Pack of 6).

My cats are picky about treats. They seem to prefer only catnip flavored treats and Pounce Crunchy is their favorite of those. Unfortunately, I have not been able to find it in the store (grocery, Petco or Walmart)lately. We were running low and no one wants to be around kitties when they are out of treats! Thankfully, Amazon came to the rescue at a great price. We are now set with snacks for a while and I know where to turn next time!

When those late night cravings hit, Nature Valley Crunchy Cinnamon Granola Bars are a healthy and low calorie way to satisfy that sweet tooth. At only 90 calories each these bars have just the right amount of cinnamon richness and crunch so much so that it almost feels sinful. The bars come conveniently packaged in 6 boxes of 12 each. For an exceptionally decadent treat, try crumbling the bars over a scoop of coffee ice cream. Since the bars are individually wrapped, they're also an excellent on-the-go snack. I throw them in lunches or in my backpack when I'm in a hurry.

From the time Nature Valley released the Cinnamon bar years ago, I've felt it was the best I'd ever eaten.  I'm sorry it is no longer available in any local stores but am soooooo glad Amazon carries them. Until this purchase, I had never bought food online but I simply couldn't resist once I found them on Amazon.  The bars arrived in perfect condition, unbroken and ready to eat!!

Summary: Expiration date close, product really dry
Text:
June 28, 2011. The Expiration date. Ordered Jan 17, delivered Jan 21st. The product is really dry. Drier than usual. I mean yes these bars are really crunchy, but the Oats and Honey that came in the Variety Pack I also bought wasn't as dry as these. Part of me wonders if these have been on the shelf for too long and Amazon decided to put them on a subscribe and save sale to rotate the stock.

I bought these or emergency supplies in case of a natural disaster or something but now I see I'll have to eat them all in 5 months. That's pretty bad to me.

Yes people say they seem to love these and they can't find them on store shelves and I guess in that case it's great. But I do want to question how old these are as some products I see expiring two years (about) in the future. So just buyer beware in the case that you are the sole consumer and aren't part of a larger group who might eat these.
JUST RIGHT SIZE FOR A NICE SNACK WITH LOW CALORIES. TASTES GOOD AND POPS UP PERFECTLY ON MICROWAVE OVEN. WELL PRICED ALSO!

Text:
I couldn't live w/out this product. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars - is that sometimes i'll get a bag that is a little stale. It is a portioned bag of 100 calories, so you can eat the entire thing and not worry about over indulging. I recently lost a lot of weight - and this was my snack of choice. I eat at least one bag a day.

The amount you get for the price is a bargain - and it tastes great too! I highly recommend it.

Summary: snack gift.  loved the price and packaging
Text: I was putting snack packs together as gifts.  These were the right size and price. I think they turned out nicely.
Not the tastiest popcorn. Not very salty and not buttery at all. But it does pop up nicely and you get a lot of popcorn for 100 calories.
Good product.Good taste not graney or grtty at all. Just like fresh eggs. You do have to make sure you mix them well before cooking

Text: These powdered eggs are pricey and worth every cent.  I have invested quite a bit of money on a long and extensive 'taste test' on other products (about 30) and not one of them compares to this one.  If someone asked you to wear a blindfold and you participated in a taste test where you had to choose which scrambled egg is from a fresh egg or which one is the Ovaeasy egg... you would have a very hard time making up your mind! I love this tea.  Marvelous complex flavor.  I never get tired of it.
I have used this on steaks, pork chops, chicken, you name it, good in eggs too. Wonderful smoky flavor tastes good on anything.

This soup is one of my favorite foods.  I do tend to load it down with brown sugar, cinnamon and butter, but I could eat it every night of the week.  My only complaint is that there are only about 3 portions in a box.

I contacted the seller regarding the best type the raw or liquid type for baking and they recommended the raw type.  I was disappointed with the results. Since then, I tried this in iced tea and again, was disappointed.  I had to continually stir the contents of a large pitcher because the honey sunk to the bottom.  The taste of the honey never diminished, but it was a pain in the neck to do the stirring every time I wanted a glass of iced tea.  Next time I will buy the regular honey.

The picture shows pecans in a package that clearly says chopped. These are NOT chopped. They are powder. I was going to make pecans pies with these and am now stuck with a 30 pound box of pulverized pecans. In the heading it says mealy pecans and is followed by the word chopped. They are way past chopped. They also arrived in bulk which again the picture was deceiving as it shows the pecans neatly in bags. I am so disappointed in my purchase.

I like this Minestrone. There is a lot of vegetable in the can. Low sodium very nice I don't like a lot of salt. Thank you Health Valley,
and Amazon for selling fat free minestrone. God bless.
I had bought TWO bags 35.2 oz of this product and planning to made some sachets to put in all my drawers or closets.  Unfortunately, it is NOT clean and contains many sifted.

I was thrilled to find this on Amazon, having purchased it from Cost Plus before (who no longer carry it). I would agree that drinking this straight is probably not to most people's liking. It tastes like campari-flavored soda. However, if you like negronis, this, combined with orange juice in a highball glass over ice, tastes like a negroni without the alcohol. It also looks beautiful if you serve it without stirring, allowing the orange to merge into the red, and garnish with a swizzle stick and an orange slice. The bottles are very small and have cool graphics, too. Save them to use as individual flower vases at an outdoor party.

Bitter RedSanbitter (Pellegrino) is at first taste somewhat of a shock but as the flavor settles in it becomes clean and refreshing, an extremely acceptable alternative to an alcoholic aperative. If you must, add a splash of Campari--a take off on a Bellini.

I'm not trying to offend anyone, but this soda is definitely an aquired taste!  I just had my first bottle, as I was drawn in by the amazing packaging and love for anything Italian.  Ugh!  I swear I threw up in my mouth.  Stay away from this if you cannot tolerate the smell or taste of vomit.  Heard it tastes better with bitters in it, but I cannot stomach another sip.

These little buggers aren't the easiest to find. You won't find them in the regular spice aisle of a normal American grocery store. Sometimes you'll find them in the "Mexican" or "Spanish" aisle at the store, and I've seen them in Asian groceries, but, mostly they are elusive.

I like using these to make puerco pibil, and this is good value. They are fresh, come in a big, plastic jar and last a long time--And I love that they're easy to find on the Internet!

I love the Monkey King Jasmine Green Tea.  Buying it locally by the individual box was not only more expensive but inconvenient.  When I saw that you offered a special price when buying six boxes, not only am I saving about $2 per box, but now I can freely make my tea without feeling that I need to ration it until I can get to the store.  I am sharing tea bags and giving some as gifts. In the midst of some recently busy work weeks, making a cup of this tea was like taking a mini stress break (vacation). It tasted so good and smelled heavenly.  It is also great iced.  I add a little maple syrup or honey.  Enjoy!  Treat yourself!

As a green tea, this is a fine tea.  As a jasimine green tea, I find the jasmine to be much too subtle.  I had my first jasmine tea in a nearby chinese restaurant and absolutely fell in love with it.  It made me feel like I was relaxing in a spa.  This tea, however, tastes mostly like your typical green tea.  If I concentrate I can almost detect the jasmine.  Not quite what I was  hoping for.

This was a delightful blend of herbs and spices. Not only did I use it for the usual vinegar and oil type dressing, but also tried a honey mustard dressing. The herbs also made a delicious marinade. It also was a hit with the family when it served with the pasta. Besides using it as a dressing and a marinade, I used it as a natural seasoning for fish,or chicken. It was nice finding one blend of seasonings that I could use so many ways.

This sugar has been a great replacement for white sugar, and overall I like it better than any other "natural" sugar that I've tried. I have used it for baking and in my coffee.

The sugar has the texture of soft round sand, the grains differ in size from fine powder to large grains similar to "Sugar in the Raw" brand, but are opaque. I first tried it plain, and it had a slightly chalky/dry and faint molassas flavor but much more sweet than bitter. So yes it is different than cane sugar. However, when I use it in my coffee and in baking, it has a smooth flavor similar to brown sugar but not ever cringingly sweet like white sugar. I try to stay away from refined sugar, but of course whenever I have too much of the white stuff, I get that sugar high and then a sugar hangover - fidgity, slight headache, etc. With Rapadura sugar, I never get that feeling, it only gives me a nice perk while taking the bitterness out of my morning coffee and lending a mellow earthy sweetness to cookies and cakes.

Summary: PERFECT!!!! (and yes, I HAVE tried it)
Text:
Let ME preface MY review by saying that I actually HAVE tried it and it is well worth the price! The grind is perfect for my Solofill and tastes better than any K-cup I've ever used. But here's something I do not get at all! Did that reviewer really just say "It's a lot cheaper to continue using my Solofill cup to scoop some coffee out of the can"? I don't get it... the logic I mean. I buy a 2 liter bottle of soda when there's a birthday party or office party, picnic, etc. I KNOW that the bottle will be gone and it's cheaper by the ounce. But that doesn't keep me from buying a 12 oz. can of the same brand of soda!!! Ounce for ounce a can of soda costs FIVE times as much as a 2 liter bottle. But it doesn't take a coffee snob to figure out after a few days that the ground coffee in that can is losing its flavor the same way a bottle of coke loses its fizz after a few days. If you don't want to spend money on Ekojava coffee packets, then at least buy whole bean coffee and grind it as you use it.

But then I suppose someone would say "Why not just buy K-cups then?". Good question - easy answer (in my world anyway).

These little sticks of coffee that are ground nicely, weighed out perfectly (instead of the freaking mess you make scooping coffee out of a can or bag), and FRESH! So far, sounds like a K-cup. BUT... I use other things to brew coffee other than a Keurig. The packets work in the Melitta I have in my office. I gave a handful of sticks to my neighbor who tried it in his drip coffeemaker. After trying it a few times, he found that one packet in a drip coffeemaker using a paper filter makes 5 cups of awesome drip coffee! Try that with a K-cup! AND JUST out of curiosity, I stopped by a very cool coffee shop in Boise, Idaho (Salt Tears... VERY cool place!) They have a pour over bar and use the Coava Kone filters instead of paper. I asked him if I could use my coffee packet instead of there DOMA coffee (one of a few roasters in Idaho I would recommend). The water was at 206 degrees and he expertly poured about a third of the water in. The coffee began to de-gas (yeah... ain't gonna happen with ground coffee from a can) and then finished off the pour and we waited. We were both pretty blown away. It was awesome.

Bottom line? Not sure I'd recommend this to people who are happy with coffee from a can. And I am NOT knocking those who do. My father scooped Folgers from a can when I was a kid and for years I thought that was the epitome of great coffee (but then, I also used to think hamburger was the highest quality beef). But I confess... that sounds a bit condescending and I realize that many people truly enjoy simple store brand ground coffee in their Keurig. My point it, just because you own a Keurig and a Solofill, doesn't qualify you to write a review for something you've never even tried. Dude... At least try something before you review it. C'mon... really? Okay, I sound like a snob. But I guess that's my point. If you are happy with ground coffee from a can, this probably doesn't make sense. If you are more discriminating than that, and you need something to take with you that is a high quality, one cup solution, is fresh, and you want to use it anywhere in almost anything, then heck yeah... this is a great buy!!!

Summary: One of the Best Microwavable Meals, but Beware of Trans Fat
Text:
This was one of my college staples. I had at least 5 of these a week for years.
After a while my parents said that it contained trans fat.
I initially ignored their claim after reading the package and seeing "0g Trans Fat."

However, I later read that food manufacturers may put 0g if it contains up to .5g. There are two servings in this package, which is why they can say that it is "trans fat free." If it only listed one serving, this product would have to say 1g trans fat.

This is still my favorite microwavable noodle product, but I no longer purchase it. Unnaturally occurring trans fat is simply not good for you, no matter how delicious. Should this product ever remove the trans fat, I would rate it 5 stars and go back to eating it every day.

Look for partially hydrogenated oils in the ingredients. It's not worth it.

--- Edit Jul 12, 2012 ---

Below is what I found online when looking up PROPYLENE GLYCOL which in industrial anitifreeze. Can someone please reassure me this stuff is safe to drink?

I know it is not approved for use in cat food so what something that is used in industrial antifreeze safe for humans?

PROPYLENE GLYCOL
Propylene Glycol, Alcohol
A colourless, volatile, flammable liquid produced by fermentation of yeast and carbohydrates. Alcohol is frequently used as a solvent. As an ingredient in ingestible products, alcohol may cause body tissues to be more vulnerable to carcinogens.

Mouthwashes with an alcohol content over 25% have been implicated in mouth, tongue and throat cancers. Note, the forms of alcohol used in cosmetics are not necessarily those used in alcoholic drinks, and may be much more dangerous.

Some examples

Ethylene glycol, is commonly used in acrylic paints, brake fluid, antifreeze, tile grout, primer, sealant paste, floor polish, tyre sealant and shoe polish. Oh yes.......and it's also used in some "smoothing lotions" and "firming moisturizer"!

Known health effects: throat irritation, headache, backache, kidney problems, oedema (swelling), necrosis (cell death). If swallowed, can cause drowsiness, and slurred speech, possibly stupor, vomiting, respiratory failure, coma, convulsions, and death

Propylene Glycol

A cosmetic form of mineral oil found in automatic brake and hydraulic fluid and industrial antifreeze. In the skin and hair, propylene glycol works as a humescent, which causes retention of moisture content of skin or cosmetic products by preventing the escape of moisture or water. The Material Safety Data Sheet warns users to avoid skin contact with propylene glycol as this strong skin irritant can cause liver abnormalities and kidney damage.

Summary: Good, but not one of my top-tier Bigelow favorites
Text:
I'm clearly in the minority here, as Darjeeling is not one of my favorite Bigelow varieties. It is a good tea, and I enjoy drinking it, and I would never be unhappy if someone served it to me. In fact, I do keep some in my house, and brew up a cup every couple weeks or so. But Darjeeling isn't one of my top tier Bigelow favorites, and there are several others I drink more frequently.

This is strictly a black tea (which is what I most prefer), without any additions, although when I do my teabag deep sniff (my favorite moment with any tea, right after I rip open a foil bag!) with Darjeeling, there is a hint of what is almost a lemon scent. There is no lemon added to this tea, but it's interesting that the scent is there, particularly as another reviewer says this is the only tea he doesn't "have" to add lemon to.

The flavor is quite good, but my main complaint is that it is weaker, or more mellow, than I prefer. When I drink Darjeeling, I find myself wishing there was more of the flavor present. It is often described as "rich" or "robust" but I think there are other straight black teas that better meet those terms.

If you also find Darjeeling a little mellow for your tastes, I suggest you try the Bigelow English Breakfast (don't confuse this with the Bigelow English Teatime!) variety, which is also a straight black tea.

I always drink tea straight--no sugar, no honey, no lemon, no milk! So my reviews are my opinions of the straight tea flavor, not how it interacts with another agent. I drink Bigelow tea almost exclusively, because it's readily available, modestly priced, and has lots of varieties that are all of decent quality. If I give a Bigelow flavor less stars, it reflects only my taste preference, and is not a statement of low product quality.

It also has no sodium, but great flavor, which really gives the lie to the supposed need for all the killer doses of salt you find in so many products nowadays.

The thing that really bugs me is how hard it is to find this item on the shelves anywhere. So many places have huge racks of Spice Hunter products -- of which there are a great many to choose from, at premium prices -- but somehow THIS one never seems to make the cut. Some Whole Foods locations had it -- briefly -- years ago. I've asked Bristol Farms to add it to their stock, but I think they are phasing out of Spice Hunter entirely. The one place I could find it semi-reliably was Erewhon in L.A., and even then they were usually down to the last couple jars.
