Summary: I've just found a new favorite!
Text: Lipton's Blackberry Vanilla Herbal Tea is, to put it simply, divine. Packaged in a pyramid bag made of a mesh that is much more durable than what normal tea bags use, the all natural ingredients combine gorgeously together for a wonderful cup of tea. The ingredients are as follows: hibiscus flowers, rosehips, sweet blackberry leaves, natural flavor, dried black current pieces, dried blueberry pieces, dried raspberry pieces, and sunflower lecithin. So not only is it a blackberry tea, it also has black current, blueberry, and raspberry, making it tailor-made for me since I adore Twinings Mixed Berry Tea, 20-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6), though since that uses black tea and different berries has a completely contrasting, but delicious, taste. At first sip, the strong berry flavors seem to overwhelm the vanilla, but after savoring the tea a bit, the vanilla's undertone actually balances with the berry flavors perfectly. Since I generally only add honey to tea, I first tried it with that, which complements the flavors of Lipton's Blackberry extremely well and recommend over other sweeteners. I love this tea, it's fast become my new favorite, and as someone who's sensitive to caffeine, the fact that it's free of caffeine makes it even better. Lipton has developed a delightful new tea that I'll definitely be getting again!

I really like this tea. I was leery because I did not want the vanilla to overpower the fruity notes but it was great. The vanilla is more of a light undertone as opposed to sitting side-by-side with the blackberry flavor. I've only drank it hot with Splenda and it exceeded my expectations. I didn't overdo the water (about 6oz.) and it resulted in a strong flavor that was really pleasant.

The tea bag is made out of a material that isn't as messy as typical tea bags. I was able to pull it out without it dripping everywhere.

I would suggest it if you are into hot teas.

Hopefully Lipton will make more Pyramid Tea flavors, in addition to the Blackberry Vanilla herbal tea, because this is delicious! Raspberry, Blueberry, etc. would be a welcome addition.  The pyramid design is unique and seems to work well.  The Blackberry Vanilla is smooth, fresh and not too sweet.  I drink a pot of tea once to twice a day and this is a new favorite.

Summary: Thumbs Up From A Tea Lover
Text:
I love tea. I drink it all day.

But I'm an ice tea kind of girl, so I can't review this on how it is as a hot tea.

As an iced tea I really liked it.

Some tea's don't work well when you drink them cold, but this was not only refreshing, but the taste of the tea was very strong.

In my opinion I thought the vanilla had the stronger flavor but you could taste the blackberry.

Lipton always makes great teas and this is another one.

I also love the little pyramid teabag, make it so easy to boil, and they don't look as messy as the old type of tea bags do.

First let me say that I am a cold tea drinker or i like ice in my tea and only on really cold outside conditions do I ever drink hot tea.

Lipton has a really unusual bag here and already have a few of their flavors but wanted to try the blackberry. Although the box states it is Blackberry Vanilla, the vanilla is just a hint of a flavor and that is alright with me.

The flavor is mild and there are only 18 bags in this box whereas most of the other teas like Bigelow and Tazo have 20 in theirs. But, the price is slightly lower at the store where I checked but not only are the number of bags lower, the ounces in the bags are lower too.

I can't see where the different tea bag actually makes the flow any better. I tried both of the different bags and both floated for a time if I didn't push them down.

This is a nice flavor but it is so mild that it is almost non existant and i had to use another bag to get a good bold flavor. This flavor is caffeine free, which is a plus for night time use.

This Lipton Blackberry Vanilla Herbal Tea is sweet and tasty, and comes in little pyramid bags, which I'm very partial to and I`ve only found in Japanese teas before. You can see that it contains tiny dried pieces of fruit (black currant, blackberry, blueberry and raspberry) as well as blackberry leaves, hibiscus flowers and rosehips. It is caffeine free, so makes a lovely after-dinner drink, and is delicately sweet enough that dieters might use it as "dessert."

For a commercial tea company, this is a truly lovely tea, and in a blind tea test with more expensive teas, might fare quite well. I've tried it both hot and chilled, and it is good either way. And those little pyramid bags are such an aesthetically pleasing touch! I will certainly buy Lipton's Blackberry Vanilla Herbal Tea again.

As someone trying to reduce caffeine, cold days leave me missing my coffee, so more and more lately I have turned to hot tea. Lipton is a brand I have used since childhood, and a brand I trust. I have tried their other flavored teas using the pyramid shaped tea bag, and I love them.

The pyramid shaped bag allows me to get full flavor of the tea. Typically, I use my Keurig to dispense a cup of plain hot water into a mug that contains the tea bag. If I plan on sweetening the tea, I add the sweetener as the water dispenses, so that it fully dissolves into the flavor of the tea. For me this is a tried and true method for a quick cup that is the perfect temperature.

I really enjoyed the pairing of blackberry and vanilla flavors. Because I added sweetener, I did not find this tea at all bitter, on the contrary the flavor was quite lovely. I added a bit of milk and the tea was a lovely lilac color in my mug. The flavor and aroma both proved very relaxing. All in all, a nice, mellow bodied taste that will become a permanent part of my tea repertoire.

Summary: There's no vanilla in the ingredient list, so where does that flavor come from?
Text:
Although this is supposedly a blackberry vanilla tea, there is no vanilla in it according to the ingredients list. Instead, one presumes the vanilla flavor is listed as "natural flavor." You do know that the "natural flavor" which is often used to mimic real vanilla comes from the castor sacs of beavers, don't you? Yikes. According to wikipedia: "In the United States, castoreum, the exudate from the castor sacs of mature beavers, has been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as a food additive,often referenced simply as a "natural flavoring" in the product's list of ingredients. It is commonly used in both food and beverages, especially as vanilla and raspberry flavoring."

Ingredients: Hibiscus flowers, rosehips, sweet blackberry leaves, natural flavor, dried black currant pieces, dried blackberry pieces, dried blueberry pieces, dried raspberry pieces, sunflower lecithin.

I ordered this for my wife and she really liked it. The tea brews quickly with the more open bag that allows water to flow around it better. Excellent product with a full rich tea flavor as the end result.

This fruity herbal tea, made by combining hibiscus flowers and rosehips with dried pieces of berries, has a naturally sweet, rich taste and an enticingly delicious smell. No sugar or honey is needed unless you prefer extra sweetness. Hot tea is perfect on a cold day, especially a tea like this with the smells of summer. It hadn't occurred to me to go to Lipton for herbal teas, but now that I've tried this flavor I'll be checking out the other varieties Lipton makes.

Right off the bat the aroma from the opening the box will grab you!  Sweetly fragrant, this tastes as good as smells.  With just enough vanilla to balance the blackberry flavor, it makes a delicious cup of tea.  I shared it with friends and co-workers and they all loved it as well.  Lipton serves up a winner!
I tried it hot and really liked it. I loved the deep purple color and the tart flavor of the tea. The pyramid shape of the tea bag was fun too.

A pleasant addition to the Lipton line of teas. The blackberry vanilla is a blend of several fruits and flowers including
Hibiscus flowers, Rosehips, sweet Blackberry leaves, dried black currant pieces, dried blackberry pieces, dried blueberry pieces,
dried raspberry pieces and some "natural" flavors.

You do need to infuse the recommended time of 4-6 minutes to release the full flavors of the tea. The dominant flavor is the blackberry as
expected in the name.

We enjoyed it both hot and iced.

The pyramid bag design most closely mimics an infuser which is often used for higher end and bulk teas.
It seems to work allowing the flavors to escape through the skin of the bag.

A nice product and presentation.

Summary: Too much blackberry, not enough vanilla
Text: The Lipton Herbal Blackberry Vanilla tea was good, but a bit too fruity for me. It had almost a "medicine" taste for some reason. I thought it could have really used a bit more vanilla to tone down the fruitiness. Other than that it was a good herbal tea with a lot of flavor.

Summary: Uplifting and soothing at the same time
Text: I am not, as a rule, a big fan of herbal teas, but I'll give anything a try. Lipton's Blackberry Vanilla Tea, in its distinctive pyramid shape, allows the full essence of both flavours to circulate and infuse into a truly enjoyable tea experience. The scent alone is warming and peace-inducing, and holds a chilly day at bay. This is the tea I would choose, with a little honey, for days when I'm feeling under the weather. This is a great addition to your tea inventory.

This is another delicious tea from Lipton.  The blackberry taste is definitely stronger than the vanilla.  The pyramid shaped tea bags gives more room for water to flow between the tea, spices, and chunks of blackberries.  Yes, I said chunks of blackberry - you can really see the fruit in the tea bags.  This is perfect for the cool fall weather.  One of my favorites!

We know all about gluten free foods and this brand is the best gluten free pasta I've had so far.  It has a much better flavor and texture than just plain old brown rice pasta and the nutritional content is better too.

This has made my life (and my dog) much more pleasant.  She has to have med's twice a day/every day.  It was sometimes difficult to get her to take her med's volunterily.  Now she will sit and beg for her Pill Pocket. It saves a lot of money to order thru Amazon. She doesn't like the chicken flavor for some reason but never had a problem with the beef flavor.

I have a lab and sheppard/collie mix both on daily medications.  These are by far the easiest way to get them to take their pills.  I use the large size and break them in half for each dog.  You can smush the pill pocket around the pill so they can't find the pill and spit it out.  I also think it's much less expensive to buy them on Amazon in bult...they run $10 a bag in my area.  Both of my dogs think they are treats!
My 11 year old Golden Retriever has many allergies and must take pills to combat the itching. This product is just right for him, because I can easily put 2 pills into the pocket and pinch it closed.

Summary: Great buy on my dog's pill pockets!
Text:
My dogs love these pill pockets and they make giving our dogs their daily meds so easy! Great price as well as fast and easy shipping! Will order from Monster Pets again!
http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000O5DI1E/ref=cm_cr_rev_prod_title
A must have for giving pills to dogs. I actually split them in half for my toy poodle. You get more for your money with this size as opposed to small dog size of pockets

Summary: Great for giving dogs medication without a fight.
Text:
These pill pockets are excellent! I have an older dog, who due to some health problems is now taking 4 - 5 pills a day. The pill pockets have turned this into a treat time for her, she loves getting them and scarfs them right down without investigating what's smushed inside! It's such a relief to not have the struggle of shoving all those pills into her mouth.

The other great thing about these soft pill pockets is that they can easily be formed around multiple pills if you have many to give at one time, or split to stretch the pack for any smaller pills. This particular set is also much less expensive than what could be found at my local pet stores.
Great deal, fast shipment, great service as always.  The dogs love it and I love not having to go to the store everytime I need a pack
really great product, makes giving meds really easy.  my pet loves it and she takes a lot of medicines.  After a month she is not tired of the "treats" yet

When I started using these my dog had become wise to just about every other trick (cheese, hot dogs, peanut butter, etc.) and did not cooperate when I opened her mouth and shoved the medication down.

These were a lifesaver. She now follows me to where I keep them and eagerly awaits her 'treat'. You can't imagine her delight when she gets 3 at once!

I buy them from Entirely Pets via Amazon and they get here the next day. I love it!

The pill pockets were wonderful. I threw it in the air and had him catch and eat it. I used 2 packages before my dog, (a German Shepherd- very smart and clever animal) discovered how to eat the pocket and spit out the pill.  I was feeding him 5 pills a day so it was bound to happen, especially when he bit into the pill in the pocket which really smelled and tasted bad.

I'm a big fan of most products I've tried from Stonewall Kitchen (the pancake mix is the exception because the result was more like dessert cake than pancakes). The jams are so delicious I always have them on hand. This collection gives a newcomer to this product line a good sampling of what's available. Another Stonewall Kitchen product I recommend is the Maple Pumpkin Butter. Sooo good!

This jam collection is amazingly delicious.  I just can't pick a favorite flavor.  I love them all!  I love to spread these on my pancakes, toast, french toast, biscuts, or even just eat out of the jar.  I think this would make a great gift, but I have never been able to share :)

Summary: made in China and allegedly killing dogs... literally
Text: A lawsuit filed in federal court following multiple dogs dying after eating Waggin' Train "Yam Good" dog treats and also Waggin' Train jerky tenders--produced and supplied by JOC Great Wall Corp. Ltd. of Nanjing, China for Nestle Purina Pet Care Co. If you love your dog, would avoid this product and others made in China.

Summary: Not something you'd eat for every meal, but not bad tasting.
Text:
I am one who loves very strong flavors and a lot of spice in my food. With that in mind, This sauce was incredibly rich tasting. Very creamy, with a distinctive taste of coconut. It's not the same as taking a mouthfull of fresh coconut or drinking coconut milk, but you can discern the sweet coconut flavor. I made Chicken and shrimp Korma last night, using extremely thin sliced chicken breast (the kind of cut most oriental places put in their moo goo pai pan and other chicken dishes) The shrimp was 31-40 count. I added some fresh steamed veggies to the mix as well, and put it on a bed of Basmati rice. I heated the sauce, dumped it over top, and served it family style.

I thought the combination of the sauce with chicken, shrimp, AND veggies all worked, so its a versatile sauce. I think it might go well with just about any meat or veggie option. It did wear on my towards the end of the dish, however, due to the richness. I would have prefered a bit stronger garam masala flavor, so I compensated and added a little into the sauce. I won't be making this all the time, but every once and a while its a refreshing taste in indian cooking. I still think I'll stick to Patak's vindaloo paste. That's become a staple in my house when I'm not in the mood to make curry pastes from scratch.
BEST PEANUT BUTTER EVER. I'm addicted to peanut butter, regardless. But this is super creamy... and just great. It doesn't taste like coconut, if you're worried about that. It's amazing.
The is a wonderful product that is more safe for all who use it.  Not DEET.  Thank goodness!!  Pleasant scent, easy to use but not easily found locally.

i was eacited to buy this hot sauce because of the high rating from an Americas Test Kitchen tast test & comparison. i was surprised to find it, although very tasty, it was very mild. i like very hot hot sauces so be careful. it appears that the Americas test kitchen tasters, though i value their opinions very much, are kind of wimps for hot sauce.

yuck, yuck, and yuck.  I ate about three of them and tossed the rest.  Don't even want to subject my tricker treaters to this GRAINY caramel!  They are just weak and sugary....no sense of caramel at all!
I'm a grad student and this has good taste, very cheap, saves a ton of time. I eat this with some other meat. I put half the flavor package, because the full pack is too spicy.
I first tasted this tea at PF Changs. I loved it so much, I made the waiter go and find out what brand and type it was, so I could buy my own. This is the best!

I was extremely happy to chance upon these in a health food store shortly before I was going camping. Like many of the other reviewers before me, I haven't had marshmallows in a long time because of my commitment to vegetarianism. These marshmallows can toast in the fire just like gelatin marshmallows do! Personally, I think they taste better because I always found gelatin marshmallows a little chalky. These seem less prone to becoming stale--I stored mine for a month after opening them, and they always tasted fine. You do pay more for these marshmallows, but the $11.99 I see on Amazon right now is even steeper than the price I paid. They were $4 or $5 at the health food store.

I love Marshmallows but i do not like the store bought ones too much and i usually try to get Kosher Marshmallows but they can be hard to get so i wanted to try Vegan and i must say i was pleasantly surprised! very good texture and very "clean" taste :) i will be getting more of these!

Taste is excellent, very good, but the size is too small. I wanted these for a campfire, but I couldn't find a big size marshmallow inside the package.  During summer time, it melts easily inside the package. Even though I kept them in the refrigerator until it was time for the campfire, I had to throw away 1/3 of the package, since it turned into a huge marshmallow sticky ball.  I paid $13 on an external website (including S/H). It was not worth it.  Next time I will try Sweet and Sara.

I've been a vegetarian for a little over six years now, and for the first few years I was really bad about looking for gelatin in the ingredients of things I used to eat. The past three years or so I've gotten much better, and was ecstatic to find this alternative to marshmallows that contained no animal products. I ordered two bags for some various baking recipes to try, and I ended up making only one batch of fondant and then eating the rest of these on their own! They are SO delicious! They taste a lot better than regular marshmallows, and I gave them to my entire family to try (none of whom are vegetarians or vegans) and they loved them. Great, great product. I will definitely be ordering these more in the future.

This is a special type of brown rice that adds pizazz to any meal. It's almost as special as wild rice: dark, very aromatic and has a dense, crunchy texture. Use about 2 cups water for each cup of rinsed dry rice (you can add a bit of butter for true luxury). Cook over a low flame; it may take a bit longer, but it's worth it. I don't use salt because I find the flavor satisfactory without it. If you find the rice is too crunchy for your taste, you can add a bit more water at the end of the cooking and heat gently.
PS Amazon's price for this rice is excellent.
Love this coffee. Has a great flavor. Delivery of this product was prompt. If you like the Amaretto flavor this coffee is for you. I highly recommend this coffee product.

I'm a huge fan of the pumpkin spice coffee that's being sold at starbucks.  It gets expensive, my bestfriend told me that coffee mate was selling this so I gave it a try.  I'm very impressed by the quality and taste, the only down side is 5 grams of sugar for 1 tablespoon.  I recommend to any one reading this to buy it but go easy on the teaspoons.

I love homemade chai tea mix with the Pumpkin Spice, I have substituted with the Gingerbread but it is not as good.  Unfortunately, last Fall I couldn't find the Pumpkin Spice in the grocery store. I am hoping this season it will be available!!

Seller was awesome, Product was the worst.  Has the texture of hard wax fruit and flavor of "Twizzlers", absolute garbage.  It is so hard to find a good Licorice product, and for the record, licorice is only one color, the red stuff is NOT licorice.  This stuff made it to the garbage pail.

We recently purchased seven unsweetened chocolate bars for comparison. The goal was to find an unsweetened chocolate that was so good (to snack on) that it didn't need sugar.  It does exist:  Pralus French 100% Cocoa: Criollo Chocolate.  The Schaffen Berger Unsweetened 99% Cacao Baking Chocolate Bar came in last. The most pure and tastefull cacao in the market rich chocolate flavor with out acidity. Excellent!!!!
Who relly want to have a impressive result in cooking, must try it.

I'm a huge chocolate fan, and I've eaten lots of different brands, ranging from the lower-end Lindt and Ghirardelli to the higher-end Valrhona and Neuhaus. I was frankly disappointed by the taste of this bar, which ended up being extremely dull for a very high cacao content bar. Even Ghirardelli's 100% cacao baking bar had a more exciting fruity flavor. The only redeeming quality of this bar is that it melts extremely smoothly and makes a really thick melting chocolate, which is good for those bakers and candy-makers out there. Not really great for tasting alone.

This item was received promptly and is exactly what I expected. It's a little pricey, but it was recommended by Rocco Dispirito (chef for "The Biggest Loser" TV show), so I HAD to have it. Haven't made his "black bean brownies" yet, but I'm sure they'll be great. This stuff smells like a million dollars!

We use this product on a daily basis in all our recipes. It works very well
as replacement for regular table salt, it's great in tomato sauces and great
on salads. We love it.

Summary: Can't get past the after taste
Text: The consistency is wonderful; the convenience is great, but I really don't like the aftertaste of this product.  It could just be a personal preference.  I'm reminded of green olives for some odd reason.
I like the combination of heat and content mix, this is very well suited for both dipping and cooking situations.

If you've ever had a Lindt Lindor Truffle, you know how rich, chocolatey and buttery they are. They literally melt in your mouth. This was an amazing deal and even though a treat that we don't do all the time, wonderful to have once in awhile...hard to keep them in the house, though!!

My little guy will not eat the supposedly tasty hard pills, so these chewy ones are perfect for him.  He thinks its an awesome treat, and if I skip a day or two, I see a huge difference in how he moves around.  He will be on this stuff for life, and at 39.99, its a great price!
My dog has been having trouble walking, she is 9, almost 10. She is a lot more active now and doesn't have trouble with her joints and walking

Summary: A big improvement over hard chews
Text: It used to be a big challenge to get my dog to eat the hard chews, especially when he was stressed from traveling or around other dogs. Now his supplement is his favorite treat, which has removed a small but daily hassle from my routine. I balked at the price initially, but it's definitely worth the cost for me.

Summary: Remarkable Product at a Great Price
Text: My 15-year-old, 50-pound mixed breed has only been on the Nutramax Dasuquin Soft Chews for just under 2 weeks and I'm amazed at how much better he seems to feel already.  He is lying down and getting up more easily and quickly along with walking around with a little more pep in his step.  My 8-year-old Pug, who has shoulder issues, is now walking around without even a hint of the limp she has had for a few years now.  I am encouraged by the progress they are both showing in such a short time and I am quite optimistic this could be the one thing I do for my dogs that greatly improves their quality of life.  The seller had a great price with super fast shipping, I only wish I had bought more at that time.

I have an 8 yr old poodle that tore her ACL jumping off the couch playing. The vet gave me some options: surgery or try these pills and see if they help.  In about 3 weeks she stopped limping. In 2 months she is playing around like she is a pup again.  I would recommend this product to anyone who has animals with muscle/tendon/ortho issues.

Good product, helps especially older dogs with joint problems, my 14 year old lab-Rottie was not walking because of hip pain... She started walking after we gave glucosamin/chondroitin to her.  Science Diet has older dog food with both, we feed her that and ....Dasquin really boosted her abilities and was introduced to us by the Vet.  It is interesting to see the price for the same product vary from $34 to $72 though!  You have to search and search to get a reasonable deal.
Purchased these to make homemade vanilla extract, and I was very pleased by the quality and quantity that arrived.  Prices for these are all over the place, but this one was good in every category.

This tea was so popular, that it's already disappeared from the Peet's website.  Mint might not be a flavor everyone will enjoy, but it's a very refreshing green tea.  It's worth trying it, just for the experience.

Summary: Del Prado Juices are the Best
Text:
I am from Panamá (PTY), so i was lucky enough to have this juice everyday in my lunch box and every morning 4 breakfast. The juice is DELICIOUS. You can know is high in pulp bc of its consistence/thickness.

I have been living in the US for 12 years, and, unfortunately, I cant find it here. Every time I go to PTY, I buy cases and cases to bring because my son also love it. Gracias por ofrecernos la oportunidad de comprar esto x acá. Sigue, por favor, vendiendo esto...

Tambien tengo una tienda x acá y sería bueno tenerlo en stock. así que sería para uso personal y negocio.
These were the best brownies that I've ever eaten. Very moist and the multiple flavors will delight your taste buds.

This is really good in coffee. I bought several flavors from the Capella company, and this is my favorite so far. For a 12 oz cup of coffee, I put in 9 drops, which worked out very well. I also added about a teaspoon of Wholesome Zero sweetner (awesome stuff). It probably doesn't need any sweetner at all.

I haven't tried this disolved in water. There are instructions for it, but I think Egg Nog flavored water would be weird since plain Egg Nog should have a creamy texture to it. A fruity flavor might be better.

This would be awesome in milk shakes.

I usually buy flavored coffee (whole bean), but I think I'm going to keep investing in this and just buy regular plain coffee. That way I can have any flavor I want without having to store several pounds of expensive coffee.

Summary: great snack for on the go
Text: My children (ages 2 and 6) both love Strawberry PUFFS! They are a great snack for on the go. My little ones are older than the "average Puff eater" :) and yet they ask for these all the time. The strawberry flavor is light, not too sweet. And the Puffs seem to melt in your mouth-- much softer than O cereals. I especially like that these Puffs have considerably less sugar than the other brands, the ingredients are natural and organic. I was also happy that the packaging is recycled and the lid is easy to open for pouring or for reaching in to grab Puffs. Overall love these Puffs and they are a MUST HAVE in our home! :)

Summary: Great Seasoning for Just About Everything!
Text: I first ran across these in the "rot box" at my local grocery. They were selling them out and would no longer carry them. I bought six or eight cans at a disgracefully low price and took them home. They have that wonderful almost tobacco-like smoky flavor similar to really good ancho peppers. The sauce is thick, pungent and slightly sweet. I often take a stick blender and liquefy the peppers and sauce into a paste. You can use it as a condiment (though it packs considerable heat), or a flavoring in sauces, soups, stews.......oh who am I kidding, this stuff is great on just about everything.

Lyons Gold Blend is my favorite tea because of it's rich and smooth flavor. It costs a bit more than grocery store brands, but each  tea bag easily makes three cups of tea. I've preferred the satisfying flavor of Lyons tea since Dublin friends introduced me to it many years ago. It is the preferred tea of my Irish friends, and I'm  pleased that I can purchase it in the USA.

These are cheaply made toothpicks that are overpriced. The coloring on the toothpicks is uneven. I bought them for party sandwiches, but the plain ones I buy from Sam's Club are better made, are much cheaper and actually look better than these.

Summary: Seems healthy, and dogs love it
Text:
I have a very picky Siberian Husky, who often leaves food in the bowl if she doesn't care for the taste or is bored by it. So far she's attacked the firstmate pacific fish kibble at each meal, and finished all of it. Our second dog, a border collie, also seems to prefer it to his regular kibble, which is castor & pollux organix.

I bought this at a local Seattle pet store called Mud Bay. I trust them to do well by their customers (all their suggestions have worked well for me), and they tend to keep better brands. They highly recommended it, and the dogs seem to agree.
I really enjoy the DRY Soda beverages.  My favorites are the low acidity options.  Cucumber is my favorite.  Very refreshing, and a great alternative to soda.

Worked better than the stuff a vet gave us for a problem that the dog chewed his skin off. This created a large bloody wound. The stuff we got from the vet required re-application daily but did not work all that well. This stuff was applied a couple of times at first and now once a week or 2 and all is well.

Summary: Best option for hard to find Chipotle Powder
Text: I looked everywhere for powdered Chipotle Chile Powder but couldn't find it, even in the specialty food stores in this area. I purchased this product knowing it wasn't a powder, in hopes that I could run it through my spice grinder and get the powder I need for my recipes.  It grinds beautifull, and just takes a few seconds. The quality of this product is excellent - just be sure you have a way to grind it for recipes.  Great value too since you get 3 jars.

These nuts are "Da Bomb". Not only are these awesomely flavorful and hot for us "hot heads" but they're also a fun prank for the people who are not. You know the ones I'm talking about. The ones who are too scared to even try a medium heat sauce.
Aside from the heat, and yes they are quite hot, they also taste real good. It's not so hot that you can't enjoy the peanuts. Anyway, I'm glad I have 6 cans! I'll be ordering again!
My husband cannot get enough of this cereal.  It is very chunky and hearty and nutty good.  It keeps you full for a long time.
I Love this cereal!  It is great in that the crunch stays and doesn't get too mushy in the milk.  It also has very full flavor and is very filling.

Summary: May Develop Rancid Flavor Due To Polyunsaturated Linolenic Acid?
Text:
If I store a box of this cereal for too long, I can detect a very slight rancid flavor in it. I am extremely sensitive to this; my friends and family can't tell and think I'm crazy. As long as you eat the cereal within two weeks or so of opening the box, this shouldn't be a problem!

The rancidity may be due to the flaxseed which contains polyunsaturated linolenic oils; while they are healthy, they are also highly prone to oxidation. While it is probably not a huge issue, research has suggested that oxidized oils may pose a cardiovascular health risk!
http://dx.doi.org/10.1111%2Fj.1745-4506.2001.tb00028.x
This may be a consideration for you if you are similarly sensitive and take a while to finish the six boxes in this multipack.

Summary: Excellent Coffee, but make sure you can store it!!
Text:
Before I begin let me just explain where I am coming from. Though I am by no means a coffee expert I have become a little more sophisticated just in the regard that I own a french press as well as a chemex cofffee maker and grind my own beans as well. Though I like some of the standard coffees out there (especially Peets), I am trying to broaden my horizons and try new coffees. I decided to give this brand a try just because I saw it was a top coffee seller on amazon and had received mostly postive reviews.

When I received the bag I opened it up and it smelled wonderful. as many coffee drinkers know,opening and smelling a new bag of coffee beans is almost as good as drinking the coffee itself. As for the coffee though, it was superb. I think the best way I can describe it is to say not too strong, but not too weak so it's perfect for someone looking for the best of both worlds. also, it is not as acidic as other coffees (which I understand is a common chracteristic of Sumatran coffee in general) so that was a positive for someone like me who loves coffee, but is always popping antacids.

There are a few things to keep in mind though. This is a huge bag! It's like 3 standard supermarket bags in one. so if you drink a ton of coffee a day or have a big family of coffee drinkers, that might not be a problem. However, for someone like me who is single and drinks one or two cups a day, it prevents a bit of a challenge. The instructions tell you to put the bag in a ziplock bag and refrigerate for prolonged storage, which is what I did. Two weeks later the coffee still tastes good, but not as fresh as when I first bought it and there is still over half the bag left! If anyone out there has any suggestions on how I should store this coffee other than refrigeration, please shoot me an email.

But other then that the coffee is great. Just make sure you realize you are going to get a lot of it unless there is a smaller bag for sale on amazon, which I do not think there is.

I really wanted to like this coffee and based on the other reviewers' ratings I was eagerly awaiting my shipment.  Unfortunately, for me this coffee although obviously super high quality is just too bitter in the brew for my taste.  I ordered this on subscription for repeat delivery certain that I would like it as I am a Sumatran coffee drinker but after trying several different grinds and methods of brewing this I just do not like the bitterness in these beans.

There's not really a whole lot more to say, this is simply a great coffee.  Due to its balance of top quality beans at a reasonable price point, it has become the daily staple coffee in our house.  I haven't tried their other varieties, but if the dark, earthy and herbal notes of Sumatra suit your taste, than Cafe Altura's Sumatra is a great option.

I like my coffee really strong, and with this coffee I can go from unleaded to jet fuel mode depending on how I feel. A lot of coffee can get very bitter and can even give you an upset stomach if you grind the beans too fine. Not this stuff.

With the average price of coffee going insanely higher, I think that given the quality and quantity, you get more than you pay for with this. I have had every kind of Starbucks coffee, and none even come close to this ..oh... and this is ORGANIC TOO! Why buy overpriced, average coffee, when you can get something like this?

Summary: Suprisingly good but bet you can't eat just one!
Text:
My wife and I were shopping in our favorite supermarket last week, and we found ourselves strolling down an aisle we usually avoid: the packaged-cookie aisle. (No way you can avoid all the fresh stuff in the bakery section, which is always conveniently placed in one of the first walk-through areas when you get in the store!) I pointed out all the space being taken up by all different varieties of Oreo cookies. We grew up knowing just one Oreo, the original, but we were aware that new varieties had come to market because our kids sometimes asked for them when they were growing up: double-stuff, especially.

The next day I was here on Amazon and saw the opportunity to try this new variety, the Oreo Fudge Cremes, Peanut Butter creme style, and I just had to have it. It got here quickly, and I just couldn't wait to have a good old Oreo snack. I ripped open the pinched end of the outside wrap, pulled out the tray, and saw chocolate. Nice milk chocolate coating. I popped one of these new Oreos in my mouth and was very pleasantly surprised. I don't usually love peanut butter in anything except sandwiches--not even in Reece's Peanut Butter Cups or even Reece's Pieces--but this was a very delicate peanut flavor with a good amount of milk chocolate around it and, of course, one thin Oreo wafer to give it the crunch (and the justification to label it an Oreo brand!).

Hmm. Mmm. I popped another. Then another. And another. I had to reach into the bag, because the cookies were in a plastic rack to keep them in place, or so they wouldn't melt into each other in transit, but the bag is a bit oversized for the tray and so many of the cookies flipped over and back further into the bag. (Wait, more on this later.)

Anyway, four quick cookies, small and light, but tasty. Just over 200 calories--not so great for people watching their weight. But tasty.

I worked through the bag over the next few days, always having to reach in over the rack to get to the cookies piled up in the back, but then yesterday I suddenly realized that there was a lift-back, "easy open pull tab" right across the top of the package that exposed the whole tray and that you could easily bring back down to seal the package with a lightly glued seal--very lightly, I might add. Think Post-It Note kind of stickiness. But very convenient and good thinking!!

Duh!

I peeled it back, and it works great to allow easy access to the cookies wherever they happen to have fallen inside the tray/wrapper.

I recommend these for a convenient taste treat, but be aware that they pack a lot of calories and saturated fat.

Serving size: 3 cookies (each a fairly small coated wafer)
Per serving:
170 calories
9g total fat, of which:
4.5 g saturated
1 g polyunsaturated
2.5 g monounsaturated
100mg sodium

Have a couple, but then lock them up for at least 24 hours and then dip in again!

Summary: Another Girl Scouts rip-off? But delicious!
Text:
Just like the Mint Fudge Creme Oreos are a doppelganger for the much-loved mint Girl Scout cookies, so too are these peanut-butter variants. And, like those mint versions, they are excellent, if small. Soft chocolate coats a small portion of peanut butter and a very crunchy cookie reminiscent of the original Oreo but obviously thinner and lighter. If you are like me, you will eat too many too quickly. It is far too easy to overindulge with these.

The only real disappointments here comes only in that these cookies are *small* for the current Amazon price - very thin and not very large in diameter for something that costs so relatively much - and the fudge is so soft that they had to be kept in the fridge at our house lest they melt right onto your fingers, making for a tremendous mess. Upside: they are excellent cold.

First of all I thought these were going to be Oreo sandwich cremes with peanut butter filling, covered in a fudge coating. Well, the inside is not a 'sandwich' creme - it's one Oreo disc with some kind of processed (to the point of no-peanut-flavor) cream inside, and the whole thing is then coated in fudge (which Oreo loosely uses to mean 'chocolate,' but I knew it wasn't really going to be real fudge). Because there's only one cookie inside each unit, the proportions are pretty gross - you get the medium firm texture of the outer chocolate layer, which is fine, but a single interior cookie is not enough crunch to set off the sort of lardy faux-peanut-butter layer. My son (age 10) ate a bunch and probably would have eaten more, but I'm more of a discerning customer when it comes to both chocolate and peanut butter, so I stopped after my 2 experimental ones. I do like plain Oreos, and the plain Oreos covered in the 'fudge' - but this combo just doesn't do it for me. It seems like it's just a typical processed sweet snack food with no real flavor.

The product ain't bad, not bad at all; crispy cookie, peanut butter layer (that same highly-processed and not-really-peanut-buttery stuff one finds in Reese's and peanut-butter-esque cookies), covered in fudge. With a hint of mint, mostly in aftertaste, which you wouldn't for a second think would go with peanut butter, but it actually works. What I question is the brand association. And I admit, this is probably a personal thing and you can switch me off right now, but come on. If it's an Oreo, it's got two cookies with stuff sandwiched in the middle, not one cookie with stuff piled on top. Yes, I admit that's a petty reason to dock it a star, but come on, is it an Oreo if you can't do the Oreo Twist(TM)?

I think these guys are good enough to break from the brand association and go it on their own. Would be a good idea, IMO.

Like the Oreo Fudge Mint Cremes 8.5 Oz. (Pack of 3), these have a THIN and wonderful layer of peanut butter (rather than mint), with a chocolate cookie, covered with luscious fudge coating.

Unlike the "girl scout" peanut butter cookies, these have JUST the right amount of peanut butter for my taste. But, I have to confess - I am on a DIET. Only 1200 calories a day. That's just about one package of these wonderful cookies (57 calories per cookie), and when I say wonderful, I really mean it. I finally passed them out to a group of kids I was teaching, just to get them out of my kitchen and out of temptation's way.

Since Amazon is having problems with the Vine badge on these, I do want you to know that I received this package to try through the Vine program.

Wonderful, WAY too wonderful ...

I love Oreos. I love peanut butter. I love chocolate. Seems like a no-brainer that I should like these cookies, but I didn't. They were ok at best. I thought maybe it was just me, so I had my kids give them a try. One of my sons didn't like them at all. The other son (who has more of a sweet-tooth) liked them a little. He liked them enough that he's going to eat more, but told me not to bring home any more. He'd rather have the original Oreos. If he was in the mood for PB & chocolate, he'd just rather have a Reese's.

The other thing I'd like to point out is that I wouldn't really even consider these "cookies". They contain more PB & chocolate than cookie. The cookie wafer is really thin and is just overpowered by the other 2 ingredients. And the peanut butter part had too soft a consistency and not enough of a peanut flavor..

Summary: A Little Goes a LONG Way!
Text: I didn't expect to like this as well as I do. It's crispy, with a salty-sweetness that I sometimes just CRAVE. The pouches are the perfect amount and you get a lot of flavor for 130 calories. I find them a bit TOO sweet though and I could never eat more than just one pouch in a sitting, which I guess is actually a benefit of the product...absolutely no temptation to keep eating.

If you are a fan of caramel corn (or crackerjacks), you will enjoy these. Essentially, they are a heavily covered caramel corn, drizzled over with just the right amount of chocolate.

I am trying to be specific about the level of caramel, since the brand I have been using is actually "kettle corn" with the chocolate, and taste quite different than these do. These are much sweeter, and really hit home when it comes to having a "sweet tooth."

Since they have 150 calories, you will need to be cautious about including them in your diet, but if you are a caramel corn fan, it will be well worth finding a place for these.

Okay, if all you are looking for is a GREAT tasting portion controlled snack and don't care about anything else then this is it!  I also like that the ingredients are pretty good, brown sugar, corn syrup, cocoa, popcorn, oil, vanilla, whey, noting terrible and all pretty darn natural.  BUT, we will not be buying these again which is why despite amazing taste and good ingredients I am only  giving it 3 stars.  First off, each box only has 5 pouches, so for a family of four one box is gone like in an instant.  Next and foremost, we try to limit sugar per serving on our sweetened cereals and snacks to no more than 9 grams, each of these Snackwell pouches has 18 grams of sugar!  We are used to eating Angie's Caramel Corn which for a whopping 2.5 cups serving size has only 9 grams of sugar and 150 calories.  If Snackwell really wanted people to 'snack well' they'd take Angie's caramel corn and drizzle fudge on that and put it into their little pouches to reduce the sugar per serving.

love, love, love it. Very fresh taste of chocolate on every kernal & extremly crunchy. I don't really taste the caramel though but the flavor is still so good I don't even care. You get 5 packages in each box and each package holds 2 large handfuls. If you hold it in your hand for more than a few seconds before putting it in your mouth the chocolate will start melting so put it in your mouth right away as you take it out of the package. I love popcorn and usually eat 3 to 4 popped quarts at a time so it's too expensive for me to buy but it sure was good.......

I opened these up expecting to find maybe 8-10 pieces of popcorn in a bag, but I was pleasantly surprised to find at least twice as many.  You really do get a delicious, sweet snack for only 130 calories.  however, the popcorn was a little chewy, perhaps the result of being left at my door on a rainy day by the mailman.

Summary: A nice low calorie snack option
Text:
This is a basic 130 calore snack pack option for those watching calories.
It has just enough of a chocolate drizzle to get your taste of chocolate, coupled with a smooth Carmel coating on the popcorn it is a nice option for those sweet tooth days.

Popcorn can be a healthy snack depending on how it is made and what you add to it. Adding caramel adds a lot of sugars and calories so I was surprised by how many pieces were in one of these 130 calorie packs. It was a good size amount, a small bowl worth approximately. The popcorn tasted fresh, it was crispy but soft at the same time. The caramel was very tangy, not overly sweet at all.

As some of my regular readers may know, I've been running a group called The Chocolate Cult for some time. If this was a review for that group, the number of stars would be lowered to two because this product fails when it comes to the chocolate. First, I noticed that the chocolate itself was slightly discolored which means it had some temperature problems -- not in my house because we know how to store and use chocolate -- which allowed some of the fat to rise to the top. Some folks say this doesn't affect flavor but I think it lessens the cocoa intensity.

If you want caramel popcorn, this was great. If you wanted a strong fudge flavor this was poor. They could lessen the calories and give us more of the caramel corn but just removing the drizzle entirely and it would taste even better.
I will definitely purchase these again!  If you like Cracker Jacks and you like Chocolate, you will love these.  They taste just like Cracker Jacks with a light chocolate drizzle.

The good news is that it comes in handy small packets rated at just 130 reasonable calories per.  It does make for one yummy snack and is highly recommended for its excellent flavor.

What could be better? Caramel corn drizzled with chocolate. YUM!

This comes packaged in individual servings each totaling 130 calories. If you can stick to just ONE pouch, you have more self control than I do. It satisfies my cravings for crunchy sweet and chocolate all in one snack.

Now, if I can just train myself to eat only one package!

It's a good thing these Snackwell Fudge Drizzle Caramel Popcorn bits are packaged in a portion control pack- otherwise you'd eat the whole box at one sitting.  My family is a big fan of Crunch N Munch which we can barely keep around when we get it.  This goes Crunch N Munch one better in that the caramel clusters of popcorn are lightly drizzled with a rich chocolate coating.  Much better than the milk chocolate than you'd find on your typical candy bar.  So, go ahead and grab a box. But, make sure you tell yourself you're only going to have one package when  you go to get them from the pantry.
I throughly enjoyed these tasty tidbits! They are a great sweet addition to a sack lunch or a stand alone snack. Just 100 calories!!!

Like another reviewer, I ordered this for my wife. We've both been counting calories for several weeks now and are always on the lookout for a low(er) calorie snack. So, having no prior experience with the Snackwell brand, I ordered these to give to my wife as a little treat with her lunch.

Her reaction? She loves them! They taste great and she loves that they come in a 130-calorie pack (it's easy to calculate into her daily log). Of course, her one complaint is that it's a little small, but what do you expect for 130 calories?

I'd like to state that I know this isn't a health or diet food--from a nutritional standpoint, it has too much sugar and is basically a waste of calories. But when you're on a diet, the occasional luxury goes a long way in being able to maintain your willpower, and this is a great tasting snack that won't bust your calorie count. Although at the current price per pack, it might bust your bank account.

Summary: I like popcorn, I like chocolate
Text:
I like popcorn and I like chocolate. So, these Snackwell's fit my bill. The funny thing about "low calorie packs" is that is really just about portion control. Cut a donut into 4 pieces, put each piece in an individual bag and congratulations you have snackpacks!

I did find these Snackwell's tasty though and so did my wife.

On the plus side: To me they really taste sort of like Cracker Jacks with some chocolate on top which turns out to be a very good combo. The small bag size is a plus by preventing me from zoning out in front of the TV and finishing a giant bag before it's too late to notice.

On the minus side: The bags are small relative to the price you pay. They are not that nutritional, the "snackwell" label could give you a false sense of healthiness that is only being mitigated by small bag size.

Overall, a good item to reach for occasionally from the snack menu - 4 stars.

I love tortilla chips as a snack. But they need a dip to live up to their full snack potential! There are a lot of bland dips/salsas out there that do not satisfy me very much. But this product does the job!

I enjoy Numi's Moonlight Spice Orange Spice White Tea. It has a distinctive orangey taste and a light spicy taste (from the cinnamon, cloves, allspice, and ginger), sort of like a light, subtle, orangey chai tea. It is different and unique and all of the flavors are much more subtle than a chai-type tea, quite adventurous. It brews for a lengthier time (7-8 minutes) and is worth the wait.

Moonlight Spice is kosher, certified organic and contains amazing ingredients: organic cinnamon, organic orange peel, organic cloves, fair trade certified organic Pai Mu Tan white tea, organic hibiscus, organic allspice, organic ginger, organic schizandra berries, organic lemongrass and dried lime. The schizandra berry is a major tonic herb in Chinese medicine used to assist the body in dealing with stress, to improve memory function, and to assist with many various physical issues.

There are no oils or natural flavorings used, unlike many teas; it is also sustainable in that all packaging materials are biodegradable and recyclable, the carton is made of 100% post-consumer waste, and cello wrap is not used. Numi says that all their tea bags "are made of natural fiber paper, not the trendy, "silky" see-though nylon tea bags".

On the box, the manufacturer writes: "Numi's Orange Spice White Tea is like no other. We use an abundance of all natural, organic ingredients for an authentic cup, without using oils or flavorings. This sublime tea ingeniously blends premium Organic White Pai Mu Tan tea with orange, citrus, and spice. Pai Mu Tan is exclusively the top two leaves and a bud of the tea plant and can only be picked the day before the buds unfurl. White tea is the least oxidized and processed of all teas, making it supremely healthy. Smooth and delicate, Moonlight Spice balances citrus notes of orange, schizandra, Numi's own Dry Desert Lime, and luxurious spice for the most divine experience. Transcend into a peaceful moment through its luminous hue and enchanting fragrance."

If you like Numi teas, get it---you won't be sorry. If you are new to Numi but enjoy white tea, this will probably be one of the best you've ever had.

The folks in the United Kingdom drink more PG Tips tea than any other brand, and perhaps after you try it; it will be your #1 choice, too! (By the way, the folks in Ireland drink more tea per person than in any other country.)

PG Tips Tea and PG Tips Special Blend Tea is our home's standard tea. There are a few specialty retailers in the USA that now offer the PG Tips Special Blend Tea and hopefully Amazon will do so soon.

In the 1930s (the pre-digestive era in history) this tea was introduced by the name "Pre-Gest-Tee" suggesting the tea could be consumed before food was eaten, but it was the grocers who gave it the abbreviation of "PG" - and the company added "tips" (since the company uses only the best part of the tea plant, the two top leaves and bud of the tea plant to make the tea).

Many black teas sold in the USA are graded the basic medium grade Orange Pekoe (generally the tea leaves below the top two and bud), which is one of the reasons PG Tips gets higher reviews than most other teas. PG Tips also uses their pyramid tea bag that allows ample room for the tea to expand as it is infused. Additionally, in my opinion, PG Tips blends only two blends, rather than blending a wide assortment, thus becoming really good at what they do.

Here at Amazon PG Tips is priced at just over a nickel a tea bag (a good value for an imported product) when you order the 240 count boxes in a set of two, and even less expensive in the higher volumes. PG Tips makes wonderful ice tea too, and that's good news since Americans drink about 80% of their tea as iced tea and only 20% as hot tea. Worldwide more hot tea is consumed than iced tea, and worldwide tea is the most consumed beverage (next to water), while in the USA it is the sixth most consumed beverage (next to water).

A very good question to ponder is "Why this is?"

Drinking an adequate amount of tea daily is now being considered to be very good for one's health, and it is much more enjoyable to drink a really good cuppa (cup of tea), especially at the nominal cost of about a nickel a cup when compared to one of those gourmet coffee places who charge upwards of four to five dollars for a large cup of coffee.

When we have a guest in our home we always offer them a PG Tips cuppa, and they always say they have never tasted a tea this good - thus, I rate it 5 stars for its quality and very nominal price!

This is the best tea available and I am so glad I have found it available on Amazon.  Back in the day I used to have to drive all over town to find an English store and then pay exhorbitant prices for some English tea.  You might guess I am English and a total tea junkie but it has to be P.G. Tips because it is the greatest.  It always tastes great, you can make it mild or strong, add honey or milk or sugar and still have great tea flavour. I drink four or five pots of tea a day and P.G. Tips never dissapoints.
I am very pleased with the flavor, body, and strength of this tea.  My husband & in-laws are from England, so I have to be quite picky about what tea I serve.  PG Tips passes with flying colors!

Leave it to the British to produce the best tea on the whole planet. I don't know anything about the types of leaves it contains, but I know that I look forward to getting out of bed each morning and starting the day with PG Tips. If you have a sensitive stomach, you already know that both coffee and tea can sometimes leave you nauseated with the acidity level. Lipton, Tetley, and most other US supermarket brands are guilty as charged on the upset stomachs. Not so with PG, and it has a smooth, lovely taste that is delicious to the last drop whether you steep your tea for exactly 3 minutes, or if you leave your tea bag in the cup like I do. The only other tea I have found comparable is Harney & Sons Big Red Sun in the red tin, costing $8 per 40-count box. With Amazon's subscription I am stocked for the next 6 months at a fantastic price. I bought the 40-count boxes so that I could leave more tea sealed for a greater amount of time; if you go through 3 or 4 cups a day, look into boxes with larger counts. I store my open box in a ziplock bag in the cupboard and it is good every single time. It really is the best English Breakfast/British Breakfast style tea available, and you will never go back to Lipton's floor sweepings after trying this tea.

This is the first time I ordered this tea. I ordered based on reviews. Has a very good flavor. Me and My wife love the flavor and how it tastes. Has a feel of Indian tea. This is the recipe I follow to make two cups of tea. Comes out good everytime.

- One and a half cup of water.
- Half cup of 2% milk.
- Mix them and bring to a boil in a pot.
- When it starts boiling, add two bags of P.G tips tea.
- Bring the heat down enough to just keep boiling slowly.
- After boiling bags for 30 seconds to a minute (depending on how strong you want), gently lift tea bags out of the pot using a spoon and discard.
- If you like it stronger, gently squeeze the tea bags before taking them out of the pot.
- Add one (or more) spoons of sugar and stir.
- Ready to serve.
This tea has been my favorite black tea since I lived in England. It turned me into a tea snob. I just can't drink any other tea on a daily basis.

I am not a fan of Lipton or Tetley teas and rarely drink either. If I'm out and served these as iced tea, that's fine, I just don't order these when they are the only choice for hot tea. After reading reviews and researching the company, I ordered PG Tips Black Tea and I'm sure glad I dove into this liquid. Watching their ad on YouTube actually persuaded me to give it a try because I enjoyed the humor.

Packaging offers minimal waste in thin cardboard and cellophane. Yay! Tea bags are slightly perforated for easier flow and a pouch like shape with no string attached. Yay! Bags contain more tea than most other bags. Yay! I place one bag in my trustworthy Numi Signature Glass Teapot and pour in boiling water. The leaves infuse immediately and there is no residual powdery tea when I spoon out the swollen teabag about 3 or 4 minutes later. The color is rich, deep amber that leans toward red. The flavor is rich as well, with no tannins like I get from other "table" teas. Because I don't like my tea very strong, I pour some of the liquor into my cup, add more boiling water, and have about 3 to 4 cups of hot tea from the one teabag over a period of an hour or so. Each tastes fresh and full, without tannins developing. It also makes great iced tea by brewing 2 or 3 teabags in a pitcher, removing the bags and sprinking in a couple packets of Splenda to dissolve, then adding loads of ice. Again, the color is beautiful.

PG Tips aids in my digestion, too, but I tend to have it following meals rather than prior to eating as it was originally marketed in England. I've added milk and was reminded of Thai tea after sweetening it in the cup. So many times the color of tea looks gray when milk is added, so it's retention of the lovely amber color is another advantage of PG. I have not tried this yet, but I imagine it would also be great with lemon and honey, especially when I'm suffering with a cold.

I'm happy Amazon offers these bags in so many options and look forward to summertime when I'll be preparing pitchers and serving this as tall refreshing glasses of fresh iced tea. It's more economical than my usual premium teas, too! I only wish Amazon would offer it in the decaf variety.

Summary: A wonderful blend of granola; too bad nutrition facts betray the serving size
Text:
It has been my experience that granola has come a long way since I was a little kid. My only real memory of granola was the bars and they were alright. Now in modern times, granola is a versatile food item, finding its home on yogurt, as salad toppings, in baked goods and yes still in bar form (but even those are fancier). The one pratfall that most granola suffers from is a high fat and calorie count. I have tried other top shelf brands of granola that is promoted as healthy and it really isn't.

This leads us to "Eat. Think. Smile's" brand of granola. There are several different flavors that ETS showcases, this is the blend is "cinnamon almond". The staring flavors/ingredients are cocoa, whole grain oats, almonds and cinnamon. The granola has a wonderful taste. The flavors really blend well together, giving it a nice nutty and sweet balance. The texture is crunchy with a slight chewy aspect. In addition, since these are clusters, they would be great as salad or yogurt toppers and wonderful in baked goods.

This product is all natural which is good, but this doesn't always translate to a healthy product. A serving size is a third of a cup and is 160 calories and 6 grams of fat. Personally I feel that is high for such a small amount. Therefore, one needs to be careful not to eat too much of it. In contrast, this product has no trans fat and cholesterol. An interesting side note, I put some of this granola in a Pyrex container and it became a little stale. Which is odd considering Pyrex containers are pretty much air tight.

Overall, I really like this product. It is much better than most granola I have tried, but it must be noted that this isn't a health food. Actually, most granola isn't healthy, all natural or not. However under moderation, this is a good snack and I am sure there are worst things out there to eat.

Summary: Switching baby from exclusive breast fed to this formula at 1 year!
Text:
So I know that it is ok to give a baby cow's milk at 1 year old, but I have exclusively breastfed and my son has never had any formula or cow's milk before 1 year. So I am transitioning to this, it has more vitamins than regular milk, it doesn't stink like formula (while it doesn't smell great, but I'm used to breast milk) and I think it is a healthier option than giving him regular whole milk. I am still weaning---down to 2 nursing sessions a day) but I am doing 50% breast milk with 50% formula and he seems to like it fine! The first time I tried it, he furrowed his brow a couple of times but still drank 4 oz (I have never been able to get my son to drink more than 5 or 6 oz from a bottle). So we are very pleased, I am going to taper him over to this gradually from breast milk so hopefully he will have no problems and will hardly notice the transition. I'm planning to do 70% formula to 30% breast milk next week and then just straight formula, depending on how long my breast milk stash lasts.

I honestly believe the hardest part in introducing any food/milk is patience and consistency. I think I have put peas and sweet potatoes in front of my son 8 times until one day he decided he would eat it. I think so much of it is nutrition training...

Summary: DO NOT BUY - Contains high levels of arsenic
Text: As some of the other reviewers have noted, Baby's Only Organic Formula contains high levels of arsenic. I would love to have exclusively breastfed, but, due to a low milk supply that couldn't meet my baby's needs, I have to supplement with formula. I did a ton of research before buying Baby's Only and thought I was giving my baby the next best thing to breastmilk. I didn't want to buy Earth's Best because it contains hexane. Baby's Only was the only organic formula I could find without hexane. So I was appalled when I learned that Baby's Only dairy formula tested for high levels of arsenic (read the story on the Boston Globe's website: "Arsenic hidden in baby formula, cereal bars, and energy shots?") due to the brown rice syrup in it. Baby's Only hasn't issued a recall, voluntary or otherwise. I cannot believe this formula is still being sold. DO NOT BUY BABY'S ONLY. I ended up ordering another organic formula called Holle from a website in Germany. It's not available in the US, but the international shipping cost was worth it for my baby's health.

Nature's One, the company that makes Baby's Only, has done nothing but lied, deceived, evaded and deflected blame since the arsenic finding was publicized. They're not even regulated by the FDA, though their reps will tell you they are if you call them! I wish I'd never heard of this company. Roll the dice with another brand. This one can't even be considered the best of the worst.

In other words.. Do not feed to newborns or infants!

I'm reading about all these babies reacting with constipation, and as a mother of 3, it makes me feel bad that those babies have to go thru all that pain!

C'mon people! A little bit of common sense isn't gonna hurt.

After doing months of research on all different formulas, I decided to go with Baby's Only. If you read the overwhelming amounts of positive feedback from satisfied moms, the choice is clear. Summary: Arsenic in Formula? I am waiting this one out
Text:
Like most moms when I read and saw the arsenic report by Dartmouth College, I was upset and terrified. I have been supplementing my baby's diet with 2 bottles a day for over a month now since I don't seem to produce enough milk any more. Before I chose a formula, I spent 2 days researching different options until I settled on Baby's Only. Hence, when I learnt about the findings, I was angry and felt deceived. After some more research, I decided to stick with this formula and this is why:

1. There is no real alternative. Similac, Enfamil or Earth's Best? Those have their own issues - from BPA to Hexane.
2. Sabotage on Organic food?
3. This is a response by Professor Brian Jackson that headed the Dartmouth Research team responsible for this discovery:

SHORT ANSWER:
"Sorry, so many telephone calls and e-mails; try to reply as quickly as I can. Yes, that is the brand but please don't be alarmed, these are not acutely toxic levels and this is a short exposure duration. Blood tests are not necessary. Arsenic does not accumulate in the body and is excreted within 2 - 3 days; this is why long term (decades to lifetime) is where we have data for risk."

LONG ANSWER:
"We found 10 ppb inorganic arsenic (30 ppb total arsenic) in the diary formulas, 15 - 25 ppb inorganic in the soy formulas. These were two cans for each product (different lot numbers) obtained from our local COOP; how representative they are of all lots of the product over time is not known, but from what we know about the range of arsenic in rice and therefore possible ranges in syrup, I'd say that much higher concentrations are quite unlikely. The levels we detected for the dairy are either equal to the safe drinking water limit (if we just consider inorganic arsenic, which, at least for juice is what the FDA would say), or 3X the limit if you consider total arsenic. For the soy they are 1.5 - 2.5 X the level for inorganic arsenic and 3 - 6 x the level based on total arsenic. Remember the drinking water limit is set assuming you'll get a lifetime exposure at that concentration; so we don't know what risks are associated with low level, limited duration exposures (in fact that is a main research aim of the groups I work with here at Dartmouth). I have been advising people not to be alarmed; if they are concerned about arsenic exposure via formula then to consider switching to a formula where rice syrup is not the main ingredient (until such time as we have standardized testing of these products). I also recognize that there are many factors that go into choosing a formula and that this is really a decision for the parents in consultation with their pediatrician.

To further put this into perspective these are similar concentrations to those we encounter for people in New Hampshire (also Maine) who are on private well water and have slightly elevated concentrations of Arsenic (due to our local geology). We encourage people to have their water tested and assist them to reduce water arsenic concentrations if it tests high."

There is a thread on Babycenter.com about this topic. [...]

My conclusion: I am sticking with Baby's Only formula for now because I don't know what other brand I would switch to. I wish I could exclusively breastfeed him...:(

Summary: Makes a truly great Microwave casserole
Text:
One 5 ounce box of the Betty Crocker Cheesy Scalloped Skin-On Potatoes makes a truly delicious potato casserole that will serve four. For me this has become a time machine to a long forgotten comfort food.

Ingredients
Half cup margarine (Smart Balance)
one cup diced onions
one 8.5 oz can sweet corn or peas
2.5 cups water
1 cup 1% milk

Directions
in a microwavable sauce pan place Milk, Water and Margarine
Microwave on high for 5 minutes
Place corn (or peas) in strainer and rinse in running water
Whisk cheese packet into the hot water sauce mix
Add onions, corn (or peas) and potato packet
Microwave at 70% power for 5 minutes then stir
Repeat the heating and stirring 2 more times
let cool for 5 minutes

Summary: So small...couldn't hurt to eat just a few...so very small...
Text:
So here's how it went down.

My teenage sons crowd around with innocent curiosity as I take the mammoth 5-pound bag out of the cardboard box, the box with the beguiling Amazon smile on the side. That knowing, wicked Cheshire grin. Within seconds the bag is neatly cut open. An oddly hypnotic aroma wafts out.

It begins.

We all sample one or two of the pleasantly rubbery candies, but find ourselves exchanging the same puzzled expression: that flavor---not really cola...vaguely medicinal, yet not offensive. Hmm. Further testing is required.

We all sit down. Sampling continues now in earnest---they're so small! Where's the harm?---and we agree that you need to eat quite a few to identify the flavor with any accuracy. Not a name brand cola, to be sure...one of those "store brands," after it's gone flat. We notice that after the first 50 or so, the flavor seems to change somewhat, perhaps because all our teeth are now caked with adherent masses of gummy residue. Our mood is high, so testing continues.

General consensus is reached after the first pound or two that the bottles in the middle of the mass are softer and more fragrant than the stuff from the top of the bag. The bag is passed around, sniffing ensues. Great effort is expended seeing how far a bottle can be stretched, while held between the front teeth, until it breaks.

The unmistakable signs of hyperglycemia ---exhilaration, rapid speech, a cola-like aroma on the breath---go somewhat unnoticed as we burrow deeper into the jiggly wad of gummies. Dinner is postponed along with homework. A telephone call from my ex-wife goes unanswered. The scientific process cannot be interrupted. Would Fermi have taken time out from inventing the x-ray deathgun to take a call from his ex-wife? Please.

The fun almost stops when a bottle goes up a nostril ---kids!--- but everything is soon back on track when we discover that moistened bottles can be stuck to the forehead for minutes at a time. Soon my sons' faces bristle with the things. A joke is made about "edible lesions". Hilarity ensues. Photos are taken. Outside it grows dark while leaves blow about, unraked. The scratching of a pet at the door stopped some time ago.

Bottles are eaten ten at a time now. Cola-stained spittle dribbles down a chin. No time to wipe. Got to keep chewing. They are SO VERY SMALL.

Suddenly the bag is empty.

Empty. The room goes quiet. The box is re-examined, but no stray gummies are found. The box with the grin. That damn, mocking grin. I have to explain to the children why I only ordered one 5-pound bag. We all feel somewhat sick. We are all trembling now.

Parents, sometimes single dads cannot be trusted to make good judgments about their kids' eating habits. Living with the stress of alimony can pervert that part of the mind which regulates dietary choices, or common sense.

I hope this will serve as a valuable object lesson for you all.

Summary: From Cane Grown in Volcanic Ash
Text:
I first found this sugar while working at Larry's Market in Seattle. The India Tree company is also located in Seattle. It was one of the greatest food discoveries I'd forgotten about. Well, not quite. I just had no idea why the sugar we ate in Africa was so rich and similar to molasses in color. This sugar is milled on the island of Mauritius off the coast of Africa and has the divine flavor only possible from cane growing on volcanic ash.

Here in America, most of the brown sugar seems like white sugar coated in a brown coloring in comparison to this rich, dark and almost seductive slightly salty tasting sugar. When I found this sugar, it brought back tons of childhood memories. Mostly memories of eating a spoonful of sugar as a treat. This sugar is "that" good.

Muscovado is slightly moist, has a very high molasses content and is delicious in gingerbread, coffee cakes, chocolate cakes and anything with chocolate in it. You can basically use this sugar in any recipe that calls for "dark brown sugar."

When making cookies, you will notice some of the lumps don't quite work themselves into the dough. This is no problem, because then you just find a few sugar lumps in your cookies. If you prefer your sugar to be perfectly soft, you can add a piece of apple or bread to your sugar jar until the sugar softens.

This is one of my "Top Ten" ingredient finds of the century.

~The Rebecca Review

I am just learning to bake bread because we are living in a small US city this year which, while it has a terrific local cuisine and lots of organic ingredients and bakeries, did not have any authentic tasting semolina bread, which happens to be my favorite.  I found a recipe online and thought I'd give it a try.  I already knew from long experience that it was always best to buy dry pasta that was "made in Italy" if you wanted the best taste and texture -- US made pasta has a tendency to go from undercooked to overcooked mush in less than a minute -- Italian pasta is more forgiving.  Anyway, for my first batch of dough, I used this Bellino semolina and, while it wasn't perfect (I needed to make many adjustments in the recipe due to the very high altitude here), the taste was really good, very authentic.  For the next batch, I used a bag of Bob's Redmill(?) semolina because I found it at the local Whole Foods store.  The first two loaves I baked were so tasteless compared to the original ones I made, and I couldn't understand why since I had finally gotten the texture right in spite of the high-altitude complications.  Then I remembered that the Bellino semolina was from Italy, and the Bob's stuff wasn't.  Indeed the dough looked fine, but when I tasted even the raw dough, it lacked the rich creamy taste of real semolina.  My advice: don't mess around with semolina that's not from Italy if you're making pasta or bread!  Just like New York bagels, you really can't get the right result if you don't have ingredients from the right place.

What I did notice from using just a generic brand that the cats soon lost interest in the toys that they were playing with after the catnip shake-up in the plastic bag. This cycle of play continued until I decided to try another catnip brand. Sojos Certified Organic Catnip is only slightly more expensive, but it was worth the shot. I wanted my cats to enjoy their toys and to use some of that hunting instinct that's in all cats, in a more constructive manner. By using this hunting instinct a cat feels more like a cat and is a happier cat. One of a cat's purposes in life has been fulfilled. They feel more confident, their tails are up in the air, and they don't use you for their hunting instinct. Which mean less scratches to you and your cat opens up for petting, especially when they expose their underside to you for a quick petting.

When you own a cat you have to have things around the house that makes your cat a confident, well balanced mentally, playful, and wanting to be around you as your protector. The Sojos Catnip works very well to help give your cat a feeling of confidence. Thus, your relationship with your cat is better for you and definitely better for your cat. This catnip works well for a 5 star rating.

Addendum: 9/17/11 I've ordered this catnip several times and when the package arrives at the door, my cats let me know the catnip has arrived. My cats will pace at the door and make a figure 8 and their tails will be straight up in the air, noses sniffing at the door, with a specific cheerful speech announcing to me that I need to open the door. After I open the shipping package, they play for hours with the box. This catnip is that good. I've never seen that type of response to a catnip product as I do with Sojos Certified Organic Catnip. For playful, cheerful, energetic cats all I can say is the proof is in the cats response.

This product was one of my first forays into the "molecular gastronomy" field of cooking. I was apprehensive, because I've never been good at chemistry (although I'm a very good cook -- go figure).

Tapioca maltodextrin is a chemical used to make powders out of fat. For example, adding the chemical to olive oil or melted butter will allow you to make olive oil powder or butter powder. I bought it because I wanted to try making a powder from aged cheddar cheese. Well, it failed to do that, but I have no idea whether it was *supposed* to work with cheese, so I can't give it a great positive or a great negative mark.

The tapioca maltodextrin powder is very light, so if you open the bag and inadvertently jostle it too much, the powder will go flying everywhere. It's best to open the bag, measure out what you want, and then seal the bag back up again.
