Summary: The salmon is not what I hoped - Everything else is not bad
Text: The crackers, fruit and nut mix, the dry roasted edamame and the dark chocolate were OK. The salmon was oily yet it did not taste natural. It was also a relative small share of the entire box package. This is definitely a small snack even for one person. Like other reviewers, I would compare it to airline food.

The first thing I want to mention is that this package - consisting of a chili-lime-salmon spread, organic crackers (think Ritz-type crackers), dry-roasted and salted edamame, an organic dark chocolate square, and a fruit-nut mix - comes with a plastic fork, but no knife. Struck me as kind of weird - spreading the salmon mixture with a fork? One doesn't really need either utensil for the rest of it, unless one puts it all together in a bowl or something. One could also carp with GoPicnic's use of the word "meal" in the name - this is definitely a snack, not a meal, though it's a decent-sized snack.

Secondly, the fruit-nut mixture contains peanuts, as well as dried bananas and cranberries, with ginger flavoring. I am allergic to peanuts, so I didn't try this part of the product. While the fine print on the bottom of the box and the side (under the nutrition info) mentions this clearly, it's not stated on the front or back of the box. Just a minor caveat - it does say "nuts" and anyone with nut allergies of any kind will know to read the fine print.

That said, the rest of the product is quite nice. The salmon spread is quite salmon-y, and one can detect some hints of both the chili and lime, though I wouldn't say it's strongly spicy by any means. It's got a nice texture, not grainy but not too mushy either, and tastes fresh enough, and the crackers are light, buttery and crisp. The edamame are fine, also fresh and crunchy, and it's nice that they use sea salt instead of table salt. The chocolate is strong - maybe not intense enough for hardcore chocolate nuts, but it was fine for this chocolate liker (not lover).

The nutritional info on the package as a whole claims that it provides 44% of daily fiber, and 28% sodium, with 410 calories - so it's a good energy source without having a huge amount of salt, despite all the nuts and fish and crackers. The package is supposed to be shelf-safe for several months; I just got it so I can't vouch for that but I'll probably save one of the six boxes for a few months and update then, if there's any deterioration in quality before the expiration date.

This isn't typically the sort of product I buy; had I not gotten it through Vine I don't know that I would have ever tasted it. But it's a nice snack overall, and apart from not being able to eat the fruit/nut mixture I have no significant issues. I would definitely consider other products in this line, particularly if I can eat all the elements in the box!

When I saw the size of this "picnic in a box" (only 4.4 ounces), I didn't expect much. Was surprised at how good everything tasted and how filling and satisfying it was.  For a child who doesn't eat much, this might be a perfect meal on a picnic.  While I wouldn't call it an adult meal, it's a great snack.  The dry roasted edamame was crunchy and delicious, but a bit on the dry side.  Not quite as tasty as peanuts, but a lot healthier.  The Ginger Zip fruit and nut mix was really good; wish there had been more of it.  The main course is crackers with Chili Lime Salmon Spread, which was adequate, but nothing special.  A child might not like it because of the slight spiciness.  For dessert, there is a nice and very good tasting dark chocolate square.  Except for the sodium, which was a little higher than I would have liked (660mg), this seems pretty healthy (no trans fats, no high fructose corn syrup, no MSG.)  The real beauty of these little picnics is that they are not perishable, are very compact to carry and come in a convenient box that you can re-close if you don't eat everything at one time.  I would stock a few of these up as emergency provisions, as they are nutritious and tasty, probably have a long shelf life and you won't go hungry in an emergency when you have no power to cook anything.  Great idea, but a slightly larger version might be better.  They are worth trying.  Seems like a good meal for diabetics who are supposed to eat frequently for their meal or snack in between the main meals of the day.

Summary: Crunchy and Fun but Pack a Drink Also
Text:
I found the GoPicnic Salmon & Crackers lunch to be a cut above most commercially packed lunches in flavor and nutritional value. With only 410 calories, it still made a satisfying meal with lots of "chew appeal". The dominant texture was crunchy: crackers, fruit and nut snack and the little bag of dry roasted soybeans each made a different crunchy noise in the mouth. The banana chips in the fruit snack were quite hard and the soybeans (called edamame on the package) needed lots of chewing. The latter were dry to the core and lightly salted so when chewed they gradually ground to powder in the mouth and provoked thirst. I remembered eating these (in a fresher version) in Japanese bars. The salmon spread is brightly colored, spicy hot and is a great foil for the soybeans which are neutral underneath the light salting. The crackers are delicate and make perfect platforms for the salmon. The dark chocolate is excellent--a very pure flavor, not too sweet.

Although salt is not laid in with a deliberately heavy hand, nearly everything here has salt in it. Because one box contains 660mg of sodium, this isn't designed for folks on a low salt diet. I'd definitely pack a drink of fruit juice if this was to be my lunch box for the day or/and add an apple or orange to counterbalance the dryness of this portable lunch. Beer would work also but might not be practical...

Summary: Great concept, nice snacks, not quite a picnic...
Text:
Growing up on the free lunch program at school I wasn't exposed to the unhealthy treats and convinience foods of my peers until I was in my teens. Maybe that's part of why I prefer a warm soup with toast or a sandwich piled with veggies over peanut butter sandwiches and pudding cups. Keeping that in mind I thought this version of the Ready-to-Eat Meal would suit my palate and fill my tummy nicely.

I'll admit, I love novelty and there's just something about single-serving packaging that makes me all excited. Lime-chili Salmon Spread? Snack mix with Ginger Peanuts? It all sounded so fancy and grown-up. But then I looked at the outer package's nutritional info. At 400+ calories for this handful of snackage I was a little leary. Lots of fat (though I'd say with salmon some of it is the good kind) and lots of fiber. Read the nutrition info and you be the judge whether this would be for you.

Let me offer my assessment of the individual food items. The crackers were perfect, just the sort of thing I'd want to put a spread on, crisp and mild in flavor, solid enough to handle being topped. The salmon spread was nice in theory but had a (for lack of a better word) sludgey quality to it. I didn't taste lime and the chili was barely noticable, this felt like someone had tossed raw salmon in a blender and canned it. I was not impressed and I am a salmon LOVER. The Edamame were too dry but not overly salted as some can be. The portion on those was pretty big and since they aren't my favorite alone I was happy to move on. The mix of dried cranberries, banana chips and ginger peanuts was interesting and actually pretty yummy. The portion size looks like a lot on the box but was actually much smaller. My one complaint was that most of the ginger was rubbed off the peanuts and had settled into the bottom of the package. Lastly, the dark chocolate was a nice treat at the end, a decent quality and with a great texture.

Overall this was not quite my cup of tea. Aside from my comments regarding the individual items I must say I was still hungry after my GoPicnic. This would make a nice item to toss into your bag for a post-gym nosh if you're a lunch-time gym-goer or a good thing to pack when taking that dreaded family road trip so you could skip the fast food. I'd probably pick a different pack for myself but overall I really dig this idea and think the options in these being fruit, whole grains and healthy protiens are brilliant.

gopicnic is a more healthy version of the Lunchables that are so popular, and this variety is quite good.

For allergy sufferers, the warnings for all the internal packets are printed clearly on the side of the box under the nutrition information. Similarly, all the ingredients are on an end panel, and I can pronounce all of them. I like the lack of MSG, trans fats, or the dreaded HFCS.

Everything in the package was fresh tasting and flavorful. The light crispy crackers have a Ritz-like flavor. Salmon spread had a good flavor with nice spice bite, but not overpowering. A knife would have been a better implement, rather than the included plastic fork, for spreading the salmon. The ginger zip fruit & nut mix was also fresh crispy, but I didn't detect much ginger flavor, even in the bits of coating that had come off the nuts. The edamame was crispy and crunchy, lightly salty. The chocolate square is a nice dark chocolate, but not bitter.

With the addition of a beverage of your choice, this would make a healthier option for lunch than a trip to the burger joint or the vending machine.

The only down side to this type of meal is the amount of packaging. While the carton is made of 100% recycled fiber (at least 35% post-consumer) and can go into the recycling bin, everything else goes in the trash. Even that, though, is a minimum. The only plastic is the cup for the salmon and the fork. The rest is cellophane or foil wrap.

Though a homemade lunch may be cheaper this isn't a bad alternative.

Summary: Good tasting source of fiber Best place to purchase
Text:

Tasting as good as they do also make it an easy way to do so especially with all the chocolate they are much like a candy bar with fiber. These are my favorite bars of their type. Amazon has had the best consistent pricing on these vs local stores. If you subscribed to have them delivered every month or two or three, it is your choice, you get an additional 15% discount which is obviously the way to go. Do watch though as prices may fluctuate and you may find that the deal on the 5 pack version is priced lower or vice versa the 10 pack may be priced lower as is currently the case, however it is for exactly the same number of bars. If you sign up for the subscription delivery and find that the price has changed or one of the other box sizes is a better value I have changed so that I am getting the same best deal. Amazon has always been easy to work with so just keep an eye on pricing and call them before being billed when it is about time for your delivery.

That said these are not completely health food bars. I have recently started a fairly strictly healthy diet and am using some things such as cracked Flax seed in my diet to increase fiber. I still eat these bars a bit like candy from time to time and they are not bad and the best of their type. There are however even healthier (and less expensive ways) to add fiber to ones diet. I simply add the seeds to a healthy smoothie or oatmeal which are a major part of my daily diet.

But since this is a review about the bars they taste good and have lots of fiber and are priced well here so worth trying and getting here if this is the type of product you are interested in.
They are low in calories, high in fiber and taste really good. And I don't have any upset stomach or "other" issues like I have gotten with Fiber One bars in the past.

I have used dandruff shampoo for most of my life. It seems as though I have tried most of the dandruff shampoos that exist. Though it seems like some of them occasionally work, they do not seem to work all the time. Consequently, I have used Head & Shoulders literally for decades. When the opportunity came to try a new dandruff shampoo, I was all for it.

The very first thing I noticed about this shampoo is that it seems very thick, much thicker than any shampoo I can recall using. I tried trusty Head & Shoulders for comparison a couple of times. My perception seems to be reality. Clear Men Scalp Therapy shampoo is noticeably, pleasurably thicker than Head & Shoulders shampoo.

The next thing I wondered about is the smell. Head & Shoulders smells like - well - shampoo. While the smell is relatively mild, it is nothing special. In contrast, I think Clear Men Scalp Therapy has a pleasant fragrance. I did have to hold the shampoo close to my nose to smell it because the smell is not overly strong and does not fill a room with its odor, which is a positive attribute in my mind.

I could say something about how well the shampoo cleans, but it cleans like shampoo. My hair felt soft and clean, which is how it should feel. It also felt clean a second day after I used it.

The magic question with respect to this shampoo is how well it does with respect to dandruff. Well, it seems to work about the same as Head & Shoulders. Since the dandruff-fighting ingredient in Clear Men Scalp Therapy is the same ingredient that is in Head & Shoulders, it should hardly be surprising that both shampoos work the same with respect to fighting dandruff.

This shampoo also has a bunch of miscellaneous stuff that falls under the heading of nutrients and botanicals. I am unable to tell much about the effectiveness of these various ingredients. The ingredients sound impressive, but your hair is dead and I am unsure as to the effectiveness of fertilizing your skin.

There remains one important aspect to this shampoo, and that is price. After comparing the price of this shampoo to my standby, Head & Shoulders, I have concluded that this shampoo is relatively expensive. I looked at several sizes of Head & Shoulders and without pulling out a calculator, it seems like this shampoo is about 50% more expensive than Head & Shoulders, give or take 10 or 20%. I love the thickness of the shampoo and the smell, but I am unable to justify the price. I know more expensive shampoos exist, but think about it, shampoo is essentially soap for your hair. I struggle to think one soap that costs approximately 50% more than another soap is really worth 50% more unless the more expensive shampoo does something magical. I am missing the magic here.

Shampoo serves a useful and important function. Dandruff shampoo serves two important functions, cleaning your hair and reducing or eliminating the dry skin that is dandruff. This shampoo does the first quite well and the second about as well as Head & Shoulders. The only question I have is whether a shampoo significantly more expensive than another shampoo is value added in my life, or any other person's life.

Enjoy!

It was seredipity that this showed up in the Vine program on the very day I had determined to buy this product over the counter. I had been having some bouts with itchy scalp that my current shampoo was not able to tackle. No flakes or dandruff, just itchyness. Thankfully it worked!

The label describes the content as "tea tree, natural mint, vitamins b5 and e, sunflower, soybean, almond and coconut oils" as well as the standard zinc pyrithione dandruff ingredient. Not sure what 'tea tree' is... leaves, bark or roots from the Camillia (tea) family, or melaleuca oil from the Australian tree from the Myrtle family. The latter I suspect; the product has a distinct and pleasant odor.

The product stings the eyes if you ae not careful; I have experienced this even after substantial rinsing and suspect that warm water may volatilize which ever ingredient causes this. In any event, it seems to work well.

Summary: Smells great, works good on women's hair too!
Text:
For reference, I have baby fine, long, wavy hair and I have lowlights and highlights. My hair tends to be dry on the ends and get oily on the crown and in cool weather my scalp gets flaky. I'm a sucker for a highly scented shampoo and this one smells heavenly. It also rinses out really well and it does seem to condition the scalp.

I'd highly recommend for men or women with similiar hair types.

Summary: Good Shampoo For Dry, Itchy Scalp
Text:
If your scalp is starting to itch,
And you fear flakes may soon fly,
To this product you need to switch,
Read on and I'll tell you why.

This shampoo is nice and thick,
And the smell is really quite nice,
The scent will not make you sick,
And you won't have to rinse more than twice.

This stuff leaves your hair soft and clean,
And without the urge to scratch,
Whether you are old or a teen,
Go out and get some of this batch.

Summary: I used it as I would a body wash
Text: In addition to washing my hair, I used it on my whole body. The white cream comes out slowly and I used small amounts at a time. I would guess that I used less than a tablespoon for my shower. Although it has conditioner, it does not create the slickness of a dedicated conditioner. I like the pleasing scent which is stronger than I expected. My overall opinion is that I was pleasantly surprised and happy with the product. I am giving it 4 stars until I see if over time it keeps my skin from drying out (that would boost it to 5 stars).

Nice stuff.  Works well on dandruff and does a nice job of helping to hydrate your scalp.  Based on the ingredients they list it contains (ginseng, mint, and tea tree) I would have expected to be much much more fragrant than it is.  When applying it has a pretty muted scent and after rinsing out you can barely smell the stuff at all.  I have used other hair products with similar advertised ingredients and the scent was considerably stronger.  I would not be surprised if the aroma was intentionally muted as I am sure some men prefer a lighter scented product.  However, my thinking is that if one is attracted to this or this type of product due to the ingredients listed one would want them to be more or at least seem more potent.  A good product that seems to do what it claims.  I would just prefer a stronger presence or scent of the listed ingredients.

I love the feeling that this shampoo leaves in your hair. Clean, fresh, shiny. It works great as an anti-dandruff shampoo. As well if not better then leading dandruff shampoos. It is clearly head and shoulders above the competition.

This is one of my favorites of the Tasty Bite entrees; it's wonderfully flavorful and, as other reviewers have pointed out, it's a terrifically convenient option for folks on a vegan diet. My favorite way to eat it is over quinoa or brown rice, topped with chopped black olives. Hmm, it's just occurred to me that it would probably be excellent over pasta as well (with the olives)--a sort of Indian/Italian fusion. I used to purchase this product from Amazon via Subscribe & Save, and it was a great deal. Unfortunately, the price is now more than 30% higher than it was when I first subscribed--it's now actually cheaper for me to buy it from my local supermarket. Amazon, if you'll make the price competitive again, I'll subscribe again!

I keep a few of these in my desk at work for days when I don't feel like going out to lunch. They are super convenient because you can microwave them as is, just tear open slightly to vent and put in the microwave. No bowl required, just a spoon, or in a pinch, tilt your head back and slurp it!

The taste is great. I love Indian food, and I love vegetables so this is perfect for me. The only thing to mention is that one of my co workers complained about the smell, but he's that sorta complainy person who doesn't eat Indian food and prefers Burger King. It tastes great, smells great, and is super convenient.
I tried this today and it was delicious!  It's not the texture you at first expect from eggplant, the flavors bridge that, and are really great.  Next time I will put this over rice. : )
Had it today for the first time and liked it a lot. Idiot simple to heat up; reasonably healthy; and quite tasty. Am ordering a bunch more.
We like the Barbeque flavor David Sunflower seed very much especially the kids. We would recommend to everyone whom likes sunflower seed. Enjoy.

I am not sure if I'd actually want to describe it as 'bitter', but I decided to purchase this product because I make coffee using milk. But then if I want a sugared cup, I would still usually have to add sugar and flavoring. So I principally bought this product just to forgo steps in the process.

And the packets also seemed to provide convienience for me.

But, I would like a stronger hazelnut flavor. Right now, it seems to be very sugary, so people drinking this product might not always detect if they are using flavoring at all. And this actually negates the point of producing the specific product. It would be better to just buy a can of regular sugar plus a bottle of syrup.

Still, the product is edible and affordable in the markets where it is for sale. I am able to successfully drink the cups which I've made. And the individual serviving sizes are convienient. So it's not the worst thing which is produced on the market. It's just not the premiere accessory for coffee consumption.
I really like Splenda, but this Hazelnut flavor has a distinctly over-chemicaled taste and just doesn't have much nuttiness to it.  Perhaps the other flavors are better.

We have been using the McCormick Perfect Pinch Salad Supreme Seasoning for a few months now. It has become our go-to seasoning for many things including popcorn! The small 2.62 oz. shaker from our local store can go as high as $4.00 a container. Buying this larger size is a little bit cheaper and the convenience of just having it around is cost savings enough. I would like to bring to everyone's attention you will get this larger container with a white label covering the bar code. What is also covered is the storage instruction of "Refrigerate after opening to prolong freshness."
In addition to sprinkling it on popcorn, fresh and raw vegetable salads, pasta salads, we also use it mixed in the flour coating for sauted chicken breasts. We are still experimenting. The first ingredient is Romano cheese cured with salt. The next ingredient is salt. Obviously, if you are on a salt restricted diet this may not be for you. If you can eat salt, I would suggest moderation.
Remember, put into the refrigertor once you open the container and shake before using.
This is sometimes difficult to find.  However, it came nicely wrapped and was just what I expected. This is one of our favorite powder lemonades.

I ordered this Lime Matcha primarily for the mixing capabilities it offered. I have quite a few Matcha flavors on hand, and I thought that the Lime flavored Matcha might add an interesting dimension of flavor ... of particular interest is a blend with the Watermelon. It sounds refreshing, no?

On it's own, though, it's really quite delicious too. The aroma is very much like a lime tree. I smell the bright, citrus-y notes of the lime, and even a hint of the lime blossom. I smell the leaves and the earth and the tree itself.

The sweet, tart, and slightly bitter taste of the lime offers a unique perspective into the Matcha - allowing me to explore the earthier qualities of Matcha in a way that I've never quite experienced them before. It's a wonderful and very tasty Matcha!

My dog was recently diagnosed with arthritis. She is about 8 years old, she is a chocolate lab. She absolutly lovess Chunky Chews and they last her about a week, which is really good! This is the only kind of chews that I buy for her. LOVE LOVE LOVE this brand!
My Mal absolutely loves this chew ring.  It is very sturdy and keeps her busy for hours.  She loves it so much that she sleeps with it,too.  Highly Recommended.

Black Dragon Pearl Tea tastes even better than I had expected. It is a smooth black/red tea that is strong without being bitter. There is a definite cocoa component, yet it subtly compliments the Yunnan tea flavor rather than overpowering it. There is also a sweet, earthy quality, but nothing near what one might find in a Pu-Erh tea. The pearls are good about five infusions, with the flavor starting to taper off in the fourth. The dry leaves have an aroma reminiscent of honey and 2-3 pearls per cup is a good place to start. If you have a glass teapot, you can enjoy watching the gold and brown marble-sized leaf balls unfurl in the hot water. The brewing tea has an almost malty aroma. To begin with, brew for about 4 minutes with near boiling water and adjust from there.

Black Dragon Pearls is a relaxing, comforting tea that I'll be keeping in regular rotation. My suggestion is that you purchase yours from Adagio Teas rather than Teavana; you get more ounces for your hard-earned dollar and shipping is less expensive as well.

I use this tea at night to help me go to sleep. This brand tastes great even if oversteeped or made very strong and never gets bitter. I keep the cup of brewed tea by my bedside and drink it during the night if I awake and can't get back to sleep. In less than 10 minutes I'm back in dreamland.
As far as we can tell good quality tea, fast shipping, Lemon Balm tea is hard to get around here, so I will order again even though it seems priced on the high side.

I tried so many different brands & flavors of powdered coffee creamer & Coffee-Mate French Vanilla is the best one. It makes coffee taste so much better. It sells out in every store that I go to & is very hard to find; I was so happy to find it here - Thank you Amazon!

After I was diagnosed with Celiac Disease.... I was looking for good pasta, like I used to like and after much research and reviews bought this. I have been buying this ever since. Even non-Celiacs can't tell the difference between this and wheat pasta. I am so happy that I found this.

I first ordered, pondering how long it would take to get to me if it came from New Zealand.  I was delighted and amazed to received the jar about three days later.  The Honey, like Korunaturals, did not disappoint.  I won't go into my medical fixes, you have to try it.  The best things in life always cost more, how wonderful when they deliver healing too.  I'm only on my third jar, but figure I've saved Office visit fees more than once. East Cape Manuka Honey is smooth, with a wonderful flavor.  It doesn't get any better than this!

Summary: Libby's Naturals Whole Kernel Sweet Corn
Text: I am so pleased with Libby's Naturals Whole Kernel Sweet Corn.  This is the freshest and sweetest canned corn I have ever tasted.  I will be ordering this item regularly.

Summary: Tasty treat that can't be found anywhere in my area (SW Houston)
Text: Use to buy these at a store around the corner from a movie theater, but that was back in 2008. I have looked in several groceries and chain retailers but can only find the original gummiburst, not the sour one. Item arrived quick and packaged nicely, but the Texas heat melted most of the gummibursts. I opened the first bag and they were all squished and stuck together. I will try putting a bag in the freezer and see if that helps separate them. I would advise purchasing this when the weather cools down a bit

This is the best thing since slice bread. You don't have to make a full pot of coffee just to have one cup. You can have coffee anywhere you can find hot water. you don't have to buy a 100.00 coffee pot all you need is a cup and water. it's the best.

"The Passion of this blend will enhance any encounter. Roses have long held the romance of lovers within their silky petals. Sip and linger, love is yours." ~Zhena

As you pour the Gypsy Love tea into your teacup on a summer morning, the delicate fragrance of fresh picked roses makes your day seem a little more romantic.

Ingredients: Finest Organic Chinese Black Tea, Red & Pink Rose Petals and All Natural Flavor.

The main appeal in this blend is the rose petals and the tea is very mild. This allows for the addition of other ingredients or you can make it twice as strong as recommended.

~The Rebecca Review

If you LOVE peanut butter but want to save some serious calories.... this IS the way to go!! I use it in my smoothies and oatmeal, I just add a couple TBSPP and am good to go! I get the wonderful PB taste and save TONS of calories and fat!! If you mix it with water to use as a spread, it is good... Not AS GOOD as regular PB, but still good. You can also mix it with a healthy oil (like grapeseed) and it is very similar to regular PB but with a healthier oil! I have been a PB2 fan for over a year! My next try will be the chocolate version!

Summary: Hot sauce concentrate, use at your own risk
Text:
This is like hot sauce concentrate. You MUST dilute it to use it. Do not try to eat this stuff straight or you will be miserable for hours, and then some. Lets just say it burns both ways. A teaspoon in an entire crock of chili will make the chili hot enough to be near inedible, and I like very hot and spicy foods. Five or six drops is probably more than enough for an entire dish. Tabasco isn't even comparable to this, because no amount of tabasco would make a dish that hot. This is truly the hotest sauce I have ever had, I think it killed my tastebuds (slight sarcasm).

Wash your hands thoroughly after use as there will often be residue on the lid. If you rub your eyes they will burn for a long time, and I would suggest flushing them with water for about 10 minutes if you have the unfortunate experience.

The first listed ingredient is habaneros.

I bought this for my roommate as a Christmas gift. He eats Dave's Insanity Sauce (black label) on EVERYTHING (including his breakfast cereal) in large quantities (more than a table spoon for a small sandwich) and says he longer feels a burn from it. After eating a plate full of migas with only 1 drop of Ultimate Insanity Sauce, he started sweating and his eyes watered. If you're looking for an incredibly and unbelievably hot sauce, look no further!

This is a hot sauce you buy just to dare your friends to eat it, then you put it away since it really doesn't have a good flavor just really hot. Maybe you will take it out next time another friend comes by and you want to dare them.  Try Marie Sharps it is very hot and great tasting not just a party prank.

Summary: CAREFUL!!!This is by far the hottest sauce on earth!!!
Text: I purchase a few bottle for friends who did not believe this IS the ultimate hot sauce. They are now believers! Use this with caution---someone posted keep in frig after opening plus a LARGE roll of toilet paper in the freezer!!!!!

For a few dollars more, you can get larger pig ears elsewhere. See my other review.
The dogs did like these and they were packed in a bag in a box which is a plus. The problem was there were about 25% smaller ears 1/2 the size of the largest ones.

They aren't bad, but I spent $7 more to get a much better product size wise from a different vendor and it was worth it as there were only a few smaller ones in that order.

Summary: good crackers, good price, good for you
Text: I'm on a low fat low sodium diet.  These are great for my diet and they're tasty too.  I live here in Hawaii where everything is expensive.  I save about 30% ordering them from Amazon.  Free shipping with Amazon prime.  I thought they would get here in crumbs but they didn't.  12 packs of fragile crackers all intact.

We order this product a couple of times a year for my father, an old Italian guy. He loves it! I'm so happy we are able to find it on Amazon; it makes it easy for us to surprise him with a couple of bottles every now and then.

If you haven't tried this product, I highly recommend that you find a good recipe for Bollito Misto (mixed boiled meats) that includes beef, beef tongue, chicken, and sausage. This is the perfect and traditional accompaniment. Enjoy!

If you have a bunny lover in the house, Annie's has you covered. Bunny-shaped cereal, bunny shaped crackers in several varieties, bunny (and carrot!)-shaped pretzels, bunny-shaped pastas, and bunny-shaped fruit snacks. My 5-year-old daughter is in bunny heaven, thanks to Annie. Oh, and they're tasty, too!

Que BUENO!!  I cannot believe I found this olive oil here. I have had the hardest time finding it anywhere else. Thank you so much! Delivery was right on time. Do you have any gift specials? I think this would be a great idea. MUCHAS GRACIAS!!

Summary: Tastes Good. And Good for Uou (?)
Text: I love the taste of Glenny's Low Fat Soy Crisps.  They have a good, crispy crunch, are low fat, and have relatively high protein and high fiber, compared with typical junk food.  Glenny's Low Fat Soy Crisps can be hard to find, both in retail stores and on Amazon. The Amazon price is much more reasonable than Glenny's own price.
Actually good tasting health food.  Without the salt they would taste alot like rice cakes, but with a texture more like pork rinds.  Awesome alternative to tater chips!

I bought these since many people commented on how great they taste.  I think they are bland and need to be salted (even though there IS salt on them and I ALMOST NEVER add salt to my food).  I don't think they replace chips and  I don't know that I'll be able to eat the rest.  I certainly didn't think "these are yummy" as I tried them.  Also, each bag is 2 servings--I mistakenly thought each bag was 1 serving.  I will by Stacy's soy chips again before these---those are YUMMY--I never should have tried something new.

really good got a box full and love them
got some at a store and they were very expensive the price here is really worth it
Enjoy!!!
I grew up in Germany close to the Netherlands and used to eat them as a child.  These licorice have the perfect balance in taste and texture.  They are not too salty or sweet....just right!

Summary: ARRIVED BROKEN IN A MILLION PEIECES!!!
Text: I RECEIEVED MY ORDER TODAY AND IT WAS BROKEN LIKE SOMEONE RAN OVER WITH A VEHICHLE. I PURCHASED FROM AMERICARX, AND THEY SHIPPED IT IN A PLASTIC BAG WITH PLASTIC WRAPPING ON THE OUTSIDE PACKAGE, NO PROTECTION FOR THIS GLASS ITEM AT ALL. NOT EVEN FRAGILE WRITTEN ON THE PACKAGE. IT ALSO TOOK FOREVER TO SHIP. THE ONLY UPSIDE TO THIS IS THAT THE SMELL OF THE STUFF WHICH WAS ALL OVER THE WHOLE SHIPMENT SMELLED AMAZING.

I played it safe and only ordered 2 bags because I was ordering other stuff, and now I'm kicking myself!  My husband got a bag with all his favorites in it, mostly chocolate, and I got what I swear was a 40 flavor blend! Love the odd little shapes, and can't wait to buy more!
Had a great mix of various flavors with no discernible decrease in taste.  Most excellent choice.
with over 40 flavors of jelly beans, it is hard to believe that they only had mess ups on five flavors.

Summary: Avert your eyes, open your mouth
Text:
My bag of flops was quite varied. I was afraid of a pound of pina colada and nutmeg or something, but I got a good combination of all sorts.

I thought these would mostly be minor defects, misprintings, that sort of thing. There are some freakishly huge jellybelly monsters in there though: five or six ugly mutants all fused into a sugar bomb you can barely get in your mouth, or weird distorted oddball shapes. Some of the colors also seem...not right.

Once you start chewing you can't tell any of this of course, which is why this is such a good bargain.

Unlike most of the other low reviewers, I got a pretty good variety of intact jelly bellies.  Inside the sealed bag, however, were four live ants crawling all over the candy.  Yuck.  I inspected the bag for holes and couldn't find any, so I think the problem was there pre-shipping.
This was our 2nd order of Belly FLops - a completely different assortment this time. The best description , well, they're all gone!

Ya pop one in your mouth & enjoy.... that's the whole reason for these little guys to exist, so who's to say they're flops? I disagree wholeheartedly; they are PERFECT!!! My mouth doesn't care what they look like 'cause every single, beautiful gem is just as yummy as their so-called perfect lil' brothers & sisters! The adventure of discovery enhances each reach into the bag. Just let your tongue reveal whatever flavor happens to come up. After all, life's a gamble so let this be a pleasurable roll of the snack food dice!

I bought 2 bags and they were 90% chocolate pudding--and I really can't stand that flavor, so I gave them to my mom.  But she did say that they were good, and so did her co-workers. They taste the same, I'm sure, but I can't say since none of the flavors I like were in the bags.  The bags were huge though--2 LBS of Jelly Bellies.

Summary: Belly Flops are not that great of a value
Text: I love Jelly Bellys, I am certifiable addict. I originally thought Belly Flops were a terrific value, I ordered 2 bags and with shipping the total was almost $22. I was at Costco the other day and happened to stumble upon a plastic tub of Jelly Bellys which were not defect and their total price for 4 pounds, the same equivalence as 2 two-pound bags of flops, was  about $15. I'd recommend getting them at Costco if thats possible--more variety, better taste, and you don't have to pay for shipping, or wait. It's a win win!

We've been huge fans of Jelly Belly for years, and we recently decided to try our the BellyFlops - partly as a way to save some money on our addiction, and partly just for fun. We ordered two of the 2-lb bags, and both of them looked to have a good mix of flavors. While not every flavor is represented, we do have a nice variety, and some of the flavors appear to be from the special lines like the Sours, which we wouldn't normally get in a mixed bag.

For the most part, the beans just seem to be misprints. The signature Jelly Belly stamp is missing, or the colorful spots on a Tutti-Fruitti bean are not very apparent, but there are some of those crazy monster globs in there! They do look crazy, but they taste fine. For the 2-3 bean conglomerates, it's kind of like eating one of those larger jelly beans you traditionally get at Easter. For larger lumps, you might want to eat them in bites! (We just ran into an enormous 10-bean fusion!)

The best part about the Belly Flops, however, is that they're unique! I remember years ago when Jelly Belly was harder to find and the concept of a Buttered Popcorn or Strawberry Daiquiri flavored jelly bean was still a novelty that sparked people's interest and got them excited about trying all the different flavors. The Belly Flops seem to recreate this same reaction! We took one of our bags to a party, and once we explained what they were, everyone was eager to dive in and see what kinds of unusual beans they encountered. The Flops made a great conversation piece and really got people laughing and talking!

This is a GREAT product.  I bought 2 bags for my husband and he LOVED them!  There are several "FLOPS" in each handful, but they are just as delicious as the "normal" bellys!  I have ordered twice from this company - very timely and product arrives in good shape!

I got a bunch of different flavors, a lot of cinnamon though (which isn't really a fave of mine), and a lot were stuck together.  I'd seriously get like a super bean with like 10 beans stuck together.  But it's a good price.
This is a wonderful product that makes delicious marmalade.  I would highly recommend it for its quality.

My dog goes crazy for these. They are BIG like 8" long and 1/4" in diameter.
The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because they have 28% crude fat but I just cut them with scissors and give as smaller treats.
Quick delivery,  Excellent quality.  We make vegan raw protein bars for the family & go through it quite quickly.
Honestly, you shouldn't buy these. They are like having sex on ecstasy, the regular oreos just won't cut it anymore.

I absolutely love this dressing. If you like ginger and soy you will love this. It has a true taste of ginger that has a slight fresh ginger hotness. I thought no one could beat Good Seasons, the one that you mix at home with olive oil and vinegar but this is right at top for my favorite now. Excellent!

My kitty loves these as a treat.  I am completely satisfied with these but next time I am going to buy the crunchy ones as opposed to these soft ones because the crunch helps clean the tartar off her teeth.

Baron's makes the BEST HOT HOT HOT Habanero sauce in my opinion. I discovered it on St Lucia and fell in love. At first just one drop is positively NUCLEAR, then it grows on you. Since capsaicin is a neurotoxin, you develop a tolerance and need more to get the same bang. This is a common phenomenon.

I brought back several bottles and went through them, then needed to find another source, not having travel plans to return to St Lucia. It was only then that I discovered that this is actually a Hot Mustard Sauce. It was so hot and flavorful I just didn't realize it was mustard-based! And I don't care for mustard!!!

After buying a case of bottles from the local ethnic food $tore, once I went through them I thought of searching the internet. Who knew there were larger bottles???

This purchase was ideal. A large bottle (three times as large) for the same price as a smaller one, it came quickly, was fresh and had an expiration date three years hence. I will go through one bottle in about two months!

I cannot recommend this higher for anyone who likes his sauce HOT, flavorful, and yes, slightly mustardy.

These crepe cookies are out of this world! I believe everyone should try these cookies at least once in their life.

My first experience with these cookies was in a high end grocery store. Found them to be more expensive in the grocery store, but i decided ill try them once in my life. Now these cookies have become an obsession.

The cookies have a flakey texture and have this lightly sweet taste that just makes my mouth water. These crepe cookies are neatly packed into a golden wrapper with two crepe cookies. The exterior has a wonderful golden color with a slight glaze to them. Once a crepe cooke is in your mouth you can bite but the sweetness, which is not overpowering, just melts into your mouth. I would recommend these to anyone who loves flavor without the crazy overpowering taste of sugar.

I am a true believer when it comes to these cookies. I will purchase them over and over again. I wish there were more cookies per package. Makes it hard to share because these cookies are so good!

Summary: Nice size for a snack. A+++++
Text: These come in good size for a baby snack. My daughter loved it and also don't have much to waste when they get bored after eating. Will buy it again.

I used to get a certain light roast coffee from a company with a famous donkey (and man) but haven't been able to find it available lately, so I went looking for a light roast I could get all the time and landed on Camano Island. Not as much caffeine as the other but much to my liking. I brew it alone or blend it with other darker roasts to mellow them down a bit. The automatic delivery is a plus also.

i have to say that this price is not a bargain as much as i love these crackers.  there are bargains out there people...better to buy in the grocery store especially when they are on sale. this is the reason for the 3 rating.

Been drinking this stuff for about a month and I really love it. Since it's the summertime I've been drinking this stuff cold brewed. What I love about guayusa is that it can steep for a very long time and it actually accentuates the flavor. First I dissolve a couple of teaspoons of honey with warm water into a 10-cup pitcher and fill it with about 12 teaspoons of guayusa (or you can do 1 teaspoon per 8oz but I sometimes add more in case the cold brew technique doesn't bring out all the flavor). Then I just fill the entire pitcher with cold water and let it steep overnight in the fridge. Eight hours is desirable, sometimes more. I accidentally forgot about it one time and had it steeping for 24 hours and it tasted even better. It has a very nice and smooth taste to it, not bitter at all. Recommended.

The peppermint/guayusa blend is delicious. The guayusa is mild and slightly sweet so it blends very well with the peppermint. I love drinking this in the mid-afternoon for a pick-me-up that won't keep me awake at night like coffee does.

I highly recommend it!

So light and crucnhy - very low sodium. Kinda a different taste at first - but by the second cookie/cracker - you are hooked. I've tried the Sesame/Almod & the original.

However the prices on Amazon are over priced.

Summary: The Best Cocoa for All Recipes
Text: When Hershey decided to change their Dutch Process cocoa powder around 2004, I was compelled to find a replacement that was as good.  I tried every cocoa powder out there and nothing was  as good.  About a year later, Cooks Illustrated did a taste test on cocoa powder and Callebaut came out on top (January 2005).  I found it online and decided to order it even though it came in a large quantity and it was a bit pricey.  I have never used any other cocoa powder since.  It is fantastic and worth it.  I get huge compliments on all of my chocolate recipes and I know it is the Callebaut cocoa.  Your brownies will never taste as good with any other cocoa powder.  Your homemade hot chocolate will be the envy of all the kids in the neighborhood.  I find ways to use the quantity within a year and no one complains!

Summary: Better than some, but not great
Text: I have used every brand of cocoa available.  Some of the best (and cheapest) I've used are A&P's Master Choice Premium and the no longer available Hersey's European Style with the silver label.  I prefer dutch processed cocoa and found Callebaut was not quite as good as Bensdorf, available from King Arthur Flour online.

Summary: CAREFUL!!  SHIPPING COSTS MORE THAN COOKIES !!
Text:
I suggest you be careful before ordering this item, I can not see that any cookie is worth $10.50 even if it tastes great! Even if we poor Celiac patients have to make do with much dry backed goods, and I mean some of it is dust-storm-dry, even so, I just can not justify to pay more for the shipping then for the cookies themselves. So make sure you always check the shipping charges before ordering anything, especially since cookies are not a food group, unfortunately. I have been in internet shopping and selling from its start and I know many sellers do try and make some extra income charging unreasonable rates for shipping by calling it HANDLING charges. This cookie bag weighs only 3.7 oz and I don't care how good you pack it this does not cost $5.05 for shipping. Did you know that a 1 oz letter costs $.44?
I am sorry if I sound angry, but as a Celiac I am very much upset for being taken advantage of because I have a disease which makes me have to shop for special foods. And this is exactly what is going on here. By the time you have ordered from 4 to 6 sellers you end up paying enough for shipping that you could live off another month, and that is robbery. So I decided enough is enough and I am making sure you know about it before you go through quick check out(worst way to go!) or having to go back after having spent so much time online comparing prices just to find at checkout that you can't afford it because of such excess shipping charges.

Very good product and one I will reorder.  However, just after placing 3 orders, my checking acount was hacked by some entity in Dubhai. Summary: At last, great packaging that really works.
Text:

Summary: Great for cats with allergies to normal protein sources
Text: We have a beautiful five year old Abyssinian with an unfortunate tendency to vomit fairly often. Some protein sources were better than others (he did better with duck vs. chicken or turkey), but nothing seemed to completely take care of the problem - until we tried California Natural's Herring and Sweet Potato. After two weeks of this cat food, he hasn't vomited at all. Our cat's coat is glossier than it has ever been. Some reactions to previous foods were so severe that he would also lick bald patches in his coat, often on his tummy. That behavior has stopped as well. After researching many foods, this one seems to be the best and has excellent reviews as a healthy dry food for cats. I'm thrilled to have finally found a healthy food our kitty loves.

Summary: Stay away from this Food, can cause urinary problems
Text: I fed this to my cats (I have 33) and I started having MAJOR problems with urinary infections and blockages from crystals with several male and female cats. I traced it back to the food and found that 1) fish is bad news for cats because of the high mineral content and 2)on top of that Sweet Potatoes are also really bad as they contain a high level of oxalates. People who have bladder and kidney problems due to stones are advised not to eat sweet potatoes so I am going to assume that that is true for cats. Sweet potatoes and herring are not foods a cat would eat in the wild anyway. Bottom line stay away from this food, urinary blockages are serious and your cat can die within 48 hours without expensive intervention (like thousands of dollars expensive). Since I switched foods 6 months ago I haven't had the problem again.

Summary: good meatloaf, so-so potatoes, TONS of salt
Text:
I do understand that meals like this are typically high in sodium, and I didn't expect this one to be any different. I didn't score it down because of the sodium content. The meatloaf here is quite tasty. Very soft, nicely flavored. Not like the meatloaf I make at home, but good in its own right. What I didn't like so much was the side of mashed potatoes. The meatloaf nukes quickly, but the potatoes seem to stay "hard," and what I ended up doing was taking the plastic cover off, putting the whole mess on a regular plate, smushing the potatoes with a fork, and heating the whole thing up for about 30 seconds more. That seemed to do the trick, and I enjoyed the potatoes then. I liked the gravy, too, but it was a bit salty for my general taste. I ended up scraping off most of it and tossing it rather than eating it.

I do like the idea of having these in my office for an in-a-pinch situation where I can't get out to get something healthier, but I'd say that no one should eat these with any regularity if salt is an issue or if healthier options are readily available.

Summary: Surprisingly tasty for a light lunch
Text:

During the work day, I don't want to spend a lot of time on food preparation and rely heavily on packaged meals.

I decided to take a chance on the Hormel Compleats line out of curiosity - and have been pleasantly surprised.

While far (very far) from being "gourmet" fare, they are surprisingly tasty overall and super-easy to prepre.

Ninety seconds in the microwave, peel back the almost impossible to remove seal being careful not to splash the food on your clothes and you have lunch.

The meatloaf isn't the best of their line, but it is still pretty tasty, if a bit on the salty side. Overall, I like the Compleats Metloaf better than most of the frozen varieties I've tried.

If you like the convenience of meals that can be stored on a shelf and prepared in seconds, give this line a try. It isn't gourmet, but it is quick, tasty and filling.

Jerry

Luckily it went away when I discontinued use on him.  I knew that this ointment was the contributing factor because although he has sensitive skin, I have narrowed down what works for him without breaking him out.  I cannot say that it won't work for other toddlers/babies but I can say that proceeding with caution is one's best bet as there may be irritants in this product...so be very careful.  It's a good thing though that by me having two jars, my husband and I can still use the ointment without a problem.  I have to say that it did seem to calm my boy before bedtime and helped to clear his nasal passages.  Overall, an OK product but I have to keep looking for another natural ointment that will not irritate my boy's skin.

Summary: Don't buy from Easy To Grow Bulbs
Text:
THe Easy To Grow Bulbs Company provides zero customer satisfaction.

I always buy my wife an amaryllis bulb for Christmas, and have been doing so for almost 25 years. This year I ordered this very package from ETGB.* Weeks later I was still seeing no signs of life. I emailed the company and asked for a replacement. I got a letter back hinting that I was watering it improperly, or that I had not planted it in a timely manner, or that I was just being impatient. One month later the bulb is either dormant or dead, and further requests for a replacement were met with the equivalent of, "Sorry, tough luck."

My wife is an experienced gardener and has never had a failed amaryllis bulb before. Therefore, I recommend that you only order from ETGB if you won't be needing them to make good if your bulbs are bad--because they won't.

*(Not through Amazon, though. I bought directly from the ETGB web site. Buying through Amazon may give you more leverage if you need it.)

These are far from the "original" Necco Wafers. Some genius decided it would be a good idea to replace the artificial colors and flavors generations of Necco lovers have come to adore with things like beet juice, cabbage, and turmeric. The result of the switch to "natural" flavorings and colors is, at best, disappointing, at worst, an unmitigated confectionery disaster.

The black Necco, with its sweet quasi-licorice flavoring, was always my favorite. Now, it's hard to tell it apart from the other Neccos. There are only mild differences between the flavors of these false Neccos, these fraudulent wafers. And all the flavors are forgettably bland.

The New England Confectionery Company has ditched the old packaging, too. In a way, the change is a blessing. The new wrapper lets the Necco lover know not to waste money on the worst product formula change ever. Forget New Coke/Old Coke; the Necco debacle is unequaled in world history. It makes the Portland Trailblazer's decision to draft Sam Bowie instead of Michael Jordan seem enlightened.

What makes the whole sordid affair even harder to accept is company's failure to note the ruination of Necco anywhere on the package. I bought a sack of the small size rolls and thought I must have purchased an old, stale lot of Necco rejects. It was only after I tried Neccos from the regular sized roll that I realized something was horribly wrong.

Goodbye old friend. If I had known the fate your maker had in store for you I would have bought a truck load of you and would, perhaps, be savoring one of your delectable pleasure discs right now.

The ordering and delivery process was painless and efficient, very well handled. I do have a problem with the product! The "Original" Necco wafers they have come out with bear no resemblance to any product that I have seen in the last 63 years. The colors are washed out, muddy and difficult to tell apart! The only flavor that is distinct is in the ,now gray, Black licorice wafer,the licorice flavor is volatile and flavors the rest of the package. The rest of the flavors are too weak to compete! Another once dependable product gone to hell!

Summary: Best Easiest Salsa You'll Ever Make!
Text: This is not only the best salsa mix you will ever use, but also the easiest. This size packet is perfect too, makes the perfect size bowl for 2 people to enjoy. I just add a few fresh tomatoes if it's season or Red Gold whole canned (reg 15oz)work well enough in winter. I like the Classic Med. heat packages best because I can make several types of salsa from the same packet. For those who cant stand much heat, I might just add some chopped green pepper & onion. Add some finely chopped cilantro if you want. My favorite is extra chopped green pepper & onion, finely chopped cilantro & either a chopped habenero or jolokia pepper for a great HOT salsa. Just add it all to the blender & "chop" it to the consistency you desire, give it 5-6 minutes for the flavours to blend & you have the freshest salsa you can get.

Text: These cookies were a hit with everyone in our family from the oldest (35) to the youngest (17 months.)  The cookies were very soft and tasty. I had a problem with the crumbly texture, because when I tried to dip the cookie into a glass of milk, a big chunk of it broke off and fell to the bottom of the glass, where it turned into inedible mush.  Aside from that one complaint, I have nothing bad to say about these yummy cookies.

These cookies are soft, but not crumbly like so many mass-produced "soft" cookies.  They have a good amount of raisins and slight oatmeal-spice flavor.  A plus is the individual wrappings, good for taking on an outing, packing in school lunches or even selling at a bake sale.  Don't expect the same chewiness or intensity of oat flavor as bakery or homemade cookies, but as store shelf cookies go, I've had worse (Chips Ahoy "chewy gooey" for instance).

Summary: Coffee Bean Direct Papua New Guinea City Roast
Text: Disappointed:  this whole-bean Papua New Guinea has no body, no depth, no complexity, and, given how weak the bean is, is overroasted as a full city roast.  Unfortunately, I opted for a subscription which I intend to cancel.

I'll see how that works out.  We use the Cuisinart burr grinder on medium and brew it in a Cuisinart Brew Master 1200.  These products are all relatively new and along with this fine coffee have been an added pleasure to our mornings.

These beans arrived having been very freshly roasted and with excellent aroma. I brew in a French press and that first cup was excellent indeed- being a 5-star in flavor and at perhaps 4 on the aroma. It did posses a rather surprising bitterness in the aftertaste but nothing that took anything significant away from the overall enjoyment.

I have essentially finished the 5-pound bag now, and the enjoyment of that first cup continues at the same level as the first brew. Unfortunately, my own style is to drink the coffee over the morning hours, and I normally do so by warming individual refills in the microwave. After that first excellent one, subsequent rewarmed cups of this product, while a problem with many beans, drop off in quality faster than any other beans I have tried (of course, some start bad and stay bad). For that reason only- and admittedly my own habit that may not match yours- I drop this product to about 3 stars- it is a very steep drop in quality after that first cup.

I have no idea how this might show itself using other brewing and serving methods. I suspect that in any environment that does not require rewarming or perhaps held at temperature for longer periods, this is most definitely a 5-star candidate. Its oiliness might possibly be a bit of a nuisance for some machines.

Since I have found a few others that do hold their flavor extremely well after brewing and submit to rewarming quite well, I won't be using this one again. If you are a re-warmer, I would try something else. However, I think that if you can avoid the heat cycling you should definitely consider giving in giving this one a try.

Summary: Movie Theater Popcorn In Your Home!
Text:
Are you looking for GENUINE popcorn flavor and texture popped from the convenience of your own home? Then look no further than this popcorn party kit!

I purchased this popcorn as a side item when I found and purchased an at-home "authentic" popcorn machine on Amzaon. Unfortunately, the popcorn machine that I ordered during the same transaction (from a different Amazon seller than Wabash) had been discontinued; however, I received this popcorn kit from Wabash within a mater of days.

Here I was, stuck with this popcorn kit and no popcorn machine in which to pop it. The only way I knew how to pop popcorn was in a microwave. So I got out a covered, 6-qt sauce aluminum sauce pan (part of a 13-pc Calphalon cookware set I bought a couple years ago at B, B, & Beyond), followed the cooking instruction for "stovetop" popping on the back of the popcorn package, and poured the package's contents into the pan.

The results were INCREDIBLE! The scent of movie theater popcorn filled the air of my condo, and the entire sauce pan was filled to the top with buttery popcorn. It was actually pretty cool, too, watching the popcorn pop through the glass lid lol We poured it out into a popcorn bowl, sprinkled a little bit of Wabash's Popcorn Salt Popcorn Salt, and my wife and I couldn't believe how authentic this popcorn tasted (on a separate note, this salt tastes GREAT on things like french fries and tater tots). Nearly every kernel popped fully and perfectly, and nearly every piece was nicely coated in just the right amount of yellow, melted butter and oil. We then sat down and watched "Batman Begins" - we weren't even past the first five minutes when we had finished off the entire, huge batch of popcorn and were making more!!

We didn't use the paper popcorn cups because we didn't want to waste them on just us, but they're definitely a nice novelty and add to that authentic, movie-theater feeling.

We've had a few guests over for movie night at our home, and our guests agree that this is great tasting popcorn.

This Popcorn Party Kit is a MUST HAVE! If you want authentic popcorn at your home, whether for yourself, your family, or for your friends and guests, look no further than this. I'm a Wabash valley Farms customer for life!!

Summary: Good for Long Term Food Storage
Text: I'm working on creating a one year supply of long term food storage and before purchasing a significant quantity of a food item such as canned meat, I always get a sample and try it out. Expensive, but a good product to add to my long term food storage.  I would only use this product in an emergency situation and for that purpose, give this product a 5 star rating.

Summary: Slightly weird taste, minor nutritional improvment
Text:
The veggie involved here is dried cauliflower replacing some of the wheat starch in the noodles. It smells like cauliflower when boiling. It has a very mild cauliflower taste.

In exchange for a slightly unusual taste, the "veggie" version of Kraft gives you:
Vitamin C 15% daily value (vs. 1% in the regular version)
Dietary Fiber 3 grams (vs. 1.5 in the regular stuff)

Those were the only notable differences. An extra 1.5 grams of fiber doesn't seem like a lot, but that's 12% DV instead of 6%. For other nutrients, such differences matter a lot less. The veggie version has 1 gram less fat, but that's only 11 calories worth of fat shaved from a food which is already fairly low in fat, and the total calories end up being the same anyway. There are some 1% differences in some other vitamins, which doesn't matter.

Getting back to the taste...
Even though there is only a small cauliflower influence on the taste, I found that it somehow did detract from enjoyment. Blue-box Mac&Cheese has a very mild cheese flavor, which works OK when the noodles are normal. But the very slight added cauliflower taste kind of masks the cheese.

If you have kids demanding it 3 times per week, a little extra fiber and vitamin C might be a good idea. But if this is your guilty pleasure food or just a backup plan for rare occasions, I would stick with the normal stuff.

If you want to experiment with healthier noodles, there are several brands of dry pasta with omega 3 fats and added fiber. They do tend to have a wheaty flavor, but on the other hand they don't have that weird cauliflower taste.

Kraft Mac and Cheese has always been my go-to quick mac and cheese. Though there may be some subtle taste difference between this and the regular, I can't taste it and neither could my husband. There is only 1/2 serving of veggies per cup, but getting an extra half serving of veggies in your mac and cheese isn't such a bad deal, really (and if you mix in some peas or green beans, then you've got yourself a bit of a meal). (I think the real question here is if we should wonder if the federal regulations for saying something has a serving of vegetables/fruit have become too lax lately.)

I'd definitely buy it again. I'm currently pregnant, so any place I can sneak in an extra vegetable serving (especially since so many normal foods don't appeal to me now) is good. And while I don't think this is the way to get your kids to eat their veggies, again it's not a bad way to get some extra in there.

If you want a great tasting Hot sauce that will set you on fire, you need to try this one.  Quick turn around and bonus coupons.

I like really hot food, but I don't eat it just to show off (well, maybe a little). There's a pretentious part of me that likes being able to experience new tastes, tastes that the average person wouldn't even notice due to their excruciating tongue agony. If I don't enjoy those flavors, then the whole exercise is pointless.

If you can handle it, this sauce *tastes good*, which is a rare treat among the ultra-hot sauces. I would apply it liberally to many different dishes, if I didn't value my sanity so highly.

The experience differs from other sauces. With other hot foods (even mild ones like jalapeños), it's a pretty straightforward battle: it's spicy, I ate it, and now it's burning my mouth. Then there's this sauce (and other ghost pepper-based foods), which is a whole different thing... instead of it burning me, it feels like *I'm* the one burning and I just didn't notice it until now. It's a fun twist.

Word to the wise: this stuff builds up over time. When the bottle first arrived, I put a tiny dot of it on a french fry just to check it out. I tolerated that small amount with no problem, but it'll sneak up on you. It started with a mild tingle, and built to a noticeable sting over the course of about five minutes. If you forget this fact, you'll eat an enchilada with a bit of sauce on every bite and finish the meal feeling like a champ... only to be rendered speechless and near-catatonic ten minutes later.

I definitely recommend this sauce to anyone who *isn't* just in it for the bragging rights. And for those who are: I've felt more burn than this, but not often and rarely from such small amounts of the "active ingredient".

I will preface this review with a little about myself. I only recently bought a "hottest sauce" while at a kind of flea market in England. At first I was sort of proud of myself for being able to use it, but it did grow on me and I started using it as an actual condiment. After the bottle ran out I thought I would see what was on Amazon and this sauce was ranked very highly so I bought it. So I really only have one other sauce to compare this to but here goes:

The sauce is very hot. Almost too hot. It has a pasty consistency, almost exactly like tomato paste. Very finely ground. It has a more gummy consistency to it, like theres something added to it to give it a smoother texture though there's no such actual ingredient.

What there is, however, as someone else pointed out, is pepper extract. It's the second listed ingredient so there must be a considerable amount. Perhaps it's what's giving this sauce that slimy texture I was eluding to earlier. This Pepper Extract doesn't state what KIND of pepper, and as it's an extract I imagine it must have gone through quite the extraction process.

So what I'm getting at is this: the sauce feels more like a pepper extract, something which you should add small amounts of to large dishes for adding pure spice to the food. But it's missing the taste and feel of an actual hot sauce. There's little flavor, just a lot of burn. And I have to say that that's a big shame because the bhut jolokia pepper is very tasty. Almost fruity if I remember correctly.

So I give this hot sauce 4 stars for the Effort and the level of spice, but I won't give it 5 stars because I think that goes to the generic bhut jolokia ghost pepper sauces with all the scary names and pictures on the bottle. The one I had was Fear Hot Sauce with a scary ghost woman on it, and it was much more like salsa, with little ground up pieces of ghost peppers and seeds in it and equal to, if not more burn than this one.

If I change my mind as I go through this bottle, I'll update or comment on here again.

Summary: Sauce not meant to be inhaled
Text:
While heating up some oil to fry some vegetables and an egg on, I threw about a tablespoon of this sauce into the frying pan for seasoning. I had used about 1/3 of the bottle so I knew what I was getting myself into. I must have not realized that the oil was too hot to add liquid to without causing it to vaporize. Instantly after pouring it in it began to boil violently. A sizeable cloud of Dave's hot sauce quickly formed above the pan. I thought it would be OK at first. I backed off after getting a small whiff of it. It was very potent--like mace. After about 25 seconds I couldn't stop coughing but I continued cooking thinking that just the small whiff had gotten into the wrong place in my throat and I would soon return to normal. Little did I know that it's vapors were spreading throughout the house. Within minutes my roommates were coughing across the house. My dog was also wheezing.
After opening all the windows and doors in the house and turning some fans on I ate my egg/vegetable patty sandwich. Even with no visible signs of Dave's hot sauce left in the pan it was still very hot, to my liking.
This sauce should be used with caution. When consumed the wrong way it is very unpleasant.

A tip when brewing espresso using a steam espresso machine: Shut off the valve before any steaem comes through the coffee. The high temperature steam will leach unwanted flavors into the coffee.

Not really fond of the taste. I use Cafe Espresso for iced espressos and americanos. If you find it ludicrous to spend $12 on 8 ounce coffee, which i doubt since you probably have a nice machine if you are reading this, I would buy Lavazza In Blue (i can get it for $8 at World Market). If you just want a preground espresso to make coffee drinks, or iced drinks and don't want to spend too much nor buy a burr grinder and grind your own, i would get the Lavazza Cafe Espresso. Lavazza Cafe Espresso would get 3.5/5 from me. In Blue would get 4/5, Illy 4.5/5.

Summary: These are my favorite "in States" chocolate goodies.
Text:
I never was much of a chocolate person. I grew up preferring Strawberry, then Vanilla, and, lastly, chocolate.

Then when I was 35, my husband took me with him on a business trip to Switzerland. What a treat that was! Lining the main boulevards were small confectionery shops filled with cocholates the likes of which I had never, ever laid eyes upon. A tiny box of chocolates that would be about 5 inches square and hold 12 pieces of candy cost around $30. But I had no idea that Chocolate could taste so exquistely good or look so beautiful. Little candies with 3 layers of chocolate in various flavors topped with small green candy looking twigs, or hearts, or diamond shapes.
Truffles made with plain chocolate or all different types of liquors. If I could have afforded it, I would have eaten myself into the size of a blimp. And the sales people were so delightful, always reminding me that this box was made Today and was meant to be eaten TODAY or it would get stale. I thought about our boxes of chocolate that sit on the shelves for weeks or months and winced. Thankfully, lots of walking was required to see the sights and I was able to eat what I could afford and still not gain! It was like Heaven.

But then, back to the States we came. Hersheys just didn't cut it anymore. So I began taste testing what I could find locally always recalling the vendors' words "that chocolate was made today and is to be eatenn today." I tried Truffles, I tried mixed boxes whose photos made them LOOK LIKE the insides of the tiny little boxes in Switzerland. But nothing measured up.

One day, I was in a local store and sighted these Guylian Belgian Chocolate Sea Shells. It was my turn to bring treats to a group I go to on Thursdays. The chocolates were on sale and I had noted that the Belgian chocolates I had tried did seem fresher than the others, and tasted better than other brands shipped in Stateside. So I bought two boxes and trooped off to my meeting.

As Soon as I had put the chocolate out, I checked to make sure that no one else had brought chocolate as a treat. Nope. Then I took one and ambled away to give them a taste. I wanted to make certain I hadn't bought something awful. So with my back turned to the group, I tried out a piece. I popped the whole thing in my mouth and went through my usualy routine for checking chocolate. I let the piece of candy just lay on my tongue for about 25 seconds until it had softened up and then began lightly and politely sucking on the chocolate. Oh my. It was fresh and had a delightful sweet chocolate taste very similar to the Swiss Chocolate I so loved. In fact, this was just a bit creamier. With little time to spare, I went ahead and bit into the piece expecting solid chocolate. But no, there was a soft inner core of ever sweeter, softer, creamier, fresher, chocolate in the center. I was Delightfully Surprised. Hating to hurry, I went ahead and chewed the piece up so that I could join the group.

But my what an experience. I found myself going back to the counter several times during the afternoon, to get another piece of that chocolate I had brought. I urged the others to try it and each one was also very impressed with this chocolate. Where DID you get these? Were they terribly expensive? How long do they keep? Can I put them in my candy jar or will they melt? The SeaShells were an overwhelming success. I shared that I got them at the local pharmacy on the corner, that they were currently on sale, best to eat them as soon as possible, but they will keep in the freezer without problem for a year, and, yes you should be able to keep them in the candy jar as it was then winter here in Arizona, but I would not put them in a jar during the summer. I have found that even with air conditioning, delicate chocolate does not hold up well out of its box when it is hot. Somehow the candies sense the outside heat and their insides get really old and stale and melt. Ugh. Best to keep them in the fridge in the summer. If you buy them on sale as a gift, stick them in the freezer to preserve them like new.

I am amazed at how good these are and I do pick them up on sale and pop them in the freezer for gifts, and keep them hidden in the fridge as a treat for myself. They are indeed, the best "other country, Stateside Product" I have found. Whatever theis company does is amazing because these tender candies stay fresh and edible for those of us here. So, I highly Recommend them as they are my favorites. I would NOT order them in the summer or when it starts to get warmish at all as they will probably melt in transit unless they are shipped in dry ice, which I do not know. But I only have them shipped in the dead of winter because it can get so warm here at any time.

So, If you are a candy eater, and love foreighn chocolates, then get some of these. They are a wonderful treat. I hope you like them as well as I do.!

Summary: The best white bread we've found so far!
Text: My wife was recently diagnosed with Celiac Disease, which was a hard blow for us... we love our bread and pasta and I personally made a ton of bread from scratch. After many unsuccessful attempts to recreate my favorite bread recipes using mixtures of various flour types, I decided to go the boxed route to see how things stacked up. Schar products have me hooked! I made the white bread last night and it turned out better than any of the others we've tried and don't come across as too heavy on any one type of flour. I do not recommend using a bread machine for the mix. Why? It's a simple matter to throw the ingredients in a mixer and they don't require any fancy treatment. Pat the batter into a greased and floured loaf pan, stick it someplace warm with a wet towel over it and wait. That's probably the most important thing... It doesn't give a time on the box, it just says "until doubled". Give it time... Took over an hour for me, but it was a bit cooler in the house than it probably would have liked. Baked it for exactly the time mentioned on the box and placed the loaf pan on a cookie sheet filled with water. Loaf came out looking like it might be under-cooked, but it wasn't! Came out perfect, works for toast, french toast, sandwiches, etc... Love it! Buying my first five pack through Amazon now!

This bread tastes great and is super easy to make. Believe me, it would have to be for me to make it!

It's pretty good following the package directions, but what really made it fantastic was adding a full additional cup of water to the recipe, as recommended by one of the other reviewers. (This brings the total to 3 cups of water.)

Following the package directions, you really need to eat this bread the day you bake it (so make sure you make it in the morning!). Fortunately, this has not been a problem at my house. Adding the extra cup of water, it was still edible the next day.

I did put the bread in the oven to rise for 30 minutes, with the oven temperature set at "warm".

-------------------

Since writing the above, I purchased a bread machine. Sunbeam 5891 2-Pound Programmable Breadmaker

After 5 or 6 trial-and-error attempts, all moderately successful, I have cracked the code to making this bread mix work optimally in this machine. Here it is:

Instead of putting the wet ingredients in first (as the machine's booklet instructs), put the DRY ingredients in first, then the wet ingredients. Use the settings:

1 Basic
1 1/2 pound loaf
Dark crust

While following the directions (of the machine) will work, following my directions leads to bread that rises half again as high. This yields a fluffier texture which, frankly, tastes less gluten-free. (You know what I'm talking about!) The individual slices of bread are then so huge that you can literally cut one in half and make a decent-size PBJ.

We have used and enjoyed this European firm's baked bread and hoped that their mix would produce an even better product. Our first attempt was a near disaster! The dough was hard to mix, did not rise enough, and came out of the oven unbrowned and tough. Since I have baked bread for many years, I decided to try some modifications to see if the end product could be improved.

I mixed the dough using a stand mixer, rather than by hand in a bowl. I added one TBS of sugar, and increased the water from two to nearly three cups. Before putting the bread in the oven I brushed the top with melted butter.

The result was a nicely browned loaf which had risen nicely. The texture and flavor was very satisfactory. Now we can have nice tasting white bread available all the time.

I can just heat up a small pan of milk on the stove, add the Via Ready Brew to my mug, pour, mix and enjoy!  Also it is cheaper than going to Starbucks.  Their grande size latte is about $4 whereas one packet of Via Ready Brew from Amazon comes out to $2.68 for a serving.  Also, depending on your mug size you can add more or not as much milk so the flavor is to your liking.  I'm going to stock up while I can on this :)
